name: Agents behind worker
summary: Agents run on an internal-only network whose only route out is a Warden worker. Recipes ship for Ethos, Hermes, OpenClaw and ZeroClaw.

name: Identity contract + CLI
label: identity-contract
summary: Defines how any agent platform sends a user's identity to Warden, and ships a small `warden identity` CLI so any agent, script or harness can get a token and route through the worker. Warden stays platform-neutral: a harness only needs an OIDC ID token from the configured issuer and a proxy URL. Phase 1 is attribution only, so a missing or bad token never blocks a request and default-deny policy is unchanged. `warden identity exec` runs a command behind a loopback forwarder that keeps the short-lived token out of the command's environment and argv and refreshes it before expiry.
design: Contract v1 (docs/identity-contract.md): an OIDC ID token from the worker's `identity.issuer` whose `aud` contains `identity.audience`, signed RS256 or ES256, with `sub` required and `email`, `groups` and `sid` expected. The doc separates what the worker enforces (iss, aud, exp/nbf with 60s skew, alg) from what is issuer configuration (1h ID-token lifetime, groups claim). Identity is keyed on (iss, sub); email is a display attribute. Later phases may add to v1 but never change a v1 header or claim.

Getting the token from Dex: cross-client trust, with scopes `openid email profile groups offline_access audience:server:client_id:<worker audience>` on the confidential `agent-harness` client (harness platforms) or the public device-code `warden-cli` client (user machines). `groups` and `offline_access` are required, or the token has no groups claim and cannot be refreshed. The reference Dex config (W-P1-DEX-01) keeps the data-plane audience `warden` separate from the console client `warden-console`: `warden` never logs anyone in, a console login token never carries aud `warden`, and the CP console accepts only aud `warden-console`, so a harness token is never a console token. Workers should set `identity.allowedAZP: [agent-harness, warden-cli]`.

Transport: `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` on CONNECT (Bearer also accepted), which clients send from a proxy URL `http://session:<token>@<worker>:8080`. The fallback `X-Warden-Identity: Bearer <token>` only works on connections where the worker terminates TLS; on raw tunnels it cannot be read or stripped, so harnesses must prefer Proxy-Authorization. Attribution is bound per tunnel at CONNECT time. Only https through CONNECT is supported: the worker drops any other request line as unsupported_protocol (internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn).

Harness duties: keep the IdP login and refresh token out of the agent's reach (another uid or a sidecar), give each user's processes only that user's token, refresh before expiry, recycle connections after a refresh, and never put the token in prompts, model context, logs, argv or tool output. Phase 1 limit, stated plainly: a token placed in HTTPS_PROXY is readable by the agent's own tools and is a snapshot that goes stale after about 1h. That is tolerated for `warden identity env` while P1 is attribute-only. `warden identity exec` (W-P1-IDC-04) removes both limits in P1: it runs the child behind a loopback forwarder that holds the user's ID token in memory, refreshes it before expiry and injects it on each CONNECT, so the token is never in the parent's or the child's environment or argv. P2 extends the same forwarder with agent tokens (W-P2-RCP-02/06).

`warden identity` CLI: new package internal/identityclient plus a new cobra subtree in cmd/proxy that ignores the worker `--config`. Config comes from flags, `WARDEN_IDENTITY_*` env vars, or `<os.UserConfigDir()>/warden/identity.yaml`. Subcommands: `login` (OIDC discovery and RFC 8628 device-code grant via golang.org/x/oauth2, public client by default, optional secret only from `--client-secret-env NAME`), `token` (prints a valid ID token, refreshing at 2/3 of exp-iat, never prompts), `status` (prints iss, sub, email, groups and exp, never the token), `env --worker host:port` (HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy with session credentials, NO_PROXY for loopback, optional CA variables, token from cache, `--token-stdin` or `--token-file`), and `logout`.

Cache safety: refresh and ID tokens live in a 0600 file inside a 0700 directory, written by temp file, fsync and rename. The CLI refuses a cache file readable by group or others. Refresh runs under an exclusive lock and re-reads the cache after taking it, because Dex rotates refresh tokens on use. If the issuer is unreachable, `token` serves the cached token while it is valid and warns on stderr. Exit code 2 means login is required; 3 means the issuer is unreachable and no valid cached token remains. Non-loopback http issuers are refused unless `--insecure-http-issuer` is passed. Tokens, device codes and IdP error bodies are never printed to stderr or logged; `--verbose` shows only an 8-hex sha256 fingerprint.

Back-compat and upgrades: everything is opt-in. With no `identity` block, workers behave exactly as today, and existing recipes and proxy URLs without credentials keep working. The new `identity` commands change no flag or behaviour of `run` or `control-plane`. P2 extends internal/identityclient with agent keys, RFC 8693 exchange and `identity forward`, and adds `--agent-id` and `--run-as` to the P1 `identity exec`; the contract doc records that v1 Dex tokens must stay accepted on upgrade for workers that already set `identity.issuer` (see open question on W-P2-WBND-01).
done_when: From a clean state, `scripts/smoke-identity.sh` starts the control plane, Dex with LDAP and an attribute-mode worker, then routes a plain curl container (internal-only network, no direct route out, no IdP access) through the worker using `warden identity env --token-stdin` with a seeded user's token. The CP traffic API filtered by that user returns events carrying their sub, email and groups with identity_status=valid. Requests with no token and with a bad token are still allowed and recorded as `none` and `invalid`. No token appears in the script, CLI or worker logs. `warden identity exec --worker <worker> -- curl https://<allowed host>` is attributed to the same user, while the child's environment and argv contain no token and the token is refreshed without restarting the child.

tickets.title: Write the agent identity contract for harness builders
tickets.body: Add docs/identity-contract.md (Contract v1), telling harness builders exactly what token to send, how to send it, what the worker does with it, and what the harness must never do. It documents behaviour from p1-verify-token, the `warden identity` CLI and the smoke recipe, so it merges last in this feature, after the code it describes exists. A small drift test keeps the header names and status values in the doc in line with internal/identity.
requirements: Version marker `Contract v1`, with a rule that later phases may add to v1 but never change a v1 header or claim. A short 'Upgrading to Phase 2' section says that v1 Dex tokens must stay accepted for workers that already set `identity.issuer`.

Token section: iss byte-identical to `identity.issuer`, aud contains `identity.audience`, RS256/ES256 only, exp/nbf with 60s skew, `sub` required, `email`/`groups`/`sid` expected. A table marks each rule as either enforced by the worker or issuer configuration (1h lifetime, groups claim). Lists the Dex scopes, including `groups` and `offline_access`. Identity is keyed on (iss, sub); email is display-only. Explains that the worker audience (`warden` in the reference config) is a data-plane-only client separate from the console client `warden-console`, and recommends `identity.allowedAZP` listing the harness and CLI clients.

Transport section, with exact strings: `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` (username `session`, case-sensitive; Bearer also accepted) from the proxy URL `http://session:<token>@<worker>:8080`; fallback `X-Warden-Identity: Bearer <token>` only on TLS-terminated connections; both stripped before forwarding in every mode, including off; two valid identities with different sub give identity_status `conflict` and the request still proceeds in P1 (a 403 is reserved for P2 require mode); attribution bound per tunnel at CONNECT time; only https through CONNECT, plain HTTP_PROXY requests are denied. Limits: a token over 16 KiB is recorded as invalid with reason too_large, and a CONNECT header block over 32 KiB or 100 lines, or not complete within 10s, gets 431 with reason headers_too_large.

Modes and statuses: per-agent `off|attribute` (`require` is rejected until Phase 2), identity_status `off|none|valid|invalid|expired|unverified|conflict` (W-P1-VRFY-01) and what the dashboard shows for each, the event fields user_sub, user_email, user_groups, user_groups_truncated, user_sid, identity_status, identity_reason, the metric `warden_identity_verify_total{result,reason}` (Prometheus name of `warden.identity.verify.total`), and the query `/dashboard/api/traffic?user=`. Recommends alerting on the share of non-valid results per agent.

Harness duties and a do-not list: IdP login and refresh token kept out of the agent's reach, one token per user, refresh before expiry, no tokens in prompts, model context, logs, argv, tool output or `curl -v` output. A 'Phase 1 limitation' callout covers the token in HTTPS_PROXY (readable by agent tools, stale after about 1h, plaintext agent-to-worker hop) and points to `warden identity exec` (W-P1-IDC-04), which keeps the token out of the child's env and argv and refreshes it before expiry.

Client compatibility table: preemptive Basic from proxy-URL credentials (curl, Go net/http, Python requests, Node with NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1) works; clients that send credentials only after a 407 challenge get no identity in P1 because the worker never challenges. Examples use the CA variables printed by `warden identity env --ca` and show tokens only as `eyJ...redacted`.
Linked from README.md, docs/recipes/README.md and docs/identity-dex.md, and the contract doc links back to docs/identity-dex.md.
plan: Write new docs/identity-contract.md with sections: Contract v1, Token, Getting a token (Dex), Transport, Lifetimes and limits, Modes and statuses, Observability, Harness duties, Phase 1 limitations, Client compatibility, Upgrading to Phase 2.
Copy header names, status values and mode names from the exported constants in internal/identity and internal/proxy (added by W-P1-VRFY-01/02) rather than retyping them.

Add runnable examples, marked as `run` blocks, for `warden identity login`, `status`, `token`, `exec --worker 127.0.0.1:8080 -- curl ...` and `eval "$(warden identity env --worker 127.0.0.1:8080 --ca certs/proxy-ca.crt)"`, then curl, Python requests and Node, all against the compose files from W-P1-IDC-03.
Add links from README.md, docs/recipes/README.md (new 'Per-user identity' section) and docs/identity-dex.md.

Add new internal/identity/contract_doc_test.go (TestContractDocMatchesConstants) that reads ../../docs/identity-contract.md and fails if any exported header, mode or status constant is missing from it.
acceptance: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestContractDocMatchesConstants` passes, and fails when a constant such as the `conflict` status or `X-Warden-Identity` is renamed without updating the doc.
With the smoke compose stack from W-P1-IDC-03 running, every `run` block in docs/identity-contract.md exits 0 when pasted in order.
`grep -l 'identity-contract.md' README.md docs/recipes/README.md docs/identity-dex.md` lists all three files.
`grep -E 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}' docs/identity-contract.md` returns nothing.
The doc lists exactly the statuses off, none, valid, invalid, expired, unverified and conflict and the modes off and attribute, matching config validation in internal/config.
`scripts/check.sh` passes.

tickets.title: Add `warden identity` CLI for login, token, status and proxy env
tickets.body: Create new package internal/identityclient (OIDC discovery, RFC 8628 device-code grant, refresh, a locked file cache and proxy env rendering) and a new `identity` cobra subtree in cmd/proxy with `login`, `token`, `status`, `env` and `logout`. It works with any standards OIDC issuer and never hard-codes Dex. Adding the subtree changes nothing about `run` or `control-plane`, and the worker and CP are untouched.
requirements: Configuration in precedence order: flags `--issuer`, `--client-id` (default `warden-cli`, the public device-code client from W-P1-DEX-01), `--audience` (default `warden`, used only for the aud warning below; the Dex cross-client scope `audience:server:client_id:warden` is passed with `--scopes` as documented, never hard-coded), `--client-secret-env NAME` (never a literal secret), `--scopes` (added to the defaults `openid email profile groups offline_access`), `--cache-dir`; then WARDEN_IDENTITY_ISSUER, WARDEN_IDENTITY_CLIENT_ID, WARDEN_IDENTITY_AUDIENCE, WARDEN_IDENTITY_SCOPES, WARDEN_IDENTITY_CACHE_DIR; then optional `<os.UserConfigDir()>/warden/identity.yaml`. The root `--config` is never loaded. Non-loopback http issuers are refused unless `--insecure-http-issuer` is passed, which prints a stderr warning.
`login` runs discovery (issuer must match byte for byte) and the device-code grant, honouring `interval`, `slow_down` and `expires_in`, and prints the verification URI and user code to stderr only.

Cache: `<cache-dir>/<sha256(issuer|client_id)[:16]>.json` holds the refresh token, ID token and the local receipt time. The file is 0600 in a 0700 directory, written by temp file, fsync and rename. A cache readable by group or others is refused with an error naming the path. Refresh holds an exclusive flock on `<cache>.lock` and re-reads the cache after taking it.

`token` prints the cached ID token while less than 2/3 of exp-iat has passed (measured from local receipt time), and refreshes otherwise, persisting any rotated refresh token. It never prompts. If the issuer is unreachable and the cached token is still valid, it prints it and warns on stderr. Exit 2 means login required (no, expired or revoked refresh token); exit 3 means the issuer is unreachable with no valid cached token.

`env --worker host:port [--token-stdin | --token-file PATH] [--ca PATH] [--shell sh|fish|powershell] [--format dotenv|json] [--include-http]` prints HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy built with url.UserPassword("session", token), plus NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1. `--ca` adds SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. HTTP_PROXY is printed only with `--include-http`, with a note that the worker denies plain http. The token expiry and a warning that child processes can read the token go to stderr. The token is never accepted as an argv value.

`status` prints iss, sub, email, groups, exp and the cache path, never the token. `logout` deletes the cache entry. Before caching, claims are parsed (unverified; the worker verifies) and a missing groups claim or an aud without the configured audience prints a warning naming only the claim.

Only `token` and `env` write secrets, and only to stdout. By default nothing is logged except errors. `--verbose` logs issuer, client_id, scopes, expiry and an 8-hex sha256 fingerprint, never a raw token, device code or IdP error body (oauth2.RetrieveError is wrapped).
Add golang.org/x/oauth2 to go.mod, pinned to a release at least 2 weeks old, passing govulncheck. A cached `token` call does no network I/O.
plan: go.mod: add golang.org/x/oauth2 (DeviceAuth, DeviceAccessToken and the refresh grant). Use plain JSON discovery so the CLI does not need go-oidc.

New internal/identityclient/config.go and discovery.go: Config{Issuer, ClientID, Audience, ClientSecretEnv, Scopes, CacheDir, AllowInsecureIssuer}, LoadConfig(flags, env, file), and Discover(ctx, *http.Client, issuer) returning the token and device_authorization endpoints after the issuer match and https checks.
New internal/identityclient/store.go: FileStore with Load, Save (temp, fsync, rename, 0600 in 0700) and WithLock(fn) using an exclusive flock on `<cache>.lock` (unix builds only).

New internal/identityclient/client.go: Client{Config, HTTP *http.Client, Now func() time.Time} with Login(ctx, prompt io.Writer), Token(ctx) and Status(), plus typed errors ErrLoginRequired and ErrIssuerUnreachable that cmd maps to exit codes 2 and 3.
New internal/identityclient/env.go: ProxyEnv(worker, token, opts) rendering sh, fish, powershell, dotenv and json output.
New cmd/proxy/identity.go: newIdentityCmd() with login, token, status, env and logout; register it in cmd/proxy/root.go next to the existing AddCommand calls.

Tests in new internal/identityclient/*_test.go against an httptest fake issuer (discovery, device_authorization with authorization_pending then slow_down then success, refresh grant that rotates the refresh token) and a fake clock; an httptest CONNECT listener for the env test; cmd/proxy identity_test.go with a captured slog handler and stderr buffer.
acceptance: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run 'TestDeviceLogin|TestDevicePollSlowDown|TestRefreshAtTwoThirds|TestTokenNoPrompt|TestIssuerDownServesCache'` passes: login stores a refresh token, slow_down raises the poll interval, `token` refreshes exactly once after 2/3 of lifetime, an expired refresh token returns ErrLoginRequired without prompting, and an unreachable issuer still returns a valid cached token.

`go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestConcurrentRefreshSingleFlight -race` shows two concurrent Token() calls cause exactly one refresh request against a rotating fake issuer, and both get the same token.
TestCacheFilePerms checks the cache file is 0600 in a 0700 directory, and a cache chmodded to 0644 is refused with an error naming the path.

`go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestEnvConnectHeader` builds an http.Transport with http.ProxyURL from parsed `env` output and an httptest CONNECT listener sees `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)`; the default output contains no HTTP_PROXY.

`go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityCmd` confirms the subcommands are registered, no `--client-secret` flag taking a literal exists, the root `--config` is not read, and with `--verbose` captured stderr and logs contain no substring of the ID, refresh or device code values.
`go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestInsecureIssuerRejected` rejects an http non-loopback issuer unless AllowInsecureIssuer is set.
`scripts/check.sh` passes, including the coverage gate and govulncheck.

tickets.title: Add generic identity smoke test with a curl agent
tickets.body: Add an opt-in smoke recipe and script that prove a plain curl container, with no agent framework, can be attributed to a user through the `warden identity` CLI and the contract. The script plays the harness: it gets a seeded LDAP user's token from the dev Dex config and hands it to `warden identity env --token-stdin` inside the agent container. It does not loosen the SafeDialer private-IP block, so upstream header stripping stays covered by the W-P1-VRFY-05 integration test.
requirements: New deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity-smoke.yml, combined with `-f` with docker-compose.control-plane.yml and docker-compose.identity.yml (W-P1-DEX-02). It runs one worker in attribute mode and a pinned-digest curl agent on an `internal: true` network whose only route out is the worker and which cannot reach Dex. The static `warden` binary is copied from the warden image into a shared read-only volume by an init service; no new image is built.

New configs/config.control-plane.identity.yaml and configs/config.worker.identity.yaml with the identity block (defaultMode attribute, issuer http://dex:5556/dex with allowInsecureIssuer true, audience warden, allowedAZP [agent-harness, warden-cli]) and an allowlist entry for one public https host. No SSRF or private-IP setting is changed.

New scripts/smoke-identity.sh gets the token with `scripts/dex-token.sh --raw <user>` from W-P1-DEX-02 (password grant on `agent-harness`, enabled only in config.dev.yaml) run in a toolbox container on cp-net, and pipes it to `warden identity env --worker worker:8080 --token-stdin --ca /certs/proxy-ca.crt` inside the agent; the token never goes through argv or an echoed variable.

It checks the CP: `GET /dashboard/api/traffic?user=<seeded email>` returns the request with user_sub, user_email, user_groups containing the seeded group, and identity_status=valid. The smoke CP runs with console.auth none (the default), so all CP dashboard calls go through one helper that sends no credentials; an oidc-mode CP is out of scope, because W-P1-SSO-06 rejects the shared bearer on /dashboard/*. The smoke worker authenticates to the CP the same way the control-plane recipe's workers do (shared token before W-P1-WTOK-06, its own registered worker token after).
It also sends one request with no token and one with a garbage token, and checks both are allowed and recorded as `none` and `invalid`, proving attribute mode never blocks.
Hygiene: `set -euo pipefail`, no `set -x`, curl without -v, only token fingerprints printed, `docker compose down -v` in a trap, and a non-zero exit that names the failed step.
Run only on request through a new `scripts/check.sh --smoke-identity` flag, so the default check run needs no Docker.
plan: Add new configs/config.control-plane.identity.yaml and configs/config.worker.identity.yaml, modelled on configs/config.control-plane.yaml and configs/config.worker.yaml.

Add new deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity-smoke.yml with control-plane, worker, an init service that copies /usr/local/bin/warden to a shared volume, a toolbox service on the Dex network, and the curl agent on an internal network.

Add new scripts/smoke-identity.sh: run scripts/gen-certs.sh, `docker compose ... up -d --wait`, fetch the token, run `warden identity env --token-stdin` and curl in the agent, then send the no-token and bad-token requests.
Add the CP helper and poll `/dashboard/api/traffic?user=` (W-P1-VRFY-04) until the expected events appear or a 60s timeout fails the step.
Assert that `curl --noproxy '*' https://<allowed host>` from the agent fails, and grep the script output and `docker compose logs worker` for JWT-shaped strings.
Add the `--smoke-identity` flag to scripts/check.sh next to the existing `--integration` flag.
acceptance: `docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity-smoke.yml config -q` exits 0.

From a clean state, `scripts/smoke-identity.sh` exits 0 and prints PASS for each step: token, routed request, CP attribution, no-token status, bad-token status, direct-egress blocked, no token in logs.

The CP traffic API filtered by the seeded email returns at least one event for the allowed host with user_sub set, user_groups containing the seeded LDAP group and identity_status=valid; the no-token and bad-token events show `none` and `invalid` with decision allow.
`scripts/smoke-identity.sh 2>&1 | grep -cE 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}'` prints 0, and the same grep over `docker compose logs worker` prints 0.
`scripts/check.sh` without `--smoke-identity` does not start Docker and still passes.

tickets.title: Add `warden identity exec` with a loopback forwarder that refreshes the token
tickets.body: Add `warden identity exec`, which starts a CONNECT-only forwarder on loopback and runs a child command with HTTPS_PROXY pointing at it. The forwarder holds the user's short-lived ID token only in memory, refreshes it before expiry through the W-P1-IDC-02 client and injects it on each CONNECT to the worker, so the token never appears in the parent's or the child's environment or argv and never goes stale while the child runs. This removes the P1 token-in-HTTPS_PROXY limitation for laptops and CI. P2 extends the same forwarder with agent tokens and `--run-as` (W-P2-RCP-02, W-P2-RCP-06).
requirements: `warden identity exec --worker host:port [--listen 127.0.0.1:0] [--ca PATH] [--include-http] -- <cmd> [args]` in the W-P1-IDC-02 `identity` subtree. A non-loopback `--listen` is refused before any child starts. The token is never accepted as a flag, env var or argv value.

The ID token comes only from Client.Token() (W-P1-IDC-02: cache, refresh at 2/3 of exp-iat under the cache lock) and is held in the exec process's memory. A timer refreshes it at 2/3 of its lifetime, and every new CONNECT uses the current token, so tunnels opened after a refresh carry the new token without restarting the child. It is never written to the environment of the exec process or the child, to argv, to files or to logs.

The child gets HTTPS_PROXY and https_proxy as `http://wx:<credential>@127.0.0.1:<port>`, where the credential is 128 random bits generated per run, checked in constant time and never sent to the worker; a CONNECT without it gets 407. NO_PROXY and no_proxy are set to localhost,127.0.0.1,::1; HTTP_PROXY only with `--include-http`; inherited ALL_PROXY, HTTP(S)_PROXY and WARDEN_IDENTITY_* are removed (stderr warning when an existing HTTPS_PROXY is overridden); `--ca` adds the same CA variables as `warden identity env`.

Forwarder (new internal/identityclient/forwarder.go): only CONNECT (other methods 405); a CONNECT header block capped at 32 KiB and 100 lines with a 10s read deadline (431 on overflow), matching W-P1-VRFY-02; any client Proxy-Authorization is dropped and `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` is sent; it dials only the configured `--worker` and never the CONNECT target; the worker's status line is relayed verbatim; with no valid token it answers 503 and makes no dial.

Process handling: stdio is inherited; SIGTERM and SIGHUP are forwarded, and SIGINT and SIGQUIT are forwarded only when stdin is not a terminal. The exit code is the child's, or 128+signo when a signal killed it. On ErrLoginRequired at start, a terminal runs the device-code login on stderr; otherwise exec exits 2 without starting the child. Logs carry only an 8-hex token fingerprint with `--verbose`.
plan: New internal/identityclient/forwarder.go: Forwarder{WorkerAddr, Token func(ctx) (string, error), ClientCredential} with Serve(ctx, net.Listener), the bounded CONNECT header reader, the single worker dial and verbatim status relay, and a bidirectional copy.

New cmd/proxy/identity_exec.go: flag parsing, the loopback listener, the per-run credential, the refresh timer over Client.Token(), the child env builder (reusing the W-P1-IDC-02 env renderer for CA variables) and os/exec supervision with signal.Notify.
Tests in internal/identityclient with an httptest CONNECT listener as the fake worker and a fake clock, and in cmd/proxy with the helper-process pattern (the child prints its env and argv).
Document `exec` in docs/identity-contract.md through W-P1-IDC-01 and in docs/recipes/README.md, stating that a same-uid child can still read the identity cache.
acceptance: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExecForwarder` shows the fake worker receives `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` even when the client sent its own, a GET gets 405, a 40 KiB CONNECT header block gets 431, a CONNECT without the per-run credential gets 407, and dials go only to the worker address.

With a fake clock and a rotating fake issuer, a CONNECT made after 2/3 of the token lifetime carries the refreshed token while the same child keeps running: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExecForwarderRefresh`.

`go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExec` shows the child's env and argv contain the loopback HTTPS_PROXY with the per-run credential and no substring of the ID or refresh token, `--listen 0.0.0.0:0` is refused before any child starts, `exec -- sh -c 'exit 7'` exits 7, and a non-terminal run with no cached login exits 2 without starting the child.
`scripts/check.sh` passes, including the coverage gate.

summary: Extends the P1 `warden identity` client with agent keys and the RFC 8693 token exchange, extends the P1 loopback forwarder from W-P1-IDC-04 into `warden identity forward` for sidecar containers and adds agent tokens to the P1 `warden identity exec` for laptops and CI, and ships Claude Code and Codex CLI compose recipes behind a require-mode worker. The agent container never holds the agent key, the Dex refresh token, a Warden token or a real vendor API key: a separate sidecar holds the identity material and the worker swaps placeholder API keys. Everything is new and opt-in; existing recipes, `run`, `control-plane` and the P1 identity commands are unchanged.
design: Commands. All new commands live in the `identity` cobra subtree that W-P1-IDC-02 adds under the `warden` root (cmd/proxy/root.go `Use: "warden"`); there is no separate `warden-identity` tool and no `proxy identity exec`. They reuse internal/identityclient from W-P1-IDC-02: the same config precedence (flags, WARDEN_IDENTITY_*, identity.yaml), shared cache, lock file and `--client-id` default `warden-cli`. New: `enroll` (agent key) and `forward` (long-lived forwarder for a sidecar container). `exec` (forwarder on loopback plus a child process) ships in P1 as W-P1-IDC-04; P2 adds `--agent-id` and `--run-as` to it. `token` and `status` gain `--agent-id`. New env vars: WARDEN_IDENTITY_TOKEN_ENDPOINT, WARDEN_IDENTITY_AGENT_ID, WARDEN_IDENTITY_AGENT_KEY_FILE, WARDEN_IDENTITY_CP_CA.

Agent key. `warden identity enroll --agent-id <id> [--key-file PATH] [--force]` generates an Ed25519 key with crypto/ed25519 and writes it as PKCS#8 PEM to a 0600 file in a 0700 directory (default `<os.UserConfigDir()>/warden/agents/<id>.key`), by temp file, fsync and rename. It refuses to overwrite without --force and refuses a key file readable by group or others, as the P1 cache does. It prints only the public JWK (kty OKP, crv Ed25519, alg EdDSA, kid = RFC 7638 thumbprint computed with internal/keys from W-P2-KEYS-01, no `d`), which W-P2-AREG-02 and the offline CLI from p2-agent-registry accept as-is. Agent keys are per harness deployment (one sidecar fleet), not per user machine: the registry holds at most 2 keys per agent, so rotation is enroll a new key, register it, switch the sidecar, then remove the old key.

Subject token. By default it comes from the P1 Client.Token() path (refresh at 2/3 of lifetime with the refresh token, never prompts). `--subject-token-file PATH` (must be 0600, re-read before each exchange) supports harness platforms that obtain the user's ID token themselves and the CI smoke path through scripts/dex-token.sh. No new code path ever starts a device-code prompt except `warden identity login` and an `exec` run attached to a terminal. On ErrLoginRequired the forwarder keeps serving the current Warden token until it expires, then refuses new tunnels with reason login_required until the user runs `warden identity login` against the same cache.

Exchange. `Client.Exchange` POSTs form-encoded to the CP `/oauth2/token` (W-P2-TOKX-03) with grant_type token-exchange, subject_token_type id_token, audience=warden-worker, optional scope, and a private_key_jwt assertion (header alg EdDSA plus kid; claims iss=sub=agent id, aud=exactly `--token-endpoint`, iat, exp=iat+60s, 128-bit random jti; a new assertion per request, meeting W-P2-TOKX-01). The token endpoint has no implied default. CP TLS is verified against `--cp-ca` (the proxy CA in compose). The Warden token is held only in memory and never written to disk. Re-exchange starts at 2/3 of expires_in measured from local receipt time, with up to 10% random jitter, single-flighted. On network errors it retries with jittered exponential backoff (1s to 60s) while the current token is valid; on 429 it honours Retry-After. invalid_client, unauthorized_client and invalid_grant map to ErrExchangeDenied{Code} (exit 4); only the RFC 6749 error code is surfaced, never the response body. Without `--agent-id` no exchange happens and the forwarder injects the P1 Dex ID token, so the forwarder also works against P1 attribute-mode workers.

Forwarder rules (security-critical, in internal/identityclient/forwarder.go, added in P1 by W-P1-IDC-04 and extended here): it accepts only CONNECT and answers any other method with 405 without forwarding; it reads the CONNECT header block with a 32 KiB and 100-line cap and a 10s deadline (matching the W-P1-VRFY-02 worker limits); it drops any Proxy-Authorization sent by the client and injects `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` (Contract v1); it dials only the single configured `--worker` address and never resolves or dials the CONNECT target; it relays the worker's status line and headers verbatim, including 403 and 407 with Proxy-Authenticate; with no valid token it answers 503 with header `X-Warden-Forwarder-Reason: login_required|cp_unreachable|exchange_denied` and never dials the worker; it caps concurrent tunnels (`--max-tunnels`, default 512, then 503).

Token rotation and long tunnels. Each tunnel snapshots the token and its exp at CONNECT. The worker re-checks CONNECT identity expiry on every terminated request (W-P1-VRFY-02), so after a rotation the forwarder drains old tunnels: a draining tunnel is closed after 2s with no bytes in either direction, and at the latest at its token's exp. New CONNECTs always carry the newest token. This bounds how long any tunnel outlives a block, an agent disable or a key removal to the token lifetime (at most 15m for an exchanged token), with no separate max-age flag; the worker enforces the same bound by closing require-mode tunnels at exp plus skew (W-P2-WBND-09), and the client's next CONNECT carries the newest token. A 407 from the worker triggers one forced refresh and one retry of the CONNECT before the 407 is relayed.

Recipe topology (isolation preserved). The agent container joins only `<agent>-internal` (internal: true) and gets HTTPS_PROXY=http://warden-identity:3128 with no credentials. The `warden-identity` sidecar runs `warden identity forward --agent-id <id> --listen 0.0.0.0:3128 --worker warden:8080` and joins `<agent>-internal` and cp-net; it keeps the agent key and the identity cache on its own named volume, which is never mounted into the agent. The worker joins `<agent>-internal`, egress and cp-net. Dex and LDAP come from deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml (W-P1-DEX-02) and the CP from docker-compose.control-plane.yml (per-worker tokens from W-P1-WTOK-06, or worker certs once W-P2-WCA-06 moves that recipe), run with `--policy-store=versioned --bundles=require` and a CP config with `keys.enabled: true` and a `tokenService:` block; the bootstrap exports the bundle JWKS (`warden control-plane keys export --purpose bundle`) to a volume the worker pins through `controlPlane.bundleKeysFile`; neither is ever attached to the agent network. The forwarder adds no egress route because it only connects to the worker. `exec` (W-P1-IDC-04, extended by W-P2-RCP-06) is documented as the laptop and CI option: it keeps tokens out of the child's env, argv and logs, but a same-uid child can read the key and cache unless `--run-as` is used.

Agent identity at the worker. Each recipe worker is started with `warden run --agent-id <id>` (the worker binding from W-P2-AREG-05; `central.agentID` is the YAML form), so the worker's agent id equals the registry id. Without it, internal/worker/judge.go defaultAgentID falls back to `agent:<port>` from agentid.PortBindingIdentifier and W-P2-WBND-02's act check could never match. The served policy also carries exactly one `agents` entry with that id and `identity: require` (W-P2-WBND-03).

Vendor credentials. The agent gets placeholder keys only (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=anthropic_secret_001, OPENAI_API_KEY=openai_secret_001), and a recipe worker config maps each placeholder with `secrets: [{placeholder, envVar}]` as configs/config.example-worker.yaml does today, so the real key is set only on the worker container. Subscription logins (Claude.ai sign-in for Claude Code, ChatGPT sign-in for Codex) are unsupported in these recipes, because they would put real OAuth credentials in the agent's home directory.

Registration. A one-shot `identity-bootstrap` service enrolls the sidecar key if none exists and registers the agent with the offline `warden control-plane agent register --state-dir` CLI from p2-agent-registry (allowed group `eng` from the W-P1-DEX-02 LDAP seed), and is idempotent on a second `up`. The docs also show the console path (W-P2-AREG-02) for production. Warden services in the new recipes build from the repo Dockerfile (`build: {context: ../.., dockerfile: Dockerfile}`), because the published `ethosagent/warden:0.3.0` image does not contain the new subcommands.

Degraded modes, documented in docs/recipes. CP down: traffic continues until the current Warden token expires (at most 15m), then new tunnels get 503 cp_unreachable. Dex down: subject refresh fails; exchange continues while the cached ID token is valid (at most 1h), then login_required. Sidecar restart: re-exchanges from the cached subject token (Warden tokens are memory-only). Clock skew: more than `identity.clockSkewSeconds` (default 60s) breaks worker verification (W-P2-WBND-01) and more than 60s breaks the assertion, so NTP is required. Disabled agent or removed key: new tunnels are refused at the worker; old tunnels end at token exp at the latest.

Observability. Structured stderr logs only: event=tunnel_open, tunnel_close (target host:port, worker status, bytes, duration, 8-hex sha256 token fingerprint), event=token_rotated (fingerprint, exp, draining count), event=exchange (outcome, RFC error code) and event=login_required. Optional `--health-listen` (off by default; on cp-net in the recipes) serves GET /healthz returning `{"state":"valid|expiring|login_required|cp_unreachable|exchange_denied","exp":...}` without the token. Tokens, assertions, nonces, Proxy-Authorization values, key material and IdP or CP response bodies never appear in logs, errors or argv. Worker decision events carry user_sub and identity_status (W-P1-VRFY-03) plus the act and sid fields from W-P2-WBND-02, and the CP traffic API `/dashboard/api/traffic?user=` (W-P1-VRFY-04) is the attribution check.

Back-compat. Everything is new and opt-in. The existing recipes (ethos, hermes, openclaw, zeroclaw), `run`, `control-plane`, the P1 identity commands, cache format and exit codes 2 and 3 are unchanged; exit code 4 is new. docs/identity-contract.md gets a P2 addendum describing `forward` and `exec` as the replacement for the P1 token-in-HTTPS_PROXY limitation, with no change to any v1 header or claim.

Isolation proof. scripts/recipe-isolation.sh <claude-code|codex>, run only through `scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes` (no Docker in the default run), proves from inside the agent container: direct egress fails; dex:5556 and control-plane:7070 are unreachable and the identity volume is not mounted; a plain-HTTP request to the forwarder gets 405; a child-supplied Proxy-Authorization is replaced; the agent's env and $HOME hold no JWT, agent key or non-placeholder vendor key; a request through the forwarder is recorded with the seeded user's user_sub and act=<agent id>; a non-allowed host is denied; and after the agent is disabled with the offline CLI a new CONNECT is refused. A probe container on the worker network proves a CONNECT with no token gets 407. All logs contain zero JWT-shaped strings.
done_when: From a clean clone, following only docs/recipes/claude-code.md and docs/recipes/codex.md, each compose recipe (merged with docker-compose.control-plane.yml and docker-compose.identity.yml) starts the CP with signed bundles, the key manager and the token service, Dex and LDAP, a worker started with `--agent-id` and require mode, the `warden-identity` sidecar, a bootstrap that enrolls and registers the agent idempotently, and the agent container on an internal-only network. A headless run (`claude -p` or `codex exec`) reaches its vendor API only through the sidecar and the worker, and the worker decision and the CP traffic API show the logged-in user's user_sub and act=claude-code or act=codex; with only the placeholder key the upstream 401 is the expected result, and with the real key set on the worker only the prompt completes (manual step). The agent container holds only placeholder keys and no Warden token, Dex token or agent key, and `scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes` passes for both recipes, including direct-egress, CP/Dex-unreachable, no-token 407, forwarder-misuse, agent-disabled and no-token-in-logs checks.

tickets.title: Extend internal/identityclient with agent keys and token exchange
tickets.body: Extend internal/identityclient (W-P1-IDC-02) with Ed25519 agent keys, private_key_jwt assertions and the RFC 8693 exchange against the CP `/oauth2/token`, plus a Warden token source that refreshes at 2/3 of the token lifetime and never prompts. Add `warden identity enroll` and an `--agent-id` mode for `token` and `status`. This is the client half of the P2 identity flow; it changes no worker or CP code and does nothing unless the new flags are used.
requirements: `warden identity enroll --agent-id <id> [--key-file PATH] [--force]` validates the id with agentid.ValidID (p2-agent-registry), writes a PKCS#8 PEM Ed25519 key to a 0600 file in a 0700 directory (default `<os.UserConfigDir()>/warden/agents/<id>.key`) by temp file, fsync and rename, refuses an existing file without --force, and prints only the public JWK (kty OKP, crv Ed25519, alg EdDSA, kid = RFC 7638 thumbprint from internal/keys, no `d`). A key file readable by group or others is refused with an error naming the path.

Assertion: header alg EdDSA with kid; claims iss=sub=agent id, aud=exactly the configured token endpoint, iat=now, exp=iat+60s, jti=128-bit crypto/rand base64url. A new assertion is built for every exchange, so it meets W-P2-TOKX-01 (exp-iat<=5m, single-use jti).

Exchange: POST form-encoded to `--token-endpoint` / WARDEN_IDENTITY_TOKEN_ENDPOINT (required, no implied default) with grant_type token-exchange, subject_token_type id_token, client_assertion_type jwt-bearer, audience=warden-worker and optional `--scope`. CP TLS is trusted through `--cp-ca` / WARDEN_IDENTITY_CP_CA. `--agent-id` / WARDEN_IDENTITY_AGENT_ID and `--agent-key-file` / WARDEN_IDENTITY_AGENT_KEY_FILE select the agent.

Subject token: from the P1 Client.Token() (shared cache, lock file, `--client-id` default `warden-cli`), or from `--subject-token-file PATH` (0600 required, re-read before each exchange) for harness platforms and CI.

New WardenTokenSource: holds the Warden token in memory only, never on disk; re-exchanges at 2/3 of expires_in from local receipt time with up to 10% jitter; single-flights concurrent callers; retries network errors with jittered backoff from 1s to 60s while the current token is valid; honours Retry-After on 429; exposes OnRotate(func()) for the forwarder.

Errors: ErrLoginRequired from the subject source never prompts and the current Warden token is served until its exp. invalid_client, unauthorized_client and invalid_grant map to new ErrExchangeDenied{Code} (exit 4); CP unreachable with no valid token is exit 3; login required stays exit 2. Only the RFC 6749 error code is surfaced, never a response body.

`warden identity token --agent-id <id>` prints a valid Warden token on stdout for harnesses that do not use the forwarder; `warden identity status --agent-id <id>` prints sub, act.sub, cnf.jkt, scope and exp, never the token. `--verbose` logs only outcome, error code, exp, agent id and an 8-hex sha256 fingerprint.
Uses only the Go standard library and internal/keys for JOSE work; no new third-party dependency. P1 commands, the cache format and exit codes 2 and 3 are unchanged.
plan: New internal/identityclient/agentkey.go: GenerateAgentKey, SaveAgentKey and LoadAgentKey (PKCS#8 PEM, reusing the W-P1-IDC-02 permission check and atomic write helper) and PublicJWK built with the internal/keys JWK marshal and thumbprint (W-P2-KEYS-01).
New internal/identityclient/assertion.go: SignClientAssertion(key, kid, agentID, tokenURL, now) returning a compact EdDSA JWT with a random jti.

New internal/identityclient/exchange.go: Client.Exchange(ctx, subject, scope) with a dedicated http.Client (Proxy nil, `--cp-ca` root pool, 10s timeout, 64 KiB response cap), RFC 6749 error parsing into ErrExchangeDenied and ErrRateLimited{RetryAfter}.

New internal/identityclient/wardensource.go: WardenTokenSource wrapping either Client.Token() or a subject-token file, with the 2/3 schedule, jitter, singleflight, backoff and OnRotate hooks; clock injected for tests.

New cmd/proxy/identity_enroll.go registered on the W-P1-IDC-02 `identity` subtree; extend the existing token and status commands with `--agent-id`, `--agent-key-file`, `--token-endpoint`, `--cp-ca`, `--subject-token-file` and `--scope`, plus the env vars, and map ErrExchangeDenied to exit 4.

Tests in internal/identityclient against httptest fakes for the issuer and the CP: TestEnrollAgentKey, TestClientAssertion, TestExchangeRefreshAtTwoThirds, TestExchangeLoginRequiredNoPrompt, TestExchangeErrors; in cmd/proxy: TestIdentityExitCodes and TestIdentityEnrollAndTokenNoLeak.
acceptance: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestEnrollAgentKey` passes: the key file is 0600 in a 0700 directory, a second enroll without --force fails, a key chmodded to 0644 is refused with an error naming the path, and the printed JWK has kty OKP, crv Ed25519, kid equal to its RFC 7638 thumbprint and no `d` member.

`go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestClientAssertion` verifies the assertion with the public JWK: alg EdDSA, iss=sub=agent id, aud equal to the token endpoint byte for byte, exp-iat=60s, and 1000 builds give 1000 distinct jti values.

With a fake CP returning expires_in=900 and a fake clock, `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExchangeRefreshAtTwoThirds -race` shows one exchange at start, the next no earlier than 540s and no later than 600s, and two concurrent callers sharing one request.

When the fake issuer's refresh returns invalid_grant, `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExchangeLoginRequiredNoPrompt` shows ErrLoginRequired with nothing written to the prompt writer, and the still-valid Warden token is served until its exp.

Given the fake CP returns 401 invalid_client, 400 invalid_grant and 429 with Retry-After: 3, `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExchangeErrors` maps them to ErrExchangeDenied{invalid_client}, ErrExchangeDenied{invalid_grant} and a retry no earlier than 3s, and `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExitCodes` sees exit 4 for a denial.

`go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityEnrollAndTokenNoLeak` runs enroll, `token --agent-id` and `status --agent-id` with `--verbose`; stderr and slog output contain no substring of the subject token, assertion, Warden token or key seed, and the token appears only on stdout of `token`.
`scripts/check.sh` passes, including the coverage gate and govulncheck.

tickets.title: Add the token-injecting forwarder and `warden identity forward`
tickets.body: Extend the P1 CONNECT-only loopback forwarder from W-P1-IDC-04 (internal/identityclient/forwarder.go), which injects the current token as `Proxy-Authorization: Basic session:<token>` on the CONNECT to the worker, with rotation drain, a tunnel cap, client credentials, health and reason-coded 503s, and add the long-lived `warden identity forward` command that runs it as a sidecar container. Child CLIs read HTTPS_PROXY once at start, so the forwarder lets tokens rotate without restarting the agent and keeps every token out of the agent container. It adds no egress route: it only ever connects to the one configured worker.
requirements: `warden identity forward --listen <addr> --worker host:port [--agent-id ID] [--max-tunnels N] [--health-listen addr] [--client-credential-env NAME]` in the W-P1-IDC-02 `identity` subtree. `--listen` and `--worker` are required; a non-loopback `--listen` logs one startup warning. With `--agent-id` the injected token comes from WardenTokenSource (W-P2-RCP-01); without it the P1 Dex ID token from Client.Token() is injected.

The forwarder accepts only CONNECT and answers any other method with 405 without forwarding. It reads the CONNECT header block with a 32 KiB and 100-line cap and a 10s read deadline (431 on overflow), drops any client Proxy-Authorization, and sends `CONNECT host:port` to the worker with `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)`.

It dials only the configured `--worker` address (10s dial timeout) and never resolves or dials the CONNECT target. It relays the worker's status line and headers verbatim, including 403 and 407 with Proxy-Authenticate, then splices bytes both ways with a pooled 32 KiB buffer per direction.

With no valid token it answers 503 with `X-Warden-Forwarder-Reason: login_required|cp_unreachable|exchange_denied` and makes no dial to the worker. Above `--max-tunnels` (default 512) it answers 503. On a 407 from the worker it forces one token refresh and retries the CONNECT once before relaying the 407.

Rotation: the current token is held in an atomic pointer and each tunnel snapshots the token and exp at CONNECT. After a rotation old tunnels drain: each is closed after 2s with no bytes in either direction, and at the latest at its token's exp. New CONNECTs always carry the newest token.

`--client-credential-env NAME` (optional) requires clients to send that env var's value as the Proxy-Authorization password and answers 407 otherwise; the value is never forwarded to the worker. `--health-listen` (off by default) serves GET /healthz with the state enum valid|expiring|login_required|cp_unreachable|exchange_denied and exp, never the token.

Logs are structured stderr events only: tunnel_open, tunnel_close (target host:port, worker status, bytes, duration, 8-hex token fingerprint), token_rotated, exchange and login_required (logged once per transition). No token, credential or Proxy-Authorization value is ever logged.
New command only; `run`, `control-plane`, the P1 identity commands and the worker are unchanged. CONNECT setup overhead on loopback stays under 2ms per tunnel, excluding the worker.
plan: Extend internal/identityclient/forwarder.go from W-P1-IDC-04: add MaxTunnels, Clock, the reason-coded 503s and the 407 retry to Forwarder, and replace the copy loop with the pooled splice; keep the P1 header reader, single worker dial and verbatim status relay.

New internal/identityclient/tunnels.go: a tunnel registry recording token fingerprint, exp and last-activity per tunnel; on OnRotate it marks old tunnels draining and a ticker closes idle-for-2s or expired tunnels.
New internal/identityclient/health.go: the optional /healthz handler reading the WardenTokenSource state.
New cmd/proxy/identity_forward.go: builds the token source from W-P2-RCP-01 flags, listens, runs the forwarder until SIGTERM or SIGINT, then closes the listener and drains tunnels for up to 5s.

Tests in internal/identityclient with an httptest CONNECT listener as the fake worker: TestForwarderInjectsAndStrips, TestForwarderOnlyDialsWorker, TestForwarderRotationDrain (fake clock), TestForwarderNoTokenFailsClosed, TestForwarderRetryOn407, TestForwarderClientCredential, and BenchmarkForwarderConnect.
acceptance: `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderInjectsAndStrips` shows the fake worker receives `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` even when the client sent its own, a GET gets 405, and an oversized CONNECT header block gets 431.
`go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderOnlyDialsWorker` uses a recording dialer and shows CONNECTs to five different targets produce dials to the worker address only.

`go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderRotationDrain -race` with a fake clock shows a tunnel opened before a rotation keeps streaming while active, is closed 2s after it goes idle and no later than its token's exp, and a CONNECT made after the rotation carries the new token.

`go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderNoTokenFailsClosed` shows that with the token source returning ErrLoginRequired and no valid token, a CONNECT gets 503 with reason login_required and the fake worker records zero connections; a worker 407 is relayed unchanged after exactly one retry.
`go test ./internal/identityclient -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkForwarderConnect` reports CONNECT setup overhead under 2ms/op against a loopback fake worker.
`scripts/check.sh` passes, including the coverage gate.

tickets.title: Add the Claude Code compose recipe and docs
tickets.body: Add a Claude Code recipe that runs the agent on an internal-only network, the `warden-identity` sidecar holding the agent key and identity cache, and a require-mode worker bound to agent id `claude-code`. The agent holds only a placeholder Anthropic key that the worker swaps, so no real credential or token reaches it. This is the reference recipe that W-P2-RCP-04 copies.
requirements: New deploy/compose/docker-compose.claude-code.yml, used as `-f docker-compose.control-plane.yml -f docker-compose.identity.yml -f docker-compose.claude-code.yml`. Services: the CP with `--state-dir`, `--policy-store=versioned` and `--bundles=require` (W-P2-SBND-02) and a CP config with `keys.enabled: true` (W-P2-KEYS-02) and an enabled `tokenService:` block (W-P2-TOKX-03; there is no CLI flag), using the worker auth that docker-compose.control-plane.yml sets up (no WARDEN_CP_TOKEN); a worker started with `warden run --agent-id claude-code` (W-P2-AREG-05) that pins the exported bundle JWKS through `controlPlane.bundleKeysFile`, on `claude-code-internal`, egress and cp-net; `warden-identity` running `warden identity forward --agent-id claude-code --listen 0.0.0.0:3128 --worker warden:8080` on `claude-code-internal` and cp-net with its own `identity-claude-code` volume; and `claude-code` on `claude-code-internal` only (`internal: true`) with `init: true`.

New deploy/compose/claude-code/Dockerfile: node base image pinned by tag and digest, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` at an exact version at least two weeks old, non-root user. Agent env: HTTPS_PROXY=http://warden-identity:3128, NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/warden/certs/proxy-ca.crt, NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=anthropic_secret_001. The implementer confirms each variable name against the pinned release and records it in the doc.

New configs/config.recipe-claude-code-worker.yaml maps placeholder anthropic_secret_001 to envVar ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the real key is passed only to the worker container (`${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}`). New configs/config.cp-served.claude-code.yaml is default-deny, allows only api.anthropic.com:443, and has exactly one `agents` entry with id `claude-code` and `identity: require`.

New one-shot `identity-bootstrap` service: runs `warden identity enroll --agent-id claude-code` on the sidecar volume only when no key exists, then `warden control-plane agent register --state-dir` (W-P2-AREG-06) with the public JWK and `--groups eng`, and exports the bundle JWKS with `warden control-plane keys export --purpose bundle` (W-P2-KEYS-05) into a volume the worker mounts read-only; a second `up` makes no new rows. The sidecar and worker wait on it with `condition: service_completed_successfully`.

Warden services build from the repo Dockerfile (`build: {context: ../.., dockerfile: Dockerfile}`), because `ethosagent/warden:0.3.0` lacks the new subcommands. Third-party images are pinned by tag and digest. The agent never mounts the identity volume, the agent key or the CA key.

New docs/recipes/claude-code.md: prerequisites, cert generation with scripts/gen-certs.sh, bootstrap, interactive login (`docker compose run --rm warden-identity identity login`), the dev path with scripts/dex-token.sh into `--subject-token-file`, running `claude` and `claude -p`, reading attribution (worker log user_sub and act, CP traffic API `?user=`), degraded modes, troubleshooting (x509, 407 reasons, 503 reasons), the threat model, and a statement that Claude.ai subscription sign-in is unsupported. Add a row to docs/recipes/README.md.
plan: Write configs/config.cp-served.claude-code.yaml and configs/config.recipe-claude-code-worker.yaml from the existing config.cp-served.yaml and config.recipe-worker.yaml.
Write deploy/compose/claude-code/Dockerfile and deploy/compose/docker-compose.claude-code.yml with the networks, volumes, bootstrap ordering and build contexts above.
Add a short deploy/compose/claude-code/bootstrap.sh run by the `identity-bootstrap` service that enrolls when the key is missing and registers when the agent is missing.
Write docs/recipes/claude-code.md and add the docs/recipes/README.md row.
Add test/deploy/recipe_claude_code_test.go (TestClaudeCodeRecipe) parsing `docker compose config --format json` output from a fixture, and a `docker compose ... config -q` step in scripts/check.sh.

tickets.title: Add the isolation proof script for the recipes
tickets.body: Add scripts/recipe-isolation.sh, which proves for each recipe that the agent has no route out except the forwarder and the worker, holds no identity material or real vendor key, and is attributed to the logged-in user. It runs only on request through `scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes`, follows the scripts/smoke-identity.sh pattern from W-P1-IDC-03, and needs no real vendor key.
requirements: `scripts/recipe-isolation.sh <claude-code|codex>` brings the merged stack up from a clean state, puts the seeded user's token from `scripts/dex-token.sh --raw alice` into the sidecar's `--subject-token-file` without passing it through argv or an echoed variable, and runs `docker compose down -v` in a trap.

Checks from inside the agent container: direct-egress-blocked (`curl --noproxy '*' https://example.com` fails); idp-and-cp-unreachable (no TCP to dex:5556 or control-plane:7070, and the identity volume path is absent); forwarder-405 (a plain-HTTP request to warden-identity:3128 gets 405); no-secrets-in-agent (env, /proc/*/environ and $HOME contain no JWT-shaped string, no PEM private key and no vendor key other than the placeholder).

Checks of attribution and policy: attributed-allow (a request to the allowed API host through the forwarder gets an upstream answer, 401 with the placeholder is fine, and the worker decision has decision allow, user_sub of alice and act equal to the agent id); policy-deny (a CONNECT to a non-allowed host is denied); cp-attribution (`GET /dashboard/api/traffic?user=<alice email>` returns the event with identity_status valid).

Checks from a probe container on the worker network: no-token-407 (`curl -x http://warden:8080` with no credentials gets 407 with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="warden"`) and header-replaced (a client Proxy-Authorization sent through the forwarder does not reach the worker, shown by the attributed sub).
agent-disabled: after `warden control-plane agent disable` with the offline CLI (W-P2-AREG-06), a new CONNECT through the forwarder is refused within 10s.
no-token-in-logs: `grep -cE 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}'` over the script output and `docker compose logs` for the worker, warden-identity and the CP prints 0.

Each check prints PASS or FAIL with its name; the script exits non-zero at the first failure after printing the worker's last 50 log lines with JWT-shaped strings redacted. It uses `set -euo pipefail`, no `set -x`, and finishes within 5 minutes per recipe on a warm image cache.
`scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes` runs both recipes; the default `scripts/check.sh` does not start Docker. docs/testing-guide.md documents the flag.
plan: New scripts/recipe-isolation.sh with a check() helper, the trap, the token hand-off and one function per check.
Add `--smoke-recipes` to the argument loop in scripts/check.sh next to `--integration` and `--smoke-identity`.
Add a temporary negative-test override deploy/compose/test/recipe-egress-leak.yml that also attaches the agent to egress, used only by the self-test.
Document the flag and the checks in docs/testing-guide.md and link it from both recipe docs.

With the deploy/compose/test/recipe-egress-leak.yml override added, the script exits non-zero at direct-egress-blocked.

tickets.title: Extend `warden identity exec` with agent tokens and `--run-as`
tickets.body: W-P1-IDC-04 ships `warden identity exec` in P1 with the user's Dex ID token. Add `--agent-id`, so exec injects an exchanged Warden token from W-P2-RCP-01 through the W-P2-RCP-02 forwarder (rotation drain, reason-coded 503s), and `--run-as`, so a child under another uid cannot read the agent key or identity cache. Document that a same-uid child can still read them without `--run-as`, and add the P2 addendum to docs/identity-contract.md.
requirements: `warden identity exec` (W-P1-IDC-04) gains `--agent-id ID` and `--run-as uid:gid`; all P1 flags, the per-run loopback credential, the child env rules, signal handling and exit codes are unchanged.

With `--agent-id` the forwarder token comes from WardenTokenSource (W-P2-RCP-01) and uses the W-P2-RCP-02 rotation drain and 503 reasons; without it exec behaves exactly as in P1. No Warden token, Dex token or key path enters the child's env, argv or files.

`--run-as uid:gid` (Linux only; an error elsewhere) starts the child under another uid through SysProcAttr.Credential so it cannot read the key file or cache. docs/recipes/README.md states that without it `exec` protects against leaks through env, argv and logs and against stale tokens, but not against a hostile same-uid child.
On ErrExchangeDenied at start exec exits 4 without starting the child; ErrLoginRequired keeps the P1 behaviour (login on a terminal, otherwise exit 2).
docs/identity-contract.md gets a P2 addendum describing `forward` and `exec --agent-id` for require-mode agents, with no change to any v1 header or claim.
plan: cmd/proxy/identity_exec.go (from W-P1-IDC-04): add the `--agent-id` and `--run-as` flags and select WardenTokenSource when an agent id is set.
SysProcAttr.Credential behind a linux build tag, with a clear error on other platforms.
Tests in cmd/proxy using the helper-process pattern: TestIdentityExecAgentToken, TestIdentityExecExchangeDenied, and a linux-only TestIdentityExecRunAs that skips when not root.
Write the docs/identity-contract.md addendum and the exec section in docs/recipes/README.md.
acceptance: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExecAgentToken` shows that with `--agent-id` the fake worker receives the exchanged Warden token, and the child's env and argv contain no substring of the Warden or Dex token.
With the token endpoint returning invalid_client, `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExecExchangeDenied` shows exit 4 and that the child never started.

On Linux as root, `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExecRunAs` shows the child runs as the given uid and cannot open the agent key file; on other platforms `--run-as` exits non-zero before starting the child.
The P1 TestIdentityExec cases from W-P1-IDC-04 pass unchanged, and `scripts/check.sh` passes.

name: Identity client + recipes
label: identity-client

summary: Ship a reference Dex deployment that Warden and agent harnesses trust: one IdP in front of the company directory that issues short-lived ID tokens with groups. Operators get a pinned, documented compose recipe and config that they can point at LDAP, GitHub, Google or upstream OIDC connectors. Warden treats Dex only as a generic OIDC issuer. None of this exists in the repo yet: there is no deploy/compose/dex/, no identity compose file, no OIDC dependency in go.mod and no secret-literal check in scripts/check.sh.
design: Dex is only a standard OIDC issuer for Warden. Nothing in internal/ or cmd/ calls Dex-specific APIs; Dex-specific strings live only in deploy/compose/dex/, deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml, scripts/dex-token.sh and docs/identity-dex.md. Any standards-compliant OIDC issuer can replace it.

Clients (staticClients; secrets via `secretEnv`, never committed): `warden-console` is confidential and used only for CP console login, redirect `<cp-browser-url>/auth/callback`. `warden` is the data-plane audience: confidential, no redirect URIs, never used to log anyone in, with `trustedPeers: [agent-harness, warden-cli]` so those clients can mint tokens whose aud contains `warden`. `agent-harness` is confidential, for server-side harness platforms. `warden-cli` is public (no secret) and device-code only, for `warden identity login` on user machines; it lists the Dex device callback (`<issuer>/device/callback`) in redirectURIs. Splitting console and data-plane clients means a console login token never carries aud `warden`.

Grants: `oauth2.grantTypes` is set explicitly to authorization_code, refresh_token and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`; `oauth2.responseTypes: [code]`, `oauth2.skipApprovalScreen: true` (all clients are first-party). The password grant (`password` in grantTypes plus `oauth2.passwordConnector: ldap`) appears only in the dev recipe file `deploy/compose/dex/config.dev.yaml`, which the smoke and e2e tests use. The prod example `deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml` has no password grant, because it lets a client collect directory passwords and bypasses upstream MFA.

Scopes: clients must request `openid email profile groups offline_access`, plus `audience:server:client_id:warden` for agent-harness and warden-cli. Without `groups` the token has no groups claim and role and group policy silently see none; without `offline_access` there is no refresh token. With cross-client trust Dex sets aud to the requested peer and azp to the requesting client, so checks are `aud contains warden` and `azp in {agent-harness, warden-cli}`.

Expiry: `idTokens: 1h`, `signingKeys: 6h`, `deviceRequests: 5m`. Dex keeps previous public keys published until their tokens expire, and the worker verifier (p1-verify-token) refetches JWKS on an unknown kid at most once per 30s, so rotation needs no Warden restart. Refresh tokens: `validIfNotUsedFor: 168h`, `absoluteLifetime: 720h`, rotation on, `reuseInterval: 3s`; clients must serialize refresh (the CLI holds a lock file). Absolute expiry and loss of Dex storage both return `invalid_grant`; later offboarding logic must not treat that alone as a disabled user (see open cross-feature note on p3-offboarding).

Identity keys: the Dex `sub` is opaque and encodes the connector id together with the upstream user id. Connector `id` values (recipe: `ldap`) are permanent once users exist; renaming one or switching connectors changes every sub and requires re-keying user-scoped state (block list, per-user credentials in the CP-only consent.store keyed by secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) from p3-consent-signin, grants, attribution). The docs show the `federated:id` scope for diagnostics. Group names `warden-admins`, `warden-editors`, `warden-viewers`, `eng` are recipe defaults that `console.roles` and group policy map, not a contract.

Dev directory: an OpenLDAP container seeded from `deploy/compose/dex/seed.ldif` with `{SSHA}` password hashes only (dev-only, path-allowlisted in the secret check). The LDAP connector uses userSearch and groupSearch so `groups` comes from the directory, and its bindPW comes from env. Dex static passwords are not used because they cannot carry groups. Commented examples cover GitHub (orgs/teams, `teamNameField`), Google and upstream OIDC, with a table showing groups source, required scope and whether refresh re-checks the upstream user.

Issuer and transport: the dev recipe issuer is `http://dex:5556/dex`, byte-identical for browsers (documented `127.0.0.1 dex` hosts entry, port 5556 published) and containers on cp-net. Because it is plain http on a non-loopback host, local runs set `console.oidc.allowInsecureIssuer: true` (exists in W-P1-SSO-02) and the matching worker setting `identity.allowInsecureIssuer` (W-P1-VRFY-01); both are rejected unless set explicitly and log a startup warning. Production requires an https issuer with no insecure flags.

Networks: Dex joins `cp-net` (CP and workers fetch discovery and JWKS) and a new `idp-net` (`internal: true`) shared with LDAP. LDAP has no host port and joins only idp-net. Dex is never attached to an agent `internal: true` network. Tokens are obtained by the harness or host outside the agent sandbox; if an agent must refresh in-sandbox it goes through its worker with an explicit allow rule for the Dex host, a documented trade-off that keeps default-deny intact. Upstream connector examples need an extra egress network, shown commented. The identity file declares every network it uses, so it works standalone and merged with `-f` into docker-compose.control-plane.yml or docker-compose.yml.

Image pinned by exact tag and digest (`ghcr.io/dexidp/dex:v2.x.y@sha256:...`), taken from the latest stable release at least 2 weeks old at implementation time; OpenLDAP pinned the same way; both run as the image's non-root user where the image supports it.

Storage and ops: sqlite3 on the named volume `dex-data` in dev (single replica only). Production uses Postgres or Kubernetes CRD storage with at least 2 replicas and backups; losing storage invalidates every session and refresh token. `telemetry.http: 0.0.0.0:5558` serves health and Prometheus metrics on cp-net only; `logger: {level: info, format: json}`, never debug in prod. A compose healthcheck gates dependents if the pinned image ships a probe tool, otherwise clients rely on retry.

Degraded modes (documented): Dex down means console login fails (use p1-breakglass) while issued tokens stay valid until exp; a worker that cannot fetch JWKS records `identity_status=unverified` (reason jwks_unavailable) and still allows the request in P1 attribute mode; LDAP down means new logins and refreshes fail; clock skew over 60s produces `expired`, so NTP is required. Alert on spikes in `warden_identity_verify_total{result=~"invalid|unverified"}` (the Prometheus name of the worker instrument `warden.identity.verify.total`) and on Dex health.

Secret hygiene: new `scripts/check-secrets.sh`, called from `scripts/check.sh`, fails if any file under deploy/compose/dex/ or the identity compose file has a `secret:`, `bindPW:` or `clientSecret:` value that is not an env reference, and allowlists only `seed.ldif` (hashes). Compose uses `${VAR:?}` so missing secrets fail fast. No token, secret or password appears in logs, test output or docs.
done_when: With `docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml up -d` (Dex and OpenLDAP, both pinned by tag and digest, dev config): (1) `/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration` returns the same issuer string from the host (hosts entry) and from a container on cp-net; (2) `scripts/dex-token.sh` for a seeded warden-admins user via `agent-harness` returns an ID token with aud containing `warden`, azp=`agent-harness`, groups containing `warden-admins` and exp-iat=3600; (3) the public `warden-cli` client gets a device_code and user_code; (4) the prod config has no password grant (asserted by `go test ./test/deploy`); (5) after `docker compose restart dex` existing tokens still verify against JWKS and the refresh token still works; (6) the identity file validates merged with docker-compose.control-plane.yml; (7) `scripts/check.sh` passes with its secret-literal stage; (8) docs/identity-dex.md commands run as written and cover the prod checklist and failure modes.

tickets.body: Add the Dex configuration files that every later identity ticket builds on: a prod-shaped `deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml` and a dev recipe `deploy/compose/dex/config.dev.yaml` that differs only by enabling the password grant. They define the four static clients (`warden-console`, `warden`, `agent-harness`, `warden-cli`), explicit grant types, expiry, the LDAP connector with a permanent id, telemetry and logging. A static Go test and a secret-literal check make the ticket testable without running Dex; runtime checks arrive with the compose recipe in W-P1-DEX-02. No Go package or existing compose file changes.

tickets.title: Add identity compose recipe with pinned Dex and seeded LDAP
tickets.body: Add `deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml`, which runs Dex with the dev config and a seeded OpenLDAP, both pinned by tag and digest. It declares its own networks so it works standalone and merged with the control-plane and worker compose files, and it never attaches Dex or LDAP to an agent network. Add `scripts/dex-token.sh` so this ticket, W-P1-IDC-03 and W-P1-VRFY-05 share one way to fetch and check a token. This is deploy and script work only; no worker or CP code changes.
requirements: Service `dex`: image `ghcr.io/dexidp/dex:<tag>@sha256:<digest>`, mounts `dex/config.dev.yaml` read-only, named volume `dex-data:/var/dex`, publishes 5556, joins cp-net and idp-net; telemetry port 5558 is not published to the host.
Service `ldap`: OpenLDAP pinned by tag and digest, seeded from new `deploy/compose/dex/seed.ldif`, joins only idp-net, no host port, admin password from `${LDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD:?}`.

seed.ldif: groups warden-admins, warden-editors, warden-viewers, eng (groupOfNames); users alice (warden-admins, eng), bob (warden-editors), carol (warden-viewers), dave (eng only, for the 403 role test). Passwords stored only as `{SSHA}` hashes, marked dev-only.

Secrets via `${WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET:?}`, `${WARDEN_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET:?}`, `${HARNESS_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET:?}`, `${LDAP_BIND_PW:?}`; new committed `deploy/compose/dex/.env.example` with placeholder values and the dev test passwords (.env is already gitignored).
Networks declared in the file: `cp-net` (bridge, same name as docker-compose.control-plane.yml so they merge) and `idp-net` (`internal: true`). No agent network includes Dex.
Healthchecks: LDAP via ldapsearch; Dex via its telemetry health endpoint if the pinned image has a probe tool, else none and clients retry. Dex `depends_on` LDAP with `condition: service_healthy`.

New `scripts/dex-token.sh <user>`: reads the password from `DEX_TEST_PASSWORD`, runs the password grant with client agent-harness and scope `openid email profile groups offline_access audience:server:client_id:warden`, decodes the payload, asserts aud contains warden, azp=agent-harness and exp-iat=3600, prints only decoded claims, and prints the raw token only with `--raw`. Never echoes the password or client secret.
Back-compat: opt-in file; docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.control-plane.yml are unchanged.
plan: Write new `deploy/compose/dex/seed.ldif` and generate `{SSHA}` hashes with slappasswd; record the dev plaintexts only in `.env.example`.
Write new `deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml` with services dex and ldap, volume dex-data, networks cp-net and idp-net, healthchecks and env-sourced secrets.
Pin both images: resolve the digest for the chosen tags and write `image: <repo>:<tag>@sha256:<digest>`.
