tickets.title: Document Dex as Warden's IdP with connector, failure-mode and prod guidance
tickets.body: Write `docs/identity-dex.md`, the operator guide for running Dex as Warden's IdP. It explains the token flow, client split, scopes, group naming, connectors, issuer and network rules, key rotation, degraded modes and the production checklist, and cites the exact CP and worker config keys. It depends on W-P1-SSO-02 and W-P1-VRFY-01 so the keys it cites exist when it merges. This ticket-level dependency on later P1 features is intentional and accepted: p1-sso-roles and p1-verify-token depend on p1-dex, so the feature-level depends_on_items stays empty to avoid a cycle, and this docs ticket simply merges after those tickets. It states plainly that Warden only needs a standards OIDC issuer.
requirements: Token flow: harness or CLI -> Dex (device code on warden-cli, or authorization code on agent-harness) -> ID token with aud containing `warden` and azp of the requesting client -> `Proxy-Authorization: Basic session:<token>` or `X-Warden-Identity: Bearer` to the worker, verified by internal/identity. Tokens are obtained outside the agent sandbox; in-sandbox refresh only through the worker with an explicit allow rule.

Client and scope section: the four clients, why console and data-plane clients are separate, trustedPeers direction, secretEnv names, redirect URIs as the browser sees them, and the required scope set including `groups` and `offline_access`.

Group and key section: recipe groups mapped through `console.roles.{admin,editor,viewer}` (W-P1-SSO-02) and the worker `identity:` keys `defaultMode`, `issuer`, `audience`, `allowedAZP`, `allowInsecureIssuer` and the per-agent `agents[].identity` field (W-P1-VRFY-01) by exact name; connector claim shapes differ (LDAP cn vs GitHub `org:team`); connector `id` is permanent because it is encoded into sub, with `federated:id` for diagnostics.

Connector table: LDAP (ldaps or StartTLS with rootCA in prod), GitHub (orgs, teams, `teamNameField`), Google (groups need a service account), upstream OIDC; columns for groups source, required scope and whether refresh re-checks the upstream user.

Issuer, transport and network rules: byte-identical issuer, `127.0.0.1 dex` hosts entry, dev-only `console.oidc.allowInsecureIssuer` and the worker equivalent, https required in prod; Dex on cp-net and idp-net, never on agent networks; upstream connectors need an egress network.

Failure modes and rotation: Dex down, LDAP down, JWKS unavailable at worker start, clock skew over 60s, storage loss, refresh absolute expiry and reuse; signingKeys 6h with JWKS refetch on unknown kid at most once per 30s; metrics to alert on; p1-breakglass for console access.

Prod checklist: https issuer, Postgres or Kubernetes CRD storage with at least 2 replicas (sqlite3 is single replica), backups, password grant off, logger not debug, expiry values, secrets from a secret manager or Kubernetes Secret, groupSearch scoped so tokens stay well under the worker limits: 16 KiB per token (W-P1-VRFY-01) and 32 KiB and 100 lines for the whole CONNECT header block (W-P1-VRFY-02). Kubernetes guidance is prose only; no manifest is added to deploy/k8s in this phase.
No real secrets, tokens or passwords in the doc; examples show placeholders and decoded claims only.
plan: Write new `docs/identity-dex.md` with sections for token flow, clients and scopes, groups and keys, connectors, issuer and networks, rotation and failure modes, and prod checklist.
Copy the exact key names from `internal/config/console.go` (W-P1-SSO-02) and `config.IdentitySettings` (W-P1-VRFY-01) as merged on main.

Add an example CP config snippet with `console.oidc.clientID: warden-console`, `clientSecretEnv: WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET`, `redirectURL: https://localhost:7070/auth/callback` and `allowInsecureIssuer: true` marked dev-only, and a worker `identity:` snippet with `audience: warden` and `allowedAZP: [agent-harness, warden-cli]` so tokens minted for any other client are rejected.
Run every fenced shell command in the doc from the repo root against the W-P1-DEX-02 recipe, using `scripts/dex-token.sh`.
Link the doc from README.md, docs/control-plane.md, docs/setup-guide.md and deploy/compose/dex/README.md.
acceptance: Every fenced shell command in docs/identity-dex.md, run in order from the repo root against the recipe, exits 0 and produces the output shown.

`grep -nE 'console\.roles|console\.oidc|identity\.(defaultMode|issuer|audience|allowedAZP|allowInsecureIssuer)' docs/identity-dex.md` lists only keys that exist in internal/config on main, and `go test ./internal/config/...` passes.
The doc contains a prod checklist (https issuer, persistent HA storage, backups, password grant off, expiry values) and a failure-modes section, and warns that changing a connector id changes sub.
The doc names no product other than ones Warden integrates with, and contains no secret or raw token (`scripts/check-secrets.sh` passes).
`go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` and `scripts/check.sh` pass, and the doc is linked from docs/control-plane.md and docs/setup-guide.md.

name: Dex (one IdP)
label: dex-oidc

summary: Employees sign in to a consent portal on the CP with their IdP identity through a dedicated `warden-portal` OIDC client. The portal session is a separate type from the admin console and has no console privileges. When `consent.idpLink.enabled` is on, the login requests offline_access, and the CP stores the user's refresh token in the CP-only user credential store (`consent.store`), which no worker can read. P3 offboarding later uses that token to detect disabled users. Nothing in this feature exists in code yet. It builds on the P1 cpstate store, OIDC login flow, sessions, block list and ID-token verifier, and stays off unless a `consent:` block in the operator's --config enables it.
design: Scope: CP only. No worker or hot-path change. Routes are mounted only when the CP-local `consent:` block in the operator-owned --config has `enabled: true`. The block is `json:"-"` on config.Policy, never on policyWire or SettingsWire, and read by a new resolveConsent in cmd/proxy, modeled on resolveConsole (W-P1-SSO-02). The dashboard writers WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteIntegrations and WriteDetection keep it byte-identical. Enabling it requires console.auth=oidc and --state-dir, or the CP refuses to start: an open console could edit the policy, scope caps and secret mappings that the portal trusts.

Config (new): `consent.enabled` (default false); `consent.oidc {issuer, clientID (default warden-portal), clientSecretEnv, redirectURL (<cp-browser-url>/portal/callback), allowInsecureIssuer}`. Scopes are fixed: openid email profile groups, plus offline_access when idpLink is enabled. `consent.allowedGroups` is optional; empty means any user of the issuer. `consent.session {idle: 30m, absolute: 8h}` uses the same key names as console.session; the defaults are shorter than the console's 1h/12h because a portal session can approve third-party access for agents. `consent.idpLink {enabled: true, refreshLifetime: 720h}`, where 720h matches Dex absoluteLifetime from W-P1-DEX-01. Validation: 0 < idle <= absolute <= 24h; https issuer and redirectURL unless loopback or allowInsecureIssuer; the redirectURL path is exactly /portal/callback; an empty secret env fails startup naming the variable, never its value. Consent always requires console.auth=oidc and a real OIDC issuer: there is no --dev or demo path that runs consent or the IdP link without it, so dev and demo setups use the p1-dex stack (W-P1-DEX-02).

Issuer binding: consent.oidc.issuer must equal the identity.issuer that workers verify against (W-P1-VRFY-01). Otherwise a portal sub would never match a data-plane sub. The CP checks this at startup, and the CP settings writer rejects an identity.issuer change that breaks it (400 identity_issuer_mismatch). The identity key is (iss, sub); email is for display only.

Dex client: add static client `warden-portal` (confidential, secretEnv WARDEN_PORTAL_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, redirect https://localhost:7070/portal/callback, grant types authorization_code and refresh_token) to deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml and config.dev.yaml. It is kept out of `warden`'s trustedPeers, so the CP-held refresh token can never mint aud=warden data-plane tokens. Warden code makes no Dex-specific calls.

Shared web auth: P1 puts the OIDC flow and session code inside internal/controlplane, and internal/portal and internal/oauthbroker cannot import it, because controlplane mounts both. A refactor with no behaviour change moves it into a new package internal/webauth: a lazy provider with backoff, the oidc_pending store with a new `purpose` column (console|portal), a SessionStore parameterized by table, cookie name and CSRF label, the code exchange plus identity.NewIDTokenVerifier, and an httptest fake OIDC provider in internal/webauth/webauthtest.

Login flow: GET /portal/login and GET /portal/callback use auth code with S256 PKCE, state and nonce. The pending row has purpose=portal, a 10m TTL, a single-use atomic consume and the 10k cap, and is bound to the browser by the `__Host-warden_portal_login` cookie, separate from the console's `__Host-warden_login`. A console state fails on /portal/callback and the reverse. The ID token is verified with identity.NewIDTokenVerifier (Audience=consent clientID, AllowedAZP=[clientID], nonce, RS256/ES256, 60s skew). `next` accepts only same-origin paths under /portal/ or /connect/; anything else goes to /portal.

Admission: the callback creates no session and writes nothing when the principal's sub or email is on the P1 block list (login_error=blocked), when allowedGroups is set and no group matches (not_allowed), or when idpLink is enabled and the token response has no refresh_token (502, offline_access_not_granted).

Portal sessions: cpstate migration `portal_sessions/0001` adds portal_sessions(id_hash, iss, sub, email, groups_json, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at), built with webauth.SessionStore. The id is 32 random bytes and only its sha256 is stored. last_seen_at is written at most once a minute, expiry uses the CP clock, and sessions survive restarts. The cookie is `__Host-warden_portal` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when redirectURL is https. `warden_portal` is used only for http loopback or allowInsecureIssuer, with a startup warning.

Isolation: the console middleware reads only the console cookie and the `sessions` table. The portal middleware reads only the portal cookie and `portal_sessions`. portal.Principal is its own type in its own context key, so no console authz check can ever see it. The portal middleware ignores console cookies, WARDEN_CP_TOKEN, worker tokens and wak_ API keys, and rechecks the block list on each request from the in-memory BlockStore snapshot. Exported portal.RequireSession and portal.PrincipalFrom serve /portal/* and /connect/* (W-P3-BRKR-03).

CSRF: every non-GET request behind RequireSession needs `X-Warden-CSRF`, or a `csrf` form field on urlencoded posts. The value is HMAC-SHA256(raw portal session id, "warden-portal-csrf"), so a console token (label "warden-csrf") never validates on the portal. Origin, when present, must equal the redirectURL origin. GET /portal/api/me serves the token. POST /portal/logout deletes the session row and clears the cookie, but leaves the IdP link.

IdP link storage: the refresh token is written to the CP-only user credential store `consent.store` (W-P3-CSIG-06) at logical key `secrets.IdPLinkKey(userKey)` = `idp/<userKey>`, where userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub): the lowercase hex of the first 16 bytes of SHA-256("warden-user-v1\x00" + iss + "\x00" + sub), 32 characters. Every P3 feature builds per-user keys only through these W-P3-CSIG-06 helpers. With the default namePrefix the backend name is `warden-cp/idp/<userKey>`. No worker ever gets a credential for consent.store, and the CP refuses to start when it overlaps the secretStore whose credential the CP sends to workers. Migration `idp_links/0001` adds idp_links(iss, sub, user_key, email, secret_key, refresh_ref, generation, linked_at, refresh_issued_at, relink_due_at, last_refresh_at, last_refresh_status, offboarded_at). It has no value-bearing column; refresh_ref = secrets.Ref(token).String().

Write ordering and concurrency: writes are serialized per user_key with an in-process keyed mutex. Login does the secret Put first, then an upsert that increments generation. LinkStore.Rotate(ctx, iss, sub, expectedGeneration, token) takes the same mutex, returns ErrStaleGeneration without writing when the stored generation differs, and otherwise does the Put and then UPDATE ... WHERE generation=? (incrementing it), so the W-P3-OFFB-02 job never overwrites a newer login. relink_due_at = refresh_issued_at + idpLink.refreshLifetime lets offboarding tell Dex absolute expiry apart from a disabled user. A failed Put returns 503 secret_store_unavailable with no session and no row (fail-closed).

Store and guards (W-P3-CSIG-06): the CP-local `consent.store` block {backend aws|vault|echo, namePrefix (default `warden-cp/`), aws{region}, vault{addr, mount, namespace, tokenEnv}} is the one CP-only store for every per-user credential in P3: `idp/<userKey>` (this feature), `users/<userKey>/<provider>` and `revoking/<userKey>/<provider>` (p3-oauth-broker, p3-consent-portal) and `oauth-clients/<provider>` client secrets. Credentials come only from the CP environment or role, never from YAML or the wire; vault is accepted once W-P3-PUS-01 lands, and echo only with --dev. Today the CP sends its secretStore credential to workers over SettingsWire.Secrets, so the CP refuses to start when consent.store resolves to the same backend with an overlapping prefix. New optional interface secrets.Persistent { Persists() bool }, false for EchoStore and true for awsSecretStore (and later Vault KV v2); with idpLink enabled the store must be persistent. Reserved logical prefixes `idp/`, `users/`, `revoking/` and `oauth-clients/` (secrets.IsReservedKey): config validation rejects static SecretMapping placeholders that use them, storeFetcher.Fetch refuses them, and /central/secrets returns 403 reserved_key on PUT and DELETE and leaves them out of List, so no policy or console edit can make a worker swap in, read or overwrite a per-user credential.

Revocation: PortalSessionStore.DeleteBySub and DeleteByEmail are called from the W-P1-BLOCK-07 BlockStore.Add path, so blocking or offboarding ends portal sessions at once. GET and DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?kind=portal (admin only) extend W-P1-SSO-08. Expired sessions and pending rows are swept every minute.

Degraded modes: discovery is lazy, as in P1. With the IdP down, only /portal/login and /portal/callback return 503 idp_unavailable; existing portal sessions keep working, and CP start and /policy are unaffected. With consent.store down, new logins fail with 503 while existing sessions keep working. A minimal GET /portal stub (signed-in email, link status, relink_due_at, logout) is served until W-P3-PORT-01 replaces it.

Observability: log records portal_login{result,reason}, portal_logout, portal_session_revoked and idp_link_stored (secret Reference and generation only), plus W-P1-AAUD-02 Recorder entries for portal login, logout and `user.idp_linked`. In-memory counters: portal logins by result, active portal sessions, and IdP link writes by result. The code, verifier, nonce, ID token, refresh token, cookie and CSRF value are never logged.
done_when: Setup: a CP running with console.auth=oidc, `consent.enabled: true` in --config, an existing --state-dir and a persistent secret store, against the reference Dex stack that has the warden-portal client. A seeded LDAP user signs in through /portal/login and lands on /portal with a __Host-warden_portal session. consent.store holds `idp/<secrets.UserKey(iss,sub)>`, and idp_links holds only (iss, sub), a Reference, the generation and the dates. The same portal cookie gets 401 on every /dashboard/api/* route and on /central/secrets. A portal POST without a matching X-Warden-CSRF header, or with a foreign Origin, gets 403. A blocked user cannot sign in, and blocking a signed-in user ends their portal session. The CP refuses to start with an echo consent.store while idpLink is enabled, with a consent.store that overlaps the distributed secretStore, or with a placeholder under a reserved prefix, and a login without a refresh token creates no session. With Dex stopped, /portal/login returns 503 while existing portal sessions and worker /policy keep working. An ID token issued to warden-portal is rejected by the worker verifier, and no log line contains the code, verifier, nonce, ID token, refresh token or cookie value.

tickets.title: Add the CP-local consent config block and the warden-portal Dex client
tickets.body: Add the operator-owned `consent:` block, modeled on the P1 console block: read only from --config, `json:"-"`, never on the wire, and kept byte-identical by the dashboard writers. Add the `warden-portal` static client to the reference Dex configs (carried forward from p1-dex). The session keys match the console (`idle`, `absolute`) but have shorter defaults, because the portal can approve third-party access. The OIDC client and routes are built later, in W-P3-CSIG-02; with no block, or with `enabled: false`, nothing changes.
requirements: internal/config/consent.go (new): ConsentConfig{Enabled bool; OIDC ConsentOIDC; AllowedGroups []string; Session ConsentSession; IdPLink ConsentIdPLink}, ConsentOIDC{Issuer, ClientID, ClientSecretEnv, RedirectURL string; AllowInsecureIssuer bool}, ConsentSession{Idle, Absolute time.Duration}, ConsentIdPLink{Enabled bool; RefreshLifetime time.Duration}. Defaults: clientID warden-portal, idle 30m, absolute 8h, idpLink.enabled true, refreshLifetime 720h. The struct comment records why the session defaults are shorter than the console's. The struct leaves room for later `store` (W-P3-CSIG-06), `providers` and `connect` (W-P3-BRKR-01), `publicURL` (W-P3-JIT-01) and `offboarding` (W-P3-OFFB-02) keys.

Strict parsing: unknown keys are rejected. Validation when enabled: issuer, clientSecretEnv and redirectURL are required; issuer and redirectURL are https unless the host is loopback or allowInsecureIssuer is true (warning); the redirectURL is absolute, its path is exactly /portal/callback, and it differs from console.oidc.redirectURL; 0 < idle <= absolute <= 24h; refreshLifetime > 0.

Policy.Consent has `json:"-"`; rawConfig accepts `consent:` under KnownFields(true), so workers and the served copy still parse. New config.LoadConsent(path) reads only the consent node. cmd/proxy calls it on --config, never the served path; a different block in <state-dir>/config.yaml is ignored with a warning.

Startup checks in resolveConsent when enabled: console.auth must be oidc, with no --dev or demo bypass (dev setups use the W-P1-DEX-02 Dex stack), and idpLink cannot be skipped by a dev flag; --state-dir is required; os.Getenv(clientSecretEnv) must be non-empty (the error names the variable, never the value); consent.oidc.issuer must equal the identity.issuer in the loaded policy (W-P1-VRFY-01). The CP settings writer rejects a later identity.issuer change that breaks this with 400 identity_issuer_mismatch.

Dex: add `warden-portal` (confidential, secretEnv WARDEN_PORTAL_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, redirectURIs [https://localhost:7070/portal/callback]) to deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml and config.dev.yaml. It is not added to `warden`'s trustedPeers. Add `${WARDEN_PORTAL_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET:?}` to deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml and a placeholder to deploy/compose/dex/.env.example.

plan: Create internal/config/consent.go (new) with the types, defaults, validateConsent (same https/loopback helper as validateConsole) and LoadConsent(path), reusing the strict decoder that LoadConsole uses.

In internal/config/config.go add an unexported rawConsent and `Consent *rawConsent `yaml:"consent"`` to rawConfig, convert it into Policy.Consent next to Console, and call validateConsent from validate().

In cmd/proxy/controlplane.go add resolveConsent(opts, servedPath, pol) (new), mirroring resolveConsole: load from opts.configPath, warn on a differing served block, run the startup checks, and pass the result in a new controlplane.Config.Consent *config.ConsentConfig field (nil when disabled).

Extend TestDexReferenceConfig in test/deploy/dex_config_test.go (from W-P1-DEX-01): the client set includes warden-portal with its redirect and no `secret` field, and `warden`.trustedPeers does not contain warden-portal. Confirm that scripts/check-secrets.sh covers the new client.
Add a commented consent example to configs/config.control-plane.yaml matching the compose client (issuer http://dex:5556/dex, allowInsecureIssuer true).

acceptance: Table tests cover a valid block, missing issuer, missing clientSecretEnv, an http non-loopback issuer without allowInsecureIssuer, a redirectURL path other than /portal/callback, a redirectURL equal to the console one, and idle > absolute or absolute > 24h: `go test ./internal/config -run TestConsentConfig`

Given a Policy with every Consent field set, when policyWire and SettingsWire are marshalled, then neither JSON contains `consent`, `clientSecretEnv` or `warden-portal`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestConsentNotOnWire`

`go test ./test/deploy -run TestDexReferenceConfig` asserts the warden-portal client, its redirect and its absence from warden.trustedPeers. Adding `secret: abc` to it makes `scripts/check-secrets.sh` exit non-zero.

tickets.title: Implement portal login, callback and session store
tickets.body: Add the new internal/portal package with GET /portal/login, GET /portal/callback and the portal_sessions store, built on the shared internal/webauth code from W-P3-CSIG-05. Login uses the warden-portal client, a purpose=portal pending row and its own browser-binding cookie. Blocked users and users outside allowedGroups get no session. A minimal /portal page is served until W-P3-PORT-01 replaces it. Routes are mounted only when Config.Consent is set and Config.State is non-nil.
requirements: GET /portal/login stores state, nonce, the S256 PKCE verifier and `next` in oidc_pending with purpose=portal (10m TTL, single use, 10k cap), sets the `__Host-warden_portal_login` binding cookie (`warden_portal_login` on the insecure dev path), and redirects with scopes openid email profile groups, plus offline_access when idpLink is enabled. `next` accepts only a same-origin path starting with /portal/ or /connect/ (no scheme, no `//`, no backslash); anything else becomes /portal.

GET /portal/callback consumes the pending row atomically with purpose=portal; a console state, or a missing or mismatched binding cookie, fails as state_invalid. It exchanges the code with the verifier and verifies the ID token with identity.NewIDTokenVerifier (Audience=consent clientID, AllowedAZP=[clientID], nonce, RS256/ES256, 60s skew). The identity key is (iss, sub).
Admission: no session when BlockStore.IsBlocked(sub, email) is true (login_error=blocked), or when allowedGroups is set and no group matches (login_error=not_allowed). Groups are capped at 256.

Migration `portal_sessions/0001` via webauth.SessionStore: portal_sessions(id_hash PK, iss, sub, email, groups_json, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at) with indexes on sub and expires_at. PortalSessionStore exposes Create, Lookup, Touch, Delete, DeleteBySub, DeleteByEmail, List and SweepExpired. Every login issues a fresh 32-byte id. Idle and absolute expiry use the CP clock.

Cookie `__Host-warden_portal` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when redirectURL is https; `warden_portal` only for http loopback or allowInsecureIssuer, with a startup warning. Secure is never derived from r.TLS.

While discovery has not succeeded, /portal/login and /portal/callback return 503 idp_unavailable; CP start and worker routes are unaffected. Errors redirect to /portal?login_error=<code> with code from {state_invalid, nonce_mismatch, token_invalid, exchange_failed, idp_error, blocked, not_allowed, idp_unavailable}; IdP error text is never echoed.
Each attempt logs `msg=portal_login result reason sub duration_ms` and records a login entry through the W-P1-AAUD-02 Recorder. The code, state, verifier, nonce, tokens and cookie are never logged.
plan: Create internal/portal/store.go (new): PortalSessionStore built with webauth.NewSessionStore(db, webauth.SessionTable{Name: "portal_sessions", MigrationID: "portal_sessions/0001"}), plus a DeleteByEmail passthrough.

Create internal/portal/portal.go (new): New(cfg *config.ConsentConfig, db *cpstate.DB, store secrets.SecretStore, blocks Blocklist, rec Recorder, logger) *Portal, where Blocklist is a small interface {IsBlocked(sub, email string) bool} met by controlplane.BlockStore. It holds a webauth.Flow with Purpose "portal", LoginCookie "warden_portal_login" and the next-path rule, and has Routes(mux) and Start(ctx).

tickets.title: Store the IdP refresh token in a CP-only secret namespace on login
tickets.body: When consent.idpLink is enabled, the portal callback stores the user's refresh token in the CP-only consent.store (W-P3-CSIG-06) under `idp/<userKey>` and records only a Reference in idp_links. No worker holds a credential for that store, and the write is fail-closed: no token or no successful Put means no session. The table carries the generation, issue time and relink deadline that p3-offboarding needs to rotate safely and to tell Dex absolute expiry apart from a disabled user (carried forward from p1-dex).
requirements: Build the key only with secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) and secrets.IdPLinkKey(userKey) from W-P3-CSIG-06; with the default namePrefix the AWS name is `warden-cp/idp/<userKey>`.

Startup: with consent.enabled and idpLink.enabled, the CP refuses to start unless consent.store (controlplane.NewUserStore, W-P3-CSIG-06) is configured and implements secrets.Persistent with Persists() true. An echo store is refused, and the error names the backend.
In the callback, before creating the session: if the token response has no refresh_token, return a 502 page with code offline_access_not_granted, create no session and write nothing.

Migration `idp_links/0001`: idp_links(iss, sub, user_key, email, secret_key, refresh_ref, generation INTEGER, linked_at, refresh_issued_at, relink_due_at, last_refresh_at, last_refresh_status, offboarded_at, PRIMARY KEY(iss, sub)), with a unique index on user_key. No column holds a token value; refresh_ref = secrets.Ref(token).String().

Export LinkStore{Get, List, Rotate(ctx, iss, sub, expectedGeneration, token)} for W-P3-OFFB-02. Rotate takes the per-user_key mutex, returns ErrStaleGeneration without any Put when the stored generation differs, and otherwise does the Put and then UPDATE ... WHERE generation=?, incrementing generation. Rotation does not change refresh_issued_at or relink_due_at, because Dex keeps the chain's absolute lifetime.

Export LinkStore{Get, List, Rotate(ctx, iss, sub, expectedGeneration, token)} for W-P3-OFFB-02. Rotate does Put and then UPDATE ... WHERE generation=?, and returns ErrStaleGeneration on a mismatch. Rotation does not change refresh_issued_at or relink_due_at, because Dex keeps the chain's absolute lifetime.
Logout and session expiry never delete the stored token. Log `msg=idp_link_stored ref generation` and record `user.idp_linked` through the W-P1-AAUD-02 Recorder; never the token.

tickets.title: Add the portal session middleware, CSRF, logout and console isolation
tickets.body: Add the exported portal.RequireSession middleware and portal.PrincipalFrom, which later features (/connect/*, the portal page, grants) build on. Add CSRF with the console's `X-Warden-CSRF` header name (carried forward) and a portal-specific HMAC label, an Origin check, GET /portal/api/me and POST /portal/logout. Prove in tests that a portal session opens no console route and a console credential opens no portal route. Let admins list and revoke portal sessions, and end them when a user is blocked.
requirements: RequireSession reads only the portal cookie, looks the session up (idle and absolute expiry), touches last_seen_at at most once a minute, rechecks BlockStore.IsBlocked from the in-memory snapshot (a blocked principal gets 403 {"error":"user_blocked"} and its portal sessions are deleted), and puts portal.Principal{Iss, Sub, Email, Groups} in its own context key. Unauthenticated browser GETs get a 302 to /portal/login?next=<path>; API calls get 401. It ignores Authorization headers and console cookies.

CSRF on every non-GET, HEAD or OPTIONS request behind RequireSession (/portal/*, /connect/*): the `X-Warden-CSRF` header, or a `csrf` form field on application/x-www-form-urlencoded posts, must equal HMAC-SHA256(raw session id, "warden-portal-csrf") in constant time. Origin, when present, must equal the redirectURL origin. Failures return 403 {"error":"csrf"}.

GET /portal/api/me returns {sub, email, expiresAt, csrf, link:{status, relinkDueAt}} with Cache-Control: no-store, or 401. W-P3-PORT-01 extends this route rather than adding its own. POST /portal/logout (CSRF checked) deletes the row and clears the cookie, and keeps idp_links and the stored token.

Isolation: the console withSession and authz table never read the portal cookie, so /dashboard/*, /central/secrets and /auth/me return 401 for a portal-only request. Worker routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest) never touch the portal store.

Revocation: BlockStore.Add (W-P1-BLOCK-07) also calls PortalSessionStore.DeleteBySub and DeleteByEmail. GET and DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions accept ?kind=portal (admin only, W-P1-SSO-08) and return the same value-free fields.
Logs: portal_logout, portal_csrf_denied and portal_session_revoked{by_sub, target_sub, count}, with no token, cookie or full handle. With consent disabled, all /portal/* paths return 404.
plan: Create internal/portal/middleware.go (new): RequireSession, Principal, PrincipalFrom and the CSRF and Origin check, using webauth.CSRFToken(rawID, "warden-portal-csrf") from W-P3-CSIG-05.

tickets.body: P1 puts the OIDC login flow, the oidc_pending store, SessionStore and the session middleware inside internal/controlplane. internal/portal and internal/oauthbroker are mounted by controlplane, so they cannot import that code without an import cycle. tickets.title: Add the CP-only user credential store, user key helpers and reserved secret prefixes
tickets.body: Every P3 feature stores per-user credentials: IdP refresh tokens (this feature), provider grants and parked revokes (p3-oauth-broker, p3-consent-portal) and OAuth client secrets. Today the CP sends its secretStore credential to workers over SettingsWire.Secrets (internal/config/settings.go), so anything written there is readable by every worker; storeFetcher also uses a placeholder name directly as a store key, and /central/secrets can write or delete any key. Add one CP-only store, `consent.store`, that no worker ever gets a credential for, one helper that turns (iss, sub) into a fixed-length user key, and reserved logical prefixes that no static mapping or console edit can touch. This is library and config work only; nothing writes to the store until W-P3-CSIG-03 and W-P3-BRKR-04.
requirements: New internal/secrets/userkey.go: `UserKey(iss, sub string) (string, error)` returns the lowercase hex of the first 16 bytes of SHA-256("warden-user-v1\x00" + iss + "\x00" + sub), 32 characters, and errors on an empty iss or sub or one containing NUL. Key builders take that userKey: `UserGrantKey(userKey, provider)` = `users/<userKey>/<provider>`, `IdPLinkKey(userKey)` = `idp/<userKey>`, `RevokingKey(userKey, provider)` = `revoking/<userKey>/<provider>`, `UserPrefix(userKey)` = `users/<userKey>/` and `ClientSecretKey(provider)` = `oauth-clients/<provider>`. They reject a userKey that is not 32 lowercase hex characters and a provider that fails `ValidProviderID` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`). No other P3 code builds these keys from raw subs.

Reserved prefixes: `IsReservedKey(key)` is true for keys under `users/`, `idp/`, `revoking/` and `oauth-clients/`. Config validation (YAML parse, parseRemotePolicy and the CP settings and policy writers) rejects a static SecretMapping placeholder under a reserved prefix with `invalid_secret_key: reserved namespace`; storeFetcher.Fetch returns an error for reserved keys without calling Get; /central/secrets putSecret and handleSecretByKey return 403 {"error":"reserved_key"} and listSecrets leaves them out. W-P3-BRKR-06 extends the same check to /dashboard/api/secretstore.

New `type Persistent interface { Persists() bool }`: EchoStore returns false and awsSecretStore true (the W-P3-PUS-01 Vault store will also return true). A store that does not implement it counts as non-persistent.

New CP-local `consent.store` block (`json:"-"`, strict keys, never on SettingsWire or /policy): backend aws|vault|echo (echo only with --dev), namePrefix (default `warden-cp/`), aws {region}, vault {addr, mount, namespace, tokenEnv (default VAULT_TOKEN)}. Credentials come only from the CP environment or role; there is no key or token field in YAML. backend vault fails validation until W-P3-PUS-02 wires the W-P3-PUS-01 store.

New controlplane.NewUserStore(cfg) returns a secrets.SecretStore that is never exposed on /central/secrets or the dashboard secret-store tab. Startup fails, naming both keys, when consent.store has the same backend as secretStore and either namePrefix is a prefix of the other.

Docs (docs/control-plane.md, secret store section): example IAM and Vault policies that give only the CP role access to `warden-cp/*`, and a statement that worker roles and the distributed secretStore credential must never cover it. Back-compat: existing placeholders are unaffected unless they already use a reserved prefix, which now fails validation with a clear message.

In internal/secrets/store.go add Persistent and the reserved-key check in storeFetcher.Fetch; add Persists() to EchoStore (internal/secrets/echo.go) and awsSecretStore (internal/secrets/aws_store.go).

name: Consent sign-in
label: consent-auth

summary: Warden resolves a person's groups directly from Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or Google Workspace, so Dex becomes optional. The console, worker identity verification and token service accept ID tokens from one or more configured issuers, and group lookups that the token cannot carry (Entra overage, Google) go through a cached directory adapter.
design: New package internal/idp with `type GroupResolver interface { Groups(ctx context.Context, iss, sub string, claims map[string]any) ([]string, error) }` and adapters `claims` (read a configured claim, default `groups`), `okta`, `entra`, `google`; Dex keeps using the `claims` adapter.

Multi-issuer config block `identity.issuers[]: {name, issuer, clientID, audiences[], groupSource: claims|okta|entra|google, groupsClaim, cacheTTL}`; the OIDC verifier from p1-verify-token becomes a map keyed by `iss`, each with its own JWKS cache; unknown `iss` is rejected (401), never falls through to another issuer.

Entra: if the token has `_claim_names.groups` / `hasgroups` (overage), call Microsoft Graph `POST /v1.0/users/{oid}/getMemberGroups` with app-only client credentials (`clientSecretEnv` or certificate); group IDs are mapped to display names only if `entra.resolveNames: true`. Okta: `groups` claim from a custom authorization server, optional `GET /api/v1/users/{id}/groups` fallback with an SSWS token from env.

Google: Admin SDK Directory API `groups.list?userKey=<email>` using a service account with domain-wide delegation (`google.serviceAccountKeyEnv`, `google.adminSubject`); Google ID tokens carry no groups, so this path is mandatory for Google.

Resolved groups are cached per (iss, sub) for `cacheTTL` (default 10m) with singleflight; on directory API failure the cached value is used up to `staleTTL`, after which role mapping yields no groups (viewer-or-deny, never a widened role). Directory credentials are fetched via internal/secrets and never written to CP state.
Group strings are namespaced `<issuer-name>:<group>` only when more than one issuer is configured, so p1-sso-roles mappings and p1-group-policy rules stay unambiguous.
done_when: With Dex removed from the compose stack, a user signing in through Okta, Entra (including an overage account) or Google gets the correct console role and group-based policy on the worker.

name: Okta / Entra / Google direct
label: idp-adapters

name: Policy long-poll
summary: Workers long-poll GET /policy?wait=30s with an ETag and hot-reload the new policy; heartbeats every ~10s; fail-closed until the first successful pull.

name: Fleet dashboard
summary: Fleet dashboard on the control plane with per-worker slicing, a live policy editor, MCP inventory per worker, alerts and Explore.

The control-plane console gets its first authentication. Today `/dashboard/*` is mounted with no auth at all (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go `mux.Handle("/dashboard/", dash.Handler())`), including the routes that write real secret values. With `console.auth: oidc`, humans sign in to Dex (or any OIDC issuer) with auth code + PKCE, get a server-side session, and are mapped from IdP groups to admin, editor or viewer. Every dashboard route is checked against a method-and-path role table that denies anything not listed, and the shared WARDEN_CP_TOKEN is never accepted on human routes. `console.auth: none` stays the default and keeps today's open console, with warnings.
design: Scope: CP only. Worker routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest, /healthz) keep their current bearer check and are not touched. The worker-local dashboard mount (internal/worker/worker.go:581 `adminMux.Handle("/dashboard/", dashSrv.Handler())`) keeps its current behaviour; authz wraps only the CP mount.

New package `internal/cpstate`: one SQLite DB `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` (modernc.org/sqlite, already in go.mod), single connection with WAL and busy_timeout like internal/integration/store.go, and a forward-only `schema_migrations(id, applied_at)` table keyed by string IDs such as `sessions/0001` so features never collide. A DB that holds an unknown migration ID or fails `PRAGMA quick_check` stops startup (fail-closed). OIDC console mode requires `--state-dir`.

CP-local `console:` block (`json:"-"`, never on policyWire or SettingsWire): `auth: none|oidc`, `oidc: {issuer, clientID (default warden-console), clientSecretEnv, redirectURL, scopes, allowInsecureIssuer}`, `roles: {admin, editor, viewer: [groups]}`, `session: {idle: 1h, absolute: 12h}` (fixed defaults). The CP reads it only from the operator-owned `--config` file, never from the `<state-dir>/config.yaml` copy, which is seeded once (seedServedConfig in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go) and rewritten by the dashboard writers. A differing console block in the served copy is ignored with a warning.

Login: `GET /auth/login` stores state, nonce, an S256 PKCE verifier and the `next` path in a cpstate `oidc_pending` row (10 min TTL, single use, capped) bound to the browser by a short-lived login cookie. `GET /auth/callback` consumes the row atomically, exchanges the code with golang.org/x/oauth2 (new dependency), and verifies the ID token with a new `identity.NewIDTokenVerifier`, a thin wrapper over the W-P1-VRFY-01 OIDC verifier, that checks aud contains clientID, azp equals clientID when present or when aud has several entries, the nonce, RS256/ES256 only and 60s skew. The console uses its own Dex client `warden-console`, separate from the `warden` agent-token client. The identity key is (iss, sub); email is for display only.

Degraded modes: OIDC discovery is lazy and retried with backoff, so a Dex outage never stops the CP from starting or serving workers. While the IdP is unreachable only /auth/login and /auth/callback return 503 `idp_unavailable`; existing sessions keep working. Session expiry uses the CP clock only, and sessions survive CP restarts. The IdP-down admin path is break-glass (p1-breakglass).

Sessions: a fresh 32-byte random id on every login, stored only as sha256 in `sessions`. Cookie `__Host-warden_console` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when redirectURL is https; plain `warden_console` only for an http loopback or allowInsecureIssuer setup, with a warning. Secure follows the redirectURL scheme, not the local listener, so a TLS-terminating ingress works. The CSRF token is an HMAC of the raw session id, sent in `X-Warden-CSRF` on every non-GET request together with an Origin check against the redirectURL origin.

Roles: the session stores the IdP groups, and the role is recomputed on every request from the current `console.roles` (admin > editor > viewer). A login whose groups match no role creates no session. Admins can list and revoke sessions. IdP group changes take effect at the next login, so the 12h absolute lifetime bounds offboarding lag unless an admin revokes earlier.

Authz: `dashboard.Routes()` exports every {method, path, action} the dashboard registers. A CP middleware applies a table keyed by {method, path} giving the minimum role and an action name (reused by p1-admin-audit). Viewer: every GET, plus POST query and audit/verify. Editor: POST query/generate (it spends LLM tokens; also limited to 10 per minute per session), POST/PUT policy and detection, and settings writes that touch only editor fields. Admin: POST/DELETE integrations, POST/PUT llmproviders, POST/DELETE secretstore, /central/secrets and sessions. A {method, path} not in the table is denied, and a coverage test fails on any route missing from it.

Settings writes are authorized per field. Editor may change only advisory, compliance, dlp, logging, agents and cacheTTLSeconds. Any other difference from the live SettingsWire (llmProviders, secrets, explore, judge, observability, mcp, and fields added later such as identity) needs admin, because those can change where workers send real credentials. A denial returns 403 with the field names.

The request Principal is `{Kind: session|breakglass|apikey, Iss, Sub, Email, Groups, AuthMethod}`, so p1-breakglass, p1-admin-audit and p2 API keys reuse the same table. In oidc mode WARDEN_CP_TOKEN opens no /dashboard/* or /central/secrets route; it stays valid on worker routes until p1-worker-tokens.

Back-compat: a missing `console` block means `auth: none`; the console stays open as today and compose recipes keep working. none mode logs a startup warning, `/dashboard/api/setup` returns `authMode`, the UI shows a banner, and a new `--require-console-auth` flag refuses to start in none mode. Logs carry `console_login`, `console_logout`, `console_authz_denied` and `console_session_revoked` records, never tokens, codes, cookies or secret values.
done_when: On a CP started with `console.auth: oidc` in --config, an https redirectURL and an existing --state-dir: an unauthenticated request, or one carrying only the WARDEN_CP_TOKEN bearer, gets 401 on every /dashboard/api/* route and on /central/secrets, while workers keep pulling /policy. An LDAP user in warden-viewers can read every tab but gets 403 on POST /dashboard/api/policy and POST /dashboard/api/secretstore. A warden-editors user can edit policy and toggle DLP but gets 403 when a settings change touches llmProviders or the secrets backend. Only warden-admins can edit integrations, LLM providers and secrets, and can revoke a live session, which then gets 401. A POST without a matching X-Warden-CSRF header gets 403, the CP still starts and serves workers with Dex stopped, and a route-coverage test fails if any dashboard route has no authz entry.

tickets.title: Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations
tickets.body: Create new package `internal/cpstate` that opens one SQLite DB at `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` and runs forward-only migrations registered by each feature store. This ticket ships only the runner and test migrations: `oidc_pending` comes in W-P1-SSO-03 and `sessions` in W-P1-SSO-04. It follows the single-connection modernc pattern already used in internal/integration/store.go and internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go, so it is small. Admin audit, policy versions, worker tokens and backups build on this file.
requirements: API: `Open(ctx, path string, migs []Migration) (*DB, error)`, `(*DB).Close() error`, `(*DB).SQL() *sql.DB`, with `Migration{ID string; SQL string}`. `OpenReadOnly(ctx, path)` opens the file with `mode=ro`, applies no migrations, still runs quick_check and the unknown-ID check, and is what offline readers such as W-P1-AAUD-04 use. IDs are unique strings such as `sessions/0001`, so migrations from different features never collide.
`schema_migrations(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER)`. Each migration and its row commit in one transaction; a failure rolls back both.
Downgrade guard: if the DB holds a migration ID the binary does not register, Open returns an error naming that ID and leaves the file unchanged.
Connection settings match the repo: `SetMaxOpenConns(1)` and DSN pragmas journal_mode(WAL), busy_timeout(5000), foreign_keys(1). The file is created with mode 0600.
Fail-closed: a file that is not a database or fails `PRAGMA quick_check` stops startup with an error naming the path and a hint to restore from backup or move the file aside.

cmd/proxy opens the DB only when `--state-dir` is set and passes it in a new `controlplane.Config.State *cpstate.DB` field; without `--state-dir` State is nil and CP behaviour is unchanged. The DB is closed after the HTTP server drains.
One startup log line with fields `db` and `applied` (migration IDs). Row contents are never logged.

tickets.title: Implement OIDC login and callback with PKCE on the control plane
tickets.body: Add `/auth/login` and `/auth/callback` on the CP mux in oidc mode, using authorization code with S256 PKCE, a browser-bound single-use pending row in cpstate, and strict ID token checks. This ticket adds a thin ID-token verifier to internal/identity on top of the W-P1-VRFY-01 OIDC verifier (Audience=clientID, AllowedAZP=[clientID], WithNonce), so the console shares its keyset, algorithm allowlist and skew handling. On success it maps groups to a role with `ConsoleConfig.RoleFor` and creates a session through the W-P1-SSO-04 SessionStore. It uses the `warden-console` client already defined in the reference Dex config by W-P1-DEX-01.
requirements: Routes are mounted only when console.auth=oidc and Config.State is set; in none mode they return 404. `next` is accepted only as a relative path under /dashboard/ (no scheme, no `//`, no backslash), otherwise /dashboard/ is used.

OIDC discovery is lazy and retried with backoff in a goroutine started from Server.Start; until it succeeds /auth/login and /auth/callback return 503 `idp_unavailable`, and CP startup and worker routes are unaffected.

Migration `oidc_pending/0001`: `oidc_pending(state_hash PK, nonce, verifier, next, browser_hash, expires_at)` with a 10 min TTL. Callback consumes the row with `DELETE ... RETURNING` in one statement. Rows are swept every minute and capped at 10,000; above the cap login returns 503.

Browser binding: /auth/login sets `__Host-warden_login` (or `warden_login` on http; HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Max-Age 600) holding random bytes whose sha256 must equal browser_hash at callback; the cookie is cleared after use.

New `identity.NewIDTokenVerifier(ctx, IDTokenConfig{Issuer, ClientID, AllowInsecureIssuer})` built on identity.NewOIDCVerifier from W-P1-VRFY-01 with Audience=ClientID, AllowedAZP=[ClientID] and WithNonce; it adds the OIDC Core rule that azp must be present and equal ClientID when aud has several entries. RS256/ES256 only and 60s skew come from the shared verifier. The callback compares the nonce in constant time.

On success: RoleFor(groups) must match, else redirect with `login_error=no_role` and no session; groups capped at 256; SessionStore.Create issues a fresh id; offline_access is not requested and no access, refresh or ID token is stored.

Errors redirect to `/dashboard/?login_error=<code>` with code from {state_invalid, nonce_mismatch, token_invalid, exchange_failed, idp_error, no_role, idp_unavailable}; IdP error text is never echoed.

No Dex config change: the `warden-console` client (redirect https://localhost:7070/auth/callback, secretEnv WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET) comes from W-P1-DEX-01. Each attempt logs `msg=console_login result reason sub duration_ms`, never the code, state, verifier, nonce or tokens.

Create internal/controlplane/oidc_pending.go (new): migration, Put, Take(stateHash) with DELETE ... RETURNING and expiry check, Count for the cap, and Sweep(now).

Create internal/controlplane/auth.go (new): lazy provider with backoff, oauth2.Config{ClientID, ClientSecret, RedirectURL, Scopes, Endpoint}, handleLogin using oauth2.GenerateVerifier, oauth2.S256ChallengeOption and SetAuthURLParam("nonce"), and handleCallback using Exchange with oauth2.VerifierOption, then the ID-token verifier, RoleFor and SessionStore.Create.
Mount /auth/login and /auth/callback in Server.Handler (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) only in oidc mode; start the discovery and sweeper goroutines in Server.Start.
Use the existing `warden-console` client and WARDEN_CONSOLE_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET from W-P1-DEX-01/02 in the docs example; do not edit deploy/compose/dex.
Add internal/controlplane/auth_test.go (new) with an httptest fake OIDC provider (discovery, JWKS, token endpoint, RSA key) and a fake clock, plus internal/identity/idtoken_test.go (new).

tickets.title: Add server-side sessions, logout, /auth/me and CSRF
tickets.body: Add the `sessions` store, the session middleware that puts a Principal into the request context, the session cookie, CSRF checks, `POST /auth/logout` and `GET /auth/me`. It is built and tested by calling SessionStore.Create directly, so it lands before the login flow in W-P1-SSO-03. It also adds one `api()` fetch wrapper to the dashboard UI, because without the CSRF header every write would fail once oidc mode is enforced. This ticket authenticates but does not deny; enforcement comes in W-P1-SSO-05.
requirements: Migration `sessions/0001`: `sessions(id_hash PK, iss, sub, email, groups_json, auth_method, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at)` with indexes on expires_at and sub. `SessionStore` takes an injectable `now func() time.Time` and has Create, Lookup, Touch, Delete, DeleteBySub, List and SweepExpired.
Every Create issues a fresh 32-byte crypto/rand id (base64url); only sha256(id) is stored. The CSRF token is HMAC-SHA256(raw id, "warden-csrf"), so it is never stored.

Cookie: `__Host-warden_console` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when console.oidc.redirectURL is https; `warden_console` without Secure only when redirectURL is http on loopback or allowInsecureIssuer, with a startup warning. Secure is never derived from r.TLS.
Idle and absolute expiry use the CP clock; last_seen_at is written at most once per minute per session; expired rows are swept every minute from Server.Start.

`Principal{Kind, Iss, Sub, Email string; Groups []string; AuthMethod string}` with WithPrincipal and PrincipalFrom(ctx). withSession is applied only to /dashboard/, /central/secrets and /auth/*, never to /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest or /healthz.

CSRF: for methods other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS with a session, `X-Warden-CSRF` must match in constant time and Origin, when present, must equal the redirectURL origin; otherwise 403 `{"error":"csrf"}`.

POST /auth/logout (CSRF checked) deletes the row and clears the cookie; GET /auth/me returns `{sub,email,role,authMethod,csrf,expiresAt}` with Cache-Control: no-store, or 401. Both are mounted only in oidc mode.
Logs show at most the first 8 hex characters of id_hash and never the cookie value or CSRF token.

tickets.title: Enforce role checks on every dashboard route
tickets.body: Add the authz table and middleware that make oidc mode real: every {method, path} the dashboard serves gets a minimum role and an action name, and anything not listed is denied. The dashboard registers routes by path and switches on method inside each handler, and http.ServeMux cannot list its patterns, so this ticket exports a static route list for the table and its coverage test. Settings writes are checked per field, because SettingsWire carries llmProviders, the secrets selector and other fields that control where workers send real credentials. This ticket also removes the temporary oidc startup guard from W-P1-SSO-02.
requirements: `dashboard.Routes() []Route{Method, Path, Action string}` lists every method each handler accepts; Server.Handler() registers from the same list, so the worker dashboard (internal/worker/worker.go:581) behaves exactly as before.

internal/controlplane/authz.go (new) table. Viewer: GET on every dashboard path, POST query, POST audit/verify. Editor: POST query/generate (it spends LLM tokens; 10 per minute per session, then 429), POST/PUT policy, POST/PUT detection, POST/PUT settings (editor fields only). Admin: POST/DELETE integrations, POST/PUT llmproviders, POST/DELETE secretstore.

The role is recomputed on each request with console.RoleFor(principal.Groups) against the current config. No principal: 401 JSON for /dashboard/api/*, 302 to /auth/login?next= for HTML. Too low: 403 `{"error":"role_required","need":"<role>"}`. A {method, path} not in the table: 403 for every method.

Settings: editor may change only advisory, compliance, dlp, logging, agents and cacheTTLSeconds. Any other difference from the live SettingsWire, including fields added later, needs admin, and the 403 body lists the fields. SetSettingsWriter changes to `func(context.Context, config.SettingsWire) error` so the CP writer can read the Principal.
Authz wraps only the CP mount of dash.Handler(); /central/secrets is left to W-P1-SSO-06. In none mode the middleware is not installed.
index.html reads the role from /auth/me, hides controls marked data-min-role above it, and shows the user's email and a logout button. The server stays the only enforcement point.

name: SSO + 3 roles
label: console-sso-rbac

summary: Every admin change made through the CP console or API, plus logins, is recorded with who did it, what changed, and state hashes before and after. Entries are hash-chained and signed with Ed25519, using the existing receipt signer. Admins can list and verify the log in the dashboard or offline with a CLI, and each entry is also emitted as a `warden.admin.v1` JSON log line so an off-host copy anchors the chain. The feature is CP-only and off by default.
design: New package `internal/adminaudit` holds the `Entry` type, its canonical encoder, the SQLite `Store` on the `internal/cpstate` DB (W-P1-SSO-01), `Verify`, and `Recorder.Record(ctx, Entry)` as the single write API. The HTTP middleware, the auth handlers, the offline CLIs (W-P1-WTOK-03 token CLI) and later features (P2 token service and key manager, P4 grants, P5 KMS and retention) all write through Recorder, so none of them import `internal/controlplane`. `internal/controlplane` keeps only the middleware, the per-target state hashers and the wiring.

Enabled only when `--state-dir` is set and the new CP-local `console.adminAudit.enabled` is true (default false in P1). When disabled, no table, key file or middleware is created and CP behaviour is byte-identical to today. Workers never run this code; worker-local dashboard writes stay out of scope.

cpstate migration `admin_audit(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts_unix_nano INTEGER, actor_id, actor_role, auth_method, action, target, target_ref, details_json, outcome, http_status, before_hash, after_hash, client_ip, request_id, key_id, prev_hash, entry_hash, signature)` with indexes on ts, action and actor_id, plus a side table `admin_audit_actor(seq PRIMARY KEY, sub, email)`. actor_id = HMAC-SHA256(cp salt, sub), so plaintext identity sits outside the signed bytes and P5 retention can erase side rows without breaking the chain. No code path issues UPDATE or DELETE on either table. auth_method is one of oidc|breakglass|cli|none|system, validated in Go rather than with a SQLite CHECK, so later phases can add values without a table rebuild.

Canonical bytes are `encoding/json` of a fixed-order struct: v, seq, ts_unix_nano, actor_id, actor_role, auth_method, action, target, target_ref, details, outcome, http_status, before_hash, after_hash, client_ip, request_id, key_id, prev_hash. entry_hash = sha256(canonical), so prev_hash is covered. signature = Ed25519 over the domain-separated message "warden.admin.v1\x00" || entry_hash, through new `audit.Signer.SignBytes` and `audit.VerifyBytes`; `Sign(event)` stays byte-identical. Seq 1 is an `audit.genesis` entry with prev_hash of 32 zero bytes. Order comes from seq; ts is informational, so clock steps never break verification. A golden-bytes test pins the encoding.

The chain stays linear across processes: Append runs in one SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that reads the head row, builds and signs seq+1, inserts and commits. The CP and the offline token CLI can append to the same DB at the same time. A later Postgres store does the same under a row or advisory lock.

Key handling: new exported `audit.LoadOrCreateSigner(path)` (a port of the unexported worker `loadOrCreateSigner` in internal/worker/wiring.go) creates the PKCS#8 key with O_CREATE|O_EXCL at 0600 and re-reads it if another process won the race. The key defaults to `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`, and the new `--admin-audit-key-file` flag lets it live on a separate secret mount. Every row stores key_id (hex of the first 8 bytes of sha256(pubkey)). Startup fails closed if rows exist and the key file is missing or its key_id differs from the head row, instead of silently minting a new key. P1 ships one key and no rotation command; the supported rotation (`admin-audit rotate-key` with an old-key-signed handoff entry) is W-P2-KEYS-06 in p2-key-manager. Until then a documented manual rotation starts a new chain segment: with the CP stopped, the operator runs `admin-audit verify` and `admin-audit export` (W-P1-AAUD-04) to archive the old segment and its public key, puts the new key at `--admin-audit-key-file`, and starts the CP once with `--admin-audit-new-segment=<new key_id>`. The CP then appends an `audit.segment_start` entry signed by the new key, whose prev_hash is the old head entry_hash and whose details name the previous key_id; every later row is stamped with the new key_id. The flag must equal the loaded key's key_id and is a no-op once the head is on that key, so a restart can never rotate the key by accident. The key and DB share a trust boundary until p2-key-manager or p5-kms replace the signer behind a small interface.

Capture is route-table driven, not method driven. AAUD-02 extends the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route entries with `Action`, `Target` and `Audited bool`. The middleware wraps only /dashboard/*, /central/secrets* and /auth/logout, never /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest or /healthz. Audited today: policy, settings, detection, integrations, llmproviders, /dashboard/api/secretstore POST/DELETE and /central/secrets POST/DELETE. Worker tokens, the block list and policy versions register their own routes and hashers when they land. Read-only POSTs (/dashboard/api/query, /dashboard/api/query/generate, /dashboard/api/audit/verify, admin-audit/verify) are `Audited:false`. A test fails if any registered route has no classification.

Middleware order: session (sets Principal), then request id, then admin audit, then authz, then handler. Audited requests take one CP-wide admin-mutation mutex (30s context timeout) around before-hash, handler, after-hash and append, so the hashes describe exactly this change; admin writes are rare and the lock never touches worker routes. The middleware never reads request bodies. Handlers attach a non-secret `target_ref` and closed-allowlist `details` through `adminaudit.Annotate(ctx, ref, details)`, for example `secret:OPENAI_KEY` or `policy@<etag>`.

State hashers are HMAC-SHA256 with a CP-local key, so low-entropy config cannot be guessed offline from a hash. Built-in hashers cover the policy, settings, integrations, detection and llmproviders blocks. Secret stores keep state outside Warden, so their hashes are empty and only the operation and key name are recorded. Secret values, any substring of them, and `secrets.Ref` output never enter a row, log line or detail.

Outcomes: ok (2xx/3xx), denied (401/403/CSRF failure on an authenticated session), rejected (other 4xx, including 409), error (5xx). On error the after hash is still taken, because a change may have partly applied. Requests with no session are never chained, so nobody can flood the table; they get a rate-limited log line only.

Non-HTTP events go through Recorder. Hand edits of the served YAML are audited in both policy-store modes: in file mode (the default) the existing 3s re-read compares the served file hash with the hash the last CP writer produced, and a change no CP writer made appends one `config.external_change` row (auth_method system, target policy, before `file:<old sha256>`, after `file:<new sha256>`) once per distinct hash; versioned mode records the same action through W-P1-PVER-05. Also through Recorder: the auth handlers record `auth.login`, `auth.login_failed` and `auth.logout`; W-P1-OPS1-01 records every `auth.breakglass` attempt; offline CLIs record auth_method `cli` with actor `cli:<os user>`. In `console.auth: none` mode the actor is `anonymous` with auth_method `none`. client_ip is RemoteAddr unless the peer is in the new CP-local `console.trustedProxies` CIDR list (default empty), which allows X-Forwarded-For. request_id is a valid incoming X-Request-Id (64 chars or fewer of [A-Za-z0-9-]) or a newly generated id, echoed in the response.

Failure mode is fail-closed for audited mutations only. If the store health flag is bad, the middleware returns 503 `admin_audit_unavailable` before the handler runs. If an append fails after a successful change, the entry is logged at ERROR with `persist_failed=true`, the store is marked degraded until an append succeeds, and an `admin_audit_degraded` Finding is published through the CP alert pipeline. Reads, /policy serving, ingest and heartbeats never depend on audit health.

SIEM and anchoring: each entry is emitted through an `adminaudit.Emitter` seam whose default writes slog JSON `msg=admin_audit schema=warden.admin.v1` with seq, entry_hash, prev_hash and key_id plus plaintext sub and email. A periodic `admin_audit.checkpoint` line (head seq and entry_hash, default every 5m) lets an off-host copy detect tail truncation or a rollback from backup. W-P1-JAUD-03 plugs the `auditlog.Writer` into the Emitter seam; this feature only logs to the CP logger.

Verification: one `adminaudit.Verify(fromSeq, toSeq, anchor)` checks seq continuity, prev_hash links, entry_hash, the signature for each key_id (a key_id change is accepted only at an `audit.segment_start` entry, or at the `audit.key_rotated` entry W-P2-KEYS-06 adds), and the actor HMAC where a side row exists. It streams rows, caps work per call and returns `lastVerifiedSeq` so large ranges resume. The dashboard handler and the offline `warden control-plane admin-audit verify` CLI share it. At startup the CP verifies the last 1000 rows and the head signature and publishes `admin_audit_verify_failed` on failure. A signed `audit.pruned` checkpoint entry type is reserved so P5 retention can drop a prefix without breaking verification. The table grows without bound in P1; it holds admin actions only.
done_when: On a CP started with --state-dir, console.auth=oidc and console.adminAudit.enabled=true, editing policy, settings, detection, integrations, llmproviders and secrets (both /dashboard/api/secretstore and /central/secrets) each produces exactly one chained, signed row with actor, role, auth_method, target_ref and before/after hashes. OIDC logins and an authenticated viewer's denied write also produce rows, while heartbeats, ingest and read-only POSTs produce none. No secret value or secrets.Ref string appears in any row or log line. An admin can list, filter and verify the log in the dashboard (a viewer gets 403) and with `warden control-plane admin-audit verify` while the CP is stopped. Changing any column or deleting a middle row fails verification, a swapped key file stops the CP from starting (the documented manual rotation leaves a verifiable `audit.segment_start` boundary instead), and deleting the newest rows is caught against the seq/entry_hash anchor in the emitted log lines. With the audit DB unwritable, mutations return 503 and a Finding fires while /policy keeps serving. A hand edit of the served YAML in file mode writes one config.external_change row with the new file hash.

tickets.title: Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate
tickets.body: Add the new `internal/adminaudit` package with the canonical `Entry`, the SQLite store on cpstate, `Verify`, and `Recorder` as the only write API. Appends run in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction so the CP and offline CLIs can share the chain without forking it. Add domain-separated `SignBytes`/`VerifyBytes` to the existing receipt signer and an exported, race-safe key loader. Nothing records entries yet, so behaviour does not change.
requirements: Add `(*audit.Signer).SignBytes(b []byte) []byte` and `audit.VerifyBytes(pub ed25519.PublicKey, b, sig []byte) bool` in internal/audit/receipt.go; both use the message "warden.admin.v1\x00" || b. `Sign(event)` output and the receipt format do not change.

Add exported `audit.LoadOrCreateSigner(path string) (*Signer, error)` that creates the PKCS#8 key with O_CREATE|O_EXCL at 0600, re-reads the file if it already exists, and rejects non-Ed25519 keys. internal/worker is not changed.
Register cpstate migrations for `admin_audit` and `admin_audit_actor` with the columns and indexes in the design. No Go code issues UPDATE or DELETE on either table.

Canonical bytes are JSON of a fixed-order `Entry` struct with `v:1` and ts as an INTEGER unix-nano; entry_hash = sha256(canonical) with prev_hash inside canonical; seq 1 is `audit.genesis` with a 32-zero-byte prev_hash; key_id is hex of the first 8 bytes of sha256(pubkey); actor_id = HMAC-SHA256(cp salt, sub).

`Store.Append` reads the head, signs and inserts seq+1 inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. `List(filter, limit<=200, cursor)` is newest-first with a seq cursor. `Verify(fromSeq, toSeq, anchor)` streams rows and returns {ok, checked, firstBadSeq, headSeq, headHash, lastVerifiedSeq}.

Startup check `Store.Open` fails with an actionable error when rows exist and the key is missing or its key_id differs from the head row. Add the `--admin-audit-key-file` flag (default `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`). The only exception is the manual rotation: with `--admin-audit-new-segment=<key_id>` equal to the loaded key's key_id and a head row on another key_id, Open appends one `audit.segment_start` entry (signed by the new key, prev_hash = head entry_hash, details {previous_key_id}) and continues. A value that does not match the loaded key fails startup, and the flag is a no-op once the head is on that key. Scheduled or automatic rotation is out of scope for P1 (W-P2-KEYS-06).

The store is built in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go only when `--state-dir` is set and `console.adminAudit.enabled` is true (default false), and is passed as a new `controlplane.Config.AdminAudit`. The CP logs the public key and key_id at INFO; the private key and PEM are never logged.

New internal/adminaudit/entry.go: `Entry` struct in canonical field order, `canonical()`, `entryHash()`, actor HMAC helper, outcome and auth_method validation.
New internal/adminaudit/store.go: cpstate migrations, `Store` with `Append` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), `List`, `Head`, and the startup key_id check; new `Recorder` interface wrapping Append.
New internal/adminaudit/verify.go: streaming `Verify` with anchor support and per-call row cap.

Changing any single column of row N in SQL, or deleting row N from the middle, makes Verify return ok=false with firstBadSeq=N; deleting the last row passes a plain Verify but fails Verify with the previous head as anchor: `go test ./internal/adminaudit -run 'TestStoreTamper|TestStoreAnchor'`

tickets.title: Record CP admin mutations and logins through audit middleware
tickets.body: Add the admin audit middleware to the CP, driven by `Action`, `Target` and `Audited` fields added to the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route table rather than by HTTP method, so worker heartbeats, ingest and read-only POSTs are never chained. It serializes admin mutations, records before/after HMAC state hashes and the outcome, and fails closed when the store cannot write. Auth handlers record logins and logouts through the same Recorder, and every entry is emitted as a `warden.admin.v1` slog line through a seam that W-P1-JAUD-03 later points at the JSON audit writer.
requirements: Extend the SSO-05 `authzRoute` entries with `Action`, `Target` and `Audited bool`. Audited routes: dashboard policy, settings, detection, integrations, llmproviders, /dashboard/api/secretstore POST/DELETE, /central/secrets POST and /central/secrets/{key} DELETE. Read-only POSTs are `Audited:false`. /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest and /healthz are never wrapped.

Order is session, request id, admin audit, authz, handler. A 403 or CSRF failure for an authenticated principal is recorded as outcome=denied; a request with no session writes no row and only a rate-limited log line.

Take one CP-wide admin-mutation mutex (30s context timeout) across before-hash, handler, after-hash and append. Expose `RegisterStateHasher(target, fn)`; built-in HMAC hashers cover policy, settings, integrations, detection and llmproviders; secrets record empty hashes plus the key name. Worker-token and blocked-user hashers are registered by W-P1-WTOK-03 and W-P1-BLOCK-03.

The middleware never reads r.Body. Handlers set `target_ref` and allowlisted `details` through `adminaudit.Annotate`. No secret value, substring of one, `secrets.Ref` string, bearer token or body appears in a row, log line or detail.

Fail closed: if the store health flag is bad, return 503 `{"error":"admin_audit_unavailable"}` before the handler runs. If Append fails after the handler, log the entry at ERROR with `persist_failed=true`, mark the store degraded until an append succeeds, and publish an `admin_audit_degraded` Finding.
