name: Admin audit log
label: admin-audit-log

summary: Policy and distributed settings move from in-place edits of the served YAML into an append-only versioned store in CP state. Every save creates a new version with author and message, admins can diff any two versions and roll back, and workers are always served the head version. The feature is behind `--policy-store=versioned` (default `file`), credential values are never stored in versions, and the served YAML is kept as a mirror of head so turning the flag off or downgrading the binary serves the same policy. The default flips to versioned in release N+1, and YAML as a policy source is removed in release N+2.
design: Gate: new `warden control-plane --policy-store=file|versioned` flag, default `file`. `versioned` requires `--state-dir` and the cpstate DB from W-P1-SSO-01, and fails at startup with an actionable error without them. In `file` mode, or with no state dir, the CP keeps today's YAML serve, edit and 3s re-read path byte-for-byte. Release plan: release N (the first release with this feature) ships versioned only behind `--policy-store=versioned`, default `file`. Release N+1 flips the default to `versioned`; `--policy-store=file` stays as an explicit opt-out, and a CP started without `--state-dir` keeps file mode with a startup WARN. Release N+2 removes YAML as a policy source: `--policy-store=file` is removed, the served YAML is only the write-through mirror of head, and hand edits are never served (they come in through `warden policy import`).

Schema (cpstate migrations): `policy_versions(version INTEGER PK, parent_version, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind (the W-P1-AAUD-01 auth_method set: oidc|breakglass|cli|none|system), message <=512 chars, source[policy|settings|llmproviders|rollback|import], doc_json, doc_sha256)`, a one-row `policy_head(version)`, and an append-only `policy_publish_log(seq INTEGER PK, version, etag, reason, actor_sub, at)` written in the same transaction as every head move. No code path updates or deletes version rows. Later features use publish_log: signed bundles take seq as their monotonic number, explain resolves a timestamp to a version, and the CP appends a row whenever the served ETag changes without a new version (block-list edits from W-P1-BLOCK-03, AWS credential rotation), so ETag-to-version lookups never miss.

doc_json is the canonical policyWire {allowlist, denylist, settings}. Credential values are never versioned: a non-empty `settings.secrets.secretAccessKey` (internal/config/settings.go, the sanctioned credential-on-wire exception) is replaced by `sha256:<16 hex>` before hashing and storing. The live value stays in the CP-local served YAML secretStore block, as today, and is overlaid when the served wire is built, so /policy bytes and the worker behaviour are unchanged. `blockedUsers` (W-P1-BLOCK-01) is also excluded from doc_json and merged in at serve time, so rollback can never unblock a user. The /policy ETag is the hash of the merged served wire, not doc_sha256.

`PolicyVersionStore` is an interface (Create, Head, Get, List, PublishLog) with a SQLite implementation so a later Postgres store can implement it. Create is one transaction: insert the version, `UPDATE policy_head SET version=new WHERE version=expectedHead` (0 rows means ErrConflict and rollback of the transaction), append the publish_log row. This compare-and-swap works across processes, so the CLI and the CP cannot both create the same version. A doc whose doc_sha256 equals head's writes nothing and returns changed=false. Ordering always uses the version integer, never created_at.

Validation reuses the existing full loader, not a parallel validator: render the candidate (served YAML root with its policy and settings blocks replaced by the doc, using the encoders WritePolicy/WriteSettings use today), write a temp file and run config.NewLocalYAMLProvider, the same check atomicWriteConfig makes. This enforces default-deny (empty allowlist rejected), domain and rate-limit checks and cross-block references such as judge/explore llmProvider. Save, import and rollback all go through it, and a failure returns 422 with the loader error and leaves head unchanged.

One publish path: `s.publish(ctx, mutate func(*policyWire), expectedHead, msg, source)` runs under writeMu. WritePolicy (allow/deny), WriteSettings (the blocks its form owns) and WriteLLMProviders (llmProviders) each change only their own fields and carry every other wire field from head (dlp, advisory, explore and so on). CP-local writers (WriteIntegrations, WriteDetection, console) keep the YAML round-trip. A test asserts every SettingsWire field is either owned by a writer or carried.

Serving: policyServer.loadPolicy returns head doc plus credential overlay plus blockedUsers, held in the in-memory policyWatch. The /policy hot path never touches the DB. Create calls Refresh so long-poll waiters wake at once. In versioned mode the existing 3s ticker runs `SELECT version FROM policy_head` and reloads the doc only when the version changes, so out-of-process writes (CLI) reach workers within 3s plus one long-poll cycle.

Degraded modes: startup in versioned mode is fail-closed. If the store cannot be read, head points at a missing version, or a doc fails its doc_sha256 check, the CP refuses to start with an actionable error and never falls back to the possibly older YAML. A runtime read error keeps last-known-good in memory (as policyWatch does today) and logs. Workers are unaffected: they keep last-known-good.

Write-through mirror: after every head move, the CP renders head's policy and settings blocks into the served YAML through atomicWriteConfig and records the mirrored file hash. The YAML therefore always equals head, which makes `--policy-store=file` or a binary downgrade serve the same policy. A mirror failure (for example a read-only mount) logs at error and never fails the version. If the ticker finds the YAML blocks differ from the mirrored hash, that is an external edit: log a warning once per distinct file hash, show a dashboard banner, keep serving head. External edits come back in through `warden policy import`. In file mode (the default) hand edits are still served as today and are audited by W-P1-AAUD-02 as `config.external_change`.

Migration: in versioned mode with an empty store, the CP imports the served YAML's allow/deny and config.SettingsWireFromPolicy (credential redacted) as version 1, author `system:import`, and checks that the served /policy bytes and ETag are unchanged. It is idempotent: a non-empty store is never re-imported.

Concurrency contract: GET /dashboard/api/policy and /dashboard/api/settings return `version` in the body and an `X-Warden-Policy-Version: N` header. Writes send `If-Match: "v<N>"`. A stale value returns 409 `{error:"policy_conflict", head, author}` (409, not 412, so the body can name the conflicting author). Policy, settings and llmProviders share one head, so a settings save makes a concurrent allow/deny save conflict. Missing If-Match is accepted until W-P1-PVER-04 makes the UI always send it, then returns 428 in versioned mode. /policy's content-hash ETag is unchanged.

Authors: OIDC sessions record sub and email from the request Principal (W-P1-SSO-04). console.auth none records `anonymous` with author_kind none; a break-glass session records `breakglass:<username>` with author_kind breakglass. Migration records `system:import`. The CLI records `cli:<os user>`. Messages are capped at 512 characters with control characters stripped.

Rollback to N creates version latest+1 with N's doc, source `rollback`, message `rollback to v<N>` plus an optional user note. It requires If-Match, is revalidated against today's rules (422 if N no longer validates), and keeps the current credential and block list. History is never rewritten.

Diff is structural. Allow and deny lists are multisets keyed by a new `diffKey()` method on config.AllowlistEntry and config.DenylistEntry, which today returns domain|port (rateLimit and timeWindow are compared attributes, duplicates show as count changes). W-P1-GPOL-01 extends diffKey when it adds groups/users. Settings are compared by JSON path into {added, removed, changed}, and credential paths only ever show fingerprints.

Audit and observability: each save, rollback, import and migration writes an admin audit row with target `policy` and before/after `v<N>:<doc_sha256>`, through a `policy` StateHasher for HTTP paths (W-P1-AAUD-02) and direct appends for migration and CLI. slog `policy version created` carries version, parent, source, author_sub and doc_sha256, never doc content or settings values. The fleet view shows each worker's version by mapping its heartbeat ETag through policy_publish_log. Metrics hooks (head version, store errors) are noted for when CP metrics exist. P1 has no pruning; growth is one row per save.
done_when: On a CP started with `--state-dir` and `--policy-store=versioned`, an existing deployment upgrades and serves byte-identical /policy JSON as version 1. Editors make three saves (policy, settings and llmProviders), each shown as a version with author, message and a structural diff, and a concurrent stale save gets 409. Rolling back to version 1 creates version 5, workers pull it within one long-poll cycle, and the fleet view shows them on v5. The served YAML mirrors head, so restarting with `--policy-store=file` serves the same policy. The block list is unchanged by the rollback, every step has an admin audit row, and no policy_versions row or history API response contains a raw AWS secretAccessKey. docs/control-plane.md states the release plan: versioned behind `--policy-store` in release N, the versioned default in N+1, and YAML-as-source removed in N+2.

tickets.title: Add versioned policy store and serve the head version
tickets.body: Add the policy_versions, policy_head and policy_publish_log migrations and a PolicyVersionStore in internal/controlplane, plus the `--policy-store=file|versioned` flag (default `file`). In versioned mode, policyServer serves the head doc with the live AWS credential overlaid, and the 3s ticker polls the head version. Credential values are redacted before any row is written because the table is append-only. This ticket writes no versions on its own, so with an empty store or in file mode behaviour is unchanged.
requirements: Migrations create `policy_versions(version, parent_version, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind, message, source, doc_json, doc_sha256)`, `policy_head(version)` and `policy_publish_log(seq, version, etag, reason, actor_sub, at)`; the store exposes no update or delete of versions.

Create(ctx, doc, author, msg, source, expectedHead) runs in one transaction with `UPDATE policy_head ... WHERE version=expectedHead` as a cross-process compare-and-swap; 0 rows returns ErrConflict and writes nothing; a doc equal to head returns changed=false and writes nothing.

Before hashing and storing, a non-empty settings.secrets.secretAccessKey is replaced by `sha256:<16 hex>`; the live value is read from the served YAML secretStore block and overlaid only when building the served wire.
Validation renders the doc into the served YAML root, writes a temp file and runs config.NewLocalYAMLProvider; no parallel validator is added.
`--policy-store=versioned` without `--state-dir` fails at startup with an actionable error; in `file` mode, or versioned with an empty store, /policy is byte-identical to today.
Startup in versioned mode fails closed when the store is unreadable, head points at a missing version, or doc_sha256 does not match; a runtime read error keeps last-known-good.
The /policy hot path never reads the DB; the ETag stays etagFor(served wire); Create calls Refresh().
slog `policy version created` logs version, parent, source, author_sub and doc_sha256 only; doc content, settings values and the credential are never logged.
plan: Add internal/controlplane/policystore.go (new): the cpstate migrations, the PolicyVersionStore interface, a SQLite implementation (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, CAS update, publish_log append) and ErrConflict.
Add redactCredentials/overlayCredentials (new) in policystore.go for Settings.Secrets.SecretAccessKey, reading the live value from the served YAML secretStore block.

Factor the block rendering out of Server.WritePolicy and Server.WriteSettings (controlplane.go) into renderDocToRoot (new) and add validateDoc (new), which reuses the temp-file and NewLocalYAMLProvider logic of atomicWriteConfig.

Change newPolicyServer and policyServer.loadPolicy (policyserver.go) to take an optional store: when it is set and Head() > 0, decode doc_json, check doc_sha256, overlay the credential and return it; otherwise keep the YAML path. Cache the head version so Refresh reloads the doc only when it changes.

Add the `--policy-store` flag in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go and a PolicyStore field (new) on controlplane.Config; in Server.Start, when versioned, make the policyReloadInterval ticker poll the head version instead of re-reading YAML.

acceptance: Given head v3, Create with expectedHead=2 returns ErrConflict, the row count is unchanged and Head() is 3; with 20 goroutines racing Create on the same expectedHead under -race, exactly one succeeds.
Given a doc with an invalid domain pattern or an empty allowlist, Create returns a validation error and Head() and the served ETag are unchanged.
Given settings with secrets.secretAccessKey set, after Create the doc_json column and the DB file do not contain the raw value, while GET /policy still carries it.

tickets.title: Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish
tickets.body: In versioned mode, import the served config as version 1 on first start, then route every writer of a wire-carried block (WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteLLMProviders) through one publish path that builds the new doc from head and creates a version. The dashboard writer setters gain context.Context so the author comes from the request Principal, and the dashboard GET/POST handlers carry the head version and If-Match. Without WriteLLMProviders in this path, provider edits would save but never reach workers.
requirements: With an empty store in versioned mode, import allow/deny plus config.SettingsWireFromPolicy (credential redacted) as version 1, author `system:import`, message `initial import from <path>`, and append an admin audit row directly; never re-import a non-empty store.
Migration does not change the served wire: /policy bytes and ETag are identical before and after, so no worker reports `behind`.

Add `s.publish(ctx, mutate, expectedHead, msg, source)` under writeMu; WritePolicy, WriteSettings and WriteLLMProviders change only the fields they own and carry every other wire field from head; WriteSettings keeps today's preserve-on-empty rule for secretAccessKey via the stored fingerprint.

Dashboard setters take ctx and write metadata (`SetPolicyWriter(func(context.Context, config.Policy, WriteMeta) error)`, and likewise SetSettingsWriter and SetLLMProvidersWriter); author is Principal sub/email, or `anonymous` when console.auth is none.

GET /dashboard/api/policy and /dashboard/api/settings return `version` and `X-Warden-Policy-Version`; a stale `If-Match: "v<N>"` returns 409 `{error:"policy_conflict", head, author}`; a missing If-Match is accepted for now so today's UI keeps working.
Register a `policy` StateHasher with W-P1-AAUD-02 that returns `v<head>:<doc_sha256>`, replacing the built-in policy hasher in versioned mode, so HTTP saves record before and after.
In file mode all writers keep today's YAML round-trip unchanged.
plan: Add importInitialVersion (new) in internal/controlplane/policystore.go, called from controlplane.New when the store is versioned and Head()==0; compare etagFor before and after and fail startup on mismatch.

Add Server.publish (new) in controlplane.go and rewrite Server.WritePolicy, Server.WriteSettings and Server.WriteLLMProviders (llmproviders_write.go) to call it in versioned mode, keeping refresh() and reinjectExploreLLM().

Change SetPolicyWriter, SetSettingsWriter and SetLLMProvidersWriter in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go to take ctx and WriteMeta (new: ifMatch, message); parse If-Match in putPolicy and putSettings and the llmproviders handler, map ErrConflict to 409 and add the version header and field to the GET responses.

Update the ConfigEditor interface in internal/controlplane/seams.go and the wiring at controlplane.go (dash.SetPolicyWriter, dash.SetSettingsWriter, dash.SetLLMProvidersWriter) for the new signatures.
Register the `policy` StateHasher in Server.Handler when versioned.

Add a field-ownership table test listing each SettingsWire field and its owning writer or 'carried', and update internal/dashboard/policy_edit_test.go, dashboard_llmproviders_test.go and internal/controlplane/llmproviders_write_test.go for the ctx setters.
acceptance: Given a state dir with a populated config.yaml and an empty store, starting with `--policy-store=versioned` serves /policy byte-identical to file mode with the same ETag, and the store holds one version authored `system:import`.

Given a session Principal {sub:u1, email:a@x}, POST /dashboard/api/policy with the current If-Match creates a version with author_sub=u1 and author_email=a@x; replaying it with the old If-Match returns 409 with head and author.
Given a WriteLLMProviders edit in versioned mode, a new version with source `llmproviders` exists and GET /policy carries the new provider list.
Given a WriteSettings edit, the dlp and advisory blocks of the new version equal head's (carried, not dropped).
Given `--policy-store=file`, the existing internal/controlplane and internal/dashboard tests pass with only signature updates.

`go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPolicyMigrationByteIdentical|TestVersionedWriters|TestSettingsFieldOwnership'` and `go test ./internal/dashboard -run 'TestPolicyWrite|TestLLMProviders'` pass.

tickets.title: Add policy history, structural diff and rollback APIs
tickets.body: Add dashboard APIs to list versions, fetch one version, diff two versions and roll back, behind the W-P1-SSO-05 role table. The diff lives in a new internal/controlplane/policydiff.go and keys entries with a new diffKey() method so W-P1-GPOL-01 can extend it. Because internal/controlplane imports internal/dashboard, the handlers talk to the store through a new dashboard.PolicyHistory interface. Rollback creates a new version and never touches credentials or the block list.
requirements: GET /dashboard/api/policy/versions?cursor=&limit= returns metadata only (version, parent, created_at, author_sub, author_email, author_kind, message, source, doc_sha256), newest first, default 50, max 200.

name: Policy history + rollback
label: policy-versioning

summary: Admins can block a person by Dex sub or email from the console. The list is stored on the CP outside policy versions, ships to workers on the policy wire as `blockedUsers`, and workers deny any request or session whose identity claims match, within one long-poll cycle. This is the P1 offboarding and incident kill switch. In P1 attribute mode a request that carries no token at all is not matched; P2 require mode closes that gap.
design: CP store: cpstate table `blocked_users(id, sub, email, reason, created_by, created_at)`. Each row needs sub or email; email is trimmed and lowercased on write; unique indexes on sub and email. The table is outside policy_versions, so a rollback can never unblock anyone. The list is capped at `config.MaxBlockedUsers` (5000) entries.

Go API `controlplane.BlockStore{List, Add(ctx, entry, actor), Remove(ctx, id, actor)}` is shared by the HTTP handlers and by P3 offboarding, which calls `BlockStore.Add` with actor `system:offboarding` instead of writing a policy version. Every mutation runs the shared validator, goes through the admin audit `StateHasher` for target `blocked_users`, and calls `policyServer.Refresh()`.

Wire: new `config.BlockedUser{Sub, Email}` (json `sub,omitempty` / `email,omitempty`) and `config.Policy.BlockedUsers` (json `blockedUsers,omitempty`, yaml `policy.blockedUsers`). `remoteWire` embeds `Policy`, so workers decode it with no extra code. `policyWire.BlockedUsers` is added with omitempty and holds only sub and email (reason and actor stay on the CP). Entries are deduplicated and sorted by (sub, email), so an empty list keeps /policy byte-identical and the ETag only changes on a real change. `Policy.DeepCopy` copies the slice.

Validation: one exported `config.ValidateBlockedUsers` runs in YAML parse, in `parseRemotePolicy`, and in the CP write path before insert. The CP can therefore never serve an entry that workers reject, which would otherwise make every worker keep its last-known-good policy and freeze all policy updates.

CP load: `policyServer.loadPolicy` adds the `BlockStore` list to the wire it builds (from YAML today, from the head version after W-P1-PVER-01). A block-list read error makes `loadPolicy` fail, so `Refresh` keeps the last-known-good wire and ETag; the list is never served empty by accident. A `policy.blockedUsers` key in the CP policy file is ignored with a warning (console API only) and is preserved by `Server.WritePolicy`.

Worker install: `policy.Evaluator.load` builds a sub set and a lowercase email set from `p.BlockedUsers`, so `Replace` swaps them under the same `swapMu` as allow/deny. This covers boot (`policy.NewEvaluator` in worker.go), `longPollControlPlane` (`ev.Replace`) and standalone YAML with no extra wiring. New method `IsBlocked(sub, email string) bool` is added to `policy.Evaluator` and to `proxy.PolicyEvaluator`. Until the first pull the worker stays fail-closed as today.

Worker match (deny-only, fail closed): the check uses the claims of any token the worker parsed in W-P1-VRFY-02, whatever its verification status (valid, expired, bad signature), because a match can only deny. Sub is an exact match and email a lowercase match. Raw tokens are never logged. Cost per check: one read lock and at most two map lookups.

Enforcement points: at CONNECT after Proxy-Authorization identity extraction and before any dial or `200 Connection Established` (covers raw tunnels too); in a new `blockStage` after the identity stage and before `judgeGate` for every HTTP/1 request; and per stream in `serveGRPCStream` for HTTP/2 and gRPC.

Live termination: `internal/proxy` keeps a registry of open sessions keyed by normalized sub and email (raw tunnels, HTTP/1 keep-alive, HTTP/2 connections and WebSocket frame pumps). After a policy change is applied, the worker closes the sessions that now match the list and writes one deny event per closed session, so idle and long-lived sessions are cut within one long-poll cycle.

Deny response: `403` with JSON `{"error":"user_blocked"}` on the CONNECT response, the request or the h2 stream, then the session ends. The event has Decision=deny, Reason=`user_blocked` and the user fields from W-P1-VRFY-03, and the worker calls `RecordBlocked("user_blocked")`. The alert bridge raises a high-severity Finding deduplicated per user (key derived from a hash of the sub); the Finding carries the opaque sub only, never the email.

Console coupling: the API refuses a request from an admin to remove a block that matches their own identity (another admin or break-glass must do it). The CP session layer rejects login and active sessions for a principal whose sub or email is blocked.

Rollout safety: workers advertise `caps:["blocklist/v1"]` on heartbeat. Old workers decode the new wire without error (encoding/json drops unknown fields) and would otherwise look current. The CP registry stores the caps and the Blocked users panel and worker list warn about connected workers that do not enforce the list.

Degraded modes: while the CP is unreachable, workers keep their last-known-good list and never unblock on their own; new blocks apply when they reconnect. If Dex is down, admins use break-glass (W-P1-OPS1-01). A CP without --state-dir has no store: the block-list API returns 503 `state_dir_required` and /policy is unchanged. Operators can also block and unblock offline with `warden control-plane block add|remove|list --state-dir` (W-P1-BLOCK-08), which a running CP picks up within 2s.
Standalone (local-only) workers accept `policy.blockedUsers` in local YAML, with the same validation and enforcement. It applies on restart, since there is no local hot-reload today.

Known P1 gap: a blocked user whose agent sends no token at all is treated as anonymous in attribute mode and is not matched. P2 require mode (identity-enforcement) closes this. Every `Evaluator.Replace` also resets rate-limit windows, so each block or unblock resets them fleet-wide; this is documented and left to a follow-up.
done_when: On a managed deployment where every connected worker advertises blocklist/v1, an admin blocks alice@corp in the console (or with break-glass when Dex is down), and the block is audited. Within one long-poll cycle Alice's new CONNECTs get 403 user_blocked whether her token is valid or expired; her open HTTP/1 keep-alive, HTTP/2, WebSocket and tunnel sessions are closed or denied with deny events carrying reason user_blocked and her sub; one Finding is raised for her; other users are unaffected; and she can no longer use the console. A CP block-list read error, a policy rollback, a worker restart and a CP outage each leave her blocked. Unblocking restores access and returns the served ETag to its previous value. Requests with no token at all are a documented P1 gap closed by P2 require mode.

tickets.title: Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT, per request and per h2 stream
tickets.body: Build the block set inside `policy.Evaluator` so it is swapped atomically with allow/deny at boot, on every long-poll update and for standalone YAML. Check it at CONNECT, in a new request stage before `judgeGate`, and per HTTP/2 stream. A match returns 403 `user_blocked`, records a deny event and ends the session. Matching uses the claims of any token the worker parsed, verified or not, because a match can only deny.
requirements: `policy.Evaluator.load` builds a sub set and a lowercase email set from `p.BlockedUsers`; new method `IsBlocked(sub, email string) bool` reads them under `swapMu.RLock`. `IsBlocked` is added to `proxy.PolicyEvaluator`. `SettingsApplier` is not changed.

CONNECT check in `handleConn`: after identity extraction (W-P1-VRFY-02) and before policy evaluation, any dial or `200 Connection Established`; applies to both the TLS-terminating and raw-tunnel paths.

Per-request check: new `blockStage` in `runRequestStages`, after the identity stage and before `judgeGate`; a match ends the keep-alive session without forwarding, swapping secrets or calling the judge. `serveGRPCStream` checks each HTTP/2 stream and answers 403 on that stream.

Fail closed: the claims of valid, expired and bad-signature tokens are all matched (W-P1-VRFY-01 returns the parsed sub and email for expired and invalid tokens, and connIdentity keeps them); requests with no token are unaffected in attribute mode. The raw token is never logged; the event records `identity_status` so the cases can be told apart.

tickets.body: Add the `blocked_users` cpstate table, a `BlockStore` Go API, and admin-only endpoints to list, add and remove entries. `policyServer.loadPolicy` adds the stored list to the served wire, and a store read error keeps the last-known-good policy instead of serving an empty list. The list lives outside policy versions so a rollback never unblocks anyone. The dashboard panel is W-P1-BLOCK-04.
requirements: cpstate migration for `blocked_users(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, sub TEXT, email TEXT, reason TEXT, created_by TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMP)` with CHECK(sub IS NOT NULL OR email IS NOT NULL) and unique indexes on sub and email (stored lowercase).

New `controlplane.BlockStore` with `List(ctx)`, `Add(ctx, entry, actor)` and `Remove(ctx, id, actor)`. `Add` runs `config.ValidateBlockedUsers` on the resulting list; reason is at most 512 bytes. `BlockStore` is the only write path, used by the HTTP handlers and later by P3 offboarding.

Admin-only routes in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table: GET /dashboard/api/blocked-users returns 200 [{id,sub,email,reason,createdBy,createdAt}]; POST {sub?,email?,reason} returns 201, 400 on validation failure, 409 on duplicate, 422 above MaxBlockedUsers; DELETE /dashboard/api/blocked-users/{id} returns 204 or 404. Editors and viewers get 403. Without --state-dir the routes return 503 {"error":"state_dir_required"}.
Self-unblock is refused: DELETE of an entry that matches the caller's own sub or email returns 403 {"error":"self_unblock_forbidden"}.

`loadPolicy` merges `BlockStore.List` into `policyWire.BlockedUsers` (normalized and sorted) through new helper `withBlockedUsers`; any store error fails `loadPolicy`, so `Refresh` keeps the previous wire and ETag, logs one ERROR line `msg=blocklist_load_failed` (no entry values) and publishes a `blocklist_load_failed` Finding, because the CP has no metrics endpoint in P1. Each successful mutation calls `policyServer.Refresh()`.

Audit: register a `StateHasher` for target `blocked_users` with the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware; every POST and DELETE, including 403s, produces an audit row. Reason text is never written to slog or metrics.
A CP without State serves a byte-identical /policy.

tickets.title: Close open sessions of newly blocked users on policy change
tickets.body: Raw tunnels, idle HTTP/1 keep-alive connections, HTTP/2 connections and WebSocket frame pumps never pass through a per-request check, so a blocked user keeps them open indefinitely. Add a per-identity session registry in internal/proxy and close the matching sessions after each applied policy change. This makes the done_when claim about existing sessions hold for every connection type.
requirements: New session registry in internal/proxy: a map from normalized sub and email to a set of `io.Closer` behind a mutex; sessions register when identity resolves (CONNECT or first request) and deregister on close.
Covers raw tunnels (`tunnel`), HTTP/1 keep-alive sessions, HTTP/2 connections from `handleGRPC`, and WebSocket frame pumps after `s.handoff`.
New method `Proxy.CloseBlockedSessions()` checks each registered identity with `IsBlocked` and closes matches; each closed session writes one deny event with Reason=user_blocked.
`longPollControlPlane` calls it after `ev.Replace(remote)` through a new optional hook, so it runs for every applied change.
Metrics: new OTel gauge `warden.blocklist.entries` and counter `warden.blocklist.sessions_closed.total` (Prometheus names warden_blocklist_entries and warden_blocklist_sessions_closed_total).
No overhead for anonymous sessions: sessions without identity are not registered.

tickets.title: Add offline block add, remove and list commands to the control-plane CLI
tickets.body: Add `warden control-plane block add|remove|list`, which opens cpstate in --state-dir directly, so an operator can block or unblock a user while the console or the IdP is unavailable, and scripts and recipe checks can block a user without a browser session. It follows the W-P1-WTOK-05 offline CLI rules: the same BlockStore and validator as the admin API, one admin audit row per write with auth_method cli, and the existing audit key, never a new one. A running CP picks up CLI writes within 2s.
requirements: `warden control-plane block add [--sub S] [--email E] --reason R`, `block remove --id ID` and `block list [--json]`; each takes a required --state-dir and an optional --admin-audit-key-file (default `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`) and works with or without a running CP. add prints the new id; exit 1 on validation errors (same messages as the API 400/409/422), exit 2 for an unknown id on remove.

Writes go through controlplane.BlockStore (W-P1-BLOCK-03) with actor `cli:<os user>`, so validation, email lowercasing, MaxBlockedUsers and the unique indexes match the API exactly. The CLI has no console identity, so the self-unblock check does not apply; docs state that write access to the state dir already allows policy changes.

Audit: each add and remove appends one admin_audit row through adminaudit.Store.Append (auth_method cli, action blocked_users.add or blocked_users.remove, target blocked_users, target_ref the entry id), loading the key from --admin-audit-key-file and never minting a key when rows exist. When the admin_audit table does not exist the append is skipped with a one-line notice, as in W-P1-WTOK-05. Reason text never goes to slog.

A running CP sees CLI writes within 2s: BlockStore polls `PRAGMA data_version` every 2s and calls policyServer.Refresh on a change, so workers receive the new list within 2s plus one long-poll cycle and the W-P1-BLOCK-07 session snapshot is refreshed.

Tests in cmd/proxy/controlplane_block_test.go against a state dir shared with an in-process CP.

`block remove --id <id>` restores the previous /policy ETag, and an unknown id exits 2.

name: User block list
label: user-block-list

summary: The control plane issues a separate token for each worker. The token is shown once, stored only as a hash, bound to exactly one proxy id (P1 has no prefix binding: each replica gets its own token, and autoscaled per-pod identity comes with P2 mTLS enrollment in p2-worker-ca), revocable and tracked by last use. Workers use it for /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, and the token's bound proxy id becomes the identity the CP trusts instead of the self-reported header. The shared WARDEN_CP_TOKEN is retired through an explicit auth mode and a documented migration. Workers need no code change: both `controlPlane.tokenEnv` and `central.tokenEnv` carry the worker's own token.
design: Token format: `wwt_` + lowercase unpadded RFC 4648 base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes (52 characters after the prefix). Token id: `wt_` + 16 hex characters. The CP stores only sha256(token), which is enough for 256-bit random secrets. New cpstate migration `worker_tokens(id, name UNIQUE, proxy_id NOT NULL, token_hash UNIQUE, created_by, created_at, expires_at NULL, last_used_at NULL, revoked_at NULL, revoked_by NULL)`. Each token is bound to one exact proxy_id; there is no prefix binding in P1. At most 2 active tokens per proxy_id, so rotation can overlap. Plaintext is returned only by Create and never logged, audited, stored or returned by any GET.

Requires cpstate, which exists only with --state-dir (W-P1-SSO-01). One resolver picks the worker auth mode at startup and logs it once: `open` (no legacy token, not strict: today's behaviour, anonymous callers accepted as kind=none, warning logged), `mixed` (legacy token configured: worker tokens or the legacy token, anonymous rejected), `strict` (`--require-worker-tokens`: worker tokens only). Strict without --state-dir, or strict together with a legacy token, fails startup. Strict without TLS fails startup unless `--allow-insecure-worker-auth` is set; any token mode without TLS logs a warning.

Seam: `WorkerAuthenticator.Authenticate(r) (WorkerPrincipal{TokenID, TokenName, ProxyID, Kind token|legacy|none}, error)`, applied only to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest. It replaces `policyServer.token`, the bearerOK call in `handleHeartbeat`, and the string token in `analytics.NewIngestHandler` (which takes an authorizer func; `analytics.StaticTokenAuthorizer` keeps the old behaviour for the worker's own aggregator at internal/worker/worker.go:450). `bearerOK` stays on /central/secrets under W-P1-SSO-06 rules. A `wwt_` bearer is never accepted on /central/secrets, /dashboard/* or /auth/*. A `wwt_` bearer goes only through the token path and never falls back to the legacy compare.

Identity: for kind=token the principal's ProxyID is authoritative. Missing X-Warden-Proxy-ID resolves to the bound proxy_id. Only a header equal to the bound id is accepted (exact match); any other value gets 403. The registry (SeenPolicyPull, SeenHeartbeat, SeenIngest), the stored AggregatedEvent.ProxyID and the ingest/events/MCP/secrets callbacks use the principal's id, never the raw header. Legacy and none principals keep using the header and are shown as unverified.

Hot path: an in-memory index from hash to token is the only per-request lookup (one sha256 and one map read, no DB I/O). It is rebuilt after in-process Create/Revoke and reloaded when a 2s poll of SQLite `PRAGMA data_version` changes, which picks up writes from the bootstrap CLI process. A reload error keeps the last good index and never fails open. expires_at is checked against the CP clock only. `last_used_at` is updated in memory and flushed in one transaction every 60s and on shutdown.

Revocation is a soft delete (revoked_at set, row kept). Every /policy response (200 or 304) is re-authenticated before it is written, and an in-process revoke cancels that token's held long-polls through a per-token cancel registry so they return 401 at once. Bounds: API revoke takes effect on the next request; CLI revoke within 2s. Missing, malformed, unknown, expired and revoked tokens all get the same 401 body `unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; a binding failure gets 403 `proxy id mismatch`. The reason goes only to a rate-limited `worker auth rejected` log line, never the token or its hash.

Admin surfaces: `GET/POST /dashboard/api/worker-tokens` and `DELETE /dashboard/api/worker-tokens/{id}`, admin role through the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table. With console.auth=none, POST and DELETE return 403 pointing to the CLI. The offline CLI `warden control-plane token create|list|revoke --state-dir` works with or without a running CP. `create --from-env VAR|--from-file F` registers an operator-generated `wwt_` value (format checked, only the hash stored), so compose and Kubernetes Secrets can supply the value; re-running it with the same name and value is a no-op.

Audit: only token create and revoke are admin-audit events (target `worker_tokens`, auth_method oidc|breakglass|cli). Worker-plane routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest) are excluded from the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware. CLI appends must keep the chain linear across processes (append inside a SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that reads prev_hash inside it).

Observability: dashboard.WorkerView gains `tokenName`, `tokenLastUsed`, `authKind` (token|legacy|none) and `legacyRequests`; the fleet view shows a legacy/unverified badge. The CP has no /metrics endpoint in P1, so an in-memory counter `warden_cp_worker_auth_total{kind,outcome}` (bounded labels, no proxy_id) is kept and exported when the CP metrics endpoint lands (W-P5-RETN-06). Legacy request tracking per proxy id is capped at 10,000 ids.

Migration: `--legacy-token-env` (with `--token-env` kept as a deprecated alias) keeps the shared token working, so an upgraded CP behaves as before until tokens are issued. In strict mode with console.auth=none, /central/secrets is not mounted, because its only gate would otherwise be an empty shared token. A revoked worker keeps enforcing its last-known-good, default-deny policy, gets no updates and cannot heartbeat or ingest; stopping its traffic means stopping the worker. Hand-off to P2: W-P2-WCA-04 extends WorkerAuthenticator with mTLS principals, and /central/secrets stays a human route in both phases.
done_when: On a CP running with --state-dir and TLS, two workers use distinct per-worker tokens, one created in the console and one with the bootstrap CLI against the running CP. Each worker's /policy, heartbeat and ingest succeed with no worker code change, and events and fleet rows are attributed to each token's bound proxy id; a request with a spoofed X-Warden-Proxy-ID gets 403. A worker token is rejected on /central/secrets. Revoking one token in the console makes its next request on all three endpoints return 401 and a held long-poll return 401 at once; a CLI revoke takes effect within 2s. The other worker keeps working, and the revoked worker keeps its last-known-good default-deny policy. Tokens and revocations survive a CP restart. Create and revoke appear in the admin audit log with the correct actor, and worker-plane traffic does not. The plaintext appears only in the create response or CLI output. A CP started with --require-worker-tokens logs auth_mode=strict, rejects WARDEN_CP_TOKEN with 401 and refuses to start without --state-dir. The control-plane compose recipe comes up with per-worker tokens and no WARDEN_CP_TOKEN.

tickets.title: Add worker token store with hashed storage, revocation and in-memory index
tickets.body: Add the `worker_tokens` cpstate migration and a `WorkerTokenStore` in internal/controlplane that creates, authenticates, revokes and lists per-worker tokens. Only sha256 of the token is stored, and the plaintext is returned once by Create. Authentication reads an in-memory index so the request path does no DB I/O, and the index reloads when another process (the bootstrap CLI) writes the same SQLite file. Nothing calls the store yet, so this merges with no behaviour change.
requirements: Migration `worker_tokens(id TEXT PK, name TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, proxy_id TEXT NOT NULL, token_hash BLOB UNIQUE NOT NULL, created_by TEXT NOT NULL, created_at, expires_at NULL, last_used_at NULL, revoked_at NULL, revoked_by NULL)` (no prefix column: each token is bound to one exact proxy_id), registered through the internal/cpstate migration runner (W-P1-SSO-01). Without --state-dir no store exists.

Token = `wwt_` + lowercase unpadded base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes; id = `wt_` + 16 hex; name 1-64 characters; proxy_id matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`. Malformed input is rejected before hashing or any lookup.

API: `Create(ctx, CreateOpts{Name, ProxyID, ExpiresAt, Actor, Plaintext})` returns (plaintext, Token, error); an empty Plaintext generates one, a supplied one is format-checked and registered (import). `Authenticate(plaintext)` returns Token or ErrMalformed/ErrUnknown/ErrRevoked/ErrExpired. `Revoke(ctx, id, actor)` is idempotent and returns ErrNotFound for an unknown id. `List(ctx)` returns metadata only. `MarkUsed(id, t)`.

At most 2 active (not revoked, not expired) tokens per proxy_id; a third Create returns ErrTooManyActive. Create with an existing name returns ErrNameTaken, unless it is an import whose name and hash match an active row, which is a no-op.

Authenticate reads only an in-memory hash-to-token index. The index is rebuilt after in-process Create/Revoke and reloaded when `PRAGMA data_version` changes (polled every 2s by `Run(ctx)`); a reload error keeps the last good index and logs a warning. Expiry uses the CP clock.
MarkUsed updates memory only; dirty last_used_at values are flushed in one transaction every 60s (interval injectable for tests) and by `Flush(ctx)` on shutdown.
Token.String() and slog LogValue print only id, name and binding. No log, error message or test output contains the plaintext or the hash.
plan: internal/cpstate (from W-P1-SSO-01): register a new `worker_tokens` migration with an index on proxy_id.

New file internal/controlplane/workertokens.go: types Token, CreateOpts, the error values, and `NewWorkerTokenStore(db *cpstate.DB, opts StoreOptions) (*WorkerTokenStore, error)` that loads the index.

Implement Create (generate or import, validate, enforce the active-per-proxy_id limit, insert, update index), Revoke (soft delete, update index), List and Authenticate (prefix and length check, sha256, map read, revoked/expired checks).
Implement `Run(ctx)`: a ticker that reads `PRAGMA data_version` every 2s and reloads the index on change, and flushes MarkUsed state every 60s; implement `Flush(ctx)`.
Add a `Changes()`-style internal hook (unexported for now) so a later Postgres backend can replace data_version polling without changing callers.
New file internal/controlplane/workertokens_test.go and a benchmark BenchmarkWorkerTokenAuthenticate.
acceptance: Given a created token, the DB file does not contain the plaintext (bytes.Contains on the file) and token_hash equals sha256(plaintext).

Authenticate returns ErrRevoked for a revoked token, ErrExpired after expires_at (fake clock), ErrUnknown for a well-formed unknown token, and ErrMalformed for a value without the `wwt_` prefix or with the wrong length.
A token created and then revoked through a second WorkerTokenStore on the same DB file (the CLI case) authenticates and then fails with ErrRevoked in the first store within one 2s poll interval.
10,000 MarkUsed calls for 3 tokens in one interval produce exactly one write transaction, and Flush writes pending values.
A third active token for the same proxy_id returns ErrTooManyActive; re-importing the same name and value is a no-op.

`go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStore` passes and `go test ./internal/controlplane -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkWorkerTokenAuthenticate` reports a cache-hit lookup under 50µs/op.

tickets.title: Authenticate /policy, heartbeat and ingest with per-worker tokens
tickets.body: Add `WorkerAuthenticator` in internal/controlplane and apply it once to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, replacing the three separate shared-token checks. The token's bound proxy id becomes the identity the registry and ingest store record. The default mode stays as today: with no worker tokens issued, a CP with --token-env behaves exactly as before, and a CP with no token and no state stays open with a warning. /central/secrets keeps its own gate and never accepts a worker token.
requirements: `WorkerAuthenticator.Authenticate(r *http.Request) (WorkerPrincipal, error)` with `WorkerPrincipal{TokenID, TokenName, ProxyID, Kind}` (Kind token|legacy|none). A `wwt_` bearer goes only to WorkerTokenStore; any other bearer is compared in constant time with the legacy token; mode is resolved once at startup (open, mixed, strict) and logged as `auth_mode=...`.
Applied only to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest. bearerOK remains only on /central/secrets, and a `wwt_` bearer there gets 401 for every method.

Binding: for kind=token a missing X-Warden-Proxy-ID resolves to the bound proxy_id; a header equal to the bound proxy_id is accepted (exact match only, no prefix binding); anything else gets 403 `proxy id mismatch`. The registry and the ingest store always receive principal.ProxyID.

`analytics.NewIngestHandler(store, auth func(*http.Request) (proxyID string, status int))`; the returned proxyID is used for AggregatedEvent.ProxyID and every ingest callback. `analytics.StaticTokenAuthorizer(token)` keeps the old behaviour for internal/worker/worker.go:450 and existing tests.

ServePolicy re-authenticates before writing any response (200 and 304) after a wait; an in-process revoke cancels that token's held long-polls through a per-token cancel registry so they return 401 within 1s. Waking N waiters does no DB I/O.

Missing, malformed, unknown, expired and revoked tokens get the same 401 body `unauthorized` and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`. Rejections log `worker auth rejected` with reason, token_id when known and remote_addr, at most once per reason and remote_addr per minute; the Authorization header, plaintext and hash are never logged.
Successful requests call MarkUsed and record Kind and TokenID on the registry entry; in-memory counters `warden_cp_worker_auth_total{kind,outcome}` are kept for later export.

name: Per-worker tokens
label: worker-credentials

summary: Operators get a local emergency admin login for when Dex is down. It is off by default, needs TLS, uses an argon2id hash, and every attempt writes an audit row, an ERROR log line and an alert. The CP also takes scheduled, consistent backups of its SQLite state and served config, ships a restore command that refuses unsafe restores, and documents the restore drill and a production readiness checklist.
design: Scope and back-compat: break-glass and backups are both off by default. Both need --state-dir (cpstate). Break-glass also needs console.auth=oidc; validation rejects it with auth none. Workers are unchanged and nothing runs on the request hot path. When p5-postgres-ha replaces SQLite, the backup job is disabled in Postgres mode.

Degraded mode: break-glass only helps if the CP starts and serves while Dex is down. With the issuer unreachable the CP must still serve /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, and /auth/login returns 503 idp_unavailable while discovery retries with backoff. This is a requirement on W-P1-SSO-03 and is tested in W-P1-OPS1-01 by starting the CP with the issuer unreachable.

Config (W-P1-OPS1-01 adds the field, its parsing and validation to the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig): `console.breakGlass: {enabled: false, username, passwordHashEnv | passwordHashFile, sessionTTL: 1h (max 4h), allowBehindTLSTerminator: false}`. The hash is an argon2id PHC string (new dependency golang.org/x/crypto/argon2; PHC encode/parse is written in Warden). Parameters are bounded: m 19456..262144 KiB, t 2..10, p 1..4, salt >= 16 bytes, key >= 32 bytes. passwordHashFile is re-read on each attempt so a mounted secret can rotate without a CP restart. The block is CP-local and never rides policyWire.

TLS: startup fails when break-glass is enabled and the CP serves plain HTTP on a non-loopback --listen address, unless allowBehindTLSTerminator is true. In that case the session cookie is still marked Secure.

`warden control-plane hash-password` reads the password from a TTY with echo off (confirmed twice) or from stdin with --stdin, never from argv. It rejects passwords shorter than 16 characters and prints only the PHC string (m=65536 KiB, t=3, p=2).

Login: `POST /auth/breakglass` is mounted only when enabled and returns 404 otherwise. It is a public pre-auth route in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table, exempt from the W-P1-SSO-04 CSRF check and the W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware. It requires Content-Type application/json, a same-origin Origin header when one is sent, and a body of at most 4 KiB. Order: rate limit, then a 2-slot verify semaphore (429 when full), then argon2id verify. Verify always runs, against a fixed dummy hash when the username does not match, and the username is compared with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, so wrong user and wrong password take the same time and return the same 401 body.

Rate limits: 5 failed attempts per 15 min per r.RemoteAddr host (X-Forwarded-For is not trusted), plus a global ceiling of 20 failed attempts per 15 min, so one attacker behind a shared load balancer address is still bounded. The limiter is in memory and resets on CP restart; this is documented.

Session: success revokes any earlier break-glass session and creates a session with role admin, auth_method `breakglass`, sub `breakglass:<configured username>`, an absolute expiry of sessionTTL and no idle extension. /auth/me gains auth_method and expires_at, and the dashboard shows a red banner with the expiry time. While a break-glass session is active the CP logs a WARN every 5 minutes.

Loud on every attempt: the handler writes exactly one signed admin_audit row itself (action auth.breakglass, auth_method breakglass, outcome ok|denied, client_ip). actor_sub is `breakglass:<configured username>` on a username match and `breakglass:unknown` otherwise; the submitted username and password are never stored or logged. Rate-limited requests are aggregated into at most one audit row per IP per window. The handler always logs one ERROR line msg=breakglass_login (outcome, client_ip), independent of the alert pipeline. It also publishes an integration.Finding with RuleID `breakglass_login`: critical with DedupKey `breakglass_login:success:<session id prefix>` on success (one alert per login), high with DedupKey `breakglass_login:failure` on failure (aggregated by Count). Because Bus.PublishFinding drops findings when no alert manager exists, the CP logs a startup WARN when break-glass is enabled and there is no alert pipeline, or no integration's alerts.match routes rule breakglass_login.

CP instance lock: when --state-dir is set the CP takes a non-blocking flock on `<state-dir>/warden-cp.lock` for its lifetime and refuses to start if another process holds it. This also stops two CPs sharing one state dir, and it is the lock restore checks.

Backups: flags `--backup-dir` (empty means off; must not equal or sit inside --state-dir), `--backup-interval` (default 24h, min 1h), `--backup-keep` (default 7, min 1) and `--backup-include` (default `cp,alerts,config`; `fleet` is opt-in and skipped for --analytics-provider=memory). warden-fleet.db and warden-alerts.db are opened with SetMaxOpenConns(1) and no WAL, so a second connection running VACUUM INTO would make ingest and alert writes fail with SQLITE_BUSY. Each DB is therefore copied by its owning store through a new `BackupTo(ctx, path)` method that runs VACUUM INTO on that store's own *sql.DB: cpstate, integration.Store and analytics.FleetSQLiteStore. Paths come from the resolved --analytics-db and --alerts-db values. The served config.yaml is copied as a file because it drives the /policy ETag today and holds the console, integrations and detection blocks.

Set layout: a free-space check (at least 1.2x the source sizes) runs first. Files go to `<backup-dir>/.tmp-<ts>/` with dir mode 0700 and file mode 0600. manifest.json is written last (format, warden version, cpstate schema_version, ed25519 fingerprint of the admin audit public key, created_at and finished_at in UTC, files [{name, sha256, size}], skipped [...], not_included [cp-audit.key, Dex storage, secret backend]). The dir is fsynced and renamed to `<UTC ts>Z/`. Each DB copy is internally consistent; the set is not one snapshot across DBs, which is acceptable because they share no foreign keys. The sha256 manifest checks integrity, not authenticity.

Scheduling and pruning: the next run is the newest complete set's timestamp plus the interval, so a CP that restarts nightly still backs up, and an overdue backup runs at startup. Runs never overlap. Pruning keeps the newest --backup-keep complete sets, never deletes the last good set, and removes .tmp dirs older than 24h. On-demand runs use `warden control-plane backup` (only when no CP holds the lock) or an admin `POST /dashboard/api/backup`, which is audited.

Backup health: each run logs msg=cp_backup with db, bytes, duration_ms and outcome. A failure logs ERROR and raises a `backup_failed` Finding (high, DedupKey `backup_failed:<db>`). A last success older than 2x the interval raises `backup_stale` (high). Last success time, last error, last set and size appear in /dashboard/api/setup for admins. The CP has no /metrics endpoint today; CP Prometheus metrics stay with W-P5-RETN-06.

Restore: `warden control-plane restore --from <set> --state-dir <dir> [--analytics-db] [--alerts-db] [--force] [--new-audit-key]`. It takes the CP lock and exits with 'control plane is running' if held. Before touching the target it verifies every manifest sha256 and size, runs PRAGMA integrity_check on staged copies, refuses when the set's schema_version is newer than the binary's highest migration, and refuses unless the target's cp-audit.key public key fingerprint matches the manifest (--new-audit-key overrides this and the override is recorded). A non-empty target needs --force. Existing DB, -wal and -shm files move to `<state-dir>/pre-restore-<ts>/`, staged files are renamed into place with mode 0600, and the sessions and oidc_pending tables are emptied. One admin_audit row (auth_method cli, action cp.restore, target = sha256 of manifest.json) is appended. Restore prints the backup timestamp and a warning that worker-token revocations, user blocks and policy versions made after that time must be re-applied from the shipped admin_audit JSON log, because an old snapshot can bring back revoked access.

Docs: docs/runbooks/break-glass.md (enable, store the hash in a secret manager, use during a Dex outage, rotate after use, review audit and alerts), docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md (flags, set layout, off-host copy, quarterly restore drill, re-applying changes made after the backup, what is outside the set) and docs/production-readiness.md (a checklist where every row names an exact flag or key).
done_when: Break-glass, on the compose recipe: with Dex stopped, the CP is restarted and still starts and serves /policy to workers. An operator who enabled break-glass over TLS logs in at /auth/breakglass, gets an admin session marked auth_method=breakglass with a red banner, and the session expires after 1h. The login produces exactly one signed admin_audit row, one ERROR log line and one critical breakglass_login alert that reaches a configured sink. The sixth bad attempt from one IP within 15 min gets 429. Backup and restore: a scheduled backup set taken while ingest and policy writes are in flight passes integrity_check without blocking writers. `warden control-plane restore` loads it into a fresh state dir, and is refused while a CP holds the lock and for a tampered file. The restored CP serves the same /policy ETag, worker tokens valid at backup time authenticate, earlier console sessions are invalid, and the admin audit chain verifies and ends in a cp.restore entry. A failed or stale backup raises a Finding.

tickets.title: Add break-glass local admin with alerting and audit
tickets.body: Add an emergency admin login at `POST /auth/breakglass` so operators can reach the console when Dex is down. It is off by default, refuses to run over plain HTTP, verifies an argon2id hash with bounded parameters, and limits attempts by IP and globally. Every attempt writes one signed admin audit row and an ERROR log line and publishes a `breakglass_login` Finding, so use is never silent even without an alert pipeline. Also add `warden control-plane hash-password`, and test that the CP starts and serves workers while the OIDC issuer is unreachable.
requirements: Config: parse and validate `console.breakGlass {enabled, username, passwordHashEnv | passwordHashFile, sessionTTL, allowBehindTLSTerminator}` in the ConsoleConfig from W-P1-SSO-02 (CP-local, never in policyWire). Validation fails when enabled with console.auth != oidc, without --state-dir, with an empty username, with neither or both hash sources, or with sessionTTL above 4h. At CP start the hash must parse as argon2id PHC with m 19456..262144 KiB, t 2..10, p 1..4, salt >= 16 bytes and key >= 32 bytes; otherwise the CP exits non-zero with an error naming the key and never the value.

TLS: the CP fails startup when break-glass is enabled and it serves plain HTTP on a non-loopback --listen address, unless allowBehindTLSTerminator is true. The session cookie is always Secure for break-glass sessions.

Route: `POST /auth/breakglass` is mounted only when enabled (404 otherwise). It is listed as a public pre-auth route in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table and is exempt from SSO-04 CSRF and the AAUD-02 audit middleware. It requires Content-Type application/json, a same-origin Origin when present, and a body of at most 4 KiB (http.MaxBytesReader).

Verification: the limiter is checked first (5 failures per 15 min per r.RemoteAddr host, no X-Forwarded-For trust, plus a global 20 failures per 15 min), then a 2-slot semaphore (429 with Retry-After when full or limited), then argon2id. Verify always runs, against a fixed dummy hash on a username mismatch, and the username uses subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, so both failure kinds return the same 401 body.

Session: success revokes earlier break-glass sessions and creates one with role admin, auth_method breakglass, sub `breakglass:<configured username>`, absolute expiry sessionTTL (default 1h) and no idle extension, using a new AbsoluteTTL option on SessionStore.Create. /auth/me adds auth_method and expires_at, and internal/dashboard index.html shows a red banner with the expiry time. The CP logs a WARN every 5 minutes while such a session is active.

Audit and alert: each non-rate-limited attempt writes exactly one admin_audit row (action auth.breakglass, outcome ok|denied, client_ip; actor_sub is the configured username on a match, else `breakglass:unknown`), and rate-limited requests add at most one row per IP per window. Each attempt logs one ERROR line msg=breakglass_login and publishes a Finding through a small FindingPublisher seam: SevCritical with DedupKey `breakglass_login:success:<session id prefix>` on success, SevHigh with DedupKey `breakglass_login:failure` on failure. A startup WARN is logged when no alert pipeline exists or no integration's alerts.match routes breakglass_login. The password and submitted username never appear in logs, rows or Findings.

CLI and degraded mode: `warden control-plane hash-password` reads from a no-echo TTY (golang.org/x/term, new direct dependency) or from stdin with --stdin, has no password flag, rejects passwords under 16 characters, and prints only the PHC string. With console.auth=oidc and the issuer unreachable, the CP starts and serves /policy, heartbeat and ingest, and /auth/breakglass works (relies on lazy discovery in W-P1-SSO-03).
Back-compat: with breakGlass absent or disabled, routes, startup, audit behaviour and existing compose recipes are unchanged except for the two new /auth/me fields.

New internal/controlplane/ratelimit.go: a fixed-window failure limiter keyed by RemoteAddr host with a global ceiling, an injectable clock and a sweep of expired keys.

New internal/controlplane/breakglass.go: handleBreakGlass registered in Server.Handler only when enabled; request checks, limiter, semaphore, verify, session creation via SessionStore.Create with AbsoluteTTL, revocation of earlier break-glass sessions, an explicit adminaudit.Recorder.Record call (W-P1-AAUD-01), the ERROR log line, and a new Server.publishFinding that publishes via s.pipeline when it is non-nil. Mark the route public and exempt in the SSO-05 authz table.

tickets.title: Add scheduled SQLite backups with manifest and pruning
tickets.body: Add an off-by-default backup job that writes consistent copies of the CP's SQLite databases and the served config.yaml into timestamped sets with a manifest. The fleet and alerts stores use a single connection without WAL, so each DB is copied by its owning store with `VACUUM INTO` to avoid SQLITE_BUSY failures on ingest. Sets are written atomically, pruned safely, and a failed or stale backup raises a Finding. Restore is in W-P1-OPS1-04.
requirements: Flags on `warden control-plane`: `--backup-dir` (empty means off), `--backup-interval` (default 24h, min 1h), `--backup-keep` (default 7, min 1), `--backup-include` (default cp,alerts,config; fleet opt-in). --backup-dir equal to or inside --state-dir is rejected. With --backup-dir unset, behaviour is unchanged.

Each store gets a new `BackupTo(ctx, dst string) error` that runs `VACUUM INTO ?` on its own *sql.DB: cpstate (warden-cp.db), integration.Store (warden-alerts.db) and analytics.FleetSQLiteStore (warden-fleet.db). Paths come from the resolved --alerts-db and --analytics-db. Absent stores (memory analytics, no alert store) are skipped and listed in the manifest. config.yaml is read once, hashed and written from the same bytes.

A free-space check (at least 1.2x the source sizes) runs before each set. The set is written to `<backup-dir>/.tmp-<ts>/` (dir 0700, files 0600), manifest.json is written last with format, warden version, cpstate schema_version, the admin audit public key fingerprint, created_at, finished_at, files [{name, sha256, size}], skipped and not_included, then fsynced and renamed to `<UTC ts>Z/`.

Scheduling: next run = newest complete set time + interval, so an overdue backup runs at startup; runs never overlap; one background goroutine bound to the CP ctx, one DB at a time, never on a request path.
Pruning keeps the newest --backup-keep complete sets, never deletes the last good set, and removes .tmp dirs older than 24h.

Health: each run logs msg=cp_backup (db, bytes, duration_ms, outcome). A failure logs ERROR and publishes `backup_failed` (SevHigh, DedupKey `backup_failed:<db>`); a last success older than 2x interval publishes `backup_stale` (SevHigh). last_success_at, last_error, last_set and size_bytes are added to /dashboard/api/setup. No row contents appear in logs.

On demand: `warden control-plane backup` (refuses when a CP holds the lock from W-P1-OPS1-04 once that lands; until then it requires the CP to be stopped) and an admin-only `POST /dashboard/api/backup` that is recorded by the AAUD-02 middleware.
plan: cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the four flags and build a new controlplane.BackupConfig{Dir, Interval, Keep, Include} from the resolved state dir, alerts DB, analytics DB and served config path.

Add BackupTo methods: internal/cpstate (new method on the W-P1-SSO-01 DB type), internal/integration/store.go (Store.BackupTo) and internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go (FleetSQLiteStore.BackupTo), each with a unit test.
New internal/controlplane/backup.go: BackupRunner with Start(ctx) and RunOnce(ctx), the free-space check, the .tmp set, manifest writing, fsync and rename, anchored scheduling and pruning.
In backup.go, report failures and staleness through Server.publishFinding (from W-P1-OPS1-01 if merged, otherwise a local helper with the same ERROR-log fallback) and keep status for setup.
internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go: add the backup status fields to setupResponse; add POST /dashboard/api/backup as an admin route in the SSO-05 table.
Add the `control-plane backup` subcommand in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.
Tests in internal/controlplane/backup_test.go and cmd/proxy/commands_test.go.
acceptance: With a cpstate DB, alert store and fleet store under writes from 8 goroutines, a backup runs, every writer succeeds without SQLITE_BUSY, each copy passes PRAGMA integrity_check, and manifest sha256 and size match the files: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_ConsistentUnderWrites`
With --backup-keep=3, 5 complete sets and one .tmp dir older than 24h, pruning leaves exactly the 3 newest sets and removes the .tmp dir: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_Prune`

With the newest set 25h old and a 24h interval, starting the runner triggers a backup immediately; with --analytics-provider=memory the fleet DB is listed as skipped: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_Schedule`

With an unwritable backup dir, a run logs ERROR, the fake publisher gets one backup_failed Finding, and the CP keeps serving /policy: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_FailureRaisesFinding`
--backup-dir inside --state-dir is rejected at startup, and set dirs and files have modes 0700 and 0600: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBackupFlags`
