tickets.title: Add CP state-dir lock and verified restore command
tickets.body: Add a lifetime lock on the CP state dir and a `warden control-plane restore` command that loads a backup set from W-P1-OPS1-02. SQLite holds no lock an idle CP keeps, so a flock file is the only reliable way to refuse a restore while a CP is running, and it also stops two CPs from sharing one state dir. Restore checks hashes, integrity, schema version and the audit key before touching anything, clears stale WAL files and sessions, and records itself in the admin audit chain. Restoring an old set can bring back revoked access, so the command warns that later revocations and blocks must be re-applied.
requirements: Lock: when --state-dir is set, runControlPlane takes a non-blocking exclusive flock on `<state-dir>/warden-cp.lock` (new internal/cpstate/lock_unix.go and lock_other.go) for its lifetime and fails startup with a clear message if it is held. Token, hash-password and policy CLIs do not take it.

Command: `warden control-plane restore --from <set> --state-dir <dir> [--analytics-db] [--alerts-db] [--force] [--new-audit-key]`. It takes the same lock and exits non-zero with 'control plane is running' if held. DB targets come from the flags, mirroring the CP flags.

Checks before any write: every manifest entry's sha256 and size match ('manifest mismatch: <file>' otherwise), PRAGMA integrity_check is ok on staged copies, the set's schema_version is not above the binary's highest migration, and the target's cp-audit.key public key fingerprint matches the manifest unless --new-audit-key is passed. A non-empty target needs --force.

Apply: existing DB, -wal and -shm files and config.yaml move to `<state-dir>/pre-restore-<ts>/`; staged files are renamed into place with mode 0600; sessions and oidc_pending are emptied so earlier cookies stop working.

Audit: one admin_audit row is appended through adminaudit.Store.Append from W-P1-AAUD-01, with the key from `--admin-audit-key-file` (default `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`) and only when the admin_audit table exists (auth_method cli, action cp.restore, target = sha256 of manifest.json, plus whether --new-audit-key was used), so the chain stays valid.
Output: prints the backup timestamp and a warning that worker-token revocations, user blocks and policy versions made after that time must be re-applied. No file contents or secrets are printed.
plan: New internal/cpstate/lock_unix.go and lock_other.go: AcquireDirLock(dir) (release func(), error) using syscall.Flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB; the non-unix build returns an error naming the unsupported OS.
cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: acquire the lock in runControlPlane when --state-dir is set; make `control-plane backup` from W-P1-OPS1-02 take it too.
New cmd/proxy/restore.go: newRestoreCmd with manifest verification, staging under the target dir, integrity_check, schema and audit key checks.
In restore.go: move existing files to pre-restore-<ts>/, rename staged files into place, empty sessions and oidc_pending via cpstate, and append the cp.restore audit row.
Tests in cmd/proxy/restore_test.go covering round trip, tampered file, lock held, newer schema and audit key mismatch.
acceptance: Back up, restore into an empty state dir and start the CP: GET /policy returns the same ETag, a worker token valid at backup time authenticates, a pre-backup session cookie gets 401, and adminaudit.Verify passes with one cp.restore entry at the end: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_RoundTrip`

With one flipped byte in a backed-up .db file, restore exits non-zero with 'manifest mismatch: <file>' and the target dir is byte-for-byte unchanged: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_TamperedFile`

While a CP holds <state-dir>/warden-cp.lock, restore exits non-zero with 'control plane is running' and a second CP on the same state dir fails to start: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_RefusesWhileLocked`

A set with a newer schema_version, or a target whose cp-audit.key fingerprint differs from the manifest, is refused without changes; --new-audit-key allows the second case and the audit row records it: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_Refusals`
Stale -wal and -shm files in the target are moved to pre-restore-<ts>/ and not replayed onto the restored DB: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_StaleWAL`

name: Break-glass + backups
label: ops-hardening

summary: Adds a control-plane registry of agents so the token service knows which agents exist, which public keys authenticate them and which user groups may delegate to them. Workers receive each agent's status and key thumbprints on the existing /policy long-poll, can be pinned to a registered agent id, and deny all traffic for an agent an admin has disabled. The per-agent identity mode stays in the P1 settings field, so there is one source of truth for it.
design: Data model: new package internal/agentreg on the W-P1-SSO-01 cpstate DB, migration `agents/0001`. Table `agents(id PK, display_name, owner_iss, owner_sub, owner_email, allowed_groups_json, allowed_scopes_json, status active|disabled, revision INTEGER, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by)` plus `agent_keys(jkt PK, agent_id, kid, alg, jwk_json)`, so a key thumbprint can belong to only one agent. There is no identity_mode column and no environments column. Rows are never deleted and ids are never reused, so audit rows and token references stay resolvable. The registry holds at most `config.MaxRegisteredAgents` (1000) agents.

Agent ids: new `agentid.ValidID` with pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$`, compared case-sensitively and exactly. It accepts `agent:<port>` from agentid.PortBindingIdentifier and typical existing `agents[].id` values, and it rejects the P1 sentinel `!identity-scoped`. config.validateAgents keeps accepting any non-empty id; ids that fail ValidID only produce a warning there, so existing YAML still loads.

Keys: public keys are accepted only as JWKs and parsed with the internal/keys JWK code and RFC 7638 thumbprint from W-P2-KEYS-01, so agentreg, the token service (W-P2-TOKX-01) and workers (W-P2-WBND-02) compute the same jkt. Accepted: kty OKP/crv Ed25519 (32-byte x, alg EdDSA) and kty EC/crv P-256 (point on the curve, alg ES256). Rejected: RSA, oct, any private or symmetric member (d, p, q, dp, dq, qi, k, oth), x5u, jku and x5c. `use` must be sig and `key_ops` must be [verify] when present; alg defaults from kty/crv and must match when present. kid defaults to the thumbprint and is unique within the agent. At most 2 keys per agent (to allow rotation) and 2 KiB per JWK. Private keys are never accepted, stored or logged.

Authorization data: allowed_groups uses the same literal, case-sensitive semantics and caps as W-P1-GPOL-01 (trimmed, de-duplicated, sorted, at most 256 values of 256 bytes) and must be non-empty for an active agent. allowed_scopes replaces the old single default_scope: at most 32 values, each matching `^[a-z0-9:._-]{1,64}$`; the token service issues allowed_scopes when a request omits scope, and no scope claim when the list is empty. owner_iss/owner_sub default to the creating principal and are informational in P2: they grant no rights, and offboarding an owner does not disable the agent.

Identity mode is not stored in the registry. The per-agent mode stays in SettingsWire `agents[].identity` (W-P1-VRFY-01) with `identity.defaultMode` as the fallback, so it is versioned, rollback-able and later approvable like other settings. W-P2-WBND-03 adds `require` there. The console shows each agent's effective mode read-only, from live settings.

Store: `agentreg.Store{Get, List, Create, Update(ctx, a, expectedRevision, actor), SetStatus(ctx, id, status, expectedRevision, actor)}` with errors ErrNotFound, ErrConflict, ErrKeyInUse and a field-scoped ErrInvalid. It is a narrow interface with an exported conformance suite (`agentregtest.Run`) so the P5 Postgres store can implement it. A read-through in-memory cache, invalidated on every write, serves the token service so exchange takes no DB round trip on the hot path.

Admin API under the P1 console prefix, through a new `dashboard.SetAgentRegistry` seam like the P1 worker-token and blocked-user panels: `GET/POST /dashboard/api/agents`, `GET/PUT /dashboard/api/agents/{id}`, `POST /dashboard/api/agents/{id}/disable` and `/enable`. There is no DELETE. The routes are listed in dashboard.Routes(), so the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table, W-P1-SSO-04 CSRF and W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware apply with no new mount. Viewers read; every write is admin-only, because registering a key or widening allowed_groups decides who can mint agent-bound tokens. Writes require `If-Match: "r<revision>"` (409 `agent_conflict` when stale, 428 when missing). In `console.auth: none` writes return 403 `use_cli`; without --state-dir every route returns 503 `state_dir_required`; on workers the seam is unset and the routes return 404. With W-P2-APIK-02 these rows carry Scope agents:read (GET) and agents:write (writes), so API keys reach the same handlers; there is no /api alias. With approvals enabled, W-P2-APPR-08 holds widening writes as drafts.

Audit: Target `agents`, Actions agent.create, agent.update, agent.disable and agent.enable, and an `agents` StateHasher (HMAC over the canonical list, W-P1-AAUD-02 pattern). Details hold only changed field names, kids and groups added or removed, and status from/to; never JWK coordinates.

Worker wire: new `config.RegisteredAgent{ID, Status, JKT []string}` (json `id`, `status`, `jkt`) and `config.Policy.RegisteredAgents` (json `registeredAgents,omitempty`, not accepted in YAML), carried in policyWire and decoded through the existing remoteWire embedding. Owner, groups, scopes and JWK bodies never leave the CP. `policyServer.loadPolicy` merges the store list sorted by id, next to the W-P1-BLOCK-03 blocked-users merge. A store read error fails loadPolicy, so Refresh keeps the last-known-good wire and ETag. One exported `config.ValidateRegisteredAgents` runs in the CP write path and in parseRemotePolicy, so the CP never serves an entry that workers would reject. An empty registry keeps /policy byte-identical.

Versioning and bundles: registry data is outside policy_versions.doc_json, so a policy rollback never re-enables an agent or restores a removed key. In `--policy-store=versioned` mode an ETag change caused by a registry write appends a policy_publish_log row with reason `agent_registry` (the W-P1-PVER-05 path), so W-P2-SBND-02 bundle numbering stays monotonic; the signed bundle carries the same `registeredAgents` object.

Worker binding: a new worker-local `central.agentID` YAML key and `warden run --agent-id` flag pin the worker's agent id. Precedence is flag, then central.agentID, then the existing worker.defaultAgentID (Agents[0].ID when exactly one agent is configured, otherwise `agent:<port>`). The resolved id is used everywhere the worker uses defaultAgentID today (judge, identity mode) and for the registry lookup. The worker selects its own RegisteredAgent entry when it applies policy, so the per-request cost is one atomic load. The heartbeat body gains `agentID`, the effective `identityMode` and `caps:["agentreg/v1"]` next to the W-P1-BLOCK-02 caps, which answers the P1 question about reporting each worker's effective identity mode.

Kill switch (deny-only; it acts only after an admin disables a registered agent, so an empty registry changes nothing): when the worker's bound agent is disabled, every CONNECT, HTTP/1 request and h2 stream gets 403 `{"error":"agent_disabled"}` in every identity mode. Open sessions are closed through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry, deny events carry Reason=agent_disabled, and RecordBlocked("agent_disabled") is called. This covers the p1-block-list question about agent-kind block entries. Rejecting tokens whose act.sub is disabled or whose cnf.jkt is no longer registered belongs to W-P2-WBND-02. Default-deny and the secret swap are unchanged.

Degraded modes: while the CP is down, workers keep the last-known-good registry and never re-enable an agent on their own. Registry state survives CP restarts in SQLite. The fleet view warns when a disabled agent is still served by a worker without `agentreg/v1`, when a registered agent has no bound worker, and when a worker reports an agentID that is not registered. Registry logic does not depend on wall-clock time; created_at and updated_at are informational.

Offline CLI: `warden control-plane agent register|update|list|disable|enable --state-dir` writes through the same Store and validator and records admin audit rows with auth_method `cli`, so compose recipes, the token-service e2e test and `console.auth: none` deployments can register agents. The running CP picks up CLI writes on its existing 3s policyReloadInterval ticker.

Observability: bounded labels only. CP: `warden_cp_agents{status}` and `warden_cp_agent_registry_writes_total{action,outcome}`, kept in memory until CP metrics export lands (W-P5-RETN-06). Worker: RecordBlocked("agent_disabled") and a sessions-closed count. Logs carry agent id, kid and thumbprint prefix only, never JWK bodies or tokens.
done_when: On a CP with --state-dir, console.auth=oidc and console.adminAudit.enabled=true, and one worker started with --agent-id claude-code: an admin registers agent `claude-code` in the console with a public Ed25519 JWK and allowed group `warden-agents`, which writes exactly one admin audit row with target_ref agent:claude-code and no JWK body in the row or logs; a viewer or editor gets 403 on writes, a JWK containing `d` returns 400 and a stale If-Match returns 409; GET /policy carries `registeredAgents` with the agent's id, status and key thumbprint, the worker applies it within one long-poll cycle and reports `agentreg/v1` and its agentID on the heartbeat, and the token service can resolve the agent and key through agentreg.Store; disabling the agent makes that worker answer new and open sessions with 403 agent_disabled within one long-poll cycle in every identity mode, and this still holds after a policy rollback, a CP restart and a CP outage, while re-enabling restores traffic; a CP with an empty registry or without --state-dir serves byte-identical /policy with an unchanged ETag, and old workers decode the new wire without error.

tickets.title: Add internal/agentreg store, schema and validation
tickets.body: Create the new package internal/agentreg with the Agent type, the Store interface, a SQLite implementation on the cpstate DB, and the validators every later ticket shares. JWK parsing and RFC 7638 thumbprints come from internal/keys (W-P2-KEYS-01), so the registry, the token service and workers compute the same jkt. Nothing calls the package yet, so merging changes no behaviour.
requirements: New `agentid.ValidID(string) error` in internal/agentid with pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$`: `agent:8080` passes, `!identity-scoped`, `-x` and a 65-character id fail.

`agentreg.Agent{ID, DisplayName, OwnerIss, OwnerSub, OwnerEmail, Keys, AllowedGroups, AllowedScopes, Status, Revision, CreatedAt, CreatedBy, UpdatedAt, UpdatedBy}`, Status active|disabled, and `config.MaxRegisteredAgents` = 1000 enforced on create. There are no identity_mode or environments fields.

Key validation through the W-P2-KEYS-01 JWK parser: 1-2 keys; OKP/Ed25519 (alg EdDSA) or EC/P-256 on the curve (alg ES256); RSA, oct, d, p, q, dp, dq, qi, k, oth, x5u, jku and x5c rejected in the raw JSON; `use` sig and `key_ops` [verify] when present; at most 2 KiB per JWK; kid defaults to the thumbprint and is unique within the agent.

Field validation: allowed_groups normalized like W-P1-GPOL-01 and non-empty for an active agent; allowed_scopes at most 32 values matching `^[a-z0-9:._-]{1,64}$`; display_name at most 128 runes with no control characters. ErrInvalid carries the field path (for example `keys[0].crv`), never the value.

Migration `agents/0001` creates `agents` and `agent_keys(jkt PK, agent_id, kid, alg, jwk_json)`. Create, Update and SetStatus each run in one transaction; Update and SetStatus use `WHERE revision=?` and return ErrConflict on a stale revision; a jkt already bound to another agent returns ErrKeyInUse. There is no delete path.

`agentreg.Thumbprints(Agent) []string` is the one projection of key thumbprints used by the wire (W-P2-AREG-04) and the token service. A read-through cache, invalidated on every write, backs Get and List.
Exported conformance suite `agentregtest.Run(t, Store)` for the P5 Postgres store. Errors and logs carry id, kid and a thumbprint prefix only.
plan: internal/agentid/agentid.go: add `ValidID` (new) and table tests in agentid_test.go.
New internal/agentreg/agent.go: Agent, Status constants, errors (ErrNotFound, ErrConflict, ErrKeyInUse, field-scoped ErrInvalid) and the Store interface.

New internal/agentreg/validate.go: `Validate(Agent) (Agent, error)` that normalizes groups and scopes and checks keys with the internal/keys JWK parser and thumbprint from W-P2-KEYS-01; add `Thumbprints`.

New internal/agentreg/sqlite.go: `NewSQLiteStore(db *cpstate.DB)` with the `agents/0001` migration registered through the W-P1-SSO-01 migration list, revision compare-and-swap, the jkt uniqueness check and the MaxRegisteredAgents cap; new cache.go for the read-through cache.

Tests: JWK table tests (private member, wrong curve, RSA, alg mismatch, duplicate kid, 3 keys, x5u), RFC 7638 test vectors, and the conformance suite against the SQLite store.

Given an agent with every field set, Create then Get round-trips all fields, kid defaults to the thumbprint and Revision is 1.
Given agent A with key K, creating agent B with K returns ErrKeyInUse; Update on A with a stale revision returns ErrConflict.

tickets.title: Expose the agent registry admin API with admin-only writes and audit
tickets.body: Add the agent registry handlers to internal/dashboard behind a new `SetAgentRegistry` seam, mounted under /dashboard/api/agents like the P1 worker-token and blocked-user APIs. Listing them in dashboard.Routes() puts them behind the existing P1 session, CSRF, admin audit and authz chain, so no new middleware mount is needed. Writes are admin-only because a key or group change decides who can mint agent-bound tokens.
requirements: Routes: `GET /dashboard/api/agents` (200 list), `POST /dashboard/api/agents` (201 with Location), `GET /dashboard/api/agents/{id}` (200 or 404), `PUT /dashboard/api/agents/{id}` (200), `POST /dashboard/api/agents/{id}/disable` and `/enable` (200). There is no DELETE (405).

Authz entries in the W-P1-SSO-05 table: viewer for GET; admin for every write; Scope (W-P2-APIK-02) agents:read for GET and agents:write for writes, set by whichever of the two tickets lands second. Actions agent.create, agent.update, agent.disable, agent.enable; Target `agents`; Audited true for writes. An `agents` StateHasher is registered with the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware.

PUT, disable and enable require `If-Match: "r<revision>"`: 428 when missing, 409 `{"error":"agent_conflict"}` when stale. Duplicate id or ErrKeyInUse returns 409; validation returns 400 `{"error":"invalid_agent","field":"keys[0].crv"}`; bodies over 64 KiB return 413.

Example: `POST /dashboard/api/agents {"id":"claude-code","displayName":"Claude Code","keys":[{"kty":"OKP","crv":"Ed25519","x":"<32-byte b64url>"}],"allowedGroups":["warden-agents"]}` returns 201 `{"id":"claude-code","revision":1,"status":"active","keys":[{"kid":"<jkt>","alg":"EdDSA","jkt":"<jkt>"}],...}` with ETag `"r1"`. Views return public JWKs plus kid, alg and jkt only.

`console.auth: none`: writes return 403 `{"error":"use_cli"}`, reads are allowed. CP without --state-dir: every route returns 503 `{"error":"state_dir_required"}`. Worker dashboards never set the seam, so the routes return 404.

tickets.title: Bind workers to an agent id and enforce agent_disabled
tickets.body: Let an operator pin a worker to a registered agent id with `--agent-id` or `central.agentID`, and make a disabled agent a deny-only kill switch on that worker. The worker denies every CONNECT, request and h2 stream with 403 agent_disabled in every identity mode, and closes open sessions through the P1 session registry within one long-poll cycle. The heartbeat reports the resolved agent id, the effective identity mode and the `agentreg/v1` capability so the fleet view can flag workers that do not enforce it. This is worker-lane only; with no flag and an empty registry nothing changes.
requirements: New worker-local `central.agentID` YAML key (next to central.proxyID in internal/config/central.go) and `warden run --agent-id` flag. Precedence: flag, then central.agentID, then worker.defaultAgentID. A value that fails agentid.ValidID stops startup with a clear error. The resolved id replaces defaultAgentID everywhere (judge, identity mode lookup, registry lookup).
On every policy apply the worker selects its own RegisteredAgent entry and stores `disabled bool` in an atomic value read by the proxy; the per-request check is one atomic load with no allocation.

When the bound agent is disabled: CONNECT is answered 403 before any dial or `200 Connection Established`, HTTP/1 requests are answered in a new `agentStage` before judgeGate, and each h2 stream gets 403 in serveGRPCStream. The body is `{"error":"agent_disabled"}`; the event has Decision=deny and Reason=agent_disabled; RecordBlocked("agent_disabled") is called. `agent_disabled` is added to internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06).

After each applied policy change that disables the bound agent, the worker closes every open session (tunnels, keep-alive, h2, WebSocket) through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry, including sessions with no identity, and writes one deny event per closed session.

The heartbeat body (RemoteProvider.Heartbeat) gains `agentID`, `identityMode` (the effective P1 mode) and `agentreg/v1` in `caps`; it stays under the CP's 4096-byte limit. The CP side that stores and shows these fields is W-P2-AREG-03, so this ticket changes no CP code.
A worker never re-enables a disabled agent on its own: while the CP is unreachable it keeps the last-known-good list. Logs carry the agent id only, never thumbprints at info level.

name: Agent registry
label: agent-registry

summary: Adds an RFC 8693 token-exchange endpoint on the CP. It turns a user's IdP ID token plus an agent's private_key_jwt assertion into a short-lived Warden token (at most 15 minutes, never longer than the ID token). The token is bound to the agent, so workers trust one CP-signed token instead of verifying raw IdP tokens. Off by default; it is a CP-local `tokenService:` block and nothing changes on the wire while it is disabled.
design: Endpoint: `POST /oauth2/token` on the CP mux (`Server.Handler()` in internal/controlplane/controlplane.go). It is form-encoded, the body is capped at 32 KiB (a P1 subject token can be 16 KiB), and every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`. Parameters: grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, subject_token, subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer, client_assertion, an optional audience (only `warden-worker`, otherwise invalid_target), an optional requested_token_type (only ...:jwt or ...:access_token) and an optional scope. resource and actor_token are rejected, as are duplicate parameters, parameters in the query string and any Authorization header. `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) advertises issuer, token_endpoint, jwks_uri (the p2-key-manager `/.well-known/jwks.json`), grant_types_supported, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=[private_key_jwt] and token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported=[EdDSA, ES256].

Agent authentication (private_key_jwt) in new package internal/tokensvc, with compact-JWS helpers in new internal/keys/jws.go. The assertion is at most 8 KiB. A kid header is required and must equal a registry JWK's kid or its RFC 7638 thumbprint (agentreg.Store.Get, W-P2-AREG-01). alg is bound to the key type: EdDSA for OKP Ed25519, ES256 for EC P-256. none, HS*, RS*, mismatched algs and the jwk/jku/x5u/x5c/crit headers are rejected before any key is used. Claims: iss==sub==agent id; aud is a single value equal to `tokenService.issuer` or `<issuer>/oauth2/token`, always taken from config and never from the Host header; exp and iat are required; exp-iat <= 5m; iat and nbf are at most 60s in the future; jti is 1-128 printable characters. Replay protection uses cpstate `token_assertion_jti(agent_id, jti_hash, expires_at, PRIMARY KEY(agent_id, jti_hash))`. The row is inserted only after the signature and time checks pass, with one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and rows are purged after exp+60s. Unknown agent, unknown kid, bad signature and disabled agent all return the same 401 invalid_client. The bounded reason is kept only in logs and metrics.

Subject validation: one `identity.NewOIDCVerifier` (W-P1-VRFY-01). It is built at startup from the CP's served `identity` settings block (issuer, audience, jwksURL, groupsClaim, clockSkewSeconds, maxTokenTTLSeconds), so the CP and the workers trust the same IdP. AllowedAZP is overridden by `tokenService.allowedAZP` (default [agent-harness]), so ID tokens minted for other clients cannot be exchanged. Only Status valid continues, and `identity.SubjectFrom(claims, status)` must return a non-nil subject. expired -> invalid_grant/subject_expired; invalid, malformed or too_large -> invalid_grant/subject_invalid; unverified (jwks_unavailable) -> 503 temporarily_unavailable/idp_unavailable with Retry-After, so harnesses retry instead of re-logging in. The verifier accepts only the IdP issuer, so a Warden token can never be a subject_token and `act` is never nested.

Pluggable subject types: `Service.Exchange` dispatches on subject_token_type through a `SubjectResolver` map. A resolver returns a verified subject, a subject expiry and extra claims. P2 registers id_token; W-P4-DGR-04 later adds `urn:warden:params:token-type:grant` without rewriting Exchange. Any other type returns invalid_request/unsupported_token_type. The common checks and minting run once, after the resolver.

Authorization, in this order. (1) The agent is active (re-read after the assertion). (2) The user is not blocked: a tokensvc-owned `BlockChecker` interface, implemented in internal/controlplane over `controlplane.BlockStore` (W-P1-BLOCK-03) and its in-memory snapshot (W-P1-BLOCK-07), never over a policy version. It matches sub exactly, and lowercase email only when EmailVerified; a match gives invalid_grant/user_blocked, and a read error gives 503 temporarily_unavailable/block_store_unavailable, never an allow. (3) The subject's groups intersect the agent's allowed_groups, otherwise unauthorized_client/group_not_allowed. (4) Scope is space-delimited tokens matching `^[a-z0-9:._-]{1,64}$`, at most 16. Issued scope is the requested scope when it is a subset of the agent's allowed_scopes (W-P2-AREG-01), or all of allowed_scopes when none is requested, and no scope claim when the list is empty; anything else gives invalid_scope/scope_not_allowed. Errors use RFC 6749/8693 codes, and error_description is only a reason from a closed enum.

Issued JWT, signed with the internal/keys purpose=token active Signer (W-P2-KEYS-02). Header: alg (from Signer.Alg()), kid, typ=`wt+jwt`. Claims: ver=1, iss=tokenService.issuer, aud=warden-worker, sub, idp_iss (the subject's iss), email and email_verified (only when the email is verified), groups (sorted, as verified), groups_truncated (from Claims.GroupsTruncated), act={sub: agent id}, sid, idp_sid (when the ID token carries one), jti (128-bit crypto/rand, base64url), iat, nbf=iat, exp=min(iat+tokenService.ttl, subject exp), scope (omitted when empty), cnf={jkt: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the JWK that verified the assertion}. Tokens whose encoding would exceed 12 KiB are refused with token_too_large, which keeps them under the worker's 16 KiB cap. keys.ErrNoActiveKey gives 503 temporarily_unavailable/signer_unavailable. Response: access_token, issued_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, token_type=Bearer, expires_in=exp-iat, scope.

Token sessions: cpstate `token_sessions(sid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, idp_iss, sub, agent_id, created_at, last_used_at, revoked_at)`, unique on (idp_iss, sub, agent_id) while revoked_at IS NULL, migration id `tokensvc/0002`. This table is separate from the W-P1-SSO-04 console `sessions` table. sid is `wts_` plus 128-bit crypto/rand base64url, so no ULID dependency is needed. A sid is reused per (idp_iss, sub, agent) until it has been idle for 12h, reaches its 7d absolute lifetime, or is revoked. Admins can revoke one session (`POST /dashboard/api/token-sessions/{sid}/revoke`) or all sessions for a sub or an agent (`POST /dashboard/api/token-sessions/revoke`). These are admin-role routes in the W-P1-SSO-05 table, audited through the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware, and after a revoke the token service refuses exchanges whose subject token was issued at or before the revoke (invalid_grant/session_revoked), which forces a fresh sign-in. Live tokens are stopped by the block list, agent disable or emergency key rotation, within one bundle cycle or the TTL.

Binding semantics, documented in docs/identity-contract.md: the Warden token is a bearer token bound to the agent through act.sub and cnf.jkt, which workers (p2-worker-bound) check against the listener's agent and the registry key thumbprints. It is not proof of possession. Anyone holding the token can use it from that agent's listener until it expires, and real upstream credentials still never reach the agent. Proof of possession arrives with agent mTLS (cnf x5t#S256).

Abuse limits, applied in order. (a) A per-client-IP limiter (default 120/minute) runs before parsing; the client IP is RemoteAddr unless the peer is in console.trustedProxies, as in W-P1-AAUD-02. A global in-flight cap (default 64) also applies. (b) A per-agent bucket (default 300/minute, sized for one shared harness agent) is charged only after the assertion verifies. (c) A per-user bucket keyed on (idp_iss, sub) (default 30/minute) is charged only after the subject verifies. A forged iss therefore cannot drain a real agent's budget. All limits return 429 with an integer Retry-After. They use an exported `policy.ParseRateLimit` grammar (`N/second|minute|hour`) with token-bucket semantics, implemented in internal/tokensvc because go.mod has no golang.org/x/time. Each limiter map is LRU-bounded to 10k keys. Limits apply per CP replica.

Recording. Machine issuance stays out of the hash-chained admin audit. That chain is for admin actions, and P1 never chains requests without a session. Every authenticated outcome (issued, or denied after the assertion verified) writes a cpstate `token_events(id, ts, outcome, reason, agent_id, sub_hmac, sid, jti, kid, exp, scope)` row (migration `tokensvc/0003`; sub_hmac is HMAC-SHA256 with a per-CP salt stored in cpstate) and emits one slog JSON line `msg=token_exchange schema=warden.token.v1` with sub, agent, sid, jti, outcome and reason. If the row cannot be written, the response is 503 temporarily_unavailable/event_store_unavailable and no token is released. Unauthenticated failures write no row; they get a rate-limited WARN line and a counter. Rows are pruned after `tokenService.eventRetention` (default 720h) from the existing retention ticker in `Server.Start`. Session revokes and other admin actions go through adminaudit. subject_token, client_assertion and the issued token are never logged or stored.

Metrics: the CP has no meter or /metrics endpoint until W-P5-RETN-06. Following the W-P1-WTOK-02 pattern, a nil-safe `tokensvc.Metrics` keeps in-memory counters `warden_cp_tokens_issued_total{agent}` and `warden_cp_tokens_denied_total{reason}` and a `warden_cp_token_exchange_seconds` histogram. reason comes from the closed tokensvc enum, and agent is a registered id or `unknown`. sub and email are never labels. Totals appear in a console token-service summary until W-P5-RETN-06 exports them.

Config and back-compat: a CP-local `tokenService:` block with `json:"-"`, never on policyWire or SettingsWire. It is accepted by rawConfig under KnownFields(true) and read only from the operator `--config` through new `config.LoadTokenService`, the same pattern as `config.LoadConsole` (W-P1-SSO-02). Keys: enabled (default false), issuer (absolute https URL with no trailing slash; http only for loopback or with allowInsecureIssuer), ttl (default 15m, range 1m-15m), assertionMaxAge (5m), clockSkew (60s), allowedAZP ([agent-harness]), session {idle: 12h, absolute: 168h}, rateLimit {perIP, perAgent, perUser, maxInFlight} and eventRetention (720h). There is no CLI flag. Startup fails when the block is enabled without --state-dir, without a served `identity` issuer, or without a loadable token KeySet. When disabled, /oauth2/token and the discovery document return 404, no tokensvc tables are created, and /policy is byte-identical.

Degraded modes. No active token key (secret backend or KMS down): 503 temporarily_unavailable and /healthz degraded. IdP unreachable: the cached JWKS still verifies known kids, and an unknown kid or a cold cache gives 503 idp_unavailable. Block store or event store error: 503. A CP restart keeps replay protection and sessions because both are in cpstate, behind `tokensvc.ReplayStore` and `tokensvc.SessionStore` interfaces that p5-postgres-ha can implement. Assertions and subjects get 60s of clock skew; minted tokens get the worker's `identity.clockSkewSeconds` leeway (default 60s, W-P2-WBND-01). In require mode, a CP outage longer than the TTL minus the harness refresh lead (about 5 minutes with refresh at 2/3) stops that agent's traffic. This is documented as accepted until P5 HA.

Cross-feature contracts (now reflected in those features' tickets). p2-worker-bound: add Email, EmailVerified and IdPIss to its Principal and build identity.Subject from them, so email blocks and `users:` rules keep working in require mode; require typ=wt+jwt and ver=1; deny tokens whose act.sub agent is disabled in the bundle. p2-signed-bundles: carry `tokenIssuer`, so workers take iss from the signed bundle. p2-key-manager: mint only with a kid already in the served JWKS (on first key creation, refresh the policy server before the first mint), and read the overlap floor from tokenService.ttl. p2-agent-registry: require or derive a kid for each JWK. p2-security-tests: add the stolen-token-on-another-port and replay-after-restart cases.
done_when: On a CP with --state-dir, `tokenService.enabled: true` and an https issuer, a token key from p2-key-manager, an `identity` block that points at Dex (the p1-dex LDAP recipe), and an agent registered with a public JWK and allowed_groups: a user in an allowed group exchanges a Dex ID token (azp agent-harness) and a fresh agent assertion at POST /oauth2/token. The CP returns a typ wt+jwt token that verifies against /.well-known/jwks.json, carries the specified claims, and has exp = min(iat+15m, subject exp). Each specified invalid input (replayed jti including after a restart, alg none or HS256, an embedded-key header, wrong aud, an unknown or disabled agent, an expired or wrong-azp subject, a user blocked by sub or verified email, a user outside allowed_groups, a revoked session, an out-of-range scope or audience) gets its RFC 6749/8693 error and closed reason, and no token. Unauthenticated floods from one IP get 429 without using a real agent's budget. IdP unreachable with a cold cache, a missing token key, and a block-store error each return 503. Every authenticated outcome has a token_events row and a warden.token.v1 log line, and no token, subject_token or client_assertion appears in any row, log or label. With the service disabled the endpoint returns 404 and /policy is byte-identical.

tickets.title: Add private_key_jwt client assertion verification
tickets.body: Add compact-JWS helpers to internal/keys and `VerifyClientAssertion` in new package internal/tokensvc. The token endpoint uses them to authenticate an agent from its signed assertion against the registry JWKs. The rules are strict: alg is bound to the key type, embedded-key headers are rejected, aud comes from config, and replay is checked per agent in cpstate, so a stolen or forged assertion cannot be reused. Nothing is mounted, so behaviour does not change.
requirements: New internal/keys/jws.go: `ParseCompact(raw string) (Header, payload, signingInput, sig []byte, error)` (3 base64url segments, strict) and `SignCompact(ctx, Signer, Header, claims any) (string, error)`. Only EdDSA and ES256 (raw r||s) are allowed. none, HS*, RS*, and crit/jku/jwk/x5u/x5c headers are rejected.

`VerifyClientAssertion(ctx, raw string) (Client{AgentID, KID, JKT string}, error)` returns `*tokensvc.Error{Code: invalid_client, Reason}`. The assertion is capped at 8 KiB, iss must pass agentid.ValidID (W-P2-AREG-01) before lookup, and the clock is injected.

Key selection: kid is required and must equal a registry JWK's kid or its RFC 7638 thumbprint (agentreg.Store.Get). alg must match the key type (OKP Ed25519 -> EdDSA, EC P-256 -> ES256) and the alg stored for that key in the registry (agent_keys.alg). The signature is checked with keys.Verify.

Claims: iss==sub==agent id. aud is a single value (a string, or an array of one) equal to the configured issuer or `<issuer>/oauth2/token`; the CP never derives it from the request. exp and iat are required, exp-iat <= 5m, exp > now-60s, iat and nbf <= now+60s. jti is 1-128 printable characters. An optional form client_id must equal iss.

Replay: cpstate migration `tokensvc/0001` adds `token_assertion_jti(agent_id TEXT, jti_hash TEXT, expires_at INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(agent_id, jti_hash))` behind a `ReplayStore{Consume, Purge}` interface. The row is inserted only after the signature, time and status checks pass, using one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and RowsAffected. Only sha256(jti) is stored.

Unknown agent, unknown kid, bad signature and disabled agent all return the same invalid_client error, and an unknown agent still does a dummy verify so timing does not reveal which agent ids exist. Each case keeps its own reason (agent_unknown, unknown_kid, bad_signature, agent_disabled, replay, wrong_aud, expired, lifetime_too_long, alg_not_allowed, malformed, too_large) for logs and metrics only.

JKT is the computed RFC 7638 thumbprint of the verifying JWK (keys.Thumbprint, the same value agentreg.Thumbprints serves to workers), never the header kid. The raw assertion never appears in errors, logs or test output; jti appears only as an 8-hex hash prefix.
plan: New internal/keys/jws.go with ParseCompact/SignCompact and tests against RFC 8037 (Ed25519) and RFC 7515 (ES256) vectors plus header-rejection cases.

New internal/tokensvc/errors.go: `OAuthCode` (invalid_request, invalid_client, invalid_grant, unauthorized_client, invalid_scope, invalid_target, unsupported_grant_type, temporarily_unavailable), the closed `Reason` enum and `type Error{Code, Reason}`.
New internal/tokensvc/replay.go: `ReplayStore` interface and its SQLite implementation registering cpstate migration `tokensvc/0001` (cpstate.Migration from W-P1-SSO-01).

New internal/tokensvc/assertion.go: `AssertionVerifier{Agents agentreg.Store; Replay ReplayStore; Issuer string; Now func() time.Time; Skew, MaxAge time.Duration}` with VerifyClientAssertion in the order parse -> lookup -> alg/key -> signature -> claims -> status -> replay.
Tests in new internal/tokensvc/assertion_test.go: a table test for every reason, a -race replay test, and a purge test with a fake clock.
acceptance: Valid EdDSA and ES256 assertions return the agent id and a JKT equal to the keys thumbprint. alg none, HS256 signed with the public key bytes, RS256, an ES256 header on an Ed25519 key, a jwk or jku header, a missing kid and an unknown kid are each rejected with the matching reason: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestVerifyClientAssertion`.

Fifty goroutines submitting one valid assertion produce exactly one success and 49 replay failures, and a later sequential reuse also fails: `go test -race ./internal/tokensvc -run TestAssertionReplay`.

aud ["<issuer>","https://other"] is rejected with wrong_aud and `<issuer>/oauth2/token` is accepted. exp-iat=6m gives lifetime_too_long, iss!=sub gives wrong_iss, and exp 2m in the past gives expired: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestAssertionClaims`.
A correctly signed assertion from a disabled agent returns agent_disabled, an unknown agent returns agent_unknown, and neither inserts a token_assertion_jti row.
After the fake clock passes exp+60s, Purge removes the row, and the SQLite file contains no raw jti: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestAssertionJTIPurge`.

tickets.title: Implement token exchange policy checks and JWT minting
tickets.body: Add `Service.Exchange` in internal/tokensvc. It authenticates the agent (TOKX-01) and verifies the subject with the P1 `identity.NewOIDCVerifier` and `SubjectFrom`, accepting only status valid. It then checks the block list through `controlplane.BlockStore` (not a policy version), the agent's allowed groups and scope, and mints a typed, agent-bound JWT with the purpose=token signer. Every failure maps to a closed OAuth error, and any store or key failure fails closed. Nothing is mounted yet.
requirements: `Service.Exchange(ctx, ExchangeRequest{ClientAssertion, SubjectToken, SubjectTokenType, Scope, Audience, RequestedTokenType}) (*Issued, error)` dispatches on subject_token_type through a `SubjectResolver` map (id_token in P2; W-P4-DGR-04 adds grant). Unknown types give invalid_request/unsupported_token_type, and an audience other than warden-worker gives invalid_target.

Subject: an identity.Verifier built with identity.NewOIDCVerifier from the served `identity` settings, with AllowedAZP set to tokenService.allowedAZP (default [agent-harness]). Only Status valid with a non-nil identity.SubjectFrom continues. expired -> invalid_grant/subject_expired; invalid -> invalid_grant/subject_invalid; unverified -> temporarily_unavailable/idp_unavailable.

Block list: a tokensvc-owned `BlockChecker{IsBlocked(ctx, sub, email string) (bool, error)}`, with the adapter in new internal/controlplane/blockchecker.go over controlplane.BlockStore and the W-P1-BLOCK-07 snapshot (tokensvc never imports controlplane). Sub matches exactly; lowercase email matches only when EmailVerified. A match gives invalid_grant/user_blocked, and a read error gives temporarily_unavailable/block_store_unavailable.

Agent and scope: re-read the agent and require status active. Subject groups intersect allowed_groups, otherwise unauthorized_client/group_not_allowed. Scope grammar `^[a-z0-9:._-]{1,64}$`, at most 16 tokens, and a subset of the agent's allowed_scopes (an omitted scope gives allowed_scopes; an empty list gives no scope claim), otherwise invalid_scope/scope_not_allowed.

Minting with keys.SignCompact and the KeySet active signer. Header {alg, kid, typ: wt+jwt}. Claims ver=1, iss, aud=warden-worker, sub, idp_iss, email and email_verified (verified only), groups, groups_truncated, act.sub, sid, idp_sid (when present), jti (128-bit random), iat, nbf=iat, exp=min(iat+ttl, subject exp), scope and cnf.jkt, in a new `identity.WardenClaims` type that W-P2-WBND-01 can reuse. Tokens over 12 KiB give token_too_large, and keys.ErrNoActiveKey gives temporarily_unavailable/signer_unavailable. It mints only with a kid already present in the token JWKS the policy server last served (bundle `tokenJWKS` section and /.well-known/jwks.json); on first key creation the CP refreshes the policy server before the first mint.

Sessions: cpstate migration `tokensvc/0002` adds `token_sessions(sid PK, idp_iss, sub, agent_id, created_at, last_used_at, revoked_at)` (not the W-P1-SSO-04 `sessions` table) behind `SessionStore{Touch, Revoke, RevokeAll, Purge}`. The sid is `wts_` plus 128-bit base64url, reused within 12h idle and 7d absolute. After a revoke, a subject token issued at or before revoked_at gives invalid_grant/session_revoked, and a later one starts a new sid.
Exchange p99 is at most 25ms with a warm JWKS. Issued carries only the token plus {sub, agent, sid, jti, kid, exp, scope}; no subject_token, assertion or minted token is logged.
plan: New internal/tokensvc/service.go: `Config`, `Service{assertions, resolvers map[string]SubjectResolver, agents, blocks BlockChecker, keys *keys.KeySet, sessions SessionStore, now, rand}`, and Exchange running request checks -> assertion -> resolver -> agent -> block -> groups -> scope -> session -> mint.
New internal/tokensvc/subject_idtoken.go: the id_token SubjectResolver over identity.Verifier.Verify and identity.SubjectFrom, with the status-to-error mapping.
New internal/identity/wardenclaims.go: the `WardenClaims` struct and its JSON encoding, shared with the worker verifier.
New internal/tokensvc/sessions.go: the SQLite SessionStore and migration `tokensvc/0002`.
New internal/controlplane/blockchecker.go: the adapter from BlockStore to tokensvc.BlockChecker (not wired yet).
Tests in new internal/tokensvc/service_test.go using fakes.Verifier, a fixed clock and a seeded random source, with a golden file at internal/tokensvc/testdata/issued_golden.json.
acceptance: With a fixed clock, a fixed Ed25519 signer and fakes.Verifier, the minted header and claims equal internal/tokensvc/testdata/issued_golden.json, and the signature verifies with keys.Verify: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeGoldenClaims`.

A user blocked by sub, and a user blocked by an email-only entry with a verified email, both get invalid_grant/user_blocked. An unverified email does not match, and a BlockChecker error gives temporarily_unavailable with no token: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeBlockedUser`.

No group intersection gives unauthorized_client, scope `admin` outside allowed_scopes gives invalid_scope, an omitted scope yields allowed_scopes, and audience=`other` gives invalid_target: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeAuthorization`.
An expired subject, a wrong azp, an unverified status and ErrNoActiveKey each give the mapped error, and no token is minted: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeSubjectAndSignerFailures`.

A subject that expires in 5m yields exp equal to the subject exp and ExpiresIn 300. The same (idp_iss, sub, agent) within 12h keeps its sid, gets a new one after 12h+1s idle, gets session_revoked after Revoke for a subject issued before it, and a new sid for a subject issued after it: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeSessionID`.

tickets.title: Mount POST /oauth2/token with RFC 8693 request parsing and config
tickets.body: Add the CP-local `tokenService:` config block and the HTTP handler that exposes Service.Exchange at `POST /oauth2/token`, plus RFC 8414 discovery metadata so harnesses do not hard-code the endpoint. The route sits outside the console session, CSRF and worker-token middleware and is classified in the W-P1-SSO-05 route table. With the block absent or disabled, both routes return 404 and nothing else changes. There is no CLI flag; the config key is the only switch.
requirements: Config: new internal/config/tokenservice.go `TokenServiceConfig` on `Policy.TokenService` with `json:"-"`, accepted by rawConfig under KnownFields(true), and new `config.LoadTokenService(path)` called on `--config` (the LoadConsole pattern). Keys and defaults as in the feature design: enabled false, issuer, ttl 15m (1m-15m), assertionMaxAge 5m, clockSkew 60s, allowedAZP [agent-harness], session {idle 12h, absolute 168h}, rateLimit {perIP "120/minute", perAgent "300/minute", perUser "30/minute", maxInFlight 64} with each rate in the `N/second|minute|hour` grammar of policy.ParseRateLimit, and eventRetention 720h.

Validation: when enabled, issuer is required and must be an absolute https URL with no trailing slash (http only for loopback or allowInsecureIssuer, which logs a warning). Startup fails with an actionable error without --state-dir, without a served `identity` issuer, when `keys.enabled` is false or the token KeySet cannot load, or when `keys.token.overlap` is below ttl + 2m (worker skew plus one long-poll). One INFO line logs enabled, issuer and ttl.

Route: `POST /oauth2/token` is registered in Server.Handler only when the service is built (otherwise 404); other methods get 405 with Allow: POST. It is outside dash.Handler, CSRF and WorkerAuthenticator, and is classified in the W-P1-SSO-05/AAUD-02 route table as assertion-authenticated with Audited:false. Session cookies and `wwt_` or `wak_` (apikeys.LooksLikeKey) bearers are never accepted as client auth; any Authorization header is rejected with invalid_request.

Parsing: only application/x-www-form-urlencoded, http.MaxBytesReader at 32 KiB, no query-string parameters, no duplicate parameters, no Authorization header. grant_type must be token-exchange (otherwise unsupported_grant_type) and client_assertion_type must be jwt-bearer (otherwise invalid_client). actor_token and resource give invalid_request.

Responses: JSON {error, error_description=reason}. 400 for invalid_request, invalid_grant, unauthorized_client, invalid_scope, invalid_target and unsupported_grant_type; 401 for invalid_client; 503 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After. Every response has Content-Type application/json, Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache. Success is 200 {access_token, issued_token_type, token_type: Bearer, expires_in = exp-iat, scope when non-empty}.

Discovery: `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` returns issuer, token_endpoint, jwks_uri, grant_types_supported, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported [private_key_jwt] and token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported [EdDSA, ES256], only when enabled.
Back-compat: when disabled, the route set, /policy bytes and every existing response are unchanged, and no tokensvc migrations run.
plan: New internal/config/tokenservice.go with TokenServiceConfig, defaults, validation and LoadTokenService; extend rawConfig and add TestTokenServiceNotOnWire and TestWritersPreserveTokenServiceBlock.
New internal/controlplane/tokenservice.go: `(s *Server) handleToken` and `handleASMetadata`, with the tokensvc.Error -> HTTP mapping.

internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add `Config.Tokens *tokensvc.Service` and mount both routes in Server.Handler() when it is non-nil; add the routes to the authz route table in internal/controlplane/authz.go (W-P1-SSO-05).

cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: when tokenService.enabled, build identity.NewOIDCVerifier from the served identity settings, the token KeySet from the shared keys.Manager (controlplane.Config.Keys, W-P2-KEYS-02), the agentreg SQLite store, the BlockChecker adapter and tokensvc.New, and register the tokensvc migrations with cpstate.Open.
Tests: new internal/controlplane/tokenservice_test.go with a fake Service, internal/config tests, and a cmd/proxy startup test.
acceptance: grant_type=password returns 400 unsupported_grant_type. A JSON Content-Type, query-string parameters and a duplicate subject_token each return 400 invalid_request, and GET returns 405 with Allow: POST: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEndpointRequestValidation`.

With a fake Service that succeeds, the response is 200 with Cache-Control: no-store, Pragma: no-cache, expires_in equal to exp-iat, issued_token_type jwt and token_type Bearer: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEndpointSuccess`.

Every tokensvc error code maps to its documented status, 503 responses carry Retry-After, and error_description contains only enum reasons. A 33 KiB body returns 400 without calling the Service, and a valid console session cookie with no client_assertion returns 401 invalid_client: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEndpointErrorMapping`.

With tokenService absent or enabled=false, POST /oauth2/token and the discovery URL return 404 and /policy is byte-identical. ttl 16m and a non-loopback http issuer are rejected at load, and enabling without --state-dir fails startup: `go test ./internal/config -run TestTokenServiceConfig` and `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneTokenService`.

The discovery document lists token_endpoint `<issuer>/oauth2/token` and the private_key_jwt method, and the route-table coverage test passes: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestASMetadata|TestAuthzRouteCoverage'`.

tickets.title: Add rate limits, issuance records and metrics for token exchange
tickets.body: Add the three-stage rate limits, so an unauthenticated caller cannot drain a real agent's or user's budget, and record every authenticated outcome in a prunable cpstate table plus a `warden.token.v1` JSON line. Issuance stays out of the hash-chained admin audit, because P1 never chains requests without a session and machine traffic would flood the admin chain. Recording fails closed: if the row cannot be written, no token is released.
requirements: Export `policy.ParseRateLimit` from internal/policy/policy.go (grammar unchanged, `N/second|minute|hour`) with a test. New internal/tokensvc/ratelimit.go: a token-bucket `Limiter.Allow(key, now) (ok bool, retryAfter time.Duration)` with a 10k-key LRU and idle eviction.

Order: the per-client-IP limiter (default 120/minute; client IP from RemoteAddr or console.trustedProxies as in W-P1-AAUD-02) and the maxInFlight cap (default 64) run in handleToken before parsing. The per-agent limiter (default 300/minute) runs inside Exchange after the assertion verifies, and the per-user limiter on (idp_iss, sub) (default 30/minute) after the subject verifies. A limit hit gives 429 {"error":"rate_limited"} with integer Retry-After.

Records: cpstate migration `tokensvc/0003` adds `token_events(id, ts, outcome, reason, agent_id, sub_hmac, sid, jti, kid, exp, scope)`. sub_hmac is HMAC-SHA256 with a per-CP random salt stored in cpstate. A row is written for every issuance and for every denial after the assertion verified, before the response is sent.

If the row write fails, return 503 temporarily_unavailable/event_store_unavailable and release no token. Rows older than tokenService.eventRetention (default 720h) are pruned, together with expired token_assertion_jti and token_sessions rows, from the retention ticker in Server.Start.

Each recorded outcome also emits one slog JSON line `msg=token_exchange schema=warden.token.v1` with sub, agent, sid, jti, kid, outcome, reason and exp. Unauthenticated failures write no row; they get a WARN line rate-limited to once per reason and client IP per minute, and a counter.
Nothing in rows, logs or labels contains subject_token, client_assertion, the issued token, the Authorization header or the group list.

Metrics: a nil-safe tokensvc.Metrics with in-memory counters `warden_cp_tokens_issued_total{agent}` and `warden_cp_tokens_denied_total{reason}` and a `warden_cp_token_exchange_seconds` histogram, following W-P1-WTOK-02. reason is the closed enum and agent is a registered id or `unknown`. They are exported when W-P5-RETN-06 adds the CP /metrics endpoint.

The closed tokensvc Reason enum is exactly: malformed, too_large, alg_not_allowed, unknown_kid, bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, expired, lifetime_too_long, replay, agent_unknown, agent_disabled, unsupported_token_type, invalid_target, subject_invalid, subject_expired, idp_unavailable, user_blocked, block_store_unavailable, group_not_allowed, scope_not_allowed, session_revoked, token_too_large, signer_unavailable, event_store_unavailable and rate_limited. It is the label set of warden_cp_tokens_denied_total and token_events.reason, is listed in docs/token-service.md, and p2-security-tests pins it.
plan: internal/policy/policy.go: rename parseRateLimit to ParseRateLimit and update its callers; add a test in internal/policy/policy_test.go.
New internal/tokensvc/ratelimit.go and ratelimit_test.go with the token bucket and LRU.
internal/tokensvc/service.go: add the `Limiter` hooks after VerifyClientAssertion and after subject resolution, and a `Recorder` interface called before Exchange returns.
New internal/tokensvc/events.go: the SQLite Recorder (migration `tokensvc/0003`), the salt, the slog emitter and Purge. New internal/tokensvc/metrics.go.
internal/controlplane/tokenservice.go: the pre-auth IP limiter and in-flight cap. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: call the tokensvc Purge methods from the retention ticker in Server.Start.
Tests in internal/tokensvc and internal/controlplane, using a fake clock and canary token strings.
acceptance: With perAgent 30/minute, the 31st verified exchange for one agent within a minute returns 429 with Retry-After >= 1, and one more request succeeds after 2s on the fake clock: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestRateLimitBuckets`.

200 requests from one IP with forged assertions claiming agent A get 429 after the 120th, and a genuine request for agent A from another IP still returns 200: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenRateLimitForgedAgentNoDoS`.

One successful and one group_not_allowed exchange each write exactly one token_events row and one warden.token.v1 line, and write no admin_audit row. 100 bad-signature requests write zero rows and raise the bad_signature counter by 100: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEventsRecorded`.
Canary strings for subject_token, client_assertion and the minted token appear in no row, slog output or metric label: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenEventsNoLeak`.
With the event store forced to fail, a valid exchange returns 503 and the body has no access_token: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeEventStoreFailClosed`.
The set of denied-counter reasons equals the tokensvc Reason enum: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestMetricReasonsBounded`.

tickets.title: Add token service end-to-end integration test
tickets.body: Prove the exchange end to end under the integration build tag. By default it uses the in-process OIDC issuer from W-P1-VRFY-05, so CI needs no Docker; with WARDEN_IT_DEX=1 it uses the W-P1-DEX-02 recipe and its seeded LDAP users. The test reuses the existing Dex clients and does not change Dex config. It covers the happy path, the main denials, replay after a CP restart, revocation and the IdP-down 503.
