tickets.title: Add admin revocation for token sessions
tickets.body: Add admin routes that revoke one token session, or all sessions for a user or an agent, so the key-rotation runbook (W-P2-KEYS-05) and incident response have a real 'revoke sessions' step. After a revoke the token service refuses further exchanges for that session; live tokens still expire within the TTL. The routes are admin-only and audited through the P1 admin audit middleware.
requirements: `POST /dashboard/api/token-sessions/{sid}/revoke` returns 204, or 404 for an unknown sid. `POST /dashboard/api/token-sessions/revoke` with {sub?, idp_iss?, agent_id?} (at least one field) returns 200 {revoked: n}. Both call SessionStore.Revoke or RevokeAll (W-P2-TOKX-02).
`GET /dashboard/api/token-sessions?agent_id=&sub=` (admin) lists sid, agent_id, created_at, last_used_at and revoked_at, at most 200 per page.

The routes are in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table as admin-only, Scope ScopeNone (W-P2-APIK-02) and Audited:true, with target `token_sessions` and target_ref `sid:<sid>` or the filter. Editors and viewers get 403, and without --state-dir or with the service disabled the routes return 404.

A revoke sets revoked_at and never deletes the row. Exchanges whose subject token was issued at or before revoked_at get invalid_grant/session_revoked, so the user must sign in again. A subject token issued after the revoke starts a new sid.
No token value is shown or logged; the sid is not a credential.
plan: New internal/controlplane/tokensessions.go with the three handlers over tokensvc.SessionStore.
Register the routes in Server.Handler() when the token service is enabled and add them to internal/controlplane/authz.go.
Tests in new internal/controlplane/tokensessions_test.go for role checks, audit rows and the follow-up exchange.
acceptance: An admin revoke returns 204 and writes one admin_audit row with target token_sessions. An editor gets 403: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestTokenSessionRevoke`.
After a revoke, Exchange for that session returns invalid_grant/session_revoked: `go test ./internal/tokensvc -run TestExchangeSessionID`.
Revoke-all by agent_id revokes only that agent's sessions, and the response count matches.
With tokenService disabled, every /dashboard/api/token-sessions route returns 404.

name: Token service
label: token-exchange

summary: Adds a default-off signing-key subsystem to the control plane that owns the keys the CP signs Warden tokens and policy bundles with, and stores the worker CA key. Keys carry an RFC 7638 kid, are kept in a CP-only key store that workers can never read, rotate with a pre-published next key and an overlap window, and token keys are published as a JWKS. It also adds the supported rotation path for the P1 admin audit key.
design: Scope and gate: CP only. A new CP-local `keys:` block (`json:"-"`, read only from the operator `--config` by a new `config.LoadKeys(path)`, like `console:` in W-P1-SSO-02, never on policyWire or SettingsWire) with `enabled: false` by default. `enabled: true` requires `--state-dir` (cpstate, W-P1-SSO-01). When disabled no table, key files, goroutines or routes are created and the CP behaves as today. Token service (p2-token-service) and signed bundles (p2-signed-bundles) fail startup with an actionable error if they are enabled while `keys.enabled` is false. Workers never run this code.

New package internal/keys holds the one signing interface: `type Signer interface { KID() string; Alg() string; Public() crypto.PublicKey; Sign(ctx context.Context, signingInput []byte) ([]byte, error) }`. Sign takes the full JWS signing input; Ed25519 signs it directly and ES256 hashes it with SHA-256 and returns JOSE raw r||s (64 bytes, never DER). Algorithms: EdDSA (Ed25519, default) and ES256 (P-256), stdlib only. p5-kms adds backends behind this same interface; it does not define a second one.

kid is the RFC 7638 thumbprint itself (base64url, no padding, SHA-256 over the canonical required members), exported as `keys.Thumbprint(JWK)` for TOKX cnf.jkt and the agent registry. `keys.ParseJWK` accepts only public OKP/Ed25519 and EC/P-256 keys (rejects `d`, other curves, bad lengths, off-curve points). `keys.Verify(jwk, alg, signingInput, sig)` rejects none, HS*, RS* and any alg that does not match the key type or jwk.alg.

Purposes: `token` (scheduled rotation, published in JWKS and the bundle jwks), `bundle` (manual rotation only, EdDSA only because W-P2-SBND-03 pins EdDSA keys, public keys pinned on workers out of band and never served by URL) and `ca` (store only, for the W-P2-WCA-01 intermediate key: no JWKS, no schedule, never auto-generated; `warden control-plane ca init|csr` imports it through `Manager.ImportKey`). Each key belongs to one purpose, so a token key can never verify a bundle. The name `audit` is reserved; the admin audit key stays in internal/adminaudit.

Private key store seam `keys.PrivateKeyStore` (Put, Get, Delete, List). Backend `file` is the default: PKCS#8 PEM at `<dir>/<purpose>/<kid>.pem`, dir 0700, file 0600, O_CREATE|O_EXCL plus fsync, where `keys.store.file.dir` defaults to `<state-dir>/keys` and can point at a separate secret mount. Backend `aws` (W-P2-KEYS-07) uses secrets.NewAWSSecretStore with a CP-local `keys.store.aws.{region, namePrefix}` (default `warden-cp-keys/`) and env or IMDS credentials only. It never reuses the `secretStore` block that is sent to workers, startup fails if its namePrefix overlaps `secretStore.aws.namePrefix` in either direction, and echo or env backends are rejected.

Metadata in cpstate migration `signing_keys/0001`: `signing_keys(kid PK, purpose, alg, state, public_jwk, store_backend, created_at, publish_at, activate_at, retire_at, destroyed_at, created_by)`, states next|active|retired|revoked|destroyed, with partial unique indexes allowing at most one active and one next row per purpose. Private bytes never enter the DB. Write order: generate, Put, Get back and compare the public key, then INSERT the row inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE; material with no row is swept and logged at startup. JWKS and bundle jwks are built from public_jwk rows only.

Lifecycle: state only moves forward (next, active, retired, destroyed; or revoked in an emergency), computed from stored timestamps on the CP clock and written as compare-and-swap UPDATEs, so the scheduler, the console and the CLI never race and a restart applies missed transitions in order. A `next` key is always kept published, so a rotation promotes a key verifiers already hold. When a key retires its private material is deleted at once (it no longer signs); its public JWK stays published until retire_at + overlap, then the row becomes destroyed. Other-process writes are picked up by polling `PRAGMA data_version` every 2s, as in W-P1-WTOK-01.

Timing settings under `keys.token` and `keys.bundle`: `rotationInterval` (token 720h, bundle 0 = manual), `prepublish` (default 1h, min 10m: covers the 60s maxLongPollWait plus the 300s JWKS cache with margin) and `overlap` (retired window, default 48h, min 20m: at least 15m token TTL + 60s worker `identity.clockSkewSeconds` + 60s long-poll; W-P2-TOKX-03 also refuses startup when `keys.token.overlap` is below `tokenService.ttl` + 2m). A next key cannot activate before publish_at + prepublish except in an emergency. rotationInterval must be 0 or at least prepublish + overlap. `keys.bundle.rotationInterval` must be 0, because workers pin bundle keys; bundle rotation is the staged `--stage`/`--activate` flow of W-P2-SBND-07, which checks heartbeat pinnedKids (W-P2-SBND-05) before it calls Rotate with ConfirmPinned. The block shape `keys.<purpose>.*` is what p5-kms extends with `backend`/`keyRef`.

Emergency rotation (`emergency: true` / `--emergency`) promotes next at once, marks the old kid revoked (out of JWKS and the next bundle immediately, private key deleted), and fires `KeySet.Subscribe` so W-P2-SBND-02 rebuilds the bundle and wakes long-poll waiters. Tokens signed by the old kid fail once verifiers refresh, within one bundle long-poll for workers and one 300s JWKS cache period for harnesses.

Endpoints: `GET /.well-known/jwks.json` on the CP mux next to /healthz, public, outside withSession, the authz table, the admin audit middleware and worker auth. It serves token keys in states next, active and retired-within-overlap with public members only, precomputed bytes, `Content-Type: application/jwk-set+json`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` and ETag = quoted base64url sha256 of the body (304 on If-None-Match). `GET /dashboard/api/keys` (admin) and `POST /dashboard/api/keys/rotate` (admin, X-Warden-CSRF, Audited) go through a new `dashboard.SetKeysSource` seam and the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table.

Degraded modes: /healthz stays pure liveness. A new `GET /readyz` returns 503 `{"keys":"no_active_key"}` only when keys are enabled and a purpose has no loaded active key (W-P5-RETN-06 later adds store and KMS checks to it). If material cannot be loaded, the CP still starts and serves /policy, signing returns `keys.ErrNoActiveKey` (token endpoint 503, no new bundle so workers keep last-known-good), a `signing_key_unavailable` Finding is published, and loading retries with backoff from 1s to 60s. It never generates a replacement when rows exist. Loaded keys sit in memory behind an atomic.Pointer, so a later backend outage only blocks rotation; a failed rotation keeps the current key and raises `key_rotation_failed`, and an active key older than 2x the interval raises `key_overdue`.

Audit and observability: every generate, activate, retire, revoke, destroy and rotate request goes through the optional adminaudit.Recorder (W-P1-AAUD-01) with actions keys.*, target `keys:<purpose>`, target_ref `kid:<kid>` and auth_method system, oidc, breakglass or cli; a `keys_transition` slog line with kid, purpose and state is always written. Key material never appears in logs, rows, API responses, errors or backups. In-memory counters `warden_cp_key_transitions_total{purpose,to}`, `warden_cp_key_sign_errors_total{purpose}` and gauge `warden_cp_key_active_age_seconds{purpose}` are added to the W-P5-RETN-06 export list. Sign is CPU only and off every worker path.

Ops: `warden control-plane keys list|rotate|export|reset` works against cpstate and the key store directly, like W-P1-WTOK-05; list, rotate and export run with or without a running CP, and `reset` (replace a purpose's keys after a restore that lost material) refuses while the W-P1-OPS1-04 lock is held. The W-P1-OPS1-02 manifest lists the file key dir under not_included, and restore warns when live rows have no readable material. The admin key routes are ScopeNone for API keys in P2 (W-P2-APIK-02), so the CLI works on the state dir only.

Admin audit key rotation (carry-forward from p1-admin-audit): `warden control-plane admin-audit rotate-key` (offline, takes the state-dir lock) appends an `audit.key_rotated` entry signed by the old key naming the new key_id and public key, then switches the key file. adminaudit.Verify, VerifyExport, the AAUD-01 startup check and the OPS1-04 restore fingerprint check accept a key change only at such an entry. A dedicated command is used instead of a startup flag so a restart can never rotate the key. This is the supported admin-audit key rotation; P1 ships a single key with only the documented manual new-segment procedure (W-P1-AAUD-01/04), and chains containing those `audit.segment_start` entries keep verifying.
done_when: On a CP started with --state-dir and `keys.enabled: true` using the default file store, the CP creates one active and one next key for token and bundle, restarts keep the same kids, and /.well-known/jwks.json returns only public members for the token keys with an ETag and 304 on revalidation. No private key bytes appear in warden-cp.db, logs, admin audit rows, API responses or a P1 backup set; with `keys.store.backend: aws` startup is refused when the keys namePrefix overlaps the worker secretStore namePrefix. A test drill signs a JWS every simulated second and verifies each against JWKS snapshots cached for 5 minutes across a scheduled rotation (fake clock) and a console rotation with zero failures; an emergency rotation removes the old kid from JWKS at once; bundle Rotate is refused without ConfirmPinned (set only by the W-P2-SBND-07 `--activate` pin check or `--force`). With the key store unreadable at startup the CP still serves /policy and /healthz, /readyz reports no_active_key, signing returns ErrNoActiveKey, and signing recovers without a restart once the store returns. After `admin-audit rotate-key`, `warden control-plane admin-audit verify` passes across the key change. With `keys.enabled` false the CP is unchanged.

tickets.title: Add internal/keys Signer, JWK and RFC 7638 kid helpers
tickets.body: Create new package internal/keys with the Signer interface, local Ed25519 and ES256 signers, PKCS#8 helpers, a public-only JWK type with strict parsing, the RFC 7638 thumbprint used as kid, and a Verify helper. W-P2-TOKX-01, W-P2-SBND-01 and W-P2-AREG-01 reuse these instead of writing their own JOSE code. It is a library with no wiring, so merging changes no behaviour. internal/audit's receipt Signer is not changed.
requirements: `type Signer interface { KID() string; Alg() string; Public() crypto.PublicKey; Sign(ctx context.Context, signingInput []byte) ([]byte, error) }`, constants AlgEdDSA and AlgES256, and errors ErrNoActiveKey, ErrUnsupportedAlg, ErrAlgMismatch and ErrBadSignature. Stdlib only; no new go.mod dependency.
`GenerateLocal(alg)`, `NewLocalSigner(crypto.Signer)`, `MarshalPKCS8PEM` and `ParsePKCS8PEM`; any key that is not Ed25519 or P-256 is rejected. Sign is safe for concurrent use and does no I/O.
Ed25519 signs the signing input directly. ES256 signs the SHA-256 digest and returns fixed 32+32 byte r||s; DER is never returned and Verify rejects it.

kid = RFC 7638 thumbprint: base64url without padding of SHA-256 over the canonical members (crv, kty, x for OKP; crv, kty, x, y for EC), with no second hash. `Thumbprint(JWK) (string, error)` is exported.

`JWK{Kty, Crv, X, Y, Kid, Alg, Use}` has no field for `d`. `ParseJWK([]byte)` rejects a `d` member, kty other than OKP/EC, crv other than Ed25519/P-256, wrong coordinate lengths, off-curve points and an alg that does not match the key type.
`Verify(jwk JWK, alg string, signingInput, sig []byte) error` requires alg to match the key type and jwk.alg when set, and rejects none, HS*, RS* and anything else with a typed error.
The local signer implements String, GoString and slog.LogValuer to show only {kid, alg}; errors never include key bytes; the package does not log.
Benchmarks BenchmarkSignEd25519, BenchmarkSignES256 and BenchmarkVerify; Ed25519 Sign stays under 100µs per op.
plan: Create internal/keys/signer.go (new): the Signer interface, alg constants and error values.
Create internal/keys/local.go (new): LocalSigner, GenerateLocal, NewLocalSigner, the ES256 r||s encoder, PKCS#8 PEM helpers and the redacting String/GoString/LogValue methods.
Create internal/keys/jwk.go (new): JWK and JWKS types, PublicJWK(pub, alg), (JWK).PublicKey(), ParseJWK and Thumbprint.
Create internal/keys/verify.go (new): Verify with the alg allowlist and key-type match.

Add internal/keys/keys_test.go (new): round trips, tamper cases, RFC 8037 Appendix A.3 thumbprint vector, a pinned P-256 golden kid, DER rejection, ParseJWK rejection table, JSON shape and redaction tests, FuzzParseJWK and the benchmarks.
acceptance: Given fresh Ed25519 and ES256 signers, sign then Verify with the public JWK succeeds, and flipping one byte of input or signature returns ErrBadSignature: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestSignVerifyRoundTrip`

Thumbprint of the RFC 8037 Appendix A Ed25519 public key equals `kPrK_qmxVWaYVA9wwBF6Iuo3vVzz7TxHCTwXBygrS4k`, and a fixed P-256 key matches its pinned golden kid: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestThumbprint`
ES256 signatures are exactly 64 bytes and the same signature re-encoded as DER fails Verify: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestES256JOSEEncoding`
JWKs with `d`, crv P-384, kty RSA, a 31-byte x, an off-curve point, or alg HS256 or none are each rejected with a typed error: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestParseJWKRejects`

A marshalled Ed25519 JWK has kty=OKP, crv=Ed25519, use=sig, alg=EdDSA and kid and no `d`, and formatting the signer with %v, %#v or slog shows no key bytes: `go test ./internal/keys -run 'TestJWKMarshal|TestSignerRedaction'`
`go test -race ./internal/keys ./internal/audit` passes with the receipt tests unchanged.

tickets.title: Add the keys config gate, file key store and signing_keys metadata
tickets.body: Add the default-off CP-local `keys:` block, the `keys.PrivateKeyStore` seam with the default file backend, the cpstate `signing_keys/0001` migration and `KeySet` loading for the token, bundle and ca purposes. Private keys live only in the key store and the DB holds public metadata, so JWKS never needs the backend. The existing secrets.SecretStore is not used: echo persists nothing, env has no store, and the AWS block is shared with workers. With `keys.enabled` false nothing is created.
requirements: Config: `keys.enabled` (default false), `keys.store.backend` (file only in this ticket; aws arrives in W-P2-KEYS-07; echo and env rejected), `keys.store.file.dir` (default `<state-dir>/keys`), and `keys.token.alg` / `keys.bundle.alg` (bundle must be EdDSA for W-P2-SBND-03 pins). The field on Policy has `json:"-"`; `config.LoadKeys(path)` reads it only from `--config`. enabled without --state-dir is a startup error.
File backend: `<dir>/<purpose>/<kid>.pem`, PKCS#8 PEM, dir 0700, file 0600, O_CREATE|O_EXCL plus fsync. The same seam serves purpose `ca` for W-P2-WCA-01.

Migration `signing_keys/0001` with kid PK, purpose, alg, state (next|active|retired|revoked|destroyed), public_jwk, store_backend, created_at, publish_at, activate_at, retire_at, destroyed_at, created_by, and partial unique indexes for one active and one next row per purpose.

Write order: generate, Put, Get back and compare public keys, then INSERT inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE; on insert failure the material is deleted best-effort. Startup sweeps material with no row and logs kid and purpose only.

`LoadKeySet(ctx, purpose)` creates the first active key and a next key only when the purpose has zero rows. When rows exist but active material is missing or unparsable it never generates a key: Sign returns ErrNoActiveKey, a `signing_key_unavailable` Finding is published and loading retries with 1s to 60s backoff. The CP keeps serving /policy and /healthz.
`KeySet.Active(purpose)` reads an atomic.Pointer snapshot; Sign never touches the DB or store.

Generation writes a `keys.generated` entry through the optional adminaudit.Recorder (auth_method system, target `keys:<purpose>`, target_ref `kid:<kid>`) and always a `keys_loaded` slog line; PEM, seeds and key bytes are never logged.

Purpose `ca` is never auto-generated, scheduled or loaded into a KeySet. `Manager.ImportKey(ctx, purpose, crypto.Signer, actor)` stores externally created material (used by W-P2-WCA-01 `ca init|csr`) with an active signing_keys row, and `Manager.Signer(ctx, "ca")` loads it; LoadKeySet runs only for token and bundle.
plan: Add internal/config/keys.go (new): KeysConfig types, defaults, validateKeys and LoadKeys(path); add `Keys *rawKeys yaml:"keys"` to rawConfig in internal/config/config.go and `Policy.Keys` with `json:"-"`.
Create internal/keys/store.go (new): the PrivateKeyStore interface and fileStore.
Create internal/keys/meta.go (new): the `signing_keys/0001` migration, MetaStore over *cpstate.DB with List, Insert and CAS UpdateState in BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
Create internal/keys/manager.go (new): Manager, KeySet snapshot, LoadKeySet, the orphan sweep and the background reload with backoff.

In cmd/proxy/controlplane.go runControlPlane, when keys are enabled, register the migration with cpstate.Open, build the store and Manager, and pass a new `controlplane.Config.Keys *keys.Manager` field (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go); nil when disabled.
Tests: internal/config/keys_test.go, internal/keys/manager_test.go and a disabled-path case in cmd/proxy/commands_test.go.
acceptance: Given a CP state dir with the file backend, a restart keeps the same active and next kids and creates no extra rows: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestKeyStoreReloadSameKID`
Searching warden-cp.db, its -wal file and captured logs for the PEM body and raw seed finds neither: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestNoPrivateKeyInStateDB`

Given existing rows and a store whose Get fails, the CP starts, Sign returns ErrNoActiveKey, no new row is created, GET /policy returns 200, a signing_key_unavailable Finding is published, and signing works once Get recovers without a restart: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestKeysBackendDownAtStartup`
Two goroutines calling LoadKeySet on an empty state dir produce exactly one active and one next row per purpose, key files 0600 and dirs 0700: `go test -race ./internal/keys -run TestFirstKeyRace`
Config with backend echo, bundle alg ES256, or enabled without --state-dir fails naming the field: `go test ./internal/config -run TestKeysConfig`
With keys.enabled false, no keys dir or signing_keys table exists and existing tests pass: `go test ./cmd/proxy ./internal/controlplane`

tickets.title: Implement per-purpose rotation with prepublish and overlap windows
tickets.body: Add the rotation state machine and the 1-minute scheduler, started in Server.Start next to the retention pruner. Token keys rotate on a schedule; bundle keys rotate only by hand because workers pin them in `controlPlane.bundleKeys`. A next key is always published before it activates, and separate prepublish and overlap windows cover key propagation and token lifetime. Transitions are compare-and-swap writes so the scheduler, console and CLI cannot fork the state.
requirements: Settings under `keys.token` and `keys.bundle`: `rotationInterval` (token 720h, bundle 0 = manual), `prepublish` (default 1h, min 10m) and `overlap` (default 48h, min 20m). rotationInterval must be 0 or at least prepublish + overlap, and `keys.bundle.rotationInterval` must be 0 (bundle keys are pinned on workers, W-P2-SBND-07); violations fail config load naming the field.

`(*Manager).Rotate(ctx, purpose, RotateOpts{Emergency, ConfirmPinned bool; Actor})` promotes the next key to active (never before publish_at + prepublish unless Emergency), moves the old active to retired, deletes its private material, and creates a new next key. For bundle, Rotate without ConfirmPinned returns ErrBundleNotPinned.
Emergency marks the old active revoked (out of JWKS and bundle jwks at once, material deleted) and promotes next immediately. Retired keys become destroyed at retire_at + overlap.

State moves only forward, is derived from stored timestamps, and every transition is one CAS UPDATE in BEGIN IMMEDIATE. After downtime the scheduler applies missed transitions in order and never leaves two active keys.

`KeySet.JWKS(purpose)` returns next, active and retired-within-overlap keys; `KeySet.Subscribe(func(purpose string))` fires once per transition so W-P2-SBND-02 can rebuild the bundle and wake long-poll waiters. Writes from other processes are picked up by polling `PRAGMA data_version` every 2s; a reload error keeps the last good set.

Each transition writes keys.activated, keys.retired, keys.revoked, keys.destroyed or keys.generated through the optional Recorder (auth_method system for the scheduler) and a `keys_transition` slog line. A failed rotation keeps the current key and raises `key_rotation_failed`; an active token key older than 2x the interval raises `key_overdue`.
In-memory counters `warden_cp_key_transitions_total{purpose,to}`, `warden_cp_key_sign_errors_total{purpose}` and gauge `warden_cp_key_active_age_seconds{purpose}`; labels never include kid.
plan: Extend internal/config/keys.go with the per-purpose timing fields, defaults and validation; add cases to internal/config/keys_test.go.
Create internal/keys/rotate.go (new): a pure `plan(now, rows, cfg) []transition`, Rotate with RotateOpts, and the CAS apply loop.
Add JWKS(purpose), Version() and Subscribe to KeySet in internal/keys/manager.go, plus the data_version poller and the counters.
In internal/controlplane/controlplane.go Server.Start, when s.cfg.Keys is non-nil, start s.cfg.Keys.Run(ctx) next to the retention pruner block.
Publish key_rotation_failed and key_overdue Findings through the existing CP findings path.
Add internal/keys/rotate_test.go (new) with a fake clock and two Managers on one DB.
acceptance: With a fake clock, interval 720h and prepublish 1h, the next kid is in the token JWKS before activation and signing switches kid at 720h: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestRotationSchedule`

A token signed just before rotation verifies against every JWKS snapshot taken each minute until 16m later, and a retired key leaves JWKS only after overlap with its material deleted at retirement: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestRotationNoVerifyGap`
Bundle with interval 0 never rotates on its own, and Rotate for bundle without ConfirmPinned returns ErrBundleNotPinned: `go test ./internal/keys -run TestBundleManualRotation`
Overlap 19m, prepublish 9m, or an interval shorter than prepublish + overlap fails config load naming the field: `go test ./internal/config -run TestKeysConfigValidation`

Two Managers on one DB rotating concurrently under -race end with one active and one next key, and a Manager reloads within 3s after the other rotates: `go test -race ./internal/keys -run 'TestRotateCAS|TestReloadOnDataVersion'`

After a simulated three-interval downtime, restart leaves exactly one active key per purpose, and each transition writes one audit row with auth_method system and fires Subscribe once: `go test ./internal/keys -run 'TestCatchUp|TestRotationAudit'`

tickets.title: Serve the token JWKS, readiness and admin key API from the control plane
tickets.body: Mount the public `GET /.well-known/jwks.json` for token keys, a `GET /readyz` that reports missing keys without touching /healthz, and admin-only `GET /dashboard/api/keys` and `POST /dashboard/api/keys/rotate` through the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table. The JWKS bytes are precomputed on every key change so the public route does no I/O. Bundle public keys are shown to admins for pinning but never served on a public URL.
requirements: `GET /.well-known/jwks.json` sits outside withSession, the authz table, the admin audit middleware and worker auth; GET and HEAD only, other methods 405. It returns 404 when keys are disabled and 503 `{"error":"signing_unavailable"}` when enabled with no published token key.

The body is `{"keys":[...]}` with token keys in next, active and retired-within-overlap states, members kty, crv, x, y, kid, alg and use only. Headers `Content-Type: application/jwk-set+json`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`, ETag = quoted base64url sha256 of the body; matching If-None-Match gives 304.
`GET /readyz` (new) returns 200, or 503 `{"keys":"no_active_key"}` when keys are enabled and any purpose lacks a loaded active key. /healthz is unchanged.
`GET /dashboard/api/keys` (admin, Audited:false) returns kid, purpose, alg, state, timestamps, backend and public JWK per key plus per-purpose {loaded, lastError}; never private material.

`POST /dashboard/api/keys/rotate {purpose, emergency, confirmPinned}` (admin, X-Warden-CSRF, Audited:true, Action keys.rotate_requested, Target `keys:<purpose>`) calls Manager.Rotate with the session actor. With console.auth none it returns 403 pointing to the CLI. Purpose bundle returns 409 `use_cli`, because bundle rotation is staged through the CLI (W-P2-SBND-07).
Routes are added through a new `dashboard.SetKeysSource` seam and to `dashboard.Routes()` and the authz table; workers and CPs without the seam return 404.

name: Key manager
label: key-management

summary: Adds short-lived mTLS client certificates for workers, issued by a CP-held worker intermediate CA that is separate from the proxy MITM CA. Workers enroll once with a `wet_` enrollment token (single-use, or prefix-bound and multi-use for replica pools), renew on their own, and are cut off by revoking their certs on the CP. Cert auth extends the P1 WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest; P1 `wwt_` tokens keep working until the operator opts in to `--require-worker-certs`.
design: Scope: CP and worker. Cert principals are accepted only on the worker-plane routes /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, plus the new /control/enroll and /control/renew. /central/secrets, /dashboard/* and /auth/* stay human-only and never accept a worker cert or a `wwt_` token (W-P1-SSO-06, W-P1-WTOK-02). The `/oauth2/token` route comes from p2-token-service and is not touched here.

Separate trust root: the worker CA is its own root and intermediate (intermediate CA:true, MaxPathLen 0, KeyUsage certSign, URI name constraint for the trust domain). Client certs are verified only against the pinned Warden worker intermediates (`workerCA.certFile`, plus an optional `workerCA.previousCertFile` during rotation), never against an operator root and never against --ca-cert. Startup fails if a worker intermediate has the same SPKI as, or chains to, the proxy MITM CA or the --ca-cert used by MintServerTLS (internal/controlplane/tls.go), because compose workers hold proxy-ca.key.

CP-local config block `workerCA` (`json:"-"`, read only from --config like the W-P1-SSO-02 console block, never served on /policy): `enabled` (default false), `trustDomain` (required when enabled, lowercase DNS name), `certFile`, `previousCertFile`, `certTTL` (default 24h, 1h-7d), `enrollTokenTTL` (default 1h), `enrollTokenMaxTTL` (default 24h, at most 7d), `keySource` (`keys` default | `file`), `keyFile`.

CA key custody: internal/workerca only receives a crypto.Signer, so p5-kms can later supply `keys.ca`. With keySource=keys (the default, which requires `keys.enabled`) the PKCS#8 key is stored through `keys.PrivateKeyStore` under purpose `ca` (`<keys.store.file.dir>/ca/<kid>.pem`, or the aws store ref `ca/<kid>` under the CP-only `keys.store.aws.namePrefix`; metadata in signing_keys) by `Manager.ImportKey`, and purpose ca is never auto-generated or rotated on a schedule, because a new key needs a new intermediate signed by the root (W-P2-KEYS-02). keySource=file reads a 0600 key file outside --state-dir and logs a dev-only warning. The key store is separate from the worker-facing secretStore, so no policy placeholder can reach it; W-P2-WCA-07 also reserves the `cp/` secret namespace as defense in depth. The key never enters the cpstate DB, logs or errors.

Issuance: `CA.Issue(csr, workerID, ttl)` checks the CSR self-signature and accepts only ECDSA P-256 or Ed25519 keys. It ignores every CSR subject, SAN and extension and sets exactly one URI SAN `spiffe://<trustDomain>/warden/worker/<id>`, EKU clientAuth only, KeyUsage digitalSignature, IsCA=false, a 128-bit random serial, NotBefore now-5m and NotAfter min(now+ttl, intermediate NotAfter). Worker ids use the P1 proxy_id rule `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`.

Data model (cpstate migrations behind `EnrollmentTokenStore` and `WorkerCertStore` interfaces so p5-postgres-ha can implement them): `worker_enroll_tokens(id 'et_'+16hex, name UNIQUE, token_hash UNIQUE sha256, worker_id NULL, worker_id_prefix NULL, max_uses default 1, uses, created_by, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at, revoked_by)` with exactly one of worker_id and worker_id_prefix set; `worker_certs(serial PK, worker_id, spki_sha256, issuer_kid, prev_serial, enroll_token_id, issued_via enroll|renew, issued_at, not_after, revoked_at, revoked_by, revoke_reason)`. Rows 30 days past not_after are pruned.

Enrollment tokens: `wet_` plus lowercase unpadded base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes, stored only as sha256, visibly distinct from `wwt_`. A token is bound to one worker id, or to a worker id prefix with max_uses up to 100 for replica pools and Kubernetes pods; the enrolling worker then sends a suffix (default its hostname) and the id is prefix+suffix. Offline CLI `warden control-plane enroll-token create|list|revoke --state-dir` (with `--from-env`/`--from-file` import, mirroring W-P1-WTOK-05) and admin API `GET/POST /dashboard/api/worker-enrollments`, `DELETE /dashboard/api/worker-enrollments/{id}` (admin role, audited; 403 pointing to the CLI when console.auth=none).

POST /control/enroll {token, csr, workerIdSuffix?}: no session or client cert, body capped at 16 KiB, rate-limited to 10 per minute per remote address and per token id (429). One BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction checks the token by hash, increments uses, issues the cert, inserts worker_certs and appends the `worker.enrolled` admin-audit entry. Unknown, used-up, expired and revoked tokens all get the same 401 `unauthorized` body; the reason goes only to a rate-limited log line.

POST /control/renew {csr}: authenticated by the current verified, unrevoked, unexpired cert. The CSR must carry a new key (SPKI differs from the current cert). Renew is allowed from the worker's latest serial; a retry from the previous serial is accepted only within 10 minutes of the successor's issue and only if this CP has not yet seen the successor on a request. Any other renew from a superseded serial revokes the worker and records `worker.cert_lineage_conflict`, which catches a cloned key. Renewals are logged and counted, not admin-audited.

CP auth: W-P1-WTOK-02 WorkerPrincipal gains Kind `cert` with CertSerial, SpiffeID and NotAfter. When workerCA.enabled and TLS is on, the listener sets ClientAuth=tls.RequestClientCert, and the authenticator verifies on every request: x509.Verify with Roots = the pinned intermediates from an atomically swappable pool and KeyUsages clientAuth, the SAN shape, NotAfter against the CP clock (covers keep-alive and long-poll connections) and an in-memory revoked-serial and revoked-worker index (one map read, no DB I/O). A presented cert decides the outcome: an invalid one gets 401 and never falls back to the bearer. The P1 X-Warden-Proxy-ID binding applies (mismatch 403), and the registry and AggregatedEvent.ProxyID use the cert's worker id.

Auth modes extend the P1 resolver: with workerCA.enabled, open and mixed modes also accept cert principals and strict (`--require-worker-tokens`) accepts cert or `wwt_`. The new opt-in flag `--require-worker-certs` logs `auth_mode=strict-certs` and accepts certs only; it fails startup without --state-dir, TLS or workerCA.enabled, or together with --legacy-token-env or --require-worker-tokens. No default changes for upgraded CPs; removing P1 tokens is left to a later phase.

Revocation is CP-only and is not shipped in the signed bundle, because workers never verify other workers' certs. `POST /dashboard/api/workers/{id}/revoke` (admin, audited `worker.revoked`) and `warden control-plane worker revoke --id` set revoked_at on every unexpired serial of the worker, revoke its outstanding id-bound enrollment tokens and block later renewals. The in-memory index is rebuilt in-process, or within 2s through the P1 `PRAGMA data_version` poll for CLI writes; a reload error keeps the last good index. Held /policy long-polls for the worker are cancelled through the P1 cancel registry and return 401 within 1s.

Worker client: new `controlPlane.stateDir` (0700), the one worker state directory with a subdirectory per use: `cert/` for this feature and `bundle/` for the W-P2-SBND-06 cache and `controlPlane.enrollment.{tokenEnv, workerIdSuffixEnv}`. The worker generates a P-256 key itself (PKCS#8, 0600, O_EXCL), enrolls with a client that presents no cert, writes the cert atomically (temp file plus rename), and on restart reuses an unexpired persisted cert without contacting the CP. One shared *http.Client whose GetClientCertificate reads an atomic.Pointer cert serves config.RemoteProvider and analytics.HTTPRemoteStore, and no Authorization header is sent once a cert is loaded. Startup fails if `central.proxyID` is set and disagrees with the cert's worker id.

Renewal and degraded modes: renew at 50% of the cert lifetime ±10% jitter, measured with the monotonic clock from when the cert was received, so worker clock skew does not move it; retry with capped exponential backoff (5s to 5m). With the 24h default this tolerates a CP outage of about 12h. An expired cert gets no grace: the worker keeps enforcing its last-known-good default-deny policy, reports not-ready and logs an error. If the CA key cannot be loaded at CP startup, the CP still verifies existing certs (that needs only the public intermediate), returns 503 on enroll and renew, retries the load every 30s and reports degraded on /healthz. Behind an ingress or load balancer, worker mTLS needs TLS passthrough; forwarded client-cert headers are never trusted.

Observability: worker metrics `warden_worker_cert_expiry_seconds` and `warden_worker_cert_renewals_total{outcome}`; in-memory CP counters `warden_cp_worker_auth_total{kind=cert,outcome}`, `warden_cp_worker_enroll_total{outcome}` and `warden_cp_worker_cert_revoked_total` with bounded labels and no worker ids, exported when W-P5-RETN-06 adds the CP metrics endpoint. dashboard.WorkerView gains authKind=cert, certSerial and certNotAfter. A CP Finding fires when a worker's cert has under 25% of its lifetime left. No token, key, CSR or hash appears in logs, errors or audit rows.
done_when: Done when a CP running with --state-dir, TLS and `workerCA.enabled` (intermediate separate from the proxy CA) shows all of these: a fresh worker enrolls with a one-time `wet_` token and a two-replica pool enrolls with one prefix-bound multi-use token; each worker runs past 24h renewing on its own, and a restart reuses the persisted cert without re-enrolling; revoking a worker in the console or CLI makes its next /policy, heartbeat, ingest or renew request return 401 (held long-polls at once, CLI revokes within 2s) while other workers keep working and the revoked worker keeps its last-known-good default-deny policy; certs from a foreign CA or the proxy CA, expired certs and renews from a superseded serial are rejected; with --require-worker-certs the CP rejects `wwt_` and legacy tokens on worker routes, and worker certs are never accepted on /central/secrets or /dashboard/*; token creation, enrollment and revocation appear in the admin audit log; and the compose control-plane recipe comes up with enrollment and strict certs only.

tickets.title: Add internal/workerca intermediate CA, workerCA config and ca init
tickets.body: Create new package internal/workerca that issues short-lived worker client certs from a CP-held intermediate, plus the CP-local `workerCA` config block and the `warden control-plane ca init|csr` commands. The worker CA must be a separate trust root from the proxy MITM CA, because compose workers hold proxy-ca.key and could otherwise mint certs for any worker. Nothing loads unless `workerCA.enabled: true`, so merging changes no behaviour.
requirements: New `workerca.New(Options{Chain []*x509.Certificate, Previous []*x509.Certificate, Signer crypto.Signer, TrustDomain string, Clock func() time.Time}) (*CA, error)` and `(*CA).Issue(csr *x509.CertificateRequest, workerID string, ttl time.Duration) (*x509.Certificate, error)`. Issue checks the CSR signature, accepts only ECDSA P-256 or Ed25519 keys, ignores every CSR subject, SAN and extension, and sets exactly one URI SAN `spiffe://<trustDomain>/warden/worker/<workerID>`, EKU clientAuth only, KeyUsage digitalSignature, IsCA=false, a 128-bit random serial, NotBefore now-5m and NotAfter min(now+ttl, intermediate NotAfter). Typed errors: ErrUnsupportedKey, ErrBadCSR, ErrInvalidWorkerID.

workerID must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$` (the P1 proxy_id rule). `workerca.WorkerIDFromCert(cert, trustDomain)` returns the id only when there is exactly one URI SAN with scheme spiffe, the configured host and the path prefix `/warden/worker/`.

New CP-local `workerCA` block in internal/config (`json:"-"`, read only from --config like the W-P1-SSO-02 console block): enabled (default false), trustDomain (required when enabled), certFile, previousCertFile, certTTL (default 24h, 1h-7d), enrollTokenTTL (default 1h), enrollTokenMaxTTL (default 24h, at most 7d), keySource (keys|file, default keys), keyFile. Invalid values fail config load naming the key.

Key custody: keySource=keys loads the key with `keys.Manager.Signer(ctx, "ca")` (W-P2-KEYS-02 PrivateKeyStore, purpose ca, never auto-generated or rotated); keySource=keys while `keys.enabled` is false fails startup naming `workerCA.keySource`. keySource=file needs mode 0600 and a path outside --state-dir, and logs one dev-only WARN. workerca receives only a crypto.Signer.

Startup checks: the intermediate is CA:true with MaxPathLen 0 and certSign, its public key matches the signer, and its SPKI neither equals nor chains to the --ca-cert used by controlplane.MintServerTLS; any failure exits non-zero before listening. An expired intermediate fails startup; under 30 days left logs a WARN with not_after. If the key backend is unreachable, the CP starts in a degraded CA state (enroll and renew get 503, /healthz reports degraded) and retries the load every 30s.

`warden control-plane ca init --out-dir D --trust-domain T [--key-source keys|file] [--force]` creates a P-256 root (10y, root.key written to D at 0600 with a warning to move it offline) and an intermediate (1y, MaxPathLen 0, PermittedURIDomains [T]), writes intermediate-chain.pem, and stores the intermediate key in the key source (Manager.ImportKey for keySource=keys). It never reads the proxy CA and refuses to overwrite existing files or keys without --force. `ca csr` generates the intermediate key in the key source and prints a CSR for an offline root.
CP startup logs one line with worker_ca=enabled, trust_domain, intermediate subject, not_after and key_source. Private keys, PEM blocks and CSR bytes never appear in logs, errors or test output.
plan: New internal/workerca/ca.go: CA, New, Issue, typed errors, and the min(now+ttl, intermediate NotAfter) rule; inject the clock for tests.
New internal/workerca/spiffe.go: SPIFFEID(trustDomain, workerID) and WorkerIDFromCert.

New internal/workerca/pem.go: chain and PKCS#8 parsing (own copy, since controlplane.loadCA in internal/controlplane/tls.go is unexported and importing controlplane would create a cycle), plus SPKI comparison helpers.

New internal/config/workerca.go: WorkerCAConfig with defaults and validation, and `Policy.WorkerCA` with `json:"-"`; accept the `workerCA:` key in rawConfig so workers and the served copy still parse.

cmd/proxy/controlplane.go runControlPlane: new resolveWorkerCA that loads the chain, checks it against --ca-cert, loads the signer (keys.Manager purpose `ca` or keyFile) and passes a new `controlplane.Config.WorkerCA *workerca.CA` field; add the degraded-load retry loop.
New cmd/proxy/controlplane_ca.go: newControlPlaneCACmd() with `init` and `csr`, registered under newControlPlaneCmd().

Tests: new internal/workerca/ca_test.go (key types, CSR SAN injection, NotAfter cap, Verify against an intermediate-only pool with KeyUsages clientAuth), internal/config workerCA validation tests, and cmd/proxy TestControlPlaneCAInit and TestResolveWorkerCA (keys disabled rejected, proxy-CA intermediate rejected, warden-cp.db holds no key).
acceptance: Given a P-256 CSR that requests DNS SAN `evil.example`, URI SAN `spiffe://other/x` and CN `admin`, Issue(csr, "worker-1", 24h) returns a cert with no DNS SAN, exactly one URI `spiffe://<td>/warden/worker/worker-1`, EKU [clientAuth], NotBefore = now-5m and NotAfter = now+24h on a fake clock, and it verifies against a pool holding only the intermediate.

CSRs with RSA-2048, RSA-1024 or P-384 keys or a broken self-signature return ErrUnsupportedKey or ErrBadCSR, and workerID `../x` returns ErrInvalidWorkerID; when the intermediate expires in 2h, a 24h request gets NotAfter equal to the intermediate's NotAfter.

A CP with workerCA.enabled and keySource=keys while keys.enabled is false, or with an intermediate whose SPKI equals the --ca-cert, exits non-zero before listening with an error naming the key or flag.

`warden control-plane ca init --out-dir D --trust-domain warden.local --key-source file` creates 0600 key files, a second run without --force fails, and scanning --state-dir for the key DER finds nothing.
Without a workerCA block, existing CP tests pass unchanged: `go test ./cmd/proxy ./internal/controlplane`.

`go test -race ./internal/workerca ./internal/config -run 'TestIssue|TestCSRValidation|TestIntermediateChecks|TestWorkerCAConfig'` and `go test ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestControlPlaneCAInit|TestResolveWorkerCA'` pass.

tickets.title: Add enrollment token store, POST /control/enroll and enroll-token CLI
tickets.body: Add the cpstate tables for enrollment tokens and issued worker certs, the unauthenticated `POST /control/enroll` endpoint that trades a `wet_` token and a CSR for a cert, and the offline `warden control-plane enroll-token` CLI. Tokens can be bound to one worker id or, for replica pools and Kubernetes pods, to an id prefix with a use limit. The route is mounted only when workerCA.enabled and --state-dir are set. The admin API and console panel are W-P2-WCA-08.
requirements: cpstate migrations `worker_enroll_tokens` and `worker_certs` as in the feature design, behind new `EnrollmentTokenStore` and `WorkerCertStore` interfaces in internal/controlplane. Tokens are `wet_` plus lowercase unpadded base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes, ids `et_` plus 16 hex, and only sha256 is stored. Lookup uses an in-memory hash index reloaded on the P1 `PRAGMA data_version` 2s poll, like WorkerTokenStore.

Create takes a worker id or a worker id prefix, max_uses (default 1; up to 100, only with a prefix) and a TTL (default workerCA.enrollTokenTTL, at most enrollTokenMaxTTL). For a prefix token the worker sends `workerIdSuffix`, and the final id prefix+suffix must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`.

`POST /control/enroll` takes JSON {token, csr (PEM), workerIdSuffix?} with the body capped at 16 KiB. Responses: 201 {workerId, spiffeId, certificate, chain, serial, notAfter}; 400 for a bad CSR or suffix (checked before the token is consumed); 401 `unauthorized` with an identical body for unknown, used-up, expired or revoked tokens; 429 above 10 requests per minute per remote address or per token id; 503 when the CA key is unavailable.

Redeem runs in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction: look up by hash, check expiry, uses and revocation, increment uses, call CA.Issue, insert the worker_certs row (issued_via=enroll) and append the `worker.enrolled` entry through the adminaudit Recorder (actor `enroll:<token id>`, target `worker:<id>`, details {token_id, serial}). /control/enroll is outside the session, CSRF and W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware and is classified in the route-coverage test.

Offline CLI `warden control-plane enroll-token create (--worker-id ID | --worker-id-prefix P) [--max-uses N] [--expires-in D] [--from-env VAR | --from-file F] [--out F] --state-dir D`, plus `list [--json]` and `revoke --id`, following W-P1-WTOK-05: plaintext printed once or written to --out at 0600, re-importing the same name and value is a no-op, and create and revoke append an admin-audit row with auth_method `cli`.

In-memory counter `warden_cp_worker_enroll_total{outcome=ok|bad_token|bad_csr|rate_limited|ca_unavailable}`. Rejections log `worker enroll rejected` with reason, token_id when known and remote_addr, at most once per reason and remote address per minute. No row, log line or error holds the token, its hash or the CSR.

tickets.title: Add worker enrollment, auto-renew and cert-based CP client
tickets.body: Add the worker side: a state dir, enrollment with a `wet_` token, persisted key and cert, a renewer that keeps the cert fresh, and one shared CP HTTP client that presents the cert on /policy, heartbeat and ingest. This ticket also owns plugging the cert into config.RemoteProvider and analytics.HTTPRemoteStore, so the feature can finish without waiting on p2-worker-bound. Nothing changes unless `controlPlane.enrollment` or `controlPlane.clientCert` is set.
requirements: New worker config in internal/config/controlplane.go (rawControlPlane and ControlPlaneConfig): `controlPlane.stateDir` (created 0700; added by whichever of this ticket and W-P2-SBND-06 lands first; this ticket uses its `cert/` subdirectory, created 0700), `controlPlane.enrollment.tokenEnv`, `controlPlane.enrollment.workerIdSuffixEnv` (default: hostname), and optional `controlPlane.clientCert`/`clientKey` for certs issued outside Warden. stateDir is required when enrollment is set; enrollment and clientCert are mutually exclusive.

Enroller: load `<stateDir>/cert/worker-key.pem` (PKCS#8, 0600) and `<stateDir>/cert/worker-cert.pem`; if missing or expired and a token is set, generate a P-256 key (O_EXCL), POST /control/enroll with a client that presents no cert, and write the cert atomically (temp file, fsync, rename). An unexpired persisted cert is reused without contacting the CP. The token is read from env once and never logged.

Renewer: an atomic.Pointer[tls.Certificate] swapped after each renewal. Renewal fires at 50% of the lifetime ±10% jitter, measured with the monotonic clock from when the cert was received, POSTs a fresh-key CSR to /control/renew with the current cert, persists, swaps and calls Transport.CloseIdleConnections. Failures retry with exponential backoff from 5s to a 5m cap.

Shared client: one *http.Client per worker, built in internal/worker/wiring.go from newControlPlaneHTTPClient, whose tls.Config.GetClientCertificate reads the atomic cert and returns an empty certificate once it has expired. config.RemoteProvider and analytics.HTTPRemoteStore use it, and no Authorization header is sent once a cert is loaded.
Identity: the worker id comes from the cert SAN; if `central.proxyID` is set and differs, startup fails naming both keys. X-Warden-Proxy-ID is sent with the cert's id.

Fail-closed: a worker that has never enrolled and cannot reach the CP stays in today's fail-closed default-deny state and retries with backoff. A worker whose cert expires keeps enforcing its last-known-good policy, reports not-ready, and logs ERROR `worker cert expired` at most once per hour.

Metrics in internal/observability: `warden_worker_cert_expiry_seconds` (gauge) and `warden_worker_cert_renewals_total{outcome}`. The heartbeat body gains certSerial and certNotAfter. Keys, PEM and the token never appear in logs.

New internal/workerca/renew.go: Renewer with Run(ctx), Current() and GetClientCertificate(*tls.CertificateRequestInfo), using an injectable clock and jitter source.

Tests: internal/workerca/client_test.go and renew_test.go against an httptest TLS CP fake; internal/worker wiring test that an unset config builds no enroller and still sends the bearer.

tickets.title: Accept worker certs in WorkerAuthenticator and add /control/renew
tickets.body: Extend the P1 WorkerAuthenticator with a cert principal on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, add the opt-in `--require-worker-certs` mode, and add the cert-authenticated `POST /control/renew` endpoint. Verification happens per request in the authenticator, not in the TLS handshake, so bad certs get a uniform 401, keep-alive connections see expiry, and the pool can be swapped for intermediate rotation. /central/secrets stays human-only and never accepts a worker cert.
requirements: When workerCA.enabled and TLS are on, cmd/proxy sets ClientAuth=tls.RequestClientCert on the tls.Config from controlplane.MintServerTLS. workerCA.enabled without --ca-cert/--ca-key fails startup.

WorkerPrincipal (W-P1-WTOK-02) gains Kind `cert` with CertSerial, SpiffeID and NotAfter; ProxyID is the SAN worker id. The authenticator checks x509.Verify with Roots = pinned intermediates only (atomic pool) and KeyUsages clientAuth, the SAN shape via workerca.WorkerIDFromCert, NotAfter against the CP clock, and the in-memory revoked-serial and revoked-worker index. A presented but invalid cert gets 401 `unauthorized` with no fallback to the bearer.
Applied only to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest. A request carrying only a worker cert gets 401 on /central/secrets for every method, and /dashboard/* never consults the client cert.

Binding follows P1: a missing X-Warden-Proxy-ID resolves to the cert id; a different header gets 403 `proxy id mismatch`. The registry, AggregatedEvent.ProxyID and ingest callbacks use principal.ProxyID, and dashboard.WorkerView shows authKind=cert, certSerial and certNotAfter.

Modes: with workerCA.enabled, open and mixed accept cert principals and `--require-worker-tokens` accepts cert or `wwt_`. New flag `--require-worker-certs` (default false) logs `auth_mode=strict-certs` and accepts certs only; it fails startup without --state-dir, TLS or workerCA.enabled, or with --legacy-token-env or --require-worker-tokens.

`POST /control/renew` {csr}: needs a cert principal, a CSR with a new SPKI, and the latest serial for that worker (or the previous serial within 10 minutes of the successor's issue if this CP has not seen the successor); otherwise it revokes the worker and records `worker.cert_lineage_conflict` through the adminaudit Recorder. It issues through CA.Issue with the same id, inserts worker_certs with issued_via=renew and prev_serial, and allows at most one renew per worker per 10 minutes (429).

Hot path: no DB I/O; target under 20µs/op for a cached verify plus index read. The revoked index is rebuilt in-process and reloaded on the 2s `PRAGMA data_version` poll, keeping the last good index on error. Counters `warden_cp_worker_auth_total{kind=cert,outcome}`; rejections are logged rate-limited with reason (bad_chain|bad_eku|bad_san|expired|revoked) and serial when known.

/control/renew returns a new serial with prev_serial set; a renew from a superseded serial whose successor has been seen revokes the worker and its next /policy gets 401.

tickets.title: Implement worker cert revocation in the console and CLI
tickets.body: Add the admin revoke route, the offline CLI and the pruning that remove a worker's access by revoking its certs. Revocation is enforced only on the CP through the in-memory index, and held long-polls are cancelled so the worker is cut off at once; nothing is shipped in the signed bundle because workers never verify other workers' certs.
requirements: `WorkerCertStore.RevokeWorker(ctx, workerID, actor, reason)` sets revoked_at, revoked_by and revoke_reason on every unexpired cert of the worker and revokes its unused id-bound enrollment tokens in one transaction; it is idempotent and returns ErrNotFound for an unknown id. Later renewals for that worker are refused; re-enrolling needs a new admin-issued token.

`POST /dashboard/api/workers/{id}/revoke` (optional body {serial} to revoke one cert) returns 200 {revoked: n} or 404, with an admin entry in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table, Action `worker.revoked`, Target `worker_certs`, Scope workers:admin (W-P2-APIK-02) and Audited:true for the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware, and `adminaudit.Annotate` details {worker_id, count}.

`warden control-plane worker revoke --id ID [--serial S] --state-dir D` writes the same rows and an admin-audit row with auth_method `cli`; a running CP enforces it within 2s through the data_version reload.

An in-process revoke updates the index synchronously and cancels the worker's held /policy long-polls through the P1 cancel registry so they return 401 within 1s. The worker's next /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest or /control/renew gets 401, and it keeps its last-known-good default-deny policy.

tickets.title: Reserve the cp/ secret namespace from workers and /central/secrets
tickets.body: Reserve the `cp/` logical key namespace in the worker-facing secret store as defense in depth. Signing keys and the worker CA key live in the separate keys.PrivateKeyStore (W-P2-KEYS-02 and W-P2-KEYS-07), which no placeholder can reach, but no CP-only material may ever be added under the shared secretStore names. Today secrets.storeFetcher uses a policy placeholder directly as the store key, so a policy editor could add an auth entry whose placeholder names a CP key and have a worker inject it into an upstream request; /central/secrets could also list, overwrite or delete it. This guard is unconditional because it only rejects keys that no worker or human route should ever reach.
