name: Worker CA (mTLS)
label: worker-mtls

summary: The CP signs what it serves on GET /policy with a dedicated bundle key, and workers that pin that key apply a policy only after checking its signature, sequence number and expiry. A compromised network path, a CP replica serving stale data, or a replayed old bundle can then no longer change what a pinned worker enforces. None of this exists today: /policy serves an unsigned policyWire with a content-hash ETag (internal/controlplane/policyserver.go), and RemoteProvider applies it without verification (internal/config/remote.go). Everything ships default-off on both sides until the Phase 2 gate: the CP flag `--bundles` defaults to `off`, and a worker with no pins behaves exactly as today. In the release that closes Phase 2 the defaults flip to require.
design: Gate (default off, per conventions.md): new CP flag `warden control-plane --bundles=off|offer|require` (default `off`), same style as `--policy-store`. `offer` and `require` need `--state-dir`, `--policy-store=versioned` (W-P1-PVER-01) and a loadable purpose=bundle KeySet (W-P2-KEYS-02); otherwise startup fails with an error naming the missing flag. `off` keeps GET /policy byte-identical. In `offer` the CP serves the signed envelope only to requests with `Accept: application/vnd.warden.bundle.v1+json` and the legacy policyWire to everyone else. In `require` a legacy request gets 406 `{"error":"signed_bundle_required"}`. The CP logs the mode at startup. Phase 2 gate: in the release that closes Phase 2, `--bundles` defaults to `require` when its prerequisites (`--state-dir`, `--policy-store=versioned` and a bundle KeySet) are present; a CP without them keeps serving the legacy wire with a startup WARN naming what is missing, and an explicit `--bundles=require` without them still fails startup. `--bundles=off` stays as an explicit opt-out.

Payload (new package internal/bundle, type `Bundle`): {typ: "warden-bundle/v1", seq, policyVersion, issuedAt, expiresAt, cpID, contentSha256, policy, credentialsSha256, sections}. `seq` is `policy_publish_log.seq` (carry-forward from p1-policy-history). `policyVersion` is informational only. `policy` is the exact served policyWire bytes {allowlist, denylist, settings, blockedUsers, registeredAgents}, so blockedUsers (W-P1-BLOCK-01), settings.agents and registeredAgents (W-P2-AREG-04) are not duplicated. `cpID` is a random id generated once and stored in the cpstate DB. `contentSha256` covers cpID, policy, credentialsSha256 and sections (not the timestamps), so a re-sign of unchanged content is recognisable. `sections` holds optional named blocks; this feature defines only `tokenJWKS` (from KeySet.JWKS(), W-P2-KEYS-03). W-P2-WBND-06 adds one top-level field, `tokenIssuer` (omitempty), set from tokenService.issuer. Later features add their own section (for example W-P4-MREG-05 or W-P4-DGR-06) and workers ignore sections they do not know.

Envelope and crypto: `{payload: base64url(bytes), signatures: [{kid, sig}], credentials?}`. No JSON canonicalization: the CP marshals the payload once, and each signature covers the ASCII string `warden-bundle-v1`, one 0x00 byte, then the payload bytes. This separates bundle signatures from token signatures made by internal/keys. The worker verifies the exact received bytes and only then decodes them. The algorithm comes from the pinned JWK (EdDSA or ES256, W-P2-KEYS-01), never from the envelope. kid is the RFC 7638 thumbprint. One valid signature from a pinned key is enough, which allows signing with two keys during rotation.

Credential sidecar: the sanctioned credential on the wire (`settings.secrets.accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey`, internal/config/settings.go) is removed from the signed `policy` and sent in the envelope's unsigned `credentials` field. The signed payload carries its full SHA-256 in `credentialsSha256`. The worker uses the sidecar only when the hash matches, merges it back into settings in memory, never logs it and never writes it to disk. With no credential both fields are absent.

Ordering and freshness: every change to served content appends a publish_log row. P1 covers policy saves, rollbacks, `blocked_users` and `credential` (W-P1-PVER-05). This feature adds reason `token_jwks`, and owning features add their own reasons (for example `agent_registry` from W-P2-AREG-04), so a policy rollback always gets a higher seq. `expiresAt = issuedAt + --bundle-max-age` (default 24h), and the CP re-signs the current content every max-age/4 with the same seq. The worker accepts seq > applied, or seq == applied with the same contentSha256 and a newer issuedAt (a refresh). It rejects with a fixed reason: `malformed`, `too_large`, `unsupported_format`, `unsigned`, `unknown_kid`, `bad_signature`, `issuer_mismatch`, `credential_mismatch`, `rollback` (seq < applied), `equivocation` (equal seq, different contentSha256), `expired` (now > expiresAt + skew) and `future` (issuedAt > now + `controlPlane.bundleClockSkew`, default 5m).

CP serving: the envelope is built once per publish_log row or re-sign tick and cached in policyWatch next to the legacy wire, so the /policy hot path never signs, reads the DB or calls the key backend. The legacy wire keeps etagFor(wire), so the W-P1-PVER-05 ETag-to-version lookup is unchanged. The envelope ETag is a 16-hex hash of the envelope bytes, so a re-sign changes it and wakes long-poll waiters. The CP refuses to publish an envelope over 4 MiB, keeps the previous one and logs at error. If signing fails (ErrNoActiveKey or a backend error), it keeps serving the last signed envelope until it expires, marks /healthz degraded and logs; it never serves unsigned data to an opted-in worker.

Worker trust config: `controlPlane.bundleKeys` (inline public JWKs) and/or `controlPlane.bundleKeysFile` (JWKS JSON). Only OKP Ed25519 and EC P-256 public keys are accepted, and each kid must equal its RFC 7638 thumbprint. Optional `controlPlane.bundleIssuer` must equal payload cpID when set. Pins present means the worker sends the Accept header and accepts only verified envelopes, with no downgrade. No pins and `controlPlane.requireSignedBundles: false` (the default until the Phase 2 gate) keeps today's behaviour with one startup WARN. At the Phase 2 gate `requireSignedBundles` defaults to true for CP-managed workers, so a worker without pins fails startup unless the operator sets it to false explicitly. `requireSignedBundles: true` with no pins is a startup error. localOnly workers ignore all of this.

Worker apply: RemoteProvider.Pull and PollLong both verify through `bundle.Verify`. A verified bundle becomes one immutable snapshot (policy, settings with the sidecar credential, blockedUsers, sections) applied under one swap, so the evaluator, the onApply MCP gateway rebuild and the W-P2-WBND-01 token verifier never see a mix of two bundles. On rejection the worker keeps last-known-good and sends the rejected envelope's ETag as If-None-Match on the next long-poll, so it does not re-download the same bad bundle in a loop.

Expiry during a CP outage: an applied bundle that passes expiresAt stays enforced, which keeps default-deny without a self-inflicted outage. The worker sets `warden_bundle_stale` to 1 and reports it in the heartbeat. `controlPlane.bundleExpiry: keep|deny` (default keep) lets strict deployments deny all traffic while stale.

Last-known-good cache (opt-in, W-P2-SBND-06): the worker keeps all local state in one `controlPlane.stateDir` (0700, shared with W-P2-WCA-03) with a subdirectory per use: `cert/` for the worker key and cert and `bundle/` for this cache. There is no separate bundleCacheDir. The cache is on when stateDir is set and bundle keys are pinned; `controlPlane.bundleCacheMaxAge` defaults to 24h and 0 disables it. The worker writes the envelope without the credentials sidecar, atomically, with a 0600 file in a 0700 directory. The cache is read only when the boot Pull fails, is re-verified against the pins, and is used only if issuedAt is within the max age; otherwise the worker stays fail-closed as today (internal/worker/worker.go). Docs require the directory to be unwritable by the agent.

Bundle key lifecycle (W-P2-SBND-07, carry-back to p2-key-manager): purpose=bundle never rotates on a schedule: W-P2-KEYS-03 requires `keys.bundle.rotationInterval` to be 0. Rotation is two commands: `warden control-plane keys rotate --purpose bundle --stage` sets publish_at on the next key that W-P2-KEYS-03 keeps pre-generated (creating it if missing), after which every envelope is signed by both the active and next keys; `--activate` makes it the only signer and refuses unless every online worker lists the next kid in heartbeat `pinnedKids` (`--force` overrides and writes an admin audit row). `warden control-plane keys export --purpose bundle` prints the public JWKS to pin.

Restore and regression: restoring a CP backup (W-P1-OPS1-04) can move publish_log seq backwards, so every pinned worker would reject new bundles as rollbacks. New CP flag `--bundle-seq-floor` (default 0): at startup in offer or require mode, when the head seq is below the floor, the CP appends one publish_log row with reason `restore` at the floor. The fleet view flags workers whose reported seq is above the CP head, and the runbook takes the floor from that value.

Observability: worker OTel instruments in internal/observability, named in the existing `warden.*` style and exported to Prometheus as `warden_bundle_rejected_total{reason}`, `warden_bundle_seq`, `warden_bundle_age_seconds` and `warden_bundle_stale`. The heartbeat struct from W-P1-BLOCK-02 gains {bundleSeq, bundleKid, bundleIssuedAt, pinnedKids, bundleStale, lastRejectReason, lastRejectAt} and cap `bundle/v1` when pins are set. WorkerRegistry stores them for the fleet API and console. No log line contains payload content or credential values.
done_when: A CP runs with `--policy-store=versioned --bundles=require` and a worker pins the exported bundle JWKS; the worker enforces only verified bundles, and the fleet view shows its seq and kid. Each of these leaves the worker on its previous policy, increments `warden_bundle_rejected_total` with the matching reason and shows in the heartbeat: an unsigned body, a one-byte tamper, an unknown kid, an older seq, an equal seq with different content, an expired bundle, an issuedAt in the future and an oversized bundle. A policy rollback produces a higher seq that the worker accepts. A staged and then activated bundle key rotation completes with zero rejections, and activation is refused while an online worker lacks the next pin. With `controlPlane.stateDir` set (cache in its `bundle/` subdirectory), a worker restarted while the CP is down enforces the cached bundle within `bundleCacheMaxAge` and fails closed after that, and the cache file never contains the AWS secretAccessKey. With `--bundles=off`, or a worker with no pins, /policy and worker behaviour are byte-identical to the previous release. In the Phase 2 gate release the defaults are `--bundles=require` (when its prerequisites are present) and `requireSignedBundles: true`, with `--bundles=off` and `requireSignedBundles: false` as explicit opt-outs.

tickets.title: Add internal/bundle payload, envelope, sign and verify
tickets.body: Create new package internal/bundle with the bundle payload, the envelope, `Sign` and `Verify`. Signatures cover the exact payload bytes behind a domain-separation prefix, so no JSON canonicalization is needed and the worker checks the signature before decoding anything. Verify also enforces sequence, equivocation, expiry, issuer and credential-hash rules and returns typed errors with a fixed reason set for metrics. Nothing calls the package yet, so merging changes no behaviour.
requirements: `Bundle{Typ, Seq int64, PolicyVersion int64, IssuedAt, ExpiresAt time.Time, CPID, ContentSHA256, Policy json.RawMessage, CredentialsSHA256 string, Sections map[string]json.RawMessage}`; `Envelope{Payload string (base64url, no padding), Signatures []Signature{KID, Sig}, Credentials *Credentials (omitempty)}`. `Credentials.String()` and its slog value print only `[redacted]`.

`Sign(ctx, b Bundle, creds *Credentials, signers ...keys.Signer) ([]byte, error)` sets ContentSHA256 and CredentialsSHA256, marshals the payload once, and has each signer sign `warden-bundle-v1` + 0x00 + payload. It rejects zero signers and an envelope over `MaxEnvelopeBytes` (4 MiB).

`Verify(raw []byte, pins []keys.JWK, applied State, opt Options) (Verified, error)`, with `State{Seq, ContentSHA256, IssuedAt}` and `Options{Now, Skew, Issuer}`. Signature checking happens before any payload decode, and the algorithm comes from the pinned JWK only.

Typed errors with `Reason(err) string` mapping to exactly: malformed, too_large, unsupported_format, unsigned, unknown_kid, bad_signature, issuer_mismatch, credential_mismatch, rollback, equivocation, expired, future. An identical re-delivery (same seq, same contentSha256, issuedAt not newer) returns ErrUnchanged, which is not a rejection; a newer issuedAt with the same content is accepted with `Verified.Refresh=true`.
Error strings never contain payload content or credential values; they carry only seq, kid and a 16-hex digest prefix.
Verify of a 1 MiB payload takes under 10 ms on CI hardware.
No new third-party dependency; crypto goes through keys.Verify from W-P2-KEYS-01.
plan: Add internal/bundle/bundle.go (new): Bundle, Credentials, State, Verified, the `TypV1` constant, MaxEnvelopeBytes and the contentSha256 helper over cpID, policy, credentialsSha256 and sections.
Add internal/bundle/envelope.go (new): Envelope, Signature and Sign, building the signing input from the domain prefix and the payload bytes.

Add internal/bundle/verify.go (new): Verify in this order: size, envelope decode, signatures (unknown_kid if no kid is pinned, bad_signature if a pinned kid fails), payload decode, typ, issuer, credential hash, future, expired, then seq rules.
Add internal/bundle/errors.go (new): the Err* values and Reason().
Add internal/bundle/bundle_test.go (new): Ed25519 and ES256 round trips, a two-signer envelope, every rejection reason, refresh and unchanged cases, plus FuzzVerify and BenchmarkVerify1MiB.
acceptance: Given a bundle signed with Ed25519 and with ES256 signers, Verify against the matching pinned JWK returns the same Seq and ContentSHA256, and flipping any single byte of payload or signature returns ErrBadSignature.

Given applied {Seq: 7}, a valid seq 6 returns ErrRollback, seq 7 with different content returns ErrEquivocation, seq 7 with the same content and a newer issuedAt returns Refresh=true, and an identical envelope returns ErrUnchanged.
A malformed JSON payload with a bad signature returns ErrBadSignature, not ErrMalformed, which shows the payload is never decoded before the signature check.
A credentials sidecar whose SHA-256 differs from credentialsSha256 returns ErrCredentialMismatch, and the error text does not contain the secret value.
`go test -race ./internal/bundle -run 'TestSignVerify|TestVerifyRejects|TestReasons'` passes, and `go test ./internal/bundle -run '^$' -fuzz FuzzVerify -fuzztime 30s` finds no panic.

tickets.title: Serve the signed bundle envelope on GET /policy behind --bundles
tickets.body: Add the CP flag `--bundles=off|offer|require` (default off) and, when it is on, build and sign a bundle in policyServer.Refresh whenever a publish_log row is appended, plus a periodic re-sign for expiry. The bundle seq is `policy_publish_log.seq`, so policy rollbacks still move forward, and the envelope is cached in policyWatch so /policy never signs per request. Workers opt in with an Accept header, so existing workers keep receiving the legacy wire. This ticket is CP-only.
requirements: `--bundles` defaults to `off`, and off keeps /policy body and ETag byte-identical. `offer` and `require` fail startup unless `--state-dir`, `--policy-store=versioned` and a loadable purpose=bundle KeySet are present, with an error naming the missing piece.

Negotiation: with `Accept: application/vnd.warden.bundle.v1+json` the CP returns the envelope (same Content-Type) in offer and require modes; other requests get the legacy policyWire in off and offer, and 406 `{"error":"signed_bundle_required"}` in require. Long-poll and If-None-Match work for both formats, each against its own ETag.

seq is the latest publish_log seq; every token KeySet transition delivered through `KeySet.Subscribe` (W-P2-KEYS-03), including an emergency revocation, appends a row with new reason `token_jwks`, calls Refresh and wakes long-poll waiters. The `tokenJWKS` section comes from KeySet.JWKS(). A bundle signing key change does not append a row; it only re-signs.
The credential (`settings.secrets.accessKeyId/secretAccessKey`) is moved from the signed policy into the envelope sidecar, and its SHA-256 goes into credentialsSha256.

`--bundle-max-age` (default 24h, minimum 1h) sets expiresAt; a ticker re-signs the current content every max-age/4 with the same seq. `--bundle-seq-floor` (default 0) appends one `restore` row at the floor at startup when head seq is lower.

If signing fails, the CP keeps the last envelope until it expires, logs `bundle sign failed` with seq and kid, and reports degraded on /healthz; with no envelope yet, opted-in requests get 503. An envelope over 4 MiB is not published and is logged at error.
slog `bundle signed` logs seq, kid list, a 16-hex payload digest and size only; never payload content or the credential.
plan: cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the `--bundles`, `--bundle-max-age` and `--bundle-seq-floor` flags and their startup checks; add the matching fields (new) to controlplane.Config.
internal/controlplane: add a `cp_id` value (new) to the cpstate DB, generated once on first start in offer or require mode.

internal/controlplane/policyserver.go: add buildBundle (new), which takes the merged served wire, strips the credential, reads the latest seq from PolicyVersionStore.PublishLog and calls bundle.Sign; call it from Refresh after the W-P1-PVER-05 AppendPublish step. Add `env []byte` and `envETag string` (new) to policyWatch and wake waiters when either format changes.
policyserver.go ServePolicy: pick the format from the Accept header and the mode; compare If-None-Match against the ETag of that format; return 406 or 503 as specified.

internal/controlplane/policystore.go: allow reasons `token_jwks` and `restore` in AppendPublish, and add the seq-floor row at startup. Register a `KeySet.Subscribe` callback (W-P2-KEYS-03) that appends `token_jwks` for purpose token and calls Refresh, and re-signs on bundle-key changes. Add the re-sign ticker in Server.Start.
Add internal/controlplane/policyserver_bundle_test.go (new) covering every acceptance item.
acceptance: With `--bundles=off` (the default), GET /policy body and ETag equal a golden captured before this change: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBundlesOffByteIdentical`.

With `--bundles=offer`, a request with the bundle Accept header gets an envelope that bundle.Verify accepts against the CP's bundle public JWK with seq equal to the latest publish_log seq and no secretAccessKey inside the decoded payload; a request without the header gets the legacy wire with its old ETag.
A block-list change and a policy rollback each produce an envelope with a higher seq, and a token key rotation appends a `token_jwks` row and wakes a waiting long-poll within 1s.
With `--bundles=require`, a request without the Accept header gets 406; `--bundles=offer` without `--policy-store=versioned` fails startup with an error naming both flags.

When the bundle signer returns ErrNoActiveKey, /policy keeps serving the previous envelope and /healthz reports degraded: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestBundleServe|TestBundleNegotiation|TestBundleSeqFromPublishLog|TestBundleSignFailureKeepsLast|TestBundleResign'`.

tickets.title: Add bundle key pinning and signed-bundle options to worker config
tickets.body: Add the worker config keys that pin bundle public keys and control signed-bundle behaviour. A worker with no pins keeps today's behaviour and logs one warning, so this merge breaks no existing deployment; `requireSignedBundles: true` lets an operator make missing pins a startup error. The keys have no runtime effect until W-P2-SBND-04 reads them.
requirements: New ControlPlaneConfig and rawControlPlane fields: `bundleKeys` (list of public JWK objects), `bundleKeysFile` (JWKS JSON `{"keys":[...]}`), `requireSignedBundles` (default false), `bundleIssuer` (optional), `bundleClockSkew` (default 5m, max 1h) and `bundleExpiry` (`keep` or `deny`, default keep).
Inline and file keys are merged, at most 16 in total; a duplicate kid is an error.

Each key must be OKP/Ed25519 or EC/P-256, have no private members (d, p, q, dp, dq, qi, k), and have a kid equal to its RFC 7638 thumbprint (keys.Thumbprint from W-P2-KEYS-01). Errors name the field and index, never key material.
`requireSignedBundles: true` with no pins fails config load. No pins and the flag false logs one WARN `bundle verification disabled (no controlPlane.bundleKeys)` at worker startup.
`localOnly: true` ignores these keys with one INFO line.
Configs without the new keys parse to the same ControlPlaneConfig as before.
plan: internal/config/controlplane.go: add the fields to ControlPlaneConfig and rawControlPlane, and parse durations and the bundleExpiry enum in parseControlPlane.
parseControlPlane: read bundleKeysFile once, merge with inline keys, and validate each key; add a `BundleVerification() bool` method (new).
validateControlPlane: enforce requireSignedBundles and the key limits.
internal/worker/worker.go: log the WARN when the worker is CP-managed and BundleVerification() is false.
Tests in internal/config/config_test.go for each rule.
acceptance: With `requireSignedBundles: true` and no pins, config load fails with an error naming `controlPlane.bundleKeys`; without the flag the same config loads: `go test ./internal/config -run TestControlPlaneRequireSignedBundles`.
A JWK with a `d` member, or with kty=oct or RSA, fails load with an error naming `controlPlane.bundleKeys[0]`: `go test ./internal/config -run TestControlPlaneBundleKeysReject`.
A kid that differs from the RFC 7638 thumbprint, or two keys with the same kid, fail load; one valid Ed25519 key and one valid ES256 key both load.
A bundleKeysFile with 2 keys plus 1 inline key gives 3 pins, and a missing file fails startup with the path in the error.
Existing configs without these keys pass the current `go test ./internal/config` suite unchanged.

tickets.title: Verify signed bundles in RemoteProvider and keep last-known-good in memory
tickets.body: When pins are configured, make RemoteProvider request the signed envelope, verify it with bundle.Verify before decoding, and apply a verified bundle as one snapshot. Any rejection keeps the last-known-good policy, which longPollControlPlane already does for errors, and the rejected ETag is sent back so the worker does not re-download the same bad bundle. Without pins the request, size limit and parse path stay exactly as today. This ticket is worker-only and holds state in memory; disk persistence is W-P2-SBND-06.
requirements: With pins, Pull and PollLong send the bundle Accept header, read up to 4 MiB + 1 byte and reject a larger body as too_large instead of truncating; a legacy-format 200 is rejected as unsigned. Without pins the 1 MiB maxPolicyBytes path is unchanged.

After bundle.Verify succeeds, the bundle `policy` bytes go through the existing parseRemotePolicy (including blocked-user validation), and the sidecar credential is merged into settings in memory only.

Policy, settings, blockedUsers and sections are stored as one immutable snapshot under one lock, and new accessor `RemoteProvider.Bundle()` returns the verified seq, kid, issuedAt, tokenIssuer and sections (copy) for W-P2-WBND-01, and ok=false when no pins are set or nothing has been verified yet, so a legacy-wire policy never exposes sections or token keys.
On rejection nothing applied changes, the error wraps the bundle error, and the rejected envelope's ETag is used as If-None-Match on the next long-poll.
When the applied bundle passes expiresAt with the CP unreachable, the worker keeps enforcing it (bundleExpiry keep) or denies all traffic (bundleExpiry deny).
Logs: one WARN per distinct (reason, digest) with seq, kid and reason; one INFO `bundle applied` with seq and kid. Payload, settings values and the credential are never logged.
plan: internal/config/remote.go: add `SetBundleTrust(pins, opts)` (new) and the snapshot fields; factor the body handling of Pull and PollLong into applyResponse (new), which branches on whether pins are set.

remote.go: call bundle.Verify with the applied State; on success call parseRemotePolicy on the policy bytes, merge the credential and swap the snapshot; on failure record lastReject and the rejected ETag.
Add `Bundle()` and `BundleStatus()` (new) on RemoteProvider and add them to the ControlPlaneClient interface in internal/worker/loops.go; update the fake in loops_test.go.
internal/worker/worker.go: call SetBundleTrust from the parsed ControlPlaneConfig; apply the bundleExpiry deny mode by replacing the evaluator with deny-all when the snapshot is stale.
Tests in internal/config/remote_test.go (httptest TLS CP signing with bundle.Sign) and internal/worker/loops_test.go.
acceptance: Given a worker on seq 5 and a CP serving seq 6 with one flipped payload byte, the evaluator still enforces seq 5 and the next long-poll carries the rejected ETag: `go test -race ./internal/config ./internal/worker -run 'TestRemoteProviderSignedBundleTamper|TestLongPollSignedBundleKeepsLastKnownGood'`.
Given a worker on seq 5, a valid seq 4 is rejected as rollback and a different valid seq 5 as equivocation, with policy unchanged in both cases.
Given pins and a CP that answers with the legacy wire, the worker rejects it as unsigned; given a 4 MiB + 1 byte body, it rejects it as too_large.
Given a sidecar credential that matches credentialsSha256, Settings() returns it; given one that does not, the bundle is rejected as credential_mismatch.
Given no pins, the existing `go test ./internal/config ./internal/worker` suites pass unchanged.

tickets.title: Report bundle state through metrics, heartbeat and the fleet view
tickets.body: Add worker metrics for bundle rejections, seq, age and staleness, and extend the W-P1-BLOCK-02 heartbeat struct with the bundle state and pinned kids. The CP stores these in WorkerRegistry so operators can see which workers verify bundles, which rejected one and why, and which pins each worker holds before a key rotation. It also flags workers whose seq is above the CP head after a restore.

Recording methods are nil-safe on *Metrics.

The heartbeat body adds bundleSeq, bundleKid, bundleIssuedAt, pinnedKids, bundleStale, lastRejectReason and lastRejectAt (all omitempty) and cap `bundle/v1` when pins are set; the body stays under the CP's 4096-byte limit.
handleHeartbeat and WorkerRegistry.SeenHeartbeat store the new fields; WorkerView exposes them; old workers that send only policyETag and caps keep working.
For workers that report bundleSeq, `behind` is bundleSeq < head seq; the fleet API flags `bundle_seq_ahead` when a worker reports a seq above head and logs one ERROR per worker.
The console shows 'N connected workers do not verify signed bundles' (no `bundle/v1` cap) and a per-worker rejection badge; reason text is rendered with textContent.
The CP logs `worker bundle rejected` once per (worker, reason) change with proxy_id, seq and reason only.

Tests in observability_test.go, loops_test.go, remote_test.go, controlplane_test.go and dashboard tests.

Given a heartbeat with bundleSeq 5 while head seq is 6, the fleet API shows behind=true and the reject reason: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestFleetBundleState`.

Given a heartbeat with bundleSeq 50 while head seq is 10, the fleet API reports bundle_seq_ahead and exactly one ERROR line is logged for that worker.

tickets.title: Add an opt-in last-known-good bundle cache for worker restarts
tickets.body: Let a pinned worker persist its last verified bundle and use it at boot when the CP is unreachable. Today a CP-managed worker boots fail-closed until the first pull (internal/worker/worker.go), and that stays the default: the cache is off unless `controlPlane.stateDir` is set and bundle keys are pinned. stateDir is the one worker state directory shared with W-P2-WCA-03, and the cache lives in its `bundle/` subdirectory. The cache never holds the credential sidecar and is used only within `bundleCacheMaxAge`, so a restart cannot bring back a very old block list.
requirements: No separate cache directory key: the cache uses `<controlPlane.stateDir>/bundle/` (created 0700). Whichever of this ticket and W-P2-WCA-03 lands first adds `controlPlane.stateDir` (absolute path, created 0700). New key `controlPlane.bundleCacheMaxAge` (default 24h; 0 disables the cache). The cache is active only when stateDir is set and bundle keys are pinned; with stateDir and no pins nothing is written.

After each applied bundle the worker writes `<stateDir>/bundle/bundle.json` (envelope without `credentials`, plus applied seq and issuedAt) via temp file, fsync and rename; file mode 0600, directory 0700. A write failure logs one ERROR and never affects the applied policy.

The cache is read only when the boot Pull fails. It is re-verified with bundle.Verify against the current pins, and loaded only if issuedAt is within bundleCacheMaxAge; otherwise the worker logs a WARN and boots fail-closed as today.
A bundle loaded from cache seeds the applied State, so a later older seq from the CP is rejected as rollback.
When running from cache, the aws secret backend uses worker env or IAM credentials, since the sidecar is not cached.
The cache file never contains secretAccessKey, and its content is never logged.
plan: internal/config/controlplane.go: add and validate bundleCacheMaxAge, and controlPlane.stateDir if W-P2-WCA-03 has not added it yet.
internal/config/remote.go: add writeCache (new) called after a successful apply, and LoadCache (new) that reads, re-verifies and installs a snapshot.

internal/worker/worker.go: when rp.Pull() fails at boot and the cache is active (stateDir set, keys pinned), call LoadCache and use its policy and settings as the boot policy; keep the existing fail-closed log otherwise.
docs/control-plane.md: document the stateDir layout (`cert/`, `bundle/`), bundleCacheMaxAge, and that the state directory must not be writable or readable by the agent.
Tests in internal/config/remote_test.go and internal/worker/worker_test.go.
acceptance: Given a worker with controlPlane.stateDir and pinned keys that applied seq 5 and is restarted with the CP down, it enforces seq 5 from the cache and the file has mode 0600: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestWorkerBootFromBundleCache`.
Given a cache older than bundleCacheMaxAge, a corrupt cache, or one signed by a key no longer pinned, the worker logs one WARN and boots fail-closed (deny all).
Given a worker booted from a seq 5 cache, a CP that then serves a valid seq 3 is rejected as rollback.
Given an applied bundle with a credentials sidecar, `grep -c secretAccessKey <stateDir>/bundle/bundle.json` returns 0 in `go test ./internal/config -run TestBundleCacheHasNoCredential`.
Without controlPlane.stateDir, or with bundleCacheMaxAge 0, no cache file is written and boot behaviour is unchanged.

tickets.title: Add staged bundle key rotation, pin export and rollout docs
tickets.body: Workers pin bundle keys in static config, so scheduled rotation from W-P2-KEYS-03 would make the whole fleet reject bundles after one interval. This ticket excludes purpose=bundle from scheduled rotation, adds a two-step staged rotation where the CP signs with both keys until every online worker has the new pin, and adds a command that exports the public JWKS to pin. It also writes the operator docs for the rollout order and for recovering after a CP restore.
requirements: Bundle keys rotate only by command: W-P2-KEYS-03 rejects a non-zero `keys.bundle.rotationInterval`, and this ticket adds a test that the scheduler never touches purpose=bundle.

`warden control-plane keys rotate --purpose bundle --stage` sets publish_at on the existing next bundle key (created now if missing) and the CP signs every envelope with both the active and next keys; `--activate` calls Manager.Rotate with ConfirmPinned, makes the next key the only signer and retires the old one after `keys.bundle.overlap`.
`--activate` refuses, listing the proxy ids, unless every online worker reports the next kid in heartbeat pinnedKids; `--force` overrides and writes an admin audit row with the missing proxy ids.
`warden control-plane keys export --purpose bundle` prints the public JWKS (active and next) for `controlPlane.bundleKeysFile`; it never prints private material.
Each stage and activate step writes an admin audit row and logs the kids involved.

docs/control-plane.md and docs/runbooks/key-rotation.md cover the rollout order (offer, pin all workers, require), staged rotation, emergency rotation after compromise, and setting `--bundle-seq-floor` after a restore; the compose recipe pins the exported JWKS when `--bundles` is enabled.

Phase 2 gate flip, shipped in the release that closes Phase 2: `--bundles` defaults to `require` when `--state-dir`, `--policy-store=versioned` and a bundle KeySet are present (otherwise legacy wire plus a startup WARN naming the missing piece), and worker `controlPlane.requireSignedBundles` defaults to true for CP-managed workers. The upgrade notes in docs/control-plane.md list the explicit opt-outs (`--bundles=off`, `requireSignedBundles: false`).
plan: internal/keys: add `KeySet.Signers()` (new) that returns the active signer plus the next signer when its publish_at is set, for purpose=bundle.
internal/controlplane/policyserver.go buildBundle: pass all signers from KeySet.Signers() to bundle.Sign.

cmd/proxy: extend the W-P2-KEYS-05 `keys rotate` command with `--stage`, `--activate` and `--force`, and make `keys export --purpose bundle` without `--state` print a JWKS of the active and staged next keys; the activate check reads pinnedKids from WorkerRegistry through the admin API.
Update docs/control-plane.md, docs/runbooks/key-rotation.md and the deploy/compose recipe.
Tests in internal/keys, internal/controlplane and cmd/proxy, including a staged rotation with two simulated workers.
acceptance: After `--stage`, an envelope carries two signatures and a worker pinned only to the old key and a worker pinned only to the new key both accept it: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBundleStagedRotation`.

`--activate` fails and names the worker when one online worker lacks the next kid in pinnedKids, and succeeds with `--force` while writing one admin audit row: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestKeysRotateBundleActivateGate`.
With `keys.token.rotationInterval` elapsed on a fake clock, the token key rotates and the bundle key does not.
`warden control-plane keys export --purpose bundle` output parses as a JWKS that W-P2-SBND-03 accepts and contains no `d` member.
A full stage, pin, activate cycle against two workers produces zero `warden_bundle_rejected_total` increments.

With the gate defaults, a CP with the prerequisites serves signed bundles with no `--bundles` flag, a CP without them serves the legacy wire and logs one WARN, and a CP-managed worker with no pins and no explicit `requireSignedBundles: false` fails startup naming `controlPlane.bundleKeys`: `go test ./cmd/proxy ./internal/config -run TestBundleGateDefaults`.

name: Signed bundles
label: signed-bundles

summary: Every change that would widen what agents can reach, or where real credentials are sent, is held as a draft until a second person approves it. Before approving, the reviewer sees the structural diff, the reasons the change counts as widening, and a replay of recent fleet traffic that compares base and draft decisions. Narrowing changes still apply at once. The feature is off by default and needs OIDC console auth, the versioned policy store and admin audit.
design: Config and back-compat: a new CP-local `console.approvals` block in the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig (`json:"-"`, read only from the operator `--config` through `config.LoadConsole`, never from the served config.yaml, policyWire or SettingsWire), so a settings save can never turn the gate off. Keys and defaults: enabled false, minApprovals 1 (1..3), allowSelfApproveNarrowing true, allowEmergencyApply false, replayWindow 168h (1h..720h), replayMaxEvents 100000 (max 100000), replayTimeout 60s, replayMaxAge 24h, draftTTL 168h, maxOpenDrafts 200. A change needs a CP restart. When enabled, startup fails with an error naming the missing prerequisite unless console.auth=oidc, `--policy-store=versioned` (W-P1-PVER-01), `--state-dir` and `console.adminAudit.enabled=true` (W-P1-AAUD-01) are all set. When disabled, no approvals migration runs and every P1 endpoint, status code and /policy byte is unchanged.

One chokepoint: W-P2-APPR-06 changes the W-P1-PVER-02 `Server.publish` to take an `approvals.Clearance`, a type with unexported fields that only `approvals.Gate` can mint, and publish rejects the zero value. The Gate returns a Clearance when approvals are disabled, for a narrowing change when allowSelfApproveNarrowing is true, for an applied draft, for the `system:import` first-start migration, and for a break-glass emergency apply. Otherwise it returns ErrApprovalRequired. WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteLLMProviders, the W-P1-PVER-03 rollback route and the W-P1-PVER-06 `warden policy import` CLI all go through it, so a new publish caller that skips the gate does not compile. External YAML edits stay unserved per W-P1-PVER-05.

Data model (cpstate migration `approvals/0001`, applied only when enabled): `change_drafts(id, target policy|blocked_users|agents, target_ref, revision, base_version, state, author_iss, author_sub, author_email, author_kind, source console|rollback|cli|api|git|admin-mcp, provenance_json, message, doc_json, doc_sha256, classification_json, required_role, last_error, created_at, updated_at, expires_at, applied_version)` and append-only `change_approvals(id, draft_id, revision, doc_sha256, approver_iss, approver_sub, approver_email, approver_role, auth_method, decision approve|reject|self|emergency|post_review, replay_id, acknowledge_no_replay, comment, at)`. For the policy target, doc_json is the same redacted canonical doc (allowlist, denylist, settings) that `policy_versions.doc_json` stores, with secretAccessKey replaced by its `sha256:<16 hex>` fingerprint and blockedUsers excluded. YAML is never stored. `source` and `provenance_json` exist now so p4-gitops and p4-admin-mcp need no migration. The `approvals.Store` interface has a SQLite implementation so p5-postgres-ha can add its own.

State machine in internal/approvals, one compare-and-swap transaction per transition (`UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND state=? AND revision=?`): draft -> pending (submit); pending -> applied | rejected | needs_rebase; draft | pending | needs_rebase -> withdrawn (author) or expired (sweeper, after draftTTL); needs_rebase -> pending (rebase); pending | needs_rebase -> applied_unreviewed (emergency apply) -> applied (post-hoc review). An edit (PUT) or rebase creates revision n+1, voids earlier approvals and replays, and re-classifies. Each approval row records revision and doc_sha256. When the last required approval for the current revision arrives, the same request re-runs Classify against the live head and publishes with expectedHead=base_version through the publish path, which reruns the full NewLocalYAMLProvider validation. A 422 leaves the draft pending with last_error. An ErrConflict moves it to needs_rebase. Rebase applies the W-P1-PVER-03 structural diff (base to draft) onto the new head, and a key conflict returns 409 `rebase_conflict`, so a stale draft never silently reverts someone else's change.

Classification: pure `approvals.Classify(base, draft approvals.Doc) Classification{Widening bool; Reasons []Reason{Code, Path, Detail}; RequiredRole}` over the canonical doc. Allow and deny entries are compared as multisets keyed by an exported `DiffKey()` (the W-P1-PVER-03 diffKey, extended by W-P1-GPOL-01 with groups and users). Any added allow key is widening; there is no regex or wildcard containment analysis. The only allow narrowings are: an entry removed; an unscoped entry given groups or users, or a scoped entry's set reduced, on the same domain and port; a tighter rateLimit; a timeWindow added or narrowed. Removing or changing a deny entry is widening. Settings are compared by JSON path against a small allowlist of neutral or narrowing changes (logging.*, cacheTTLSeconds, dlp.enabled false to true, compliance.enabled false to true, advisory.enabled false to true). Every other path, including judge, llmProviders, secrets, explore, observability, mcp, agents and any field added later, is widening with code `settings.changed`. RequiredRole follows the W-P1-SSO-05 per-field table: admin for any settings field outside the editor set, else editor.

Other targets: a Classifier and Applier pair is registered per target, so p4-mcp-registry adds `mcp_registry` without a schema change. W-P2-APPR-08 registers `blocked_users`, where BlockStore.Remove (W-P1-BLOCK-03) is always widening and becomes a pending change that a second admin (not the author) must approve, while adding a block stays immediate and single-admin as the incident kill switch; a break-glass session may bypass the second admin only through the W-P2-APPR-07 emergency apply, which writes its own admin audit row and approval_bypassed Finding; the offline `warden control-plane block remove` (W-P1-BLOCK-08) creates the same pending draft; and the W-P3-OFFB-05 retention expiry of offboarding-created blocks is the one system removal outside drafts, audited as user.offboard_block_expired; and `agents`, where p2-agent-registry writes that create an agent, add an allowed group or allowed scope, add or replace a key, or re-enable an agent are widening and other agent edits (display name, removals, disable) apply directly. Lowering an agent's identity mode is a settings change (agents[].identity) and is held by the policy target.

Independence and roles: a person is identified by (iss, sub). For an API key principal the owner identity from Principal.ActorSub() (W-P2-APIK-02) is used; approve, reject, emergency-apply and review are ScopeNone, so a key can create or edit a draft but never approve one. The approver must differ from the author, and with minApprovals > 1 approvers must be distinct. Break-glass sessions (auth_method breakglass, W-P1-OPS1-01) can never approve; they can only use emergency apply. Blocked principals already lose their sessions per W-P1-BLOCK-07. Roles are recomputed per request as in W-P1-SSO-05, and the approver must hold the draft's RequiredRole at approval time.

Replay: new streaming `policyeval.Comparer` (`NewComparer(base, candidate config.Policy)`, `Add(analytics.Event)`, `Result() *CompareResult`) evaluates each event under both base and draft with the same stateless evaluator: rate limits and time windows stripped, and the W-P1-GPOL-05 subject used when the recorded identity status is valid. It reports changed_to_allow and changed_to_deny groups keyed by (domain, port, method) with count, affected users (email else sub, capped at 20), affected_users_total and anonymous_count, in a fixed sort order, with JSON tags and no URL, path, query or header. Recorded judge, DLP, block-list and rate-limit outcomes no longer show up as noise, because both sides are evaluated the same way. `policyeval.Evaluate` and `warden policy eval` are unchanged. Events come from a new `analytics.ReplayScanner` that FleetSQLiteStore implements on its read-only `ro` handle in pages of 5000 rows by id, selecting only the needed columns, so `/central/ingest` on the single read-write connection is never held for a whole scan. Other fleet stores fall back to one `GetEvents(EventFilter{Since, Limit})` call. One replay runs at a time per CP, bounded by replayTimeout, and replays left running by a CP restart are marked failed on startup.

Approval needs evidence: an approve request carries the revision and doc_sha256 the reviewer saw, plus the `replay_id` of a done replay for that revision no older than replayMaxAge, or `acknowledgeNoReplay: true` when the latest replay is failed or unavailable (memory store with no events, empty window). Both are stored on the approval row and in the audit details. The UI states that replay covers allow and deny only, and that rate limits, time windows and settings are judged from the classification reasons.

API, mounted under /dashboard/ so the W-P1-SSO-04 session and CSRF checks, the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table and the W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware apply unchanged, through a new `dashboard.ChangeDrafts` interface that only the CP sets (workers return 404): GET/POST /dashboard/api/changes, GET/PUT /dashboard/api/changes/{id}, GET .../{id}/diff, and POST .../{id}/submit|approve|reject|withdraw|rebase|replay, plus emergency-apply and review from W-P2-APPR-07. Each route has Action `change.draft.<verb>`, Target `change_draft` and Audited:true where it mutates. With approvals on, the existing policy, settings and llmProviders saves and rollback return 202 {draft_id, revision, state, widening, reasons} with a Location header when the change is held, or 200 {version} for a narrowing self-apply. The W-P1-PVER 409 and 428 If-Match rules still apply. API keys reach these routes through the W-P2-APIK-02 Scope column on the same table rows: GET routes policy:read; POST /dashboard/api/changes policy:draft; PUT, submit, withdraw, rebase and replay policy:write; approve, reject, emergency-apply and review ScopeNone. There is no policy:approve scope.

Emergency path (W-P2-APPR-07): when allowEmergencyApply is true, a break-glass session may call `POST .../{id}/emergency-apply` with a reason of 10 to 512 characters. It publishes with an emergency Clearance, writes audit action `change.draft.emergency_apply`, logs at ERROR, publishes a critical integration.Finding with RuleID `approval_bypassed` and DedupKey `approval_bypassed:<draft id>`, and leaves the draft applied_unreviewed until an OIDC admin records `POST .../{id}/review`. With the flag off, or with Dex down and no break-glass, widening changes wait; narrowing changes and narrowing rollbacks still self-apply.

Degraded modes: the worker hot path is untouched. Workers only see published versions and keep last-known-good while the CP is down. Drafts survive CP restarts in cpstate and are included in W-P1-OPS1-02 backups. With the IdP down, open sessions keep working and new logins wait. Expiry and replay windows use only the CP clock, and ordering uses version and revision integers. If admin audit is unhealthy, draft mutations return 503 per W-P1-AAUD-02.

Observability: slog `change_draft_transition` with draft_id, revision, target, state_from, state_to, actor_sub, widening and reason codes, and slog `change_draft_replay` with draft_id, status, events, duration_ms and group counts. Doc content, settings values and credential values are never logged. Admin audit rows carry target_ref `draft:<id>@r<rev>` and details {base_version, applied_version, widening, reasons, replay_status, acknowledge_no_replay}; apply also writes the existing PVER `policy` row. An info Finding `policy_approval_requested` is published when a widening draft is submitted, so existing alert routes can notify reviewers. The CP has no metrics endpoint in P1, so pending count, oldest pending age, emergency applies and replay duration are recorded as hooks for W-P5-RETN-06.

Dashboard: a Changes tab lists drafts by state and shows the W-P1-PVER-03 structural diff against base (credentials only as fingerprints), widening reasons and required role, replay status and age with the changed_to_allow and changed_to_deny tables, an acknowledge checkbox when the replay is unavailable, and approve, reject, withdraw and rebase controls. Every user-controlled string is rendered with textContent. Hidden buttons are a convenience only; the server enforces every check.
done_when: On a CP with console.auth=oidc, --policy-store=versioned, --state-dir, admin audit enabled and console.approvals.enabled=true, an editor who adds an allow entry gets 202 with a pending draft whose reasons include allow.added, and the /policy ETag does not change. The same holds for a widening settings save (an llmProviders baseURL change, which also needs an admin approver), a rollback that drops a deny entry, `warden policy import` of a widening file, removing a block-list entry, lowering an agent's identity mode in settings (agents[].identity) and adding an allowed group to a registered agent. The author's own approval and any break-glass approval get 403. A second editor sees the structural diff, the reasons and a done replay comparing base and draft over fleet events, with affected users and no URLs; their approval publishes exactly one new version that workers receive within one long-poll cycle. Editing a draft voids its approvals, and approving after head moved yields needs_rebase. A narrowing change self-applies at once. A replay over 100k events does not stall /central/ingest. Every transition has a chained admin audit row, and with approvals disabled every P1 endpoint and /policy byte is unchanged. Removing a block-list entry needs a second admin, adding one needs a single admin, and a break-glass bypass of a removal goes only through the audited emergency apply.

tickets.title: Add approvals config, draft store and state machine
tickets.body: Add the CP-local `console.approvals` config block and the new internal/approvals package with the draft and approval tables, the Store and the state machine. Drafts hold the same redacted canonical doc_json as policy_versions and are applied only through the W-P1-PVER-02 publish path with expectedHead=base_version, so approvals can never skip validation, credential redaction or the policy audit row. Nothing is mounted on HTTP yet, and cmd/proxy refuses `enabled: true` until W-P2-APPR-06 gates every write path.
requirements: `console.approvals` is parsed by the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig loader only from `--config` (`json:"-"`, never on policyWire or SettingsWire) with keys enabled (false), minApprovals (1, range 1..3), allowSelfApproveNarrowing (true), allowEmergencyApply (false), replayWindow (168h, 1h..720h), replayMaxEvents (100000, max 100000), replayTimeout (60s), replayMaxAge (24h), draftTTL (168h) and maxOpenDrafts (200); out-of-range values are validation errors.

When enabled, startup fails with an error naming the missing item unless console.auth=oidc, `--policy-store=versioned`, `--state-dir` and `console.adminAudit.enabled=true`. A temporary guard refuses enabled with `approvals enforcement is not available in this build` until W-P2-APPR-06 removes it.

Migration `approvals/0001` creates `change_drafts` and append-only `change_approvals` with the columns in the design, indexes on (state, target) and author_sub, and unique (draft_id, revision, approver_iss, approver_sub). It runs only when approvals are enabled.

For the policy target, doc_json is the canonical doc {allowlist, denylist, settings}: secretAccessKey is replaced by its `sha256:<16 hex>` fingerprint before insert, blockedUsers is excluded, and doc_sha256 matches what policy_versions would compute for the same doc. YAML is never stored.

Every transition is one transaction with `UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND state=? AND revision=?`; 0 rows returns ErrStateChanged. Illegal transitions return ErrIllegalTransition. Update in draft or pending state creates revision n+1 and voids approvals for earlier revisions.

Apply goes through a per-target `approvals.Applier`; the policy Applier lives in new internal/controlplane/approvals_apply.go over `s.publish` with expectedHead=base_version, source `approval`, and the draft author as author. internal/approvals never imports internal/controlplane. ErrConflict maps to ErrRebaseRequired and moves the draft to needs_rebase.
Create returns ErrTooManyDrafts above maxOpenDrafts open drafts. A sweeper started from Server.Start moves draft, pending and needs_rebase drafts past expires_at to expired.
Each transition logs `msg=change_draft_transition` with draft_id, revision, target, state_from, state_to and actor_sub; doc content and settings values are never logged.
plan: internal/config/console.go (from W-P1-SSO-02): add `ConsoleApprovals` (new) to ConsoleConfig with defaults and validation; add the startup prerequisite checks and the temporary enabled guard in resolveConsole in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.

Create internal/approvals (new): `Doc` with JSON tags allowlist, denylist and settings; `Author{Iss, Sub, Email, Kind}`; `Provenance`; `Draft`; the `State` enum and a pure `transition(from State, ev Event) (State, error)` table.

Add internal/approvals/store.go (new): `Store` interface and SQLite implementation on the cpstate *sql.DB with Create, Get, List(filter, cursor, limit), Update, Submit, RecordDecision, MarkApplied, MarkNeedsRebase, Withdraw and ExpireDue, plus the `approvals/0001` migration registered with cpstate.Open (W-P1-SSO-01).

Add `approvals.Service` (new) with `CreateDraft(ctx, target, doc, Author, Provenance, baseVersion)` and `Apply(ctx, id, revision)`, using the redaction helper exported from internal/controlplane/policystore.go (W-P1-PVER-01) through an injected func, and the `Applier` interface.
Add internal/controlplane/approvals_apply.go (new): the policy Applier over s.publish and the expiry sweeper goroutine, built in controlplane.New only when Config.Approvals is enabled.

Tests: internal/approvals/store_test.go (transition table, a CAS race under -race, revision bump voids approvals, no raw secretAccessKey in the DB file, expiry) and internal/controlplane/approvals_apply_test.go (stale base gives ErrRebaseRequired and no version; an applied draft creates one policy_versions row whose doc_sha256 equals the draft's); console_test.go for config validation.
acceptance: Given an applied draft, Submit, Update and Withdraw return ErrIllegalTransition and the row is unchanged; with 20 goroutines racing RecordDecision and Withdraw on one pending draft under -race, exactly one state change wins.
Given a draft with base_version 3 while head is 4, Apply returns ErrRebaseRequired, head stays 4 and the draft is needs_rebase.

Given a pending draft with base equal to head, Apply creates exactly one policy_versions row with source `approval` and the author's sub, and a second Apply returns ErrIllegalTransition without a new version.
Given settings with secrets.secretAccessKey set, neither change_drafts.doc_json nor the DB file contains the raw value after CreateDraft.
Given `console.approvals.enabled: true` with `console.auth: none`, the CP exits non-zero with an error naming console.auth; with approvals absent, /policy bytes and all P1 tests are unchanged.

`go test -race ./internal/approvals ./internal/config -run 'TestDraftStore|TestDraftTransitions|TestDraftExpiry|TestConsoleApprovals'` and `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestDraftApplyPublish` pass.

tickets.title: Implement widening-change classification
tickets.body: Add a pure `approvals.Classify(base, draft Doc) Classification` that decides whether a policy doc change widens access or changes where credentials go, and which role must approve it. It works on the canonical doc the versioned store holds, so it only classifies fields that exist there: allow and deny entries with their groups and users, and SettingsWire. Anything it does not recognise counts as widening, so a new field can never slip through as narrowing.
requirements: Signature `Classify(base, draft approvals.Doc) Classification{Widening bool; Reasons []Reason{Code, Path, Detail string}; RequiredRole config.Role}`; no I/O, deterministic, reasons sorted by (Code, Path), and entry order in the input does not change the output.

Allow and deny lists are compared as multisets keyed by an exported `DiffKey()` on config.AllowlistEntry and config.DenylistEntry (W-P1-PVER-03 diffKey renamed, including groups and users from W-P1-GPOL-01). Any added allow key is widening (`allow.added`); there is no regex or wildcard containment analysis. Removing or changing a deny entry is widening (`deny.removed`).

Removed and added allow entries with the same domain and port are paired; the pair is narrowing only when an unscoped entry gains groups or users, a scoped entry's groups and users shrink, the rateLimit is tighter, or a timeWindow is added or narrowed. Otherwise it is widening with `allow.scope_widened`, `allow.rate_relaxed` or `allow.time_relaxed`. RateLimit and TimeWindow are parsed with the internal/policy rules, and an unparseable value is widening.

Settings are compared by JSON path against an explicit table of neutral or narrowing changes: logging.*, cacheTTLSeconds, and dlp.enabled, compliance.enabled or advisory.enabled going from false to true. Every other added, removed or changed path is widening with code `settings.changed` and the path, including judge, llmProviders, secrets, explore, observability, mcp, agents and fields added later.

RequiredRole is admin when any changed settings path is outside the W-P1-SSO-05 editor set (advisory, compliance, dlp, logging, agents, cacheTTLSeconds), otherwise editor. The set is shared with authz, so when W-P2-WBND-07 makes agents[].identity and identity.defaultMode admin-only, those changes need an admin approver.
Reason Detail holds only domain, port and JSON path; credential paths show fingerprints and settings values are never included.
Classify handles 5000 entries per side in under 50ms and runs only on draft create, update, rebase and apply, never on /policy.
plan: internal/config/config.go: rename the W-P1-PVER-03 diffKey() to exported DiffKey() on AllowlistEntry and DenylistEntry and update internal/controlplane/policydiff.go callers.
Add internal/approvals/classify.go (new): multiset build by DiffKey, same-domain-and-port pairing, rate and time comparison, and the Reason codes.

Add internal/approvals/settings_rules.go (new): a JSON-path walker over config.SettingsWire marshalled to a generic map, the neutral and narrowing rule table, and the editor-field set shared with internal/controlplane/authz.go (move the set to internal/config so both import it).

Add internal/approvals/classify_test.go (new): one table case per reason code, narrowing-only cases, regex and wildcard additions, scoped-to-unscoped, an unknown settings path, and a fuzz test that Classify(x, x) is never widening; add BenchmarkClassify with 5000 entries.
acceptance: Table test flags each of these with the expected reason code: allow entry added, exact domain replaced by `*.` wildcard, `~` regex changed, port changed, deny entry removed, groups removed from a scoped entry, rateLimit raised, timeWindow widened, dlp.enabled true to false, llmProviders entry added.
A draft that only adds a deny entry, removes an allow entry, or adds groups to an unscoped entry gives Widening=false.
A change to a settings path not in the rule table gives Widening=true with code `settings.changed` and that path; a change to llmProviders gives RequiredRole admin.
Identical docs give Widening=false and no reasons, and shuffling entry order does not change the output.
`go test ./internal/approvals -run 'TestClassify|FuzzClassify' -bench BenchmarkClassify` passes with the benchmark under 50ms per call.

tickets.title: Replay fleet events against base and draft for each revision
tickets.body: Add a two-policy replay that evaluates recent fleet events under both the base version and the draft and stores the differences on the draft revision. Comparing against the recorded decision would show judge, DLP, block-list and rate-limit outcomes as false changes, so both sides use the same stateless evaluator. Events are read in pages from the fleet store's read-only handle so a 100k-event replay never holds the ingest connection.
requirements: New `policyeval.NewComparer(base, candidate config.Policy) *Comparer` with `Add(analytics.Event)` and `Result() *CompareResult`: rate limits and time windows are stripped on both sides, the W-P1-GPOL-05 subject is used when the recorded identity status is valid, and Conditional and NoMatch count as deny. `Evaluate` and `warden policy eval` output stay unchanged.

CompareResult has JSON tags: {events, agreed, anonymous_count, changed_to_allow[], changed_to_deny[]} with groups {domain, port, method, count, affected_users (email else sub, max 20), affected_users_total}, sorted by count desc then domain, port, method. No URL, path, query, header or group list is stored. MCP events are skipped.

New optional interface `analytics.ReplayScanner{ScanReplayEvents(ctx, since time.Time, limit int, fn func(Event) error) error}` implemented by FleetSQLiteStore on the `ro` handle in pages of 5000 rows by descending id, selecting only ts, domain, port, protocol, method, decision and the W-P1-VRFY-06 user columns. Stores without it fall back to one GetEvents(EventFilter{Since, Limit}).

Migration `approvals/0002` adds `draft_replays(id, draft_id, revision, base_version, status pending|running|done|failed|unavailable, window_from, window_to, events_scanned, truncated, result_json, error_code, started_at, finished_at)`.

A replay is queued on submit and on every new revision; Submit never waits. One replay runs at a time per CP, bounded by replayTimeout; on timeout the replay is failed with error_code `timeout` and a late result is discarded. Zero events gives status unavailable. On startup, pending and running replays are marked failed with `interrupted`.
`Service.Replay(ctx, id)` re-runs a replay at most once per minute per draft and returns ErrReplayBusy while the slot is in use. The route is added in W-P2-APPR-04.
Each run logs `msg=change_draft_replay` with draft_id, status, events, duration_ms and group counts, and never domains or user identifiers.

tickets.title: Add the change draft API with the two-person rule
tickets.body: Mount the draft routes under /dashboard/api/changes so the existing session, CSRF, role table and admin audit middleware cover them, and enforce the two-person rule on approve. An approval is bound to the revision, doc_sha256 and replay the reviewer saw, and the final approval applies the draft in the same request so there is no gap between approval and publish. Rerouting the existing write paths is W-P2-APPR-06.
requirements: New `dashboard.ChangeDrafts` interface and setter, set only on the CP (workers return 404), with routes: GET /dashboard/api/changes?target=&state=&cursor=&limit= and GET .../{id} and GET .../{id}/diff (viewer); POST /dashboard/api/changes and PUT .../{id} with If-Match `"r<rev>"` (editor, author only for PUT); POST .../{id}/submit, withdraw and rebase (author); POST .../{id}/approve and reject (editor or the draft's RequiredRole); POST .../{id}/replay (editor). Every route is in dashboard.Routes() and the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table with Action `change.draft.<verb>`, Target `change_draft` and Audited:true on mutations, and the W-P2-APIK-02 Scope (policy:read for GET, policy:draft for create, policy:write for PUT, submit, withdraw, rebase and replay, ScopeNone for approve and reject), set by whichever of the two tickets lands second.
GET .../{id}/diff returns the W-P1-PVER-03 structural diff of the current revision against base_version, with credential paths only as fingerprints.

Approve body {revision, doc_sha256, replay_id | acknowledgeNoReplay, comment<=1024}. It is refused with 409 `revision_changed` when revision or doc_sha256 differ from the draft, and with 409 `replay_required` unless replay_id names a done replay for that revision no older than replayMaxAge, or acknowledgeNoReplay is true and the latest replay is failed or unavailable.

Two-person rule: the approver's identity from Principal.ActorSub() (the owner for API-key principals, W-P2-APIK-02) must differ from the author's (403 `self_approval_forbidden`); auth_method breakglass can never approve (403 `breakglass_cannot_approve`); the approver must hold RequiredRole when the request runs (403 `role_required` with the fields). With minApprovals > 1 approvers must be distinct.

When the last required approval arrives, the same request re-runs Classify against the live head and applies; 200 {state: applied, version}, 409 `rebase_required` {head} when head moved (draft becomes needs_rebase), 422 with the loader error when validation fails (draft stays pending). Submit of a narrowing draft applies at once with decision `self` when allowSelfApproveNarrowing is true.
Rebase applies the PVER-03 diff (base to draft) onto head as revision n+1 and returns 409 `rebase_conflict` when a key changed on both sides.

A `change_draft` StateHasher (`<id>:<revision>:<state>:<doc_sha256>`) is registered with W-P1-AAUD-02, handlers call adminaudit.Annotate with target_ref `draft:<id>@r<rev>` and details {base_version, applied_version, widening, reasons, replay_status, acknowledge_no_replay}, and never doc content. Submit of a widening draft publishes an info Finding `policy_approval_requested` (DedupKey per draft).
Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB and comments have control characters stripped; unknown id 404, illegal transition 409 `illegal_transition`.

Tests in internal/controlplane/approvals_api_test.go (new) with editor sessions u1 and u2, a viewer, an admin and a break-glass session created through SessionStore.Create.

Given u2 with a done replay_id, POST .../approve returns 200 with version=head+1, a worker long-polling /policy receives the new ETag within one wait, and admin audit holds change.draft.create, change.draft.submit, change.draft.approve and the PVER policy row in order.
Given an approval sent with an older revision after u1 PUT a new revision, the response is 409 `revision_changed` and no version is created.
Given a widening draft that adds an llmProviders entry, u2's approve returns 403 `role_required` naming llmProviders and an admin's approve succeeds.

The server stays the only enforcement point; hidden buttons are a convenience.

Approve sends revision, doc_sha256 and replay_id. When the replay is failed or unavailable, an acknowledge checkbox must be ticked to send acknowledgeNoReplay. A pending replay polls every 2s up to replayTimeout and then offers re-run.

tickets.body: Make `Server.publish` require an `approvals.Clearance` that only `approvals.Gate` can mint, so no write path can publish a widening change without a draft. Emergency clearance is added in W-P2-APPR-07.

Stale If-Match still returns 409 `policy_conflict` and a missing one 428.

POST /dashboard/api/policy/versions/{v}/rollback with approvals enabled creates a draft whose doc is version v (source rollback), classified against head; a narrowing rollback applies at once.

`warden policy import` with approvals enabled creates a pending draft authored `cli:<os user>` (author_kind cli, source cli) instead of a version, prints the draft id and writes an admin audit row; the CP queues its replay on the next sweep. The CLI cannot approve or apply. It detects approvals through a new single-row `approvals_meta` table the CP writes at startup.
