name: Approvals + replay
label: policy-approvals

summary: Adds scoped, expiring API keys so scripts and CI can call the CP admin API without sharing the WARDEN_CP_TOKEN bearer. Each key acts for a human owner, is limited to the scopes it was given and to the owner's current console role, and is never accepted on worker, secret or key-minting routes. Users create, list and revoke their keys in the console, admins can revoke anyone's keys, and an offline CLI can revoke a leaked key during an incident.
design: Gating: new CP-local config `console.apiKeys: {enabled: false, defaultTTL: 2160h, maxTTL: 8760h, maxPerOwner: 25, ratePerKey: 10}` in the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig. Like the rest of the `console:` block it is read only from --config and never rides policyWire or SettingsWire. Enabling it requires --state-dir and console.auth=oidc, and startup fails otherwise with an error naming the setting. When disabled, no migration runs, no middleware is installed, the management routes return 404, and CP behaviour is unchanged. Workers run none of this code.

Format: `wak_<16 lowercase hex id>_<52-char lowercase unpadded base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes>`, a fixed 73 characters. This matches the P1 `wwt_` worker-token style (base32 secret, 16-hex id) and avoids base64url, whose `_` and `-` break splitting on the separator. Parse checks prefix, length, offsets and alphabet before any hashing or lookup.

Storage: new package `internal/apikeys` (CP admin credentials, unrelated to internal/auth.APIKeyInjector, which swaps upstream credentials). It holds Generate, Parse, a scope registry, a `Store` interface and a `SQLiteStore` on cpstate migration `api_keys/0001`: `api_keys(id PK, name, description, owner_iss, owner_sub, owner_email, owner_groups_json, scopes_json, secret_hash UNIQUE, created_at, expires_at NOT NULL, last_used_at, last_used_ip, revoked_at, revoked_by)` with `UNIQUE(owner_sub, name)`. Only sha256(secret) is stored; a 256-bit random secret needs no slow hash. Revoke is a soft delete. p5-postgres-ha adds a Postgres implementation behind the same interface.

Hot path: an in-memory `apikeys.Index` (the W-P1-WTOK-01 pattern): one map read, one sha256 and a constant-time compare per request, no DB I/O. It is rebuilt synchronously after an in-process create or revoke and reloaded when a 2s `PRAGMA data_version` poll changes, which picks up CLI revokes. A reload error keeps the last good index and never fails open. Expiry is checked against the CP clock only. last_used_at and last_used_ip are kept in memory and flushed in one transaction every 60s and on shutdown.

Scopes: a registry of `resource:verb` scopes, each with a minimum console role. P2 registers policy:read, policy:draft, policy:write, settings:read, traffic:read, audit:read, adminaudit:read, agents:read, agents:write and workers:admin; mcp:read and mcp:write are reserved for p4-mcp-registry. There is no policy:approve and no keys:admin scope. Create rejects unknown scopes, and a key's scopes are fixed at creation.

One route table: the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table (extended with Action/Target/Audited by W-P1-AAUD-02) gains a `Scope` column and becomes the single registry for every `/dashboard/api/*` route. P2 adds no `/api/` prefix: every P2 admin route, including the API-key routes, lives under `/dashboard/api/*`, and `/api/` is reserved for a future public, key-authenticated API. Every row must classify its scope explicitly: a registered scope, `ScopeNone` (keys denied) or `ScopeSelf` (any valid key). The coverage test fails on any /dashboard/api/* route without a row or a classification, on any route mounted under `/api/`, and fails when a route's minimum role is above its scope's minimum role.

Never keyable in P2 (`ScopeNone`): /central/secrets*, POST/DELETE /dashboard/api/secretstore, settings, integrations and llmproviders writes (they change where real credentials go), /dashboard/api/sessions, /dashboard/api/setup, POST /dashboard/api/backup, /dashboard/api/query/generate (spends LLM tokens), worker-token create, every API-key create and revoke route, and, when p2-approvals lands, draft approve, reject and apply. /auth/*, /dashboard/ HTML and the worker routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest, and /oauth2/token, /control/enroll and /control/renew once they exist) never run the API-key authenticator; WorkerAuthenticator (W-P1-WTOK-02) rejects a `wak_` bearer with 401 before the legacy-token compare.

Authentication: the API-key authenticator sits in the principal slot of the W-P1-AAUD-02 order (principal, request id, admin audit, authz, handler) for routes in the table. It handles `Authorization: Bearer wak_...` only. A request carrying both a `wak_` bearer and a console or portal cookie gets 400 `ambiguous_credentials`; a key in a query string gets 400. A cookieless key request skips the W-P1-SSO-04 CSRF and Origin checks, because browsers never attach Authorization on their own. Unknown, malformed, wrong-secret, expired and revoked keys all get the same 401 `{"error":"unauthorized"}` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, with no fallback to a session.

Principal: the P1 Principal gains `KeyID`, `Scopes` and `OwnerSub`. A key sets `{Kind: apikey, AuthMethod: apikey, Iss: owner_iss, Sub: "apikey:<id>", OwnerSub, Email: owner_email, Groups: owner_groups snapshot}`. New method `ActorSub()` returns (Iss, OwnerSub) for keys and (Iss, Sub) otherwise; p2-approvals uses it to compare draft author and approver, so an owner cannot approve their own widening draft through a key.

Authorization: allow only when the row's Scope is held by the key, the owner's role (recomputed on every request from console.RoleFor(owner_groups) under the current console.roles, as P1 does for sessions) is at least the row's minimum role, and the W-P1-SSO-05 per-field settings rules pass for that role. Otherwise 403 `{"error":"insufficient_scope","need":"<scope>"}`. A per-key token bucket (ratePerKey per second, burst 2x) returns 429. The groups snapshot is taken at creation, so IdP group removal is handled by revoke-by-owner on offboarding.

Management: `GET/POST /dashboard/api/api-keys`, `DELETE /dashboard/api/api-keys/{id}`, `DELETE /dashboard/api/api-keys?owner_sub=` and `GET /dashboard/api/api-keys/self`. Only an OIDC console session can create keys; break-glass sessions and keys get 403 `session_required`, so no key can mint or extend a key. Requested scopes are capped by the creator's role, the TTL by maxTTL, and active keys by maxPerOwner. Create returns 201 with the plaintext once and `Cache-Control: no-store`; no GET ever returns the secret or its hash. Admins list and revoke any key and revoke all keys of an owner. `/self` accepts any valid key and returns id, name, scopes, effective scopes, expiry and owner email for p4-admin-mcp.

Audit: add `apikey` to the Go-validated admin_audit auth_method set (W-P1-AAUD-01); no table change. Key-made requests are audited by the existing middleware with actor_id = HMAC(salt, owner sub), the side row holding the owner sub and email, actor_role = the owner's current role, and `details.api_key_id` added to the closed details allowlist. The `key_id` column keeps its P1 meaning (audit signer). Create, revoke, revoke-by-owner and CLI revoke are audited with target `api_keys` and target_ref `api_key:<id>`. Denied writes by a valid key are chained, as for sessions; invalid keys write no row, only a rate-limited `apikey_auth_rejected` log line with the parsed id or `malformed`, the reason and client_ip.

Operations: offline CLI `warden control-plane api-key list|revoke --state-dir` works with the CP stopped, or running with the IdP down, and its revokes reach a running CP within 2s. Restore (W-P1-OPS1-04) warns about API-key revocations and gains `--revoke-api-keys`. An `api_key_expiring` Finding is published 7 days before expiry through Server.publishFinding (W-P1-OPS1-01). An in-memory counter `warden_cp_apikey_auth_total{outcome}` with bounded labels is exported once W-P5-RETN-06 adds CP metrics. Keys do not depend on the IdP, so automation keeps working while Dex is down, bounded by expiry and offline revoke.

Leak detection (worker lane, separate S ticket): internal/scan gains `warden_api_key` and `warden_worker_token` credential patterns behind a new default-off `dlp.wardenTokens` setting, so a Warden admin key or worker token in agent egress is flagged or blocked like other credentials.
done_when: On a CP with --state-dir, console.auth=oidc, console.adminAudit.enabled=true and console.apiKeys.enabled=true, an editor creates a policy:read key in the console and sees the plaintext only once. A script using it gets 200 on GET /dashboard/api/policy, 403 insufficient_scope on POST /dashboard/api/policy, 401 on /policy and /central/ingest, and 403 on /central/secrets, POST /dashboard/api/secretstore and POST /dashboard/api/api-keys. A viewer cannot create a policy:write key, and an editor's policy:write key gets 403 after the editor's group is moved to viewer in console.roles. A revoked key gets 401 on its next request (within 2s for `warden control-plane api-key revoke`), an expired key gets 401, keys and revocations survive a CP restart, and keys keep working while Dex is stopped. Every create, revoke and key-made write is a chained admin_audit row with auth_method apikey and details.api_key_id, and no row or log line holds the plaintext or its hash. With console.apiKeys.enabled=false all existing CP tests pass unchanged. Every API-key route is under /dashboard/api/api-keys, and nothing is served under `/api/`, which stays reserved for a future public key-authenticated API.

tickets.title: Add internal/apikeys format, scope registry, store and index
tickets.body: Create the new internal/apikeys package that generates and parses `wak_` keys, holds the scope registry, stores keys in cpstate and authenticates them from an in-memory index. It follows the W-P1-WTOK-01 worker-token pattern so the request path does no DB I/O and revocations from another process are picked up within 2s. Nothing calls it yet, so merging changes no behaviour.
requirements: Format: `wak_` + 16 lowercase hex id + `_` + 52-char lowercase unpadded base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes, exactly 73 characters. `Parse` checks prefix, length, separator offset and alphabet before any hashing and returns a single `ErrMalformed`; `LooksLikeKey(s)` is exported for WorkerAuthenticator and later token endpoints. `Generate` retries on an id collision.

Scope registry: `type Scope string`, `Register(Scope, minRole)`, `Lookup`, `ParseScopes` (rejects unknown and duplicate scopes) and the constants `ScopeNone` and `ScopeSelf`. P2 registers policy:read, settings:read, traffic:read and audit:read at viewer; policy:draft and policy:write at editor; adminaudit:read, agents:read, agents:write and workers:admin at admin. The package doc says these are CP admin credentials, unrelated to auth.APIKeyInjector.

cpstate migration `api_keys/0001` with the columns in the feature design, `UNIQUE(owner_sub, name)` and indexes on owner_sub and expires_at. secret_hash is sha256 of the secret bytes. No code path deletes rows in P2; revoke sets revoked_at and revoked_by.

`type Store interface { Create; Get; List(ListFilter); Revoke(id, by); RevokeByOwner(iss, sub, by) (int, error); FlushLastUsed; Snapshot }` and `SQLiteStore` on *cpstate.DB. Create requires 1h <= ttl <= the caller-supplied maxTTL and enforces the caller-supplied per-owner active cap (`ErrInvalidTTL`, `ErrTooMany`).

`Index.Authenticate(token string, now time.Time) (Key, Reason, error)`: Parse, map lookup by id, `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` on sha256, then expiry and revocation against the injected clock. Every failure returns `ErrUnauthorized`; the Reason (malformed|unknown|bad_secret|expired|revoked) is for logs and the counter only.

Freshness: the Index is rebuilt synchronously after in-process Create, Revoke and RevokeByOwner, and `Run(ctx)` polls `PRAGMA data_version` every 2s and reloads on change. A reload error keeps the last good index. last_used_at and last_used_ip are recorded in memory and flushed in one transaction every 60s and on shutdown.
No exported method or String/LogValue returns or prints the secret, the plaintext or secret_hash.
plan: New internal/apikeys/doc.go and format.go: Generate, Parse, LooksLikeKey and ErrMalformed, using crypto/rand and base32.StdEncoding.WithPadding(base32.NoPadding) lowercased.
New internal/apikeys/scopes.go: Scope, Register, Lookup, ParseScopes, ScopeNone, ScopeSelf and the P2 registrations with minimum roles from the W-P1-SSO-02 Role type.
New internal/apikeys/store.go: the `api_keys/0001` migration registered with the W-P1-SSO-01 cpstate migration runner (not run until W-P2-APIK-02 enables it), the Store interface and SQLiteStore.
New internal/apikeys/index.go: Index with Authenticate, Rebuild, Run (data_version poll), MarkUsed and the 60s flush, copying the W-P1-WTOK-01 WorkerTokenStore structure.
New tests in internal/apikeys: format_test.go, scopes_test.go, store_test.go, index_test.go with a fake clock, and BenchmarkIndexAuthenticate.
acceptance: Given inputs `wwt_...`, `WAK_...`, 72- and 74-char strings, a secret containing `-`, `=`, `1` or uppercase, a missing `_` separator and the empty string, Parse returns ErrMalformed for each, and every Generate output round-trips: `go test ./internal/apikeys -run TestParse`

After a key is created through SQLiteStore, neither the 73-char plaintext nor the base32 secret appears in any column or in the raw warden-cp.db and -wal bytes, and secret_hash is 32 bytes: `go test ./internal/apikeys -run TestStoreNoPlaintext`

With a fake clock and a key expiring at T, Authenticate succeeds at T-1s and returns ErrUnauthorized with reasons expired (at T), revoked (after Revoke) and bad_secret (right id, wrong secret): `go test ./internal/apikeys -run TestIndexAuthenticate`

With two SQLiteStores on the same file, a revoke through store B is rejected by store A's Index within 2s, and with A's reload forced to fail, keys revoked before the failure stay rejected: `go test -race ./internal/apikeys -run TestIndexCrossProcessReload`

1000 Authenticate calls on one key run zero SQL statements against a counting store until the flush, after which last_used_at is written once; ParseScopes rejects `foo:bar`; Create with ttl 0, ttl above maxTTL or a 26th active key with cap 25 returns ErrInvalidTTL or ErrTooMany and writes no row
`go test -race ./internal/apikeys` and `scripts/check.sh` pass

tickets.title: Authenticate API keys and enforce per-route scopes in the authz table
tickets.body: Wire `wak_` keys into the CP request chain behind `console.apiKeys.enabled` (default false) and make the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table the single place that says which scope each admin route needs. A key is allowed only where a route names a scope it holds and its owner's current role still covers the route, so a new route is unreachable by keys until someone classifies it. Key-made requests are recorded in the admin audit chain under the owner. CP only; workers are untouched.
requirements: Config: add `APIKeys ConsoleAPIKeys{Enabled bool; DefaultTTL, MaxTTL Duration; MaxPerOwner, RatePerKey int}` to ConsoleConfig (`console.apiKeys`, json:"-"). Defaults enabled=false, defaultTTL 2160h, maxTTL 8760h (also the hard ceiling), maxPerOwner 25, ratePerKey 10. Enabled with console.auth != oidc or without --state-dir fails startup naming the setting. When disabled no migration runs and no middleware is installed.

Routes: no new prefix is mounted. Every key-reachable route is under /dashboard/api/*, and `/api/` stays reserved for a future public key-authenticated API (nothing is served there in P2). Add a `Scope` column to the authz table and classify every existing /dashboard/api/* row: policy:read (GET policy, policy/versions*, detection, blocked-users), policy:write (POST policy, POST detection, POST/DELETE blocked-users), settings:read (GET settings, which returns secretAccessKey only as a configured flag and its last 4 characters through dashboard.maskSecretsSettings), traffic:read (GET traffic, analytics, endpoints, workers, mcp, alerts, query/schema; POST query), audit:read (GET audit, POST audit/verify), adminaudit:read (admin-audit*). Every other row, including the never-keyable list in the feature design, is `ScopeNone`.

Authenticator: a `wak_` bearer on a table route goes only through apikeys.Index. Cookie plus `wak_` bearer gets 400 `ambiguous_credentials`; a key in the query string gets 400; failures get the uniform 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` and no session fallback. Cookieless key requests skip CSRF and Origin checks. Non-`wak_` bearers on /dashboard/* stay ignored as in W-P1-SSO-06. WorkerAuthenticator rejects a `wak_` bearer with 401 before the legacy compare.

Principal gains KeyID, Scopes and OwnerSub plus `ActorSub()`. Authz for Kind=apikey allows only when route.Scope is held, console.RoleFor(owner_groups) under the current config is at least the route's minimum role, and the per-field settings rules pass for that role; otherwise 403 `{"error":"insufficient_scope","need":"<scope>"}`. A per-key token bucket returns 429 above ratePerKey.

Admin audit: add `apikey` to the auth_method allowlist and `api_key_id` to the closed details allowlist; actor_id = HMAC(salt, owner sub), side row = owner sub and email, actor_role = owner's current role. Valid-key denials are chained with outcome=denied. Invalid keys write no row, only a rate-limited `apikey_auth_rejected` line with the parsed id or `malformed`, the reason and client_ip.

Counter `warden_cp_apikey_auth_total{outcome=ok|malformed|unknown|bad_secret|expired|revoked|insufficient_scope|rate_limited}` kept in memory with no per-key labels, for W-P5-RETN-06 to export. The middleware adds no DB I/O per request.
Neither the token nor its hash appears in any log line, audit row, error body or test output.

Other P2 admin routes stay under /dashboard/api/* and carry their Scope in the same table, set here or in their own ticket, whichever lands second: agents (agents:read GET, agents:write writes, W-P2-AREG-02); worker-enrollments (workers:admin GET and DELETE, ScopeNone POST because it mints a credential, W-P2-WCA-08); workers/{id}/revoke (workers:admin, W-P2-WCA-05); keys and token-sessions (ScopeNone, W-P2-KEYS-04 and W-P2-TOKX-07); changes (policy:read GET, policy:draft create, policy:write edit, submit, withdraw, rebase and replay, ScopeNone approve, reject, emergency-apply and review, W-P2-APPR-04). No P2 route lives under /api/; the API-key routes are /dashboard/api/api-keys* (W-P2-APIK-03).

New internal/controlplane/apikey_auth.go: withAPIKey authenticator, the ambiguous-credentials and query-string checks, the per-key token bucket, the rejection logger and the counter. Register it in controlplane.go Handler in the principal slot for /dashboard/api/* routes; mount nothing under /api/.

Tests in internal/controlplane: TestAPIKeyScopes, TestAPIKeyRejectedOutsideAdminAPI, TestAPIKeyOwnerDowngrade, TestAPIKeyAmbiguousCredentials, TestAPIKeyRateLimit, TestAPIKeyAdminAudit, and BenchmarkAPIKeyMiddleware.

A valid key holding every P2 scope gets 401 on /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest, /dashboard/ and /auth/me, and 403 on /central/secrets, POST /dashboard/api/secretstore, POST /dashboard/api/settings, POST /dashboard/api/worker-tokens and /dashboard/api/query/generate: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAPIKeyRejectedOutsideAdminAPI`

tickets.title: Add the API key management and self-introspection API
tickets.body: Add the CP routes that create, list and revoke API keys, plus `GET /dashboard/api/api-keys/self`, which p4-admin-mcp calls to learn its scopes. Only an OIDC console session can create a key, and the creator's role caps its scopes, so neither a break-glass session nor a key can mint lasting access. Revoke takes effect on the key's next request, and revoke-by-owner gives offboarding one call to remove a person's keys. The console page is W-P2-APIK-04.
requirements: Routes under /dashboard/api/, behind the same session, CSRF, admin audit and authz chain as every other admin route (W-P2-APIK-02): `GET /dashboard/api/api-keys` (own keys; all keys for admins; `?owner_sub=` filter for admins), `POST /dashboard/api/api-keys` with `{name, description?, scopes[], expiresIn?}`, `DELETE /dashboard/api/api-keys/{id}` (owner or admin), `DELETE /dashboard/api/api-keys?owner_sub=` (admin, returns `{revoked: n}`) and `GET /dashboard/api/api-keys/self` (`ScopeSelf`). All create and revoke rows are `ScopeNone`. With keys disabled every route returns 404.

Create is allowed only from a session with auth_method oidc; break-glass sessions and key principals get 403 `{"error":"session_required"}`. Each requested scope's minimum role must be at most the creator's current role, otherwise 403 listing the scopes. Unknown scope, empty scopes, or a name outside 1-64 chars get 400; a duplicate name for the owner gets 409; expiresIn defaults to defaultTTL and above maxTTL gets 400; exceeding maxPerOwner gets 409.

Create returns 201 `{id, name, scopes, createdAt, expiresAt, key}` with `Cache-Control: no-store`, and stores the creator's iss, sub, email and current groups as the owner snapshot. The plaintext appears in no other response, log line, audit row or Finding.

List and /self return id, name, description, scopes, effectiveScopes (scopes the owner's current role still covers), ownerEmail, createdAt, expiresAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt and status (active|expired|revoked); never the secret or secret_hash.

DELETE rebuilds the Index before returning 204, so the next request with that key gets 401. Revoking an already-revoked key returns 204 and writes no second audit row; an unknown id returns 404; an editor revoking another owner's key gets 403.

Admin audit: rows are `Audited:true` with actions `api_key.create`, `api_key.revoke` and `api_key.revoke_owner`, target `api_keys`, target_ref `api_key:<id>` and details {scopes, expires_at}; a `RegisterStateHasher("api_keys", ...)` hashes (id, scopes, expires_at, revoked_at).

Expose `apikeys.Store.RevokeByOwner` to in-process callers through a small `Server.RevokeAPIKeysForOwner(iss, sub, by)` method so the W-P1-SSO-08 `DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?sub=` path revokes that owner's keys too, and so p3-offboarding's Offboard(sub) can call it.

Add the api_keys state hasher through adminaudit RegisterStateHasher (W-P1-AAUD-02 pattern).
Add Server.RevokeAPIKeysForOwner and call it from the W-P1-SSO-08 session revoke-by-sub handler when keys are enabled.
Tests in internal/controlplane: TestAPIKeysAPIPlaintextOnce, TestAPIKeysCreateCaps, TestAPIKeysRevokeImmediate, TestAPIKeysRevokeOwner, TestAPIKeysValidation, TestAPIKeysSelf, TestAPIKeysDisabled404.

tickets.body: Give operators a way to kill a leaked key when the console is unusable, and stop old keys from coming back after a restore. `warden control-plane api-key list|revoke` writes to cpstate directly and a running CP picks the change up within 2s. summary: Adds an in-process security suite under test/security that attacks the identity, token exchange, worker mTLS, enrollment and signed-bundle paths of the real CP and worker code with known-bad inputs. Every case asserts the exact rejection reason, that nothing reaches the upstream, and that no token or swapped secret leaks; a positive control in each category proves the harness is not rejecting everything. The suite runs in the default scripts/check.sh test stage, so a regression in any of these controls fails every PR.
design: Location and gating: new package test/security as ordinary Go tests with no build tag, so `go vet ./...`, golangci-lint and the existing `go test -race -coverprofile ./...` stage in scripts/check.sh all compile and run it with no new flag. The suite is hermetic: loopback only, 127.0.0.1:0 ports, t.TempDir state, no Docker and no outside network. Budget: the whole package finishes in under 60s with -race on the CI runner. .github/workflows/ci.yml only calls scripts/check.sh, so no workflow change is needed.

Real code paths only. Workers start through `worker.Run(ctx, out, worker.Params)` from a generated YAML config, and the CP starts through a new `controlplane.Run(ctx, out, controlplane.RunParams)` that W-P2-SECT-05 extracts from runControlPlane in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go, so the harness and `warden control-plane` build the same server, TLS config (MintServerTLS plus ClientAuth=RequestClientCert from W-P2-WCA-04), token service, keys, worker CA, bundle signer, BlockStore and agent registry. No identity, mTLS, bundle or block check is re-implemented in test code.

Test seams (W-P2-SECT-05, Go-only): `worker.Params.TestHooks *worker.TestHooks{UpstreamDial, UpstreamRootCAs, OnReady}` and `controlplane.RunParams.OnReady` report bound addresses and let a loopback upstream fake be reached. proxy.New keeps NewSafeDialer for every real deployment: the hook is a Go struct field that no YAML key or flag can set, and a cmd/proxy test proves it is nil in the shipped binary.

Shared fakes in test/fakes (non-test files, keys generated at runtime, nothing committed, no import of internal/controlplane): `fakes.OIDCIssuer` promoted from the W-P1-VRFY-05 helper in test/integration (discovery, JWKS, token endpoint, claim, header, alg and key overrides, key rotation, Stop for issuer-down cases); `fakes.AgentKey` (Ed25519 or ES256 JWK and private_key_jwt assertion builder); `fakes.TestCA` (foreign CA, expired, wrong-EKU and multi-SAN leaves); `fakes.Upstream` (TLS server counting requests and recording headers and body); `fakes.TamperProxy` (sits between worker and CP on /policy and can replay, mutate or replace envelopes). The P1 SSO tests and P3 consent tests reuse OIDCIssuer.

Topology: one CP with tokenService, keys, workerCA, `--bundles=require`, `--require-worker-certs` and console OIDC login against fakes.OIDCIssuer; two workers pinned with `central.agentID` (agent-a and agent-b, W-P2-AREG-05), each enrolled with a `wet_` token, pinning `controlPlane.bundleKeys`, with `controlPlane.longPollWait: 2s` and observability metrics on. `tokenService.rateLimit` is raised for the matrix; one case uses the default. Each test category starts with a positive control: a valid user and agent request gets 200 through CONNECT, terminated HTTP/1.1 and MCP, the upstream sees exactly one hit carrying the swapped secret, and the bundle seq gauge is above 0. Attack subtests run only after it passes.

One case matrix: `Case{Name, Path(worker|token|cp-route|enroll|bundle), Attack, WantStatus, WantResult, WantReason, WantAudit, WantUpstreamHits}`. Assertion sources: the HTTP response (OAuth error, 407 with Proxy-Authenticate on CONNECT, 403 `identity_required` on terminated traffic (never 401, W-P2-WBND-03), 403 `user_blocked` or `agent_disabled`, plain JSON 403 on MCP); the worker deny event Reason from its SQLite store; the worker admin /metrics scrape (`warden_identity_verify_total{result,reason}`, the P1 instrument extended in P2, and `warden_bundle_rejected_total{reason}`); and on the CP, which has no metrics endpoint until W-P5-RETN-06, the admin audit row (`worker.revoked`, `worker.cert_lineage_conflict`), the cpstate `token_events` row (token denials are not admin-audited, W-P2-TOKX-04) or the captured rate-limited rejection log line with its reason.

Enum completeness: a test fails if any `identity.Reason` value, any `bundle.Reason` value, any token-service denial reason or any worker-facing CP route (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest, /control/enroll, /control/renew, /oauth2/token) has neither a matrix case nor an entry in `test/security/pending.go` naming the ticket that will add it. Later tickets remove their entries; the feature is done when the list is empty, so a new reason or route without a test breaks the build.

Leak invariant: the harness plants a canary swapped secret and a canary valid Warden token. After every case it checks that the token, every client assertion, subject_token, enrollment token and private key PEM never appear in the agent-visible response, the upstream request, CP or worker logs, admin audit rows, deny events or the /metrics scrape; that the swapped secret appears only in upstream requests of allowed cases; and that Proxy-Authorization and X-Warden-Identity never reach the upstream. Failure messages print kid and claim names only, never token strings.

Token attacks (worker and /oauth2/token): alg none; HS256 keyed with the CP public JWK bytes or the issuer RSA public PEM; a foreign key under a real kid; unknown kid; embedded jwk, jku or x5u header (ignored, so verification uses only bundle or JWKS keys); unknown crit; JWE-shaped 5-segment token; over 16 KiB; wrong iss or aud; missing exp; exp-iat over the TTL; expired and nbf-future at `identity.clockSkewSeconds` plus and minus 5s; missing act.sub or cnf. Type confusion: a raw Dex ID token in require mode (rejected whether `identity.acceptDexTokens` is true or false, attribution only in attribute mode); a console-audience token at the worker and as subject_token; a Warden token (aud warden-worker) as subject_token. Client assertions: replayed jti, wrong aud, exp over 5m, iss != sub, agent-b key claiming agent-a.

Issued-token lifetime: each case mints a valid token, warms the P1 verify cache (sha256(token) LRU) with one allowed request, then disables the agent, blocks the user through POST /dashboard/api/blocked-users, rotates the agent registry key out, or emergency-rotates the token key through POST /dashboard/api/keys/rotate. The next request must be denied within 3s (longPollWait 2s, and BlockStore and key changes wake the long-poll at once), and a CONNECT tunnel opened before the change is closed (W-P1-BLOCK-05). A stolen token replayed on the same agent's port is a documented known gap (no proof of possession in P2), kept as a skipped test.

Transport and bundles: on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, no cert, revoked, foreign-CA, expired, wrong-EKU and multi-SAN client certs get 401, and a `wwt_` token gets 401 in strict-certs mode; the worker refuses a CP server cert outside its `controlPlane.caCert`. Through TamperProxy each `bundle.Reason` (malformed, too_large, unsupported_format, unsigned including the legacy wire to a pinned worker, unknown_kid including an envelope signed with the token key, bad_signature, issuer_mismatch, credential_mismatch, rollback, equivocation, expired, future) leaves the worker on last-known-good with the same seq gauge and the same decisions. Rollback and future cases are signed with the pinned test key through `bundle.Sign`, so they reach the seq and time checks.

CP route boundaries and enrollment: a worker cert or `wwt_` token on /central/secrets and /dashboard/api/* never authenticates; a `wak_` API key on /policy and /oauth2/token is rejected; a console session cookie on /policy is ignored. /control/enroll rejects reused, expired and revoked `wet_` tokens with one identical 401 body, ignores CSR SANs (exactly one SPIFFE URI SAN), rejects RSA CSRs with 400; /control/renew rejects revoked certs and same-SPKI CSRs, and a renew from a superseded serial revokes the worker with `worker.cert_lineage_conflict`.

Degraded and restart modes: CP down mid-run keeps require-mode enforcement with the last-known-good JWKS, block list and disabled-agent state; a worker restarted with the CP down loads its bundle cache from `<controlPlane.stateDir>/bundle/` only after re-verifying it, and fails closed (deny all) on a tampered or too-old cache; a CP restart on the same state dir still rejects a replayed assertion jti and a used enrollment token; with the OIDC issuer stopped, exchange fails with no token minted and running workers keep serving valid Warden tokens.

Go native fuzz targets in test/security for the worker token verifier and `bundle.Verify` (no success unless the input equals a validly signed seed); their seed corpora run inside normal `go test`, and longer fuzz runs are manual and outside CI.
done_when: Plain `scripts/check.sh` runs test/security with no flag and no build tag on every PR and push to main, in under 60s with -race. Every matrix case is rejected with its expected status, result, reason and audit or log record, and reaches the upstream zero times, while each category's positive control reaches it once. test/security/pending.go is empty and the enum-completeness test passes. No canary token, assertion, enrollment token or key appears in responses, upstream requests, logs, audit rows, events or metrics. The PR for the last ticket records a drill showing the suite is not vacuous: disabling aud checking, cnf binding, cert revocation lookup and bundle signature verification, one at a time, each makes at least one case fail.

tickets.title: Add security test harness with in-process CP, workers and shared fakes
tickets.body: Create test/security with a harness that boots the real CP through controlplane.Run and two workers through worker.Run, plus shared fakes in test/fakes, so later tickets only add cases. The harness owns the positive controls, the case matrix runner, the leak invariant and the enum-completeness test, so no attack case can pass because the harness rejects everything or tests a copy of production code.
requirements: New package test/security with no build tag; it runs in the existing `go test -race -coverprofile ./...` stage of scripts/check.sh and is linted by golangci-lint with no config change. Loopback only, 127.0.0.1:0 ports, t.TempDir state, no Docker.

Promote the W-P1-VRFY-05 in-process issuer from test/integration/oidc_issuer_test.go into a new non-test file test/fakes/oidcissuer.go as `fakes.OIDCIssuer` (Mint with claim, alg, kid, key and header overrides, RotateKey, Stop), and switch test/integration to it. Add new `fakes.AgentKey`, `fakes.TestCA` and `fakes.Upstream`. test/fakes must not import internal/controlplane or internal/identity, and no private key is committed.

`StartStack(t, StackOptions)` runs controlplane.Run with tokenService, keys, workerCA, `--bundles=require`, `--require-worker-certs` and console OIDC login, then two workers with `central.agentID` agent-a and agent-b, `wet_` enrollment, pinned `controlPlane.bundleKeys`, `controlPlane.longPollWait: 2s`, metrics on and the upstream fake wired through worker.TestHooks. Readiness is awaited through OnReady and the bundle seq gauge, never sleeps.

Observation helpers: `Metric(t, w, name, labels)` parses the worker admin /metrics scrape; `AuditRows(t, cp, action)` reads admin audit rows; `DenyEvents(t, w)` reads the worker event store; `Logs(t)` returns captured CP and worker log output.

Case matrix runner `Run(t, []Case)` asserting status, result, reason, audit or log record and upstream hits per case, and `AssertNoLeak` after every case: no planted token, assertion, enrollment token or key PEM in responses, upstream requests, logs, audit rows, events or metrics; the swapped secret only in allowed upstream requests; Proxy-Authorization and X-Warden-Identity never at the upstream.

Positive control `TestHarness_ValidFlow`: an admin registers agent-a, a user exchanges a fakes.OIDCIssuer ID token at POST /oauth2/token, and the Warden token gets 200 on CONNECT, terminated HTTP/1.1 and MCP with exactly one upstream hit each.

Enum-completeness test over `identity.Reason`, `bundle.Reason`, token-service denial reasons and worker-facing CP routes, with a new test/security/pending.go listing every value not yet covered and the ticket key that will cover it.
`TestCanary` is skipped unless the new test-only env var WARDEN_SECURITY_CANARY=1 is set, then fails, which proves the stage gates check.sh.
plan: Move the issuer helper into new test/fakes/oidcissuer.go as fakes.OIDCIssuer with MintOption helpers (WithAlg, WithKID, WithKey, WithHeader, WithClaims) and update test/integration/identity_test.go to use it.

Add new test/fakes/agentkey.go (fakes.AgentKey with JWK() and ClientAssertion(opts)), test/fakes/testca.go (fakes.TestCA) and test/fakes/upstream.go (fakes.Upstream with atomic hit counter and header and body recorder), with unit tests in test/fakes.

Add new test/security/harness.go with StartStack: write CP and worker YAML under t.TempDir, run controlplane.Run and worker.Run in goroutines with a shared log buffer, enroll workers with `wet_` tokens created through POST /dashboard/api/worker-enrollments, and wait on OnReady plus the `warden_bundle_seq` gauge.

Add new test/security/actors.go: AdminSession(t) (console OIDC login and X-Warden-CSRF), RegisterAgent(t, id, key, groups) through POST /dashboard/api/agents, Exchange(t, agentKey, idToken) against POST /oauth2/token, and Request(t, worker, token, transport) for CONNECT, terminated HTTP/1.1 and MCP.
Add new test/security/observe.go (Metric, AuditRows, DenyEvents, Logs) and new test/security/matrix.go (Case, Run, AssertNoLeak).

Add new test/security/harness_test.go with TestHarness_ValidFlow, TestHarness_Budget (stack ready in under 10s with -race), TestEnumCompleteness, TestNoLeakGuard (a planted token in a log line makes AssertNoLeak fail) and TestCanary, plus new test/security/pending.go and doc.go describing how to run the suite.
acceptance: `go test -race -count=1 ./test/security -run TestHarness_ValidFlow` passes: 200 on all three transports, exactly one upstream hit each, and `warden_identity_verify_total{result="valid"}` rises by 3.
`WARDEN_SECURITY_CANARY=1 scripts/check.sh` exits non-zero with `FAIL` for test/security, and plain `scripts/check.sh` passes.
`go test ./test/security -run TestNoLeakGuard` passes, proving AssertNoLeak fails when a planted token appears in captured logs.
`go test ./test/fakes` passes and shows OIDCIssuer can emit alg none, HS256 and an unknown kid, and that `identity.NewOIDCVerifier` accepts its valid tokens.
`go test -tags=integration ./test/integration/...` still passes using fakes.OIDCIssuer, and `git grep -l 'BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY' test/` returns nothing.

tickets.title: Add token forgery, confusion and replay cases
tickets.body: Add the worker and /oauth2/token matrices for forged, malformed, confused and replayed tokens and client assertions. Each case pins its expected status, result and reason, so a regression in alg, kid, iss, aud, lifetime or type checks fails the build. A raw Dex token must never pass require mode, and Warden, console and Dex tokens must each be rejected wherever they are not the expected type.
requirements: Worker matrix in require mode for agent-a over CONNECT (407 with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="warden"`), terminated HTTP/1.1 (403 `{"error":"identity_required",...}`, never 401) and MCP (plain JSON 403, no JSON-RPC body): alg none, HS256 keyed with the CP public JWK bytes, a foreign key under a real kid, unknown kid, embedded jwk/jku/x5u header, unknown crit, 5-segment JWE shape, over 16 KiB, wrong iss, wrong aud, missing exp, exp-iat over 15m, expired and nbf-future at `identity.clockSkewSeconds` plus 5s, a token signed by the bundle key.
Boundary controls: tokens expired or not-yet-valid by `identity.clockSkewSeconds` minus 5s are accepted, so the leeway is tested from both sides with margins that -race slowness cannot flip.

Type confusion: a valid raw Dex ID token is rejected in require mode with `identity.acceptDexTokens` true and false, and gives attribution only (allowed on policy, identity fields set) in attribute mode; a console-audience token is rejected at the worker; Proxy-Authorization and X-Warden-Identity carrying different valid subjects give result conflict and a deny in require mode.

/oauth2/token matrix: subject_token forged (alg none, HS256 with the issuer RSA public PEM, wrong iss, wrong aud, expired), a Warden token or console token as subject_token, client_assertion with alg none, HS256, wrong key, unknown kid, iss != sub, aud other than the token URL, exp-iat over 5m, agent-b key claiming agent-a, and a reused jti. Each expects the RFC 6749 error (invalid_grant or invalid_client) and status 400 or 401.

Every worker case asserts a +1 on `warden_identity_verify_total{result,reason}` with the pinned reason, a deny event with the same reason and zero upstream hits; every CP case whose assertion verified asserts one `token_events` row with outcome denied and the pinned W-P2-TOKX-04 reason (earlier failures assert the rate-limited WARN line and counter instead) and a response body carrying only the error and reason code.

Rate limit: with the default `tokenService.rateLimit`, the 31st exchange in one minute for one user (default perUser 30/minute) gets 429 with Retry-After and a `token_events` row with reason rate_limited.

Fuzz target FuzzWardenToken in test/security feeds mutated tokens to the worker verifier; its seed corpus (the matrix tokens) runs in normal go test, and no input other than an unmodified valid seed verifies.
Remove the covered identity.Reason and token-service reason entries from test/security/pending.go.
plan: Add new test/security/forge.go with raw JWS helpers: header and claims JSON, base64url, signing with internal/keys signers, HMAC-SHA256 or none, and header injection.

Add new test/security/token_worker_test.go: positive control first, then the worker table run on all three transports for alg none and unknown kid and on CONNECT for the rest, through the matrix runner.
Add the Dex downgrade cases, restarting the stack with `identity.acceptDexTokens` true and false and with agent-a in attribute mode.
Add new test/security/token_exchange_test.go with the /oauth2/token table, including the replayed jti and the default rate-limit case on a separate stack.
Add new test/security/fuzz_token_test.go (FuzzWardenToken) with the forged tokens as seeds.
Remove covered entries from test/security/pending.go.
acceptance: `go test -race -count=1 ./test/security -run 'TestTokenWorker'` passes, and each case increments `warden_identity_verify_total` once with its pinned result and reason and leaves the upstream hit counter unchanged.

`go test -race -count=1 ./test/security -run 'TestTokenExchange'` passes, and each case returns its pinned OAuth error and status and writes one `token_events` row (when the assertion verified) containing no token string.

Given an accepted client assertion, when the same jti is resent within its TTL, then the CP returns 401 invalid_client and issues no token: `go test ./test/security -run TestTokenExchange/replayed_jti`.
A valid Dex ID token in require mode is denied with reason unbound_token with acceptDexTokens true and false: `go test ./test/security -run TestTokenWorker/raw_dex`.
`go test ./test/security -run FuzzWardenToken` runs the seed corpus and passes.

tickets.title: Add binding, cross-agent and issued-token lifetime cases
tickets.body: Add cases proving a valid token is bound to its agent and stops working when the agent, the user or the signing key is cut off, even while the 15-minute token is unexpired and its verify result is cached. This covers cnf and act.sub binding, an ambiguous worker agent id, group checks, the agent kill switch, the block list and emergency key rotation, each with a 3s deadline.
requirements: cnf mismatch: after agent-a's registry key is replaced through PUT /dashboard/api/agents/agent-a, a token minted with the old key is denied with reason cnf_mismatch once the worker's bundle seq advances, even though its verify result was cached.

Cross-agent: agent-a's valid token on agent-b's worker is denied with reason agent_mismatch on CONNECT and terminated HTTP. A worker with no central.agentID and two configured agents (agent id `agent:<port>`, not registered) denies every token in require mode with agent_unregistered.

Groups: a user whose groups do not intersect agent-a's allowed_groups gets unauthorized_client at POST /oauth2/token and a `token_events` row with reason group_not_allowed. A token issued before allowed_groups shrank stays valid on the worker until exp (the accepted gap stated in p2-worker-bound), and the case asserts that a new exchange is refused.

Disabled agent: after POST /dashboard/api/agents/agent-a/disable, a new exchange gets invalid_client, and within 3s every request on agent-a's worker gets 403 `{"error":"agent_disabled"}` with deny event Reason agent_disabled, including requests with a valid token; a tunnel opened earlier is closed. agent-b keeps working.

Block list: after POST /dashboard/api/blocked-users {sub}, within 3s the user's next request with a still-valid token gets 403 `{"error":"user_blocked"}`, the earlier tunnel is closed, a new exchange gets invalid_grant with reason user_blocked, and a second user is unaffected. The label is `user_blocked` everywhere.
Key cut: after POST /dashboard/api/keys/rotate {purpose: token, emergency: true}, a cached-valid token signed by the old kid is denied with unknown_kid within 3s, and a token from the new key works.
A skipped, documented `TestStolenTokenSamePort_KnownGap` records that a stolen token replayed on the same agent's port passes until exp in P2 (no proof of possession).
Each denial asserts the reason metric, the event or audit row and zero upstream hits, and removes its entries from test/security/pending.go.
plan: Add new test/security/binding_test.go: positive control on both workers, then cross-agent and ambiguous-agent-id cases (the latter starts a third worker without central.agentID).
Add the cnf rotation case: warm the cache with one allowed request, PUT a new key with If-Match, wait for the `warden_bundle_seq` gauge to advance, then present the old token.
Add new test/security/lifetime_test.go with a helper that opens a CONNECT tunnel, warms the cache, applies a cut, and polls every 100ms up to 3s for denial and tunnel closure.
Apply the helper to agent disable, user block and emergency token-key rotation, checking that the other agent and the other user still get 200.
Add the group-mismatch exchange case and the asserted allowed_groups-shrink behaviour.
Add the skipped known-gap test and update test/security/pending.go.
acceptance: agent-a's token on agent-b's worker is denied with agent_mismatch and zero upstream hits: `go test -race ./test/security -run TestBinding/agent_mismatch`.
A cached-valid token whose key was rotated out of the registry is denied with cnf_mismatch: `go test ./test/security -run TestBinding/cnf_rotated`.

Given a user with an open tunnel and a valid token, when an admin blocks them, then within 3s their next request gets 403 user_blocked, the tunnel is closed and a second user still gets 200: `go test -race ./test/security -run TestLifetime/user_blocked`.
After disable, every request on agent-a's worker gets 403 agent_disabled within 3s and a new exchange gets invalid_client: `go test ./test/security -run TestLifetime/agent_disabled`.
After an emergency token-key rotation, a cached token with the old kid is denied with unknown_kid within 3s: `go test ./test/security -run TestLifetime/token_key_revoked`.

tickets.title: Add worker cert and signed bundle attack cases
tickets.body: Add cases proving only valid, unrevoked worker certs reach the worker-plane routes and that a pinned worker applies only bundles that pass every check. Malicious bundles are served through fakes.TamperProxy, so the worker's real RemoteProvider and bundle.Verify are under test. After every rejected bundle the worker must keep its last-known-good policy.
requirements: With `--require-worker-certs`, direct HTTPS clients on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest get 401 for no cert, a foreign-CA cert, an expired cert (minted with a past NotAfter, no clock waits), a wrong-EKU cert, a multi-URI-SAN cert and a `wwt_` token; each matches a rate-limited CP log reason (bad_chain, expired, bad_eku, bad_san) and the positive control with an enrolled cert gets 200.

Revocation: after POST /dashboard/api/workers/{id}/revoke, a held /policy long-poll returns 401 within 1s, the next request on the same keep-alive connection gets 401, a `worker.revoked` audit row exists, and the worker keeps enforcing its last-known-good policy.
The worker refuses a CP server cert not chaining to its `controlPlane.caCert` (a stub CP using fakes.TestCA) and keeps its last-known-good policy.

New fakes.TamperProxy between worker and CP serves one case per `bundle.Reason`: malformed, too_large, unsupported_format, unsigned (including the legacy policyWire to a pinned worker), unknown_kid (including an envelope signed with the token key), bad_signature (one flipped payload byte), issuer_mismatch, credential_mismatch, rollback (an older valid envelope replayed, including the pre-block one), equivocation, expired and future. Rollback, equivocation, expired and future are signed with the pinned test key through `bundle.Sign`.

After each rejection `warden_bundle_rejected_total{reason}` rises by 1 with the matching reason, the next heartbeat carries lastRejectReason, the `warden_bundle_seq` gauge is unchanged, a host allowed only by the malicious bundle stays denied and a previously allowed host still gets 200.

Fuzz target FuzzBundleVerify calls bundle.Verify on mutated valid envelopes (including duplicate JSON members and trailing data) and asserts no input other than an unmodified seed verifies; the seeds run in normal go test.
Remove the covered bundle.Reason and route entries from test/security/pending.go.
plan: Add new test/security/workercert_test.go: positive control with the enrolled cert, then the cert table using fakes.TestCA leaves and a minted `wwt_` token, asserting 401 and the captured CP log reason.
Add the revocation case: hold a /policy long-poll and a keep-alive connection, call the revoke API with an admin session, and assert 401 timing, the audit row and unchanged worker decisions.
Add new test/fakes/tamperproxy.go (fakes.TamperProxy with Replay, Mutate and Replace hooks over /policy) and point a worker's controlPlane.url at it.
Add new test/security/bundle_test.go with one case per bundle.Reason, building validly signed hostile envelopes with bundle.Sign and the harness's pinned test signer.
After each case assert the metric delta, heartbeat lastRejectReason from the fleet API, the seq gauge and two probe requests.
Add new test/security/fuzz_bundle_test.go (FuzzBundleVerify) and update test/security/pending.go.
acceptance: After revoke, the worker's held long-poll returns 401 within 1s and its next heartbeat gets 401, with a `worker.revoked` row: `go test -race ./test/security -run TestWorkerCert/revoked`.
No cert, foreign-CA, expired, wrong-EKU and multi-SAN certs each get 401 on /policy: `go test ./test/security -run 'TestWorkerCert/(no_cert|foreign_ca|expired|bad_eku|multi_san)'`.

For every bundle.Reason, `warden_bundle_rejected_total` rises once with that reason, the seq gauge is unchanged and earlier allow and deny decisions hold: `go test -race ./test/security -run TestMaliciousBundle`.
A pinned worker served the legacy unsigned wire rejects it with reason unsigned and keeps last-known-good: `go test ./test/security -run TestMaliciousBundle/legacy_downgrade`.
`go test ./test/security -run FuzzBundleVerify` runs the seed corpus and passes.

tickets.title: Add Go-only test seams for in-process CP and worker runs
tickets.body: The suite cannot prove anything today: proxy.New always installs NewSafeDialer, which blocks the loopback upstream fake, and the CP is assembled only inside runControlPlane in cmd/proxy, which tests cannot import. Add Go-only seams so test/security drives the same assembly as the shipped binary and can reach a loopback upstream, without any YAML key or flag that could weaken the SafeDialer in production.
requirements: New `worker.TestHooks{UpstreamDial func(ctx, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error); UpstreamRootCAs *x509.CertPool; OnReady func(proxyAddr, adminAddr string)}` and field `worker.Params.TestHooks *TestHooks` (nil by default). It is passed to new `proxy.Config` fields `TestUpstreamDial` and `TestUpstreamRootCAs`; when nil, proxy.New keeps `NewSafeDialer(10*time.Second, nil)` unchanged.
No YAML key, env var or CLI flag can set the hooks. A new test in cmd/proxy asserts the worker command builds worker.Params with TestHooks == nil.

Move the assembly in runControlPlane (cmd/proxy/controlplane.go) into new `controlplane.Run(ctx context.Context, out io.Writer, p RunParams) error` in new internal/controlplane/run.go, mirroring worker.Run; RunParams carries every value the cobra flags set today plus `OnReady func(addr string)`. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go becomes flag parsing plus one call.

Behaviour is unchanged: existing cmd/proxy and internal/controlplane tests pass without edits, startup log lines and flag errors are byte-identical, and listening on port 0 reports the bound address through OnReady.
The hooks are documented in the Go doc as test-only, and a startup WARN `test hooks active` is logged if any hook is set, so accidental use outside tests is visible.
No secret, token or key appears in any new log line.
plan: Add new internal/worker/testhooks.go with TestHooks and thread Params.TestHooks into the proxy.Config built in worker.Run, calling OnReady after both listeners are bound.
Add the hook fields to proxy.Config and use them in proxy.New in place of the SafeDialer only when set; add a proxy unit test showing that with nil hooks a loopback dial is still blocked.
Add new internal/controlplane/run.go with RunParams and Run, moving the body of runControlPlane and binding the listener with net.Listen so OnReady gets the real address.
Reduce runControlPlane in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go to building RunParams from cpOptions and calling controlplane.Run.
Add new cmd/proxy/testhooks_test.go asserting TestHooks is nil for `warden run` and that no flag or config field references it.
acceptance: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestSafeDialerDefault` passes: with no hooks a CONNECT to 127.0.0.1 is still refused.
`go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestNoTestHooksInBinary` passes.
A test starting controlplane.Run on 127.0.0.1:0 receives the bound address through OnReady and gets 200 from /healthz: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestRunOnReady`.
`scripts/check.sh` passes with no change to existing tests, and `git grep -n TestHooks -- internal/config` returns nothing.

tickets.title: Add CP route-boundary and enrollment attack cases
tickets.body: Add cases proving each credential works only on the CP routes meant for it, and that enrollment and renewal cannot mint certs for the wrong worker or revive a revoked one. Worker certs and `wwt_` tokens must never reach human-only routes, API keys must never act as worker or agent credentials, and a renewal must never change the worker id.
requirements: A valid worker cert or `wwt_` token on /central/secrets (every method) and /dashboard/api/* gets 401 or 403 and never data; a console session cookie on /policy and /control/heartbeat does not authenticate.
A valid `wak_` API key (W-P2-APIK-02) on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /oauth2/token is rejected and never treated as a worker or agent credential.

/control/enroll: a reused, expired or revoked `wet_` token gets 401 with a byte-identical body; a CSR requesting extra SANs, a CN or CA:true yields a cert with exactly one SPIFFE URI SAN for the token's worker id, EKU clientAuth only and IsCA false; an RSA CSR gets 400 without consuming the token; the 11th request in a minute from one address gets 429.

/control/renew: a revoked cert gets 401 and no cert; a CSR with the current SPKI is rejected; a renew from a superseded serial outside the 10-minute window revokes the worker and writes a `worker.cert_lineage_conflict` row.
No case returns or logs the enrollment token, its hash or the CSR, checked through AssertNoLeak.
Remove the covered route entries from test/security/pending.go.
plan: Add new test/security/routes_test.go with a table of (credential, route, method, want status) covering worker cert, `wwt_`, `wak_` and console cookie, plus a positive control per credential on its own route.
Add new test/security/enroll_test.go creating `wet_` tokens through POST /dashboard/api/worker-enrollments and driving /control/enroll with crafted CSRs.
Parse issued certs and assert SANs, EKU, IsCA and the worker id from workerca.WorkerIDFromCert.
Add renew cases: revoke then renew, same-SPKI CSR, and a renew from the previous serial after the window, asserting the audit row.
Update test/security/pending.go.
acceptance: `go test -race ./test/security -run TestRouteBoundary` passes, and no worker cert, `wwt_` or `wak_` credential gets a 2xx outside its own routes.
A CSR asking for extra SANs yields a cert with exactly one SPIFFE URI SAN for the token's worker id: `go test ./test/security -run TestEnroll/csr_sans_ignored`.
Reused, expired and revoked enrollment tokens get byte-identical 401 bodies: `go test ./test/security -run TestEnroll/bad_token`.
A revoked worker's /control/renew gets 401 and issues no cert: `go test ./test/security -run TestRenew/revoked`.

tickets.title: Add degraded-mode and restart cases
tickets.body: Add cases proving the security controls hold when parts of the system are down or restart: the CP, the OIDC issuer and the worker itself. Require mode must keep enforcing from last-known-good state, a tampered or stale bundle cache must make the worker fail closed, and replay protection must survive a CP restart.
requirements: CP down mid-run: with the CP stopped, require mode keeps accepting valid Warden tokens and rejecting forged ones, the blocked user stays blocked and the disabled agent stays disabled until tokens expire.

Worker restart with the CP down and `controlPlane.stateDir` set (bundle cache in its `bundle/` subdirectory): a valid cache is re-verified against the pins and enforced; a cache with one byte changed, or older than `controlPlane.bundleCacheMaxAge`, is refused and the worker denies all traffic. Without a cache the worker stays fail-closed as today.
CP restart on the same state dir: a client assertion jti used before the restart is still rejected, a used `wet_` token still gets 401, and the block list and agent registry are unchanged.
OIDC issuer down (fakes.OIDCIssuer.Stop with a new signing key not yet fetched): exchange fails with an OAuth error and no token minted, and running workers keep serving existing valid Warden tokens.
Restarts reuse the same t.TempDir state dirs, and each case finishes in under 10s with -race.
After this ticket test/security/pending.go is empty, and the enum-completeness test runs with no pending entries.
plan: Add Stop and Restart helpers to test/security/harness.go that cancel the Run context and start again on the same state and config paths.
Add new test/security/degraded_test.go with the CP-down case using tokens minted before the stop.
Add the worker restart cases, tampering `<stateDir>/bundle/bundle.json` by one byte and rewriting its issuedAt past bundleCacheMaxAge through a re-signed test envelope.
Add the CP restart replay cases and the issuer-down exchange case.
Empty test/security/pending.go and make TestEnumCompleteness fail on any pending entry.
acceptance: With the CP stopped, a valid token still gets 200 and a forged one 407 on CONNECT: `go test -race ./test/security -run TestDegraded/cp_down`.
A worker restarted with the CP down and a one-byte-tampered bundle cache denies all traffic: `go test ./test/security -run TestDegraded/tampered_cache`.
A jti used before a CP restart is rejected with invalid_client after it: `go test ./test/security -run TestDegraded/cp_restart_replay`.
`go test -race -count=1 ./test/security` passes in under 60s with test/security/pending.go empty.

name: Security test suite
label: security-tests

summary: The CP runs OAuth authorization code + PKCE flows to third-party providers for signed-in employees, starting with Google and GitHub. Tokens go only to the CP-only user credential store `consent.store` (W-P3-CSIG-06; aws, or vault once W-P3-PUS-01 lands) under users/<userKey>/<provider>; workers never hold a credential for that store, the CP is the only party that refreshes or revokes a grant, and the CP database keeps only grant, pending and attempt metadata.
design: Gate and back-compat: the broker is mounted only when the CP-local `consent.providers` list is non-empty, the cpstate DB from W-P1-SSO-01 is open (--state-dir), the consent sign-in block (W-P3-CSIG-01) is configured, and `consent.store` (W-P3-CSIG-06) is configured and persistent (aws today, vault after W-P3-PUS-01). With no store or an echo store and providers set, CP startup fails with `oauth broker requires a persistent consent.store`, because EchoStore.Get returns the key itself. With no providers, no routes, migrations, goroutines or wire fields are added.

Provider config (CP-local, never on /policy): `consent.providers[]` {id passing secrets.ValidProviderID (W-P3-CSIG-06), type google|github|githubApp|generic, clientID, exactly one of clientSecretEnv or clientSecretKey (`oauth-clients/<id>` in consent.store, W-P3-BRKR-06), authURL, tokenURL, revokeURL, userinfoURL, allowedScopes[], defaultScopes[] (subset of allowedScopes), extraAuthParams, allowedAccountDomains[], requireEmailMatch}. `consent.connect.redirectURL` defaults to the origin of consent.oidc.redirectURL plus /connect/callback; `consent.connect.pendingTTL` defaults to 15m (allowed 1m-1h) and is also the JIT pending TTL (W-P3-JIT-01). Either secret source works for every type, because only the CP refreshes (W-P3-PUS-03). githubApp requires empty allowedScopes (permissions come from the app). extraAuthParams may not set client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, scope, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, nonce or include_granted_scopes.

Built-in endpoints, overridable (for GitHub Enterprise Server): google auth https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, revoke https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke, params access_type=offline and prompt=consent; github and githubApp auth https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize, token https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token, revoke https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/grant, userinfo https://api.github.com/user. generic requires authURL and tokenURL, all https except loopback.

Key layout: every key comes from the W-P3-CSIG-06 helpers: userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) (32 hex characters of a domain-separated SHA-256 over iss and sub) and secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider) = `users/<userKey>/<provider>` in consent.store. With the default namePrefix the AWS name is `warden-cp/users/<userKey>/<provider>`, and no email or raw sub reaches a secret name. The reserved prefixes `users/`, `idp/`, `revoking/` and `oauth-clients/` are owned by W-P3-CSIG-06 (config validation, storeFetcher and /central/secrets); W-P3-BRKR-06 adds the worker-local /dashboard/api/secretstore.

Data model (cpstate migrations oauthbroker/0001..0003, behind a GrantStore interface with a conformance suite for p5-postgres-ha): `pending_authorizations(id, iss, sub, user_key, agent_id NULL, provider, scopes_json, message NULL, request_method NULL, request_host NULL, request_path NULL, mcp_tool NULL, status pending|granted|denied|expired, reason, created_at, expires_at, completed_at)` is the long-lived intent shared with W-P3-JIT-01, which fills the request columns shown on the W-P3-PORT-03 landing page. `connect_attempts(state_hash PK, pending_id NULL, user_key, iss, sub, provider, scopes_json, verifier, browser_hash, created_at, expires_at +10m)` is one browser attempt, consumed once with DELETE ... RETURNING, like W-P1-SSO-03 oidc_pending (plaintext in the 0600 cpstate file; no extra encryption key). `oauth_grants(user_key, iss, sub, provider, grant_id, state connecting|active|reconsent_required|revoked, scopes_json, provider_account_id, provider_account_login, granted_at, updated_at, last_used_at, revoked_at, UNIQUE(user_key, provider))`. reconsent_required is set by the W-P3-PUS-03 refresh engine; the name leaves `grants` to the P4 delegation grants. No table has a column that can hold a token.

Start: `POST /connect/start` (form fields provider, scopes, pending, csrf) behind the W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session middleware, CSRF = the session's X-Warden-CSRF value as header or form field plus an Origin check. GET only redirects (303) to the PORT-03 landing page or /portal and changes nothing. Checks in order: provider exists; user not blocked (BlockChecker over controlplane.BlockStore, fail closed 503); a given pending belongs to this (iss, sub) (otherwise 404 identical to unknown) and is open; scopes ⊆ allowedScopes and, with a pending, ⊆ pending.scopes, else defaultScopes (400 scope_not_allowed before any row is written). The per-agent cap is applied when the pending is created (W-P3-JIT-01), so the broker trusts pending.scopes and needs no dependency on per-user secrets; without a pending, a caller may pass an extra ceiling (the portal passes allowedScopes ∩ the union of perUserSecrets scopes, W-P3-PORT-03). The exported Broker.Start returns the provider URL and is shared by POST /connect/start (303) and the portal JSON actions. The request asks for the union of the active grant's scopes and the new scopes. Rate limit 10/minute per user_key (internal/ratelimit, moved from W-P2-TOKX-04) and at most 20 open attempts per user.

Callback and write order: `GET /connect/callback` consumes the attempt by state hash, requires the browser cookie hash and the current portal session's (iss, sub) to match (403 before any code exchange), re-checks the block list, and exchanges code + verifier with golang.org/x/oauth2 (W-P1-SSO-03) using Accept: application/json, 10s timeout, no redirects and a 64 KiB cap; a 200 response with an `error` field is a failure. Then: (1) upsert oauth_grants with state=connecting and a new grant_id; (2) Put the oauthbroker.TokenRecord JSON at secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider) in consent.store {v:1, grant_id, provider, client_id, token_type, access_token, refresh_token, scope, expiry (absolute UTC, 0 when the token never expires), refresh_expiry, obtained_at}, keeping the stored refresh_token when the response has none; (3) set state=active with the returned scopes; (4) re-check the block list and, if blocked now, delete the key and revoke the grant; (5) complete the pending, which notifies subscribers. The previous token is never revoked on reconnect, because Google revoke ends the whole grant. The callback, the refresh engine (W-P3-PUS-03), RevokeUserGrant (W-P3-PORT-02) and offboarding all take oauthbroker.GrantLocks, one mutex per (userKey, provider).

Scopes: provider scope strings are parsed on spaces or commas. Granted scopes outside the cap (plus openid and email for account identity) mean nothing is stored (reason scope_exceeded). Granted scopes missing requested ones are stored as returned and the pending is marked denied with reason insufficient_scope so JIT callers stop retrying. A grant's token carries the union of its scopes; the per-agent cap is a consent-time ceiling and per-request limits come from egress policy.

Account identity: after the exchange the broker records the provider account (Google id_token sub, email and hd read from the token endpoint response; GitHub GET /user id and login; generic userinfoURL when set) and enforces optional allowedAccountDomains and requireEmailMatch (account email equals the portal session's verified email). A mismatch denies with reason account_not_allowed, and the token is dropped and revoked.

Refresh: workers never refresh and never receive provider metadata, client secrets or refresh tokens. W-P3-BRKR-07 adds the CP-side refresh_token client that the W-P3-PUS-03 engine calls, next to the code exchange (W-P3-BRKR-04) and revoke (W-P3-BRKR-05) clients, so every provider HTTP call lives in internal/oauthbroker and nothing is added to /policy or the signed bundle.

Failure modes: provider down fails the attempt and leaves the pending open for retry. Secret backend failure after the code exchange drops the token from memory, leaves the grant connecting and returns 503 secret_store_unavailable. A 1-minute sweeper (not the hourly analytics retention ticker) prunes attempts, expires pendings and moves `connecting` grants older than 10m to revoked after deleting any key; an hourly pass flags keys under users/ with no active grant. GetPending reports expired lazily. JIT status waiters are in memory per replica (documented for p5-postgres-ha).

Audit and observability: when admin audit is enabled, adminaudit.Recorder.Record gets connect.granted, connect.denied and connect.revoked with the new auth_method `portal`, target `grant:<provider>`, target_ref `grant_id:<id>` and details {provider, scopes, pending_id, provider_account_id}; an unhealthy Recorder fails the callback with 503 before the code exchange. No secrets.Ref, token, code, state, verifier or client secret appears in any row or log line. In-memory counters warden_cp_oauth_connect_total{provider,stage,outcome}, warden_cp_oauth_token_exchange_seconds{provider}, warden_cp_oauth_revoke_total{provider,outcome} and gauges for open pendings and orphaned grants are added to the W-P5-RETN-06 export list; labels use configured provider ids only.
done_when: With `consent.providers` and a persistent consent.store (aws, or vault) configured, a signed-in employee connects Google and GitHub through POST /connect/start and GET /connect/callback; the versioned token JSON with its grant_id lands at users/<userKey>/<provider> in consent.store (warden-cp/users/... on AWS), and a scan of the cpstate file finds no token bytes. A callback from another portal session, a blocked user, a scope outside the cap, a replayed state, an account outside allowedAccountDomains and a missing or echo consent.store at startup are all refused with no secret written. Reconnecting without a refresh_token keeps the stored one, static placeholders and secret-store writes under reserved prefixes are rejected, a stored grant refreshes through the CP provider client, and with no providers configured the CP behaves exactly as today.

tickets.title: Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults
tickets.body: Add `consent.providers[]` and `consent.connect` to the CP-local consent block and a provider Registry in new package internal/oauthbroker, with built-in endpoints for google, github and githubApp. Also add the shared scope helpers and the redacting token record type that every later P3 ticket uses; user keys come from W-P3-CSIG-06. Nothing is mounted, so behaviour does not change.
requirements: Config fields: id passing secrets.ValidProviderID (W-P3-CSIG-06), unique, type google|github|githubApp|generic, clientID, exactly one of clientSecretEnv or clientSecretKey (must equal `oauth-clients/<id>`), authURL, tokenURL, revokeURL, userinfoURL, allowedScopes, defaultScopes (subset of allowedScopes), extraAuthParams, allowedAccountDomains, requireEmailMatch; plus `consent.connect.redirectURL` and `consent.connect.pendingTTL` (default 15m, allowed 1m-1h; W-P3-JIT-01 uses it too). Strict parsing; the block never appears on /policy.

Validation: URLs absolute https unless loopback; generic needs authURL and tokenURL; githubApp needs empty allowedScopes; scopes contain no whitespace or commas; extraAuthParams rejects client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, scope, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, nonce and include_granted_scopes. redirectURL defaults to the origin of consent.oidc.redirectURL plus /connect/callback and must end in /connect/callback. Errors name the field path.

Defaults by type, each overridable: google auth https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, revoke https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke, access_type=offline, prompt=consent; github and githubApp auth https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize, token https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token, revoke https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/grant, userinfo https://api.github.com/user. Do not import golang.org/x/oauth2/google.

Client secrets: clientSecretEnv is read at startup and a missing variable is a fatal error naming the variable; clientSecretKey is read through an injected SecretResolver (wired to consent.store by W-P3-BRKR-06), and a read failure logs WARN and is retried on first use (503 provider_unavailable). Secrets live in a type whose String, GoString and LogValue redact them.

Shared helpers: `oauthbroker.ParseScopes` (space or comma separated) and `CapScopes(requested, allowed) (capped, rejected)`; `oauthbroker.TokenRecord` {v, grant_id, provider, client_id, token_type, access_token, refresh_token, scope, expiry, refresh_expiry, obtained_at} with Marshal/Parse (unknown versions rejected) and redacting String and LogValue. TokenRecord is the only stored grant format: W-P3-BRKR-04 writes it, W-P3-PUS-03 refreshes it and W-P3-PORT-02 reads it for provider revoke.

The registry is fixed after startup (change needs a CP restart, as for the console block). One startup INFO line `oauth_providers_loaded ids=[...]`; configs without consent.providers load and serve exactly as before.
plan: internal/config consent block (added by W-P3-CSIG-01): add OAuthProviderConfig and ConsentConnectConfig with strict-field registration and validation as in the existing secretstore config.
New internal/oauthbroker/provider.go: Provider, the defaults table, NewRegistry(cfgs, SecretResolver), Get(id) returning ErrUnknownProvider, and sorted List().
New internal/oauthbroker/scopes.go: ParseScopes and CapScopes, sorted and de-duplicated.
New internal/oauthbroker/token.go: TokenRecord{V, GrantID, Provider, ClientID, TokenType, AccessToken, RefreshToken, Scope, Expiry, RefreshExpiry, ObtainedAt} with redacting String/LogValue.
Tests: provider_test.go, scopes_test.go, token_test.go and an internal/config consent provider validation test.
acceptance: A google provider with only id, type, clientID and clientSecretKey gets the documented Google URLs and access_type=offline, prompt=consent. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRegistryDefaults`.

A generic provider without tokenURL, a duplicate id, an id starting with `_`, a non-loopback http URL, extraAuthParams with redirect_uri or include_granted_scopes, or a githubApp with allowedScopes fails validation with an error naming the field path. Verify with `go test ./internal/config -run TestConsentProvidersValidate`.
Registry.Get("unknown") returns ErrUnknownProvider and List returns only the configured ids, sorted.
TokenRecord JSON round-trips with v 1 and Parse rejects an unknown version. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestTokenRecord`.
slog JSON, %v and %#v output of Provider and TokenRecord contain no client secret or token value.

tickets.title: Add pending authorization, attempt and grant metadata stores
tickets.body: Add cpstate migrations for pending_authorizations, connect_attempts and oauth_grants behind a GrantStore interface in internal/oauthbroker, with a conformance suite so a Postgres store can replace it later. The pending row is the long-lived intent shared with W-P3-JIT-01; each browser attempt gets its own single-use row like W-P1-SSO-03 oidc_pending, so retries and second tabs do not overwrite each other. A dedicated 1-minute sweeper replaces the earlier plan to use the hourly analytics retention ticker.
requirements: Migrations oauthbroker/0001 pending_authorizations(id 16 random bytes base64url PK, iss, sub, user_key, agent_id NULL, provider, scopes_json, message NULL, request_method NULL, request_host NULL, request_path NULL, mcp_tool NULL, status CHECK pending|granted|denied|expired, reason NULL, created_at, expires_at, completed_at NULL) indexed on (status, expires_at) and (user_key); oauthbroker/0002 connect_attempts(state_hash PK, pending_id NULL, iss, sub, user_key, provider, scopes_json, verifier, browser_hash, created_at, expires_at +10m); oauthbroker/0003 oauth_grants(user_key, iss, sub, provider, grant_id, state CHECK connecting|active|reconsent_required|revoked, scopes_json, provider_account_id NULL, provider_account_login NULL, granted_at, updated_at, last_used_at NULL, revoked_at NULL, UNIQUE(user_key, provider)).

GrantStore methods (ctx, injectable now): CreatePending, GetPending (reports expired when expires_at <= now even before a sweep), CompletePending(id, status, reason) as compare-and-set from pending only (else ErrNotPending), CreateAttempt, ConsumeAttempt(stateHash) single use via DELETE ... RETURNING, BeginGrant (state=connecting, new grant_id), ActivateGrant(grantID, scopes, account), RevokeGrant(userKey, provider) idempotent, GetGrant, ListGrants(userKey, includeRevoked), TouchLastUsed(userKey, provider, at) at most one write per minute per pair (called by the W-P3-PUS-07 mint endpoint), Sweep(now).
Notifier seam: Subscribe(id) (<-chan Status, cancel func()); the channel closes after CompletePending or expiry, so W-P3-JIT-04 attaches later and nothing here references JIT.

Sweeper: started from the CP Server.Start only when the broker is enabled, every 1m; deletes expired attempts, marks expired pendings, deletes terminal pendings older than 7 days, and returns connecting grants older than 10m for the reconciler in W-P3-BRKR-04.
Limits: at most 10,000 live attempts in total, 20 open attempts and 20 open pendings per user_key; beyond that ErrTooMany.

No token, refresh token or client secret column or struct field exists; the verifier lives only in connect_attempts in the 0600 cpstate file and is never logged. Logs show pending ids and at most 8 hex chars of a state hash. With the broker disabled, no migrations run.
plan: New internal/oauthbroker/store.go: GrantStore interface, Pending, Attempt and Grant types, and the three Migration{ID, SQL} values passed to cpstate.Open from cmd/proxy/controlplane.go only when consent.providers is non-empty.
New internal/oauthbroker/store_sqlite.go: implementation over the cpstate DB, one statement per method, compare-and-set for CompletePending and DELETE ... RETURNING for ConsumeAttempt.
New internal/oauthbroker/notify.go: the Subscribe map, closed from CompletePending and Sweep.
New internal/oauthbroker/sweeper.go: RunSweeper(ctx, interval), started from controlplane Server.Start when the broker is enabled.
New internal/oauthbroker/oauthbrokertest/conformance.go: Run(t, newStore) covering every method.
Tests: store_test.go with a fake clock, a reflect test on Grant, Pending and Attempt, and a `PRAGMA table_info(oauth_grants)` column check.
acceptance: A pending past expires_at reads as expired before any sweep; after Sweep its stored status is expired and a Subscribe channel for it is closed within 1s. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestPendingExpiry`.
Two concurrent CompletePending calls on one id give exactly one success; the other returns ErrNotPending.
ConsumeAttempt returns an attempt once; a second call with the same state hash returns ErrNotFound.
BeginGrant then ActivateGrant twice for the same (user_key, provider) leaves one row with a new grant_id and advanced updated_at; RevokeGrant twice succeeds.

The 21st open pending for one user_key returns ErrTooMany, and no struct field or oauth_grants column is named or typed as a token, secret or value. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker/... -run TestGrantStoreConformance`.

tickets.title: Implement POST /connect/start with PKCE, CSRF and scope capping
tickets.body: Add `POST /connect/start` on the CP behind the portal session middleware. It checks the block list, caps scopes against the provider and the pending row, creates a single-use attempt with state and PKCE S256, and redirects to the provider. A GET changes nothing and only redirects to the landing page, so a cross-site link cannot start a consent flow.
