The per-agent cap is applied when JIT creates the pending (W-P3-JIT-01), so this ticket needs no per-user-secrets dependency.
requirements: POST form fields provider, scopes (space separated), pending, csrf; CSRF is the portal session's X-Warden-CSRF value as header or `csrf` field, compared in constant time, and Origin, when present, must equal the portal origin (403 csrf). GET /connect/start returns 303 to /portal/connect/<pending> or /portal and writes nothing.
Authentication: W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session middleware; no session gives 303 to /portal/login with a relative next; console sessions, worker tokens and API keys get 401.

Block list: an oauthbroker-owned BlockChecker implemented in internal/controlplane over controlplane.BlockStore and its snapshot (the W-P2-TOKX-02 pattern), matching sub exactly and lowercase email only when verified; a match gives 403 user_blocked and a read error gives 503, in both cases before any row is written.

Scopes: with a pending, it must belong to the session's (iss, sub) (otherwise 404 with a body identical to an unknown id), be status pending and unexpired (else 409 pending_not_active), and requested scopes must be a subset of pending.scopes; without a pending, requested scopes must be a subset of allowedScopes and of an optional caller-supplied ceiling (the portal passes allowedScopes ∩ the union of perUserSecrets scopes, W-P3-PORT-03), or defaultScopes are used. Any scope outside the cap gives 400 scope_not_allowed listing the names, before any row is written. The provider request asks for the union of the active grant's scopes and the capped scopes.

Attempt: 32-byte random state (only SHA-256 stored), oauth2.GenerateVerifier with S256 challenge, and a `__Host-warden_connect` cookie (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age 600) whose hash is stored as browser_hash. Redirect 303 with Cache-Control: no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer; extraAuthParams are appended; githubApp sends no scope parameter.

Limits: 10 starts per minute per user_key using the W-P2-TOKX-04 token bucket, moved without behaviour change into new leaf package internal/ratelimit so oauthbroker does not import tokensvc (W-P3-PUS-07 and W-P3-JIT-01 reuse it) (429 with Retry-After); ErrTooMany from the store gives 429. No outbound network I/O in this handler.

Gate: /connect/* is mounted only when the broker is enabled (providers set, cpstate open, persistent consent.store); otherwise 404. Providers configured with no consent.store or an echo one fail CP startup with `oauth broker requires a persistent consent.store`.

Observability: log line `msg=oauth_connect_start provider user_key pending_id scopes_count outcome reason` (never state, verifier or challenge) and counter warden_cp_oauth_connect_total{provider,stage="start",outcome}.
plan: New internal/oauthbroker/server.go: Broker{reg, store, blocks BlockChecker, limiter, cfg, now}, New(...), the exported Start(ctx, StartRequest) (redirectURL string, err error) shared with the portal JSON actions, and Handler() mounting /connect/start (and /connect/callback in W-P3-BRKR-04).
New internal/oauthbroker/start.go: handleStart with the check order above, CreateAttempt, the cookie and the AuthCodeURL built with oauth2.Config, oauth2.S256ChallengeOption and SetAuthURLParam.
internal/controlplane: new blockchecker adapter over BlockStore for oauthbroker.BlockChecker, and mounting of the broker handler in the CP mux only when enabled.

cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: build the Registry and GrantStore, refuse startup for a missing or echo consent.store when providers are set, and wire the broker. Move the W-P2-TOKX-04 token bucket into new internal/ratelimit and point internal/tokensvc at it.
Tests in internal/oauthbroker/start_test.go and a controlplane wiring test for the startup refusal and the 404 when disabled.
acceptance: A signed-in user with a valid CSRF token posting provider=google with allowed scopes gets 303; the Location carries code_challenge_method=S256, a code_challenge equal to base64url(SHA-256(stored verifier)), a state whose SHA-256 equals the stored hash, exactly the capped scopes and the configured redirect_uri, and __Host-warden_connect is set. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestConnectStart`.
A scope outside allowedScopes (or outside pending.scopes) returns 400 scope_not_allowed and connect_attempts and pending_authorizations gain zero rows.
A pending owned by another (iss, sub) returns 404 byte-identical to an unknown id, and a blocked user gets 403 user_blocked with no row written.
GET writes nothing and returns 303; a POST without valid CSRF returns 403; no session gives 303 to /portal/login; the 11th start in a minute returns 429.

With providers set and no consent.store or an echo one, CP startup fails with the documented error; with no providers, /connect/start returns 404. Verify with `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestOAuthBrokerGate`.

tickets.title: Implement /connect/callback and write tokens to the secret backend
tickets.body: Add `GET /connect/callback`: consume the attempt once, require the same browser and portal user, exchange the code with the PKCE verifier, and write a versioned TokenRecord to `secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider)` in consent.store. The grants row is written as `connecting` before the secret and set `active` after it, so a failed step never leaves a token the portal cannot see or revoke; a reconciler cleans up rows stuck in `connecting`. Connect events go to admin audit without any secret reference.
requirements: Consume the attempt by SHA-256(state); unknown, expired or replayed state, or a __Host-warden_connect hash mismatch, gives 400 state_invalid on a generic page. A portal session whose (iss, sub) differs from the attempt gives 403 before any code exchange; no session gives a 401 page and the code is not stored. The block list is re-checked before the exchange.

Exchange with oauth2.Config.Exchange and oauth2.VerifierOption, through an http.Client that sends Accept: application/json, has a 10s timeout, follows no redirects and caps responses at 64 KiB. A response with an `error` field (GitHub returns these with HTTP 200), an empty access_token or a non-bearer token_type is a failure. error=access_denied marks the pending denied; invalid_grant and other errors fail only this attempt and the pending stays open. Provider error text is never echoed to the user.

Scopes: parse the returned scope (spaces or commas; absent means the requested set). Granted scopes outside the cap plus openid and email give scope_exceeded, nothing stored, WARN logged. Granted scopes missing requested ones are stored as returned and the pending is completed denied with reason insufficient_scope.

Write order under oauthbroker.GrantLocks (new, one mutex per (userKey, provider), shared with W-P3-PUS-03, W-P3-PORT-02 and W-P3-OFFB-01): BeginGrant (connecting, new grant_id); consent.store Put of TokenRecord {v:1, grant_id, provider, client_id, token_type, access_token, refresh_token, scope, expiry absolute UTC or 0, refresh_expiry, obtained_at}, keeping the stored refresh_token when the response has none; ActivateGrant; re-check the block list and, if blocked, delete the key and revoke the grant; CompletePending(granted). The previous token is never revoked at the provider on reconnect.

If Put fails, the token is dropped from memory, the grant stays connecting and the page returns 503 secret_store_unavailable. The sweeper's connecting grants older than 10m are reconciled by deleting the key if present and marking the grant revoked; an hourly pass counts keys under users/ with no active grant into an orphan gauge.

Audit: when admin audit is enabled, an unhealthy Recorder gives 503 admin_audit_unavailable before the exchange; connect.granted and connect.denied are recorded with actor = portal sub, auth_method `portal` (new value), target `grant:<provider>`, target_ref `grant_id:<id>`, details {provider, scopes, pending_id}. A slog line `msg=connect schema=warden.consent.v1` is always written. No secrets.Ref, token, code, state or verifier appears in any row or line.

On success, 303 to fixed internal paths only: /portal/connect/<pending>?result=granted or /portal?connected=<provider>. Counters warden_cp_oauth_connect_total{stage="callback"} and warden_cp_oauth_token_exchange_seconds{provider}.
plan: New internal/oauthbroker/callback.go: handleCallback with the checks, exchange, scope handling and write order above.

New internal/oauthbroker/exchange.go: the provider http.Client (dials through proxy.NewSafeDialer from internal/proxy/safedial.go so generic provider URLs cannot reach private addresses; tests inject a client) and the error-field check.
New internal/oauthbroker/reconcile.go: reconciler run from the W-P3-BRKR-02 sweeper; new internal/oauthbroker/locks.go: GrantLocks.
internal/adminaudit: add `portal` to the validated auth_method set.

New test/fakes/oauthprovider.go (httptest authorize and token endpoints with PKCE check, Google-style JSON and GitHub-style comma scopes and 200-with-error); tests use fakes.MemorySecretStore from W-P3-CSIG-06 as consent.store.
Tests in internal/oauthbroker/callback_test.go, including a log and audit capture test.
acceptance: Start then callback against fakes.OAuthProvider leaves fakes.MemorySecretStore holding users/<userKey>/google with the fake's access_token and a grant_id equal to the active grants row, the pending granted, and its Subscribe channel closed within 1s. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestConnectCallback`.

A callback with a valid state but a different portal user returns 403, the fake token endpoint receives 0 requests and the store and grants stay empty; replaying a used state returns 400 state_invalid.
error=access_denied sets the pending denied and records connect.denied; a GitHub-style HTTP 200 with error=bad_verification_code writes no secret and leaves the pending open.
A reconnect whose response lacks refresh_token keeps the previously stored refresh_token; a granted scope outside the cap writes no secret and no active grant.
With fakes.MemorySecretStore set to fail Put, the response is 503 secret_store_unavailable and after the reconciler runs the grant is revoked and no key exists.
Logs and audit rows across all cases contain no access token, refresh token, code, state, verifier or `sha256:` reference. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestCallbackNoSecretLeak`.

tickets.title: Add provider revoke client for Google and GitHub
tickets.body: Add `oauthbroker.Revoke(ctx, provider, rec TokenRecord)` for Google, GitHub, GitHub Apps and RFC 7009 generic providers. It only calls the provider; deleting the secret and the grant row stays with W-P3-PORT-02 RevokeUserGrant and W-P3-OFFB-01. It is a pure library, so it can be built in parallel with the HTTP tickets.
requirements: Google: POST revokeURL form-encoded token=<refresh_token>, falling back to access_token; 200 is success and 400 invalid_token counts as already revoked.

github and githubApp: DELETE revokeURL (default https://api.github.com/applications/{client_id}/grant) with basic auth clientID:clientSecret, JSON body {"access_token":...}, Accept: application/vnd.github+json; any 2xx is success, 404 is already revoked, 422 is a permanent error. Document that this removes every token of that app for the user.
generic: RFC 7009 POST token plus token_type_hint=refresh_token with client_secret_basic; no revokeURL returns ErrRevokeUnsupported with no HTTP call, so callers still delete the stored secret.

Errors: *RevokeError{Provider, Status, Retryable}; network errors, 429 and 5xx are retryable, 401 and 403 are not. 10s timeout, no redirects, response read capped at 16 KiB; error strings never contain the token or the response body.
Observability: counter warden_cp_oauth_revoke_total{provider,outcome=ok|already|retryable|failed|unsupported} and `msg=oauth_revoke provider user_key status outcome duration_ms`, never the token.
plan: New internal/oauthbroker/revoke.go: Revoke, RevokeError and ErrRevokeUnsupported, using the provider http.Client shape from W-P3-BRKR-01 config (injectable for tests).
Per-type request builders for google, github/githubApp and generic in the same file.
Tests: internal/oauthbroker/revoke_test.go with httptest servers for each provider type and a log-capture check.
acceptance: The fake Google endpoint receives form-encoded token equal to the refresh token, or the access token when the refresh token is empty. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRevokeGoogle`.

The fake GitHub endpoint receives DELETE /applications/<client_id>/grant with client basic auth and an access_token JSON body, and 204 returns nil. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRevokeGitHub`.
Google 400 invalid_token and GitHub 404 return nil and record outcome=already.
A 503 returns RevokeError with Retryable=true and a 401 returns Retryable=false.
A generic provider without revokeURL returns ErrRevokeUnsupported and the fake receives no request; no token substring appears in logs or error strings.

tickets.title: Guard reserved prefixes on the worker dashboard and load client secrets from consent.store
tickets.body: W-P3-CSIG-06 owns the reserved prefixes (`users/`, `idp/`, `revoking/`, `oauth-clients/`) and enforces them in config validation, storeFetcher and /central/secrets. This ticket covers the remaining write surface, the dashboard secret-store tab (/dashboard/api/secretstore), and resolves provider client secrets from consent.store at `oauth-clients/<id>`, so a client secret never sits in the store whose credential the CP sends to workers. Operators load client secrets directly in the backend or use clientSecretEnv; no console path writes them.
requirements: /dashboard/api/secretstore POST and DELETE return 403 {"error":"reserved_key"} for keys where secrets.IsReservedKey is true, and its List hides them, matching the W-P3-CSIG-06 /central/secrets behaviour.

clientSecretKey must equal secrets.ClientSecretKey(id). The Registry's SecretResolver reads it from consent.store at startup; a read failure logs WARN with the key only and is retried on first use (503 provider_unavailable). It is never read from the distributed secretStore.
No flag or route writes `oauth-clients/` keys through /central/secrets or the dashboard; docs/consent-portal.md (W-P3-PORT-04) gives the aws secretsmanager and vault kv commands for loading them.
The broker, the W-P3-PUS-03 refresh engine and W-P3-OFFB-01 use consent.store directly and are not affected by the guard.
With no reserved keys in use, every existing request and config behaves exactly as before.
plan: internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go: enforce secrets.IsReservedKey in handleSecretStore for writes, deletes and List.
internal/oauthbroker/provider.go: a SecretResolver over consent.store and the clientSecretKey rule; cmd/proxy/controlplane.go passes the consent.store built by W-P3-CSIG-06.
Tests in internal/dashboard and internal/oauthbroker.
acceptance: POST and DELETE /dashboard/api/secretstore for `users/x/google` and `oauth-clients/google` return 403 reserved_key and the store is unchanged, and its List omits reserved keys while still listing other keys. Verify with `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestSecretStoreReservedKey`.

A google provider with clientSecretKey `oauth-clients/google` resolves its secret from a fake consent.store and never calls the distributed secretStore; clientSecretKey `oauth-clients/other` for provider google fails validation. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestClientSecretFromUserStore`.
A failed read at startup logs only the key, and the first connect returns 503 provider_unavailable.

tickets.title: Add the provider refresh-token client for CP-side refresh
tickets.body: The CP is the only refresh authority (W-P3-PUS-03): workers never receive provider metadata, client secrets or refresh tokens, so no provider projection goes on /policy. Add the provider HTTP client for the refresh_token grant next to the code exchange (W-P3-BRKR-04) and revoke (W-P3-BRKR-05) clients, so every call to a provider token endpoint lives in internal/oauthbroker with the same hardening. It is a pure library; the W-P3-PUS-03 engine calls it.
requirements: `oauthbroker.Refresh(ctx, provider, rec TokenRecord, clientSecret) (TokenRecord, error)` posts grant_type=refresh_token to provider.TokenURL with client_secret_basic for google and generic and client_secret_post for github and githubApp, with Accept: application/json.

The HTTP client is https only except loopback, dials through proxy.NewSafeDialer so generic provider URLs cannot reach private addresses, follows no redirects, has a 5s timeout and caps responses at 64 KiB. A 200 with an `error` field is a failure.

The returned record keeps the stored refresh_token when the response has none, sets expiry from expires_in against local receipt time, sets refresh_expiry when the provider returns one, and keeps grant_id, provider and client_id.

Errors form a closed set: ErrRefreshInvalidGrant for invalid_grant, a permanent error for other 4xx, and a retryable error for 429, 5xx and network failures. Only the OAuth `error` code is kept, never error_description or the body.
A record with expiry 0 and no refresh_token (GitHub OAuth app) returns ErrNotRefreshable with no HTTP call.
Counter warden_cp_oauth_refresh_total{provider,outcome}; no token or client secret appears in logs or error strings.
plan: New internal/oauthbroker/refresh.go: Refresh, the error values and a request builder per provider type, using the provider http.Client shape from W-P3-BRKR-01 config (injectable for tests).
Add the counter next to the other oauthbroker counters.
Tests: internal/oauthbroker/refresh_test.go with httptest token endpoints for each provider type and a log-capture check.
acceptance: The fake Google endpoint receives grant_type=refresh_token with client basic auth; a response without refresh_token keeps the stored one and a rotated one is returned. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRefreshGoogle`.
A GitHub App refresh sends client_secret_post and a response with refresh_token_expires_in sets refresh_expiry. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRefreshGitHubApp`.
invalid_grant returns ErrRefreshInvalidGrant, 503 is retryable, a 200 with error=bad_refresh_token is a failure, and a GitHub OAuth-app record makes no HTTP call.
No log line or error string contains a token, the client secret or the response body.

tickets.title: Record the connected provider account and enforce account rules
tickets.body: Nothing records which external account was connected, so a user could connect a personal Gmail or another person's GitHub account and agents would act on it. After the code exchange, identify the account, store it on the grant, and enforce the optional allowedAccountDomains and requireEmailMatch rules before the token is written.
requirements: Google: add `openid email` to the request (exempt from the scope cap) and read sub, email, email_verified and hd from the id_token returned directly by the token endpoint over TLS, checking iss and aud=clientID; set the `hd` auth param when allowedAccountDomains has one entry.
github and githubApp: GET userinfoURL (default https://api.github.com/user) with the new token and read id, login and email; generic: use userinfoURL when set, else record nothing.

allowedAccountDomains: the account email domain (or Google hd) must match; requireEmailMatch: the account email must equal the portal session's verified email, case-insensitive. A mismatch completes the pending denied with reason account_not_allowed, drops the token and revokes it with W-P3-BRKR-05, and writes no secret.

provider_account_id and provider_account_login (the GitHub login, or the Google account email) are stored on the grant and added to the connect.granted audit details; the portal shows provider_account_login to its owner as account_label (W-P3-PORT-01), and the portal session email is not stored.
With neither rule set, identification failures are logged and the connect proceeds; with a rule set, failure to identify denies.
plan: New internal/oauthbroker/account.go: Identify(ctx, provider, token) (Account, error) per type.
internal/oauthbroker/callback.go: call Identify before BeginGrant and enforce the rules; pass the account to ActivateGrant.
test/fakes/oauthprovider.go: add an id_token and a /user endpoint to the fake.
Tests in internal/oauthbroker/account_test.go.
acceptance: A fake Google id_token with hd=example.com connects when allowedAccountDomains=[example.com] and the grant records the provider account id. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestAccountRules`.
An account with hd=gmail.com, or an email different from the session's with requireEmailMatch, gives denied account_not_allowed, no secret written and one revoke request at the fake.
A GitHub connect stores the /user id and login on the grant.

tickets.title: Add end-to-end OAuth broker test with fake Google and GitHub
tickets.body: Every other ticket tests one handler. This test runs a real CP with consent sign-in, the broker and the AWS secret store over a fake AWS client, plus fake Google and GitHub providers, and proves the done_when sentence including the refusal cases. It runs behind the existing integration build tag, so normal `go test ./...` is unaffected.
requirements: Happy path for google and github: portal login, POST /connect/start, provider redirect, callback; the fake AWS client behind consent.store holds `warden-cp/users/<userKey>/<provider>` with a versioned token JSON, and nothing is written under the distributed secretStore prefix.

Refusals with no secret written: callback from another portal session, blocked user, scope outside the cap, replayed state, account outside allowedAccountDomains, missing or echo consent.store at startup.

Reconnect without refresh_token keeps the stored refresh_token; /central/secrets writes under users/ return 403 reserved_key; a stored grant refreshes through the W-P3-BRKR-07 client against the fake provider.
After all cases, a byte scan of the cpstate file finds no access or refresh token, and a log scan finds no token, code, state or verifier.
Runs without Docker or network access to real providers.
plan: New test/integration/oauthbroker_test.go under the integration build tag.
Reuse test/fakes.OAuthProvider and the fake IdP from the consent sign-in tests; add a fake AWSSecretsClient if one is not already in test/fakes.

Add a manual check list for a real Google Web client, a GitHub OAuth App and a GitHub App to the W-P3-PORT-04 guide notes, including whether GitHub accepts PKCE for each app type (state, the browser cookie and the session binding protect the flow either way).
acceptance: `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestOAuthBrokerE2E` passes.
The test fails if any refusal case writes a secret or a grant in state active.
The cpstate byte scan and the log scan find no token, code, state or verifier.

name: OAuth broker
label: oauth-broker

summary: A small employee-facing UI on the CP at /portal. It lists the user's connected accounts with the agents that used each one in the last 7 days, lets the user connect or revoke a provider, and hosts the landing page for a pending authorization created by a JIT 403. Revoke deletes the stored tokens, revokes them at the provider and reaches every worker through the policy wire, so the next agent call returns authorization_required. It is off unless the CP-local consent block and --state-dir are set.
design: Gate and mount: the portal mounts only when the CP-local `consent` block (W-P3-CSIG-01) is set and --state-dir is present. Otherwise /portal/* returns 404 and /policy stays byte-identical. The package internal/portal (created by W-P3-CSIG-02) gains an embedded index.html plus app.js (go:embed, same pattern as internal/dashboard/dashboard.go), the JSON API under /portal/api/*, and the server-rendered landing page /portal/connect/{pending_id}.

Naming: employees see 'connections', so the API is /portal/api/connections. The word 'grants' is left to the P4 delegation grants (/portal/grants/{id}). The OAuth metadata table owned by W-P3-BRKR-02 is oauth_grants; this feature only calls the GrantStore Go API.

Auth and isolation: every /portal route uses the W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session (__Host-warden_portal) with consent.session.idle and consent.session.absolute (the console's key names; defaults 30m and 8h from W-P3-CSIG-01). Non-GET requests require the X-Warden-CSRF header plus an Origin check; the page sends it through one shared api() wrapper (W-P1-SSO-04 convention). /portal/api/me and POST /portal/logout come from W-P3-CSIG-04 and are not added again. Console sessions, WARDEN_CP_TOKEN, worker credentials, Warden user tokens and wak_ API keys get 401, so an agent holding a delegated token can never connect, continue, decline or revoke. A sub or email on the W-P1-BLOCK-03 block list gets 403 user_blocked from the W-P3-CSIG-04 middleware (in-memory snapshot, not a per-request query), which also deletes its portal sessions; this feature adds no second check.

Security headers on every /portal and /connect response: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'`, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy no-referrer (the pending id never leaks to a provider), X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and Cache-Control no-store. All dynamic text is set with textContent. The page has a viewport meta tag and no fixed width over 360px.

GET /portal/api/connections -> 200 {usage_available, usage_window_start, connections:[{provider, display_name, account_label, scopes, granted_at, last_used_at, recent_agents:[{agent, agent_display, verified, last_used_at, calls_7d}]}], available:[{provider, display_name, scopes_cap}]}. Connections come from GrantStore.ListGrants(userKey) without revoked rows, with userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) from the session; account_label is the grant's provider_account_login (W-P3-BRKR-08) and last_used_at is oauth_grants.last_used_at. `available` lists registry providers that at least one perUserSecrets wire mapping (W-P3-PUS-02) references and the user has not connected. The sub always comes from the session, never from a request parameter.

Usage data: analytics.Event.UserTokenProvider (column user_token_provider, W-P3-PUS-10, set by W-P3-PUS-04 only when a per-user token was swapped) is separate from Event.Provider, the LLM cost provider. The fleet agent_id column is filled at ingest by W-P3-PUL-07 and user_sub comes from W-P1-VRFY-06, so this feature adds no event columns. The portal reads per-agent usage through a new typed method FleetSQLiteStore.GrantUsage(ctx, sub, since, perProviderLimit) with bind parameters, never through the Query Builder's AnalyticsQuery.Query. A connection's last_used_at is oauth_grants.last_used_at, fed by the CP mint endpoint (W-P3-PUS-07 calls GrantStore.TouchLastUsed), so it does not depend on analytics. With the memory fleet store, a query error or a 2s timeout, usage_available is false and connections still list.

Connect and continue: the portal calls Broker.Start from W-P3-BRKR-03 and gets back the provider URL; it never sends the browser to a provider from a plain GET link an agent could post. POST /portal/api/connect {provider} -> 200 {redirect_url}; with no pending, the scope cap is provider.allowedScopes ∩ the union of scopes over every perUserSecrets mapping for that provider (passed to Broker.Start as the caller ceiling). POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/continue -> 200 {redirect_url}. POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/decline -> 200 and calls GrantStore.CompletePending(id, denied), which closes the W-P3-BRKR-02 Subscribe channel that p3-jit status waiters wait on. W-P3-BRKR-08 records the connected account (provider_account_login: the Google email or GitHub login, shown as account_label) and enforces optional consent.providers[].allowedAccountDomains.

Pending landing: GET /portal/connect/{pending_id}. Signed-out users go to /portal/login with next set to the path; next must be a relative path under /portal/ or /connect/ with no scheme, no `//` and no backslash (the W-P3-CSIG-02 rule). The page shows only text Warden builds: the agent display name with a verified or unregistered badge from the agent registry (W-P2-AREG-04 wire), the provider, the capped scopes, the request host, method and MCP tool when the pending carries them (W-P3-BRKR-02 request columns, filled by W-P3-JIT-01), the expiry as a relative time from the CP clock, and 'Signed in as <email>. Not you? Sign out'. There is no free-text agent message. Unknown, expired, terminal and other users' pending ids all return 404 with the same body.

Revoke: POST /portal/api/connections/{provider}/revoke -> 200 {status: revoked|partial, steps:{grant, secret_delete, epoch, provider_revoke: ok|pending|failed|skipped}, workers_without_cap}, 404 when no grant was ever recorded, 409 while a revoke for the same (user, provider) is running, and an idempotent 200 for an already revoked grant. It calls the shared oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant(ctx, iss, sub, provider, Actor{ID, Kind: user|admin|system, Reason}), which W-P3-OFFB-01 reuses with Kind system. Steps run inside Engine.WithGrantLock(userKey, provider) (W-P3-PUS-03, over the oauthbroker.GrantLocks mutex shared with the BRKR-04 callback), which also drops the CP token cache entry: (1) read the TokenRecord into memory; (2) GrantStore.RevokeGrant; (3) delete users/<userKey>/<provider> from consent.store; (4) EpochStore.Bump(userKey) (W-P3-PUS-08, through the W-P3-PORT-05 adapter) so workers drop cached tokens; (5) oauthbroker.Revoke (W-P3-BRKR-05) with the in-memory token. Delete runs before the bump, so a mint after eviction finds nothing.

Worker invalidation: the userGrantEpochs signed-bundle section from W-P3-PUS-08 ({userKey: epoch}, epoch = the publish_log seq of the bump, pruned after 2 x workerCacheTTL) is the only revocation channel to workers; this feature adds no table, wire field or heartbeat cap of its own. The section lives outside policy versions, so a rollback never un-revokes, and its keys are user keys, so no sub appears on the wire.

Worker side: W-P3-PUS-09 evicts cached tokens on each verified bundle apply and caps any cached token at perUserSecrets.workerCacheTTL (at most 15m), which also bounds GitHub tokens that never expire. Workers never write tokens back; only the CP refresh engine does, and it re-checks grant state, epoch and grant_id first (W-P3-PUS-03, W-P3-PUS-06). Workers that enforce this advertise heartbeat cap usersecrets/v1, and the revoke response lists connected workers without it (W-P3-PORT-05).

Failure handling: if the provider revoke fails with a retryable error, the TokenRecord is parked in consent.store at secrets.RevokingKey(userKey, provider) = revoking/<userKey>/<provider> and a CP ticker retries with backoff for up to 24h, then deletes it and raises an alert through internal/alertpipeline. A non-retryable failure gives up at once and the UI shows the provider's manual revoke link. An orphan sweep, run about 2 minutes after each revoke and on every CP retention tick, lists users/ metadata in consent.store (never values) and deletes any users/<userKey>/<provider> key that has no active oauth_grants row; this removes a rotated refresh token that a racing CP refresh wrote back after the delete.

Audit and logs: when console.adminAudit.enabled, connect.started, connect.declined and connect.revoked are recorded through adminaudit.Recorder (W-P1-AAUD-01) with new auth_method portal, target_ref grant:<provider> and per-step outcomes in details, never a token or secret Reference value. A structured log line with the same fields is always written, and W-P1-JAUD-03 emits the warden.admin.v1 line when admin audit is on. Unauthenticated requests are never chained. Logs never contain tokens, codes, cookies or CSRF tokens.

Degraded modes: CP down means the portal is unavailable and workers serve cached tokens for at most workerCacheTTL. IdP down means existing sessions keep working and /portal/login returns 503 idp_unavailable. Provider down means connect shows an error page and revoke takes the retry path. A CP restart loses nothing, because sessions, pendings, epochs and the retry queue are in cpstate. Mutating portal endpoints are limited to 10 per minute per session. GrantStore and the epoch store are interfaces, so p5-postgres-ha can replace them.
done_when: On a CP with the consent block, --state-dir and a Vault or AWS consent.store, an employee signed in at /portal sees each connected provider with its account label, scopes, last_used_at and only the agents that used their own grant in the last 7 days. They can connect a new provider within the computed scope cap, and open a pending link an agent posted to either continue (the pending becomes granted) or decline (it becomes denied); another user's or an expired pending id shows the same 404 page. Revoking a provider leaves no users/<userKey>/<provider> key in consent.store even after a simulated racing refresh write-back, the fake provider receives a revoke call, a failed provider revoke shows as pending and is retried, and within one long-poll cycle the next agent call through that mapping returns authorization_required on every usersecrets/v1 worker, including one holding a cached token. Bearer tokens and API keys get 401 on every portal route, the pages refuse to load in a frame, and with the consent block absent /portal returns 404 and /policy bytes are unchanged.

The page sends X-Warden-CSRF through one api() wrapper and sets all dynamic text with textContent.

tickets.title: Implement revoke with grant, secret, epoch and provider steps
tickets.body: Add POST /portal/api/connections/{provider}/revoke and the shared oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant that offboarding also calls. It marks the grant revoked, deletes the live secret, bumps the user's grant epoch so workers drop cached tokens, and revokes the token at the provider, reporting each step. The order matters: the secret is deleted before the epoch bump so a worker that re-reads after eviction finds nothing. This ticket is CP-only; worker application is W-P3-PORT-06 and the provider retry queue is W-P3-PORT-07.
requirements: New `oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant(ctx, iss, sub, provider string, by Actor) (RevokeResult, error)` with Actor{ID, Kind: user|admin|system, Reason}; userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub). EpochBumper (`Bump(ctx, userKey) error`, the W-P3-PUS-08 EpochStore through the W-P3-PORT-05 adapter) and adminaudit.Recorder are injected through the Broker constructor, so oauthbroker never imports controlplane.

Step order, each attempted after earlier failures: read the TokenRecord into memory; GrantStore.RevokeGrant; delete secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider) from consent.store; EpochBumper.Bump; oauthbroker.Revoke (W-P3-BRKR-05). A missing token skips provider_revoke and still runs the others. Steps run inside Engine.WithGrantLock (W-P3-PUS-03), which takes the oauthbroker.GrantLocks mutex shared with the W-P3-BRKR-04 callback and drops the CP token cache entry.

Responses: 200 {status: revoked|partial, steps:{grant, secret_delete, epoch, provider_revoke: ok|pending|failed|skipped}, workers_without_cap:[...]} when secret_delete succeeds; 502 when secret_delete fails; 404 for an unknown provider or no recorded grant; 409 while a revoke for the same key is running; 200 with the same terminal state for an already revoked grant; 403 without a valid X-Warden-CSRF; 401 without a portal session.
workers_without_cap lists connected workers whose heartbeat lacks usersecrets/v1 (W-P3-PORT-05), so the user and operator know propagation is not guaranteed there.

Audit: when admin audit is enabled, exactly one connect.revoked row through adminaudit.Recorder with new auth_method portal (offboarding passes Kind system), target_ref grant:<provider> and per-step outcomes in details. A `msg=connect_revoked provider outcome steps duration_ms` log line is always written. Tokens, secret Reference values and provider error bodies are never logged or returned.
Limits: the provider call is capped at 5s and the whole revoke at 10s; mutating portal routes are limited to 10 per minute per session.

tickets.title: Add the pending landing page and connect, continue and decline actions
tickets.body: Add GET /portal/connect/{pending_id}, the page an agent's authorize_url points to, plus the POST actions that start a connection or decline it. The page shows only text Warden builds from the pending row and the agent registry, never text the agent supplied, so it cannot be used for consent phishing. Continue and connect are CSRF-protected POSTs that return the provider URL, so a link an agent posts can never send the browser straight to a provider consent screen. CP-only.
requirements: GET /portal/connect/{pending_id} requires a portal session; with none it redirects to /portal/login?next=/portal/connect/<id>. next must be a relative path under /portal/ or /connect/ with no scheme, `//` or backslash; anything else falls back to /portal (the W-P3-CSIG-02 rule).

Content: agent display name with a verified or unregistered badge from the agent registry wire, provider display name, capped scopes with descriptions, the request host, method and MCP tool from the W-P3-BRKR-02 request columns when set (W-P3-JIT-01 fills them), the expiry as a relative time computed from the CP clock, and 'Signed in as <email>. Not you? Sign out'. No free text from the agent is ever rendered; every value is set with textContent.
Unknown, expired, terminal and other users' pending ids return 404 with a byte-identical generic body that holds no agent, provider or scope string.

Actions, all with X-Warden-CSRF, an Origin check and the portal session only: POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/continue -> 200 {redirect_url}; POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/decline -> 200, calling GrantStore.CompletePending(id, denied), which closes the W-P3-BRKR-02 Subscribe channel that p3-jit status waiters use; POST /portal/api/connect {provider} -> 200 {redirect_url} with scope cap allowedScopes ∩ the union of that provider's perUserSecrets scopes. Terminal pending -> 409 only for its owner.

The redirect URL comes from Broker.Start (W-P3-BRKR-03); POST /portal/api/connect passes the allowedScopes ∩ perUserSecrets ceiling, and GET /connect/start only redirects to the portal (W-P3-BRKR-03), so a posted link never lands on a provider consent screen.

tickets.title: Add provider revoke retries and the orphan token sweep
tickets.body: Make a revoke finish even when the provider is down or a racing CP refresh writes a rotated token back after the delete. A retryable provider failure parks the token under the reserved revoking/ prefix of consent.store and a CP ticker retries it for up to 24h before alerting. An orphan sweep deletes any live per-user key that has no active grant row, using metadata-only List. CP-only.
requirements: On a retryable error from oauthbroker.Revoke, RevokeUserGrant parks the TokenRecord in consent.store at secrets.RevokingKey(userKey, provider) and inserts a cpstate revoke_retries(user_key, provider, attempts, next_at, first_failed_at) row; provider_revoke reports pending. A non-retryable error gives up at once and reports failed with the provider's manual revoke URL.

A CP ticker retries due rows with exponential backoff (1m doubling, max 1h) for up to 24h, then deletes the parked key, marks the row given up and raises an alert through internal/alertpipeline. A success deletes the parked key and the row.

Orphan sweep about 2 minutes after each revoke and on every CP retention tick: consent.store List over users/ (metadata only, never values) and Delete on any users/<userKey>/<provider> key with no active oauth_grants row; idp/ and revoking/ keys are outside the listed prefix.
Each sweep deletion logs `msg=portal_revoke_resurrected provider key_prefix` and increments a CP counter; values are never read or logged.
Restart safe: the retry queue lives in cpstate and resumes after a CP restart. Without the consent block nothing runs.
Revoke results report pending until the retry succeeds; GET /portal/api/connections shows the connection as revoking while a retry row exists.

name: Consent portal
label: consent-portal

summary: A CP job refreshes each portal user's stored IdP refresh token on a schedule. It offboards a user only when the IdP refusal is confirmed as an upstream disable, never on token expiry, a lost rotation, a re-login or an IdP outage, and a circuit breaker pauses automatic offboarding when many users fail at once. Offboarding first contains the user (block list, API keys, sessions, cached worker tokens) and then, after a grace period, revokes provider grants and erases the user's vault entries. Admins can also offboard any user from the console.
design: Scope and trust: the CP uses only the standard OIDC refresh_token grant against consent.oidc (the warden-portal client from W-P3-CSIG-01); Dex is never called through its own APIs. Detection depends on the upstream connector re-checking the user on refresh: the Dex LDAP connector fails a refresh only when userSearch no longer finds the user, so userSearch.filter must exclude disabled accounts, and SAML and some upstream OIDC setups never report a disabled user. In P2 require mode the ID-token and Warden-token TTLs stay the primary cutoff; offboarding adds cleanup and coverage for attribute mode.

Config (CP-local, json:"-", never on policyWire) under consent.offboarding: mode off|observe|enforce (default off; observe classifies and alerts but never offboards), blockRetention 2160h (90 days; 0 keeps offboarding blocks forever), interval 1h (5m-24h, must stay below the IdP validIfNotUsedFor of 168h), concurrency 4, requestTimeout 10s, maxFailures 3, confirmDelay 60s, reauthWarning 72h (measured against idp_links.relink_due_at, which W-P3-CSIG-03 sets from consent.idpLink.refreshLifetime, 720h to match W-P1-DEX-01), revokeGrace 24h (automatic triggers only; manual erase is immediate), propagationWait 2m, breaker.maxPerRun 5, breaker.maxFraction 0.1. Without the consent block or --state-dir nothing is constructed and /policy is byte-identical.

Data model: idp_links (W-P3-CSIG-03) already holds iss, sub, user_key, generation, linked_at, relink_due_at, last_refresh_at, last_refresh_status and offboarded_at. Migration idp_links/0002 adds link_state active|expiring|reauth_required|token_lost|suspect|offboarded, last_ok_at, consecutive_failures, last_error_code, rotation_pending_ref and email_verified. Migration offboarding/0001 adds offboard_runs(id, sub, iss, trigger manual|idp, actor, reason_class, stage contain|erase|done|cancelled|partial, erase_after, created_at, updated_at) with a partial unique index on sub for open runs, and offboard_steps(run_id, step, status pending|done|skipped|failed, attempts, last_error_code, updated_at). Tokens stay only in consent.store (W-P3-CSIG-06); tables hold References.

Refresh job: started from controlplane.Server.Start next to the retention pruner, behind a Leader interface that is always-leader in SQLite mode so p5-postgres-ha can plug in its advisory lock. It runs once a minute after startup, then each sub at a hash(sub) offset inside the interval, with bounded concurrency and a run deadline of interval/2. Links whose relink_due_at has passed are skipped and marked reauth_required. For the others it reads idp/<userKey> from consent.store through LinkStore (W-P3-CSIG-03), refreshes, verifies the returned ID token (iss, aud warden-portal, sub equal to the row), sets rotation_pending_ref and writes the rotated token with LinkStore.Rotate(iss, sub, generation, token), which holds the per-user_key mutex shared with the portal callback and returns ErrStaleGeneration when a re-login won; then it updates email, email_verified and timestamps.

Failure classification, pinned to the Dex v2.41.1 refresh responses by a contract test: 400 invalid_request 'Refresh token expired.' is expired (reauth_required, never offboard); 400 'Refresh token is invalid or has already been claimed' or any other 400 invalid_grant is token_lost (storage loss, re-login or a lost rotation; re-auth and alert, never offboard automatically); 500 invalid_request with an empty description is upstream_refused, the only automatic offboard signal, confirmed by one retry after confirmDelay and only when at least one other refresh in the run succeeded; other 5xx, 429, timeouts and network errors are transient; 401 invalid_client is config_error and pauses the job; an ID-token sub mismatch is suspect. Links within reauthWarning of relink_due_at move to expiring. token_lost users are only alerted and asked to re-authenticate; they are never offboarded automatically.

Breaker: when confirmed candidates in one run exceed max(breaker.maxPerRun, breaker.maxFraction x active links), no automatic offboard runs; candidates are marked pending_review, a critical offboarding_paused Finding is published and an offboarding.paused audit row is written. An admin confirms or dismisses each candidate from the console. Manual offboard is never paused.

Offboard lives in new package internal/offboard as an Offboarder built from narrow interfaces (Blocker, KeyRevoker, TokenSessionRevoker, PortalSessionRevoker, PendingCanceller, GrantRevoker, EpochBumper, SecretStore, LinkStore, Recorder, FindingPublisher) wired by internal/controlplane, so oauthbroker never imports controlplane. Steps are an ordered []Step{Name, Stage, Run} persisted in offboard_steps, so a crash resumes at the first incomplete step and p4-grants can append a step. Stage contain (immediate, reversible): BlockStore.Add({Sub, Email when verified}, actor) (W-P1-BLOCK-03; duplicate counts as done; W-P1-BLOCK-07 deletes console sessions inside Add), Server.RevokeAPIKeysForOwner(iss, sub, actor) (W-P2-APIK-03), tokensvc SessionStore.RevokeAll for (iss, sub) (W-P2-TOKX-07), delete portal_sessions for the sub (BlockStore.Add already does this through W-P3-CSIG-04, so a second call is a no-op), mark the user's open pending_authorizations denied, and EpochStore.Bump(userKey) (W-P3-PUS-08).

Stage erase runs at erase_after (now for manual, now + revokeGrace for automatic). It waits until every live worker in WorkerRegistry reports via heartbeat a policy ETag served at or after the contain step, bounded by propagationWait. Then per grant it calls oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant(iss, sub, provider, Actor{Kind: system}) (W-P3-PORT-02), whose retryable provider failures go to the W-P3-PORT-07 retry queue (a final failure raises provider_revoke_failed), deletes idp/<userKey> from consent.store, runs a sweep with consent.store List over secrets.UserPrefix(userKey) (W-P3-CSIG-06; a fixed-length user key plus the trailing slash, so no other user's keys can match), and sets idp_links.offboarded_at. An admin BlockStore.Remove during the grace period cancels the erase; restoring access never restores erased grants.

Resurrection and re-entry guards: a CP refresh that raced the erase could write a rotated token back (W-P3-PUS-03 re-checks grant state, epoch and grant_id first, so this is defence in depth), so every job run re-sweeps secrets.UserPrefix(userKey) for each recently offboarded user and raises a Finding if anything was found; the W-P3-PUS-01 Vault store Delete destroys metadata and all versions (the AWS store already force-deletes). The portal callback (W-P3-CSIG-02), the portal session middleware (W-P3-CSIG-04) and /connect/start and /connect/callback (W-P3-BRKR-03, W-P3-BRKR-04) check the in-memory BlockStore snapshot and return 403 user_blocked with no idp_links, grant or consent.store write; W-P3-OFFB-06 audits and tests them together.

Console routes, each with an authz row (W-P1-SSO-05), explicit Scope ScopeNone (W-P2-APIK-02, so no API key can offboard) and the W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware: GET /dashboard/api/users (admin, lists PII), POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard {reason 1-512 bytes} returning 202 {runId} after the contain stage, GET /dashboard/api/offboard-runs/{id}, POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard/cancel and POST /dashboard/api/offboarding/review {subs[], action confirm|dismiss}. Agents whose owner_sub (W-P2-AREG-01) is blocked or offboarded are flagged in the console and never disabled automatically.

Audit and observability: one admin_audit row user.offboarded per run (actor system:offboarding or the console principal) with details trigger, reason_class, providers_revoked, providers_failed, api_keys_revoked, token_sessions_revoked, owned_agents and status, added to the closed details allowlist; user.offboard_cancelled on cancel. Findings go through Server.publishFinding (W-P1-OPS1-01) with the sub hashed in the DedupKey and no email: user_offboarded (high), offboarding_paused and offboarding_config_error (critical), idp_refresh_unavailable (one per issuer when most of a run is transient), idp_refresh_failing, offboarding_reauth_required, provider_revoke_failed and offboard_partial (medium). Nil-safe in-memory counters warden_cp_offboarding_refresh_total{outcome}, warden_cp_offboarding_runs_total{trigger,result} and warden_cp_offboarding_last_run_timestamp_seconds wait for W-P5-RETN-06. Logs carry only a sha256(sub) prefix and the class, never tokens, References or reasons.

Degraded modes: CP down pauses detection and unfinished runs resume from offboard_steps on restart; IdP down gives only transient results; secret backend down still lets the contain stage finish (it needs no vault access) while refreshes and erase retry; the worker hot path changes nothing beyond the existing W-P1-BLOCK-02 block check and userGrantEpochs lookup.

Block retention: block-list entries created by an offboard run expire automatically after consent.offboarding.blockRetention (default 90 days), keeping the list under MaxBlockedUsers (5000). An hourly sweep, which runs whenever consent and --state-dir are set regardless of mode because manual offboards also create blocks, removes only entries whose id the run's contain step recorded as created by that run (never an admin-created block) through BlockStore.Remove with actor system:offboarding, and writes one `user.offboard_block_expired` admin audit row per entry. This system expiry does not go through p2-approvals drafts; the audit row is its record.
done_when: With consent.offboarding.mode enforce and revokeGrace 0, removing a user from an upstream directory whose connector re-checks on refresh produces, within one interval plus confirmDelay: the sub in blocked_users through BlockStore with actor system:offboarding; a 403 user_blocked from workers after their next policy poll; revoked console, portal and token-service sessions and wak_ API keys; denied pending authorizations; revoke calls at the fake Google and GitHub providers; no users/<userKey>/ or idp/<userKey> key in consent.store even after a racing refresh write-back; a refused portal login and /connect; and one user.offboarded audit row plus one user_offboarded Finding. A token past its absolute lifetime, a lost rotation, a portal re-login, IdP 5xx errors and a fleet-wide refusal never offboard anyone, and the fleet-wide case pauses automatic offboarding with a critical Finding. With the default 24h grace an admin unblock cancels the erase. Admins can offboard any sub from the console; viewers, editors and API keys get 403. Mode defaults to off, token_lost users are only alerted, and blocks created by offboarding expire after the configurable 90-day blockRetention with an audit row.

tickets.title: Implement the resumable two-stage Offboarder
tickets.body: Add the Offboarder in new package internal/offboard that removes every credential a user holds, in two recorded stages. Contain runs at once and is reversible: block through BlockStore.Add, revoke API keys, token sessions, portal sessions and pending authorizations, and bump the user's grant epoch. Erase runs at erase_after, revokes provider grants through the shared RevokeUserGrant and then deletes the user's remaining keys in consent.store. Nothing calls it until W-P3-OFFB-03 or W-P3-OFFB-05, so merging changes no behaviour.
requirements: New internal/offboard package with `Offboarder.Offboard(ctx, Request{Sub, Iss, Reason, Actor, Trigger manual|idp, EraseAfter}) (Run, error)` built from narrow interfaces wired by internal/controlplane; internal/offboard and internal/oauthbroker never import internal/controlplane. A nil optional seam (for example token sessions disabled) records the step as skipped.

cpstate migration offboarding/0001 adds offboard_runs and offboard_steps as in the feature design (idp_links already has iss and offboarded_at from W-P3-CSIG-03); a partial unique index allows one open run per sub. Each step is persisted before the next starts, and Server.Start calls ResumePending so open runs continue from the first incomplete step.

Contain steps in order: BlockStore.Add({Sub, Email only when email_verified}, actor), recording on the run the entry id when this run created it (for the W-P3-OFFB-05 retention expiry), where a duplicate counts as done and records no id and the W-P1-BLOCK-07 path deletes console sessions; Server.RevokeAPIKeysForOwner(iss, sub, actor); tokensvc SessionStore.RevokeAll for (iss, sub); delete portal_sessions for the sub (PortalSessionStore.DeleteBySub from W-P3-CSIG-02, a no-op after BlockStore.Add); mark the user's open pending_authorizations denied; EpochStore.Bump(secrets.UserKey(iss, sub)) (W-P3-PUS-08). If BlockStore.Add fails (for example 422 above MaxBlockedUsers), the remaining steps still run and the run ends partial with an offboard_partial Finding.

Erase steps in order: wait until every live worker in WorkerRegistry reports via heartbeat an ETag served at or after the contain stage, bounded by consent.offboarding.propagationWait (default 2m); oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant(ctx, iss, sub, provider, Actor{ID: system:offboarding, Kind: system}) per active grant (W-P3-PORT-02; a retryable provider failure is parked for the W-P3-PORT-07 retry queue and a final failure raises provider_revoke_failed); delete idp/<userKey> from consent.store; sweep consent.store with List and Delete over secrets.UserPrefix(userKey); set idp_links.offboarded_at. Cancel(ctx, sub, actor) during the grace period marks the run cancelled and skips the erase.

Keys come only from the W-P3-CSIG-06 helpers (secrets.UserKey, IdPLinkKey, UserPrefix). The user key has a fixed length and the prefix always ends with '/', so offboarding one user never touches another user's keys, whatever their subs contain.

Idempotent: Offboard on a sub with a done run returns that run with status already_offboarded, makes no provider or store call and writes no audit row. Each finished run writes one admin_audit row user.offboarded (target users, target_ref user:<sub>, details trigger, reason_class, providers_revoked, providers_failed, api_keys_revoked, token_sessions_revoked, status) added to the closed details allowlist, and publishes user_offboarded through Server.publishFinding with DedupKey user_offboarded:<first 16 hex of sha256(sub)>.
No token value, secrets.Ref string, email or free-text reason appears in slog or Findings; log lines carry a sha256(sub) prefix and step names only.

tickets.title: Add the IdP refresh job in observe mode with safe token write-back
tickets.body: Add the CP job that refreshes each portal user's stored IdP refresh token, verifies the returned ID token and writes the rotated token back without losing the chain. This ticket only observes: it records link state and alerts on outages, expiry and lost chains, and never calls Offboard. Separating it from enforcement lets operators run it safely before trusting its signal. It ships under consent.offboarding.mode, default off.
requirements: Config: ConsentOffboarding under the consent block from W-P3-CSIG-01 with strict-field registration: mode off|observe|enforce (default off), interval 1h (5m-24h), concurrency 4 (1-32), requestTimeout 10s, maxFailures 3, reauthWarning 72h (against relink_due_at from W-P3-CSIG-03). It is CP-local and never appears in GET /policy; mode enforce is accepted but behaves as observe until W-P3-OFFB-05.

Scheduling: one goroutine from controlplane.Server.Start next to the retention pruner, behind a Leader interface (always-leader in SQLite mode); it first runs one minute after start, then refreshes each non-offboarded link at a hash(sub) offset inside the interval with bounded concurrency and a run deadline of interval/2. `RunOnce(ctx)` and an injectable clock drive tests.

Refresh: links whose relink_due_at has passed are skipped and set to reauth_required with no refresh call. Otherwise POST grant_type=refresh_token to the token_endpoint from lazy discovery as the warden-portal client (consent.oidc.clientID and clientSecretEnv), with requestTimeout, using the token from LinkStore.Get. Verify the returned ID token iss, aud and sub against the idp_links row without a nonce; a sub mismatch sets link_state suspect and never acts. Update email and email_verified from verified claims.

Rotation safety: set rotation_pending_ref, then write the rotated token with LinkStore.Rotate(ctx, iss, sub, generation, token) (W-P3-CSIG-03), which holds the per-user_key mutex shared with the portal callback and returns ErrStaleGeneration without writing when a re-login won. Rotate is retried up to 3 times on store errors while the token is held only in memory; rotation_pending_ref is cleared on success. If every attempt fails, set link_state token_lost and log only a sha256(sub) prefix.

Lifetime: a link within reauthWarning of relink_due_at moves to expiring and publishes one offboarding_reauth_required Finding per user per window; a 400 'Refresh token expired.' sets reauth_required. A portal re-login (W-P3-CSIG-03 upsert) resets the link to active.

Transient handling: transport errors, timeouts, 429 and 5xx increment consecutive_failures; at maxFailures a per-user idp_refresh_failing Finding is published only when the issuer is otherwise healthy, and one idp_refresh_unavailable Finding per issuer is published when more than half of a run is transient. 401 invalid_client publishes a critical offboarding_config_error Finding and pauses the job until restart or config reload.

Observability: nil-safe counters warden_cp_offboarding_refresh_total{outcome} and warden_cp_offboarding_last_run_timestamp_seconds with no sub label, and one INFO line per run msg=offboarding_job_run with checked, ok, transient, expired, token_lost and duration_ms.

Docs: a docs/control-plane.md section on the job, its config keys, the link states, and the requirement that the Dex LDAP userSearch.filter excludes disabled accounts, plus a commented userSearch.filter example in deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml (AD userAccountControl bit 2, nsAccountLock).

New internal/offboard/refresh.go: Job{Links LinkStore, Client, Verifier, Clock, Leader, Publisher} with RunOnce and Start; New internal/offboard/leader.go with Leader and AlwaysLeader.

tickets.title: Add the console Users tab and manual offboard routes
tickets.body: Give admins a Users tab listing portal users with link state and offboarding status, and routes to offboard any sub, follow a run, cancel a pending erase and resolve breaker reviews. The offboard route runs the contain stage synchronously and returns 202, so the audit mutation lock is never held across provider calls. Every route is admin-only with Scope ScopeNone, so viewers, editors and API keys cannot offboard.
requirements: GET /dashboard/api/users (admin, because it lists emails; cursor, at most 200 per page) returns [{sub, email, linkState, linkedAt, lastRefreshAt, consecutiveFailures, reauthDueAt, grantsCount, apiKeysCount, blocked, offboardedAt, pendingReview}] with no References or token data, and also lists subs that hold only API keys or token sessions.

POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard {reason: 1-512 bytes, erase: bool default true} runs Offboard with the console principal as actor: 202 {runId, stage} after the contain stage; 200 {status: already_offboarded, runId}; 400 for a missing or oversized reason or invalid sub; 403 role_required for viewer and editor; 403 self_offboard_forbidden for the caller's own sub; 404 when the sub has no idp_links, grants, API keys or sessions; 503 state_dir_required without --state-dir. With erase false only the contain stage runs.

GET /dashboard/api/offboard-runs/{id} (admin) returns the step list with status and fixed error codes, never raw provider errors. POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard/cancel (admin) cancels an erase still in its grace period and writes user.offboard_cancelled.

POST /dashboard/api/offboarding/review {subs[], action: confirm|dismiss} (admin) resolves breaker pending_review entries; confirm runs Offboard with the admin as actor and dismiss returns the link to active. Before W-P3-OFFB-05 the route returns 404.

Each route has a row in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table with Scope ScopeNone (W-P2-APIK-02), Audited:true, target users and target_ref user:<sub>; break-glass admin sessions may offboard and are recorded as breakglass:<user>. The reason is stored only in audit details and offboard_runs.

tickets.title: Add an E2E test for IdP-driven offboarding and its false-positive guards
tickets.body: Prove the whole chain under the integration tag: a user disabled upstream is blocked, their credentials revoked and their vault entries erased, and the worker denies their next request. Also prove the guards: expiry, a lost chain, a re-login and a fleet-wide refusal never offboard anyone. The default path uses the in-process fakes.OIDCIssuer with a refresh endpoint that returns the Dex v2.41.1 response shapes; a real Dex and LDAP run is opt-in.
requirements: New test/integration/offboarding_test.go (//go:build integration) starts the CP with --state-dir, a consent block pointing at fakes.OIDCIssuer, offboarding mode enforce with revokeGrace 0, fake Google and GitHub providers and fakes.MemorySecretStore as the persistent consent.store (W-P3-CSIG-06), plus a worker through the existing startProxy helpers.

Extend fakes.OIDCIssuer (W-P2-SECT-01) with a refresh_token grant and per-sub switches: Disable(sub) returns 500 {"error":"invalid_request"}, Expire(sub) returns 400 invalid_request 'Refresh token expired.' and Forget(sub) returns 400 'Refresh token is invalid or has already been claimed by another client.'. Fakes mint random token strings only.

Happy path: link alice through /portal/login, connect Google, make one allowed worker request, Disable(alice), call RunOnce with an advanced clock past confirmDelay, then assert block list, revoke calls, vault deletion, revoked sessions and keys, a refused portal login and a worker 403 {"error":"user_blocked"} with deny event Reason=user_blocked after the next policy poll.

Guard cases: Expire and Forget for one user never offboard; a portal re-login during a run never offboards; every user returning 500 opens the breaker with no offboard and no provider revoke; a fake racing write-back during erase is removed by the next run's re-sweep.

Opt-in: with WARDEN_IT_DEX=1 the W-P1-DEX-02 recipe deletes the seeded LDAP user with ldapdelete and the test logs Dex's actual refresh response, so the classification table stays verified against real Dex.
The test runs in the CI integration job added by W-P1-VRFY-05 (`scripts/check.sh --integration`).

summary: Users approve delegation grants that let a specific agent act for them for a stated purpose, with a fixed tool set and expiry. The token service issues tokens carrying `grant_id`, the worker limits MCP tools to the grant's tool set, and users or admins can revoke grants at any time with immediate effect.
design: New package internal/grants with a SQLite table `grants` in CP state: id (`grt_` + 128-bit random), sub, agent_id, purpose, tools (JSON array, namespaced `server__tool` or bare tool), providers/scopes, expires_at, status `pending|active|denied|revoked|expired`, created_at, approved_at, revoked_at, revoked_by, revoke_reason.

Agents request via `POST /api/grants` (agent private_key_jwt assertion + user ID token as subject); requested tools must be a subset of the agent's policy-allowed tools and expiry is capped by `grants.maxTTL` (default 30d, per-agent override). Response: {grant_id, approve_url, status_url}.
Consent portal page `/portal/grants/{id}`: only the grant's sub can act; the user can deselect tools and shorten expiry but never add; approve/deny with CSRF token.

Token service accepts `subject_token_type=urn:warden:params:token-type:grant`; validates active, unexpired, agent match; issues JWT with `grant_id`, `tools` claim, sub=user, act.sub=agent, exp=min(15m, grant expiry).

Worker: MCP `tools/call` with a grant token must name a tool in the `tools` claim (intersection with policy, never a union), otherwise Deny with reason `mcp_grant_scope`. Revoked grant ids ride the signed bundle (`revokedGrants`) so outstanding tokens die on next bundle apply.
Every lifecycle change (request, approve, narrow, deny, revoke, expire) writes an admin audit record; decision events carry `GrantID`.
done_when: An agent can obtain a grant-bound token only after the user approves it in the portal, the worker blocks tools outside the grant, and revocation takes effect on the next bundle apply.

summary: The CP keeps a registry of approved MCP servers: transport, endpoint or command, owner team, versions, approved tool sets, schema pins and binary integrity. Changes are versioned with one-click rollback and go to workers in the signed bundle, so the gateway and `warden mcp` enforce one central list instead of local config.

Schema pin hash uses the same algorithm as `gateway.hashSchema` (sha256 hex of raw inputSchema) so observed inventory hashes from CP `mcpStore` can be imported directly.

REST: `GET/POST /api/mcp/servers`, `POST /api/mcp/servers/{id}/versions`, `POST /api/mcp/servers/{id}/rollback {version}`, `GET /api/mcp/servers/{id}/versions/{v}/diff`. Writes need editor role; widening (new tools, new URL/command, removed pin) goes through the Phase 2 approval gate.
Bundle gains `mcpRegistry: [{id, transport, url, command, args, approvedTools, schemaPins, integrity, version}]`; workers keep last-known-good on bad bundles.

Worker: gateway option `WithRegistry` adds findings `mcp_unregistered_server` and `mcp_unregistered_tool`, and registry pins override per-session baselines for drift; `warden mcp --server <id>` reads integrity from the registry before local `mcp.servers`.

summary: `warden admin-mcp` is an MCP server for operators' own AI assistants, with tools to explain a decision, query traffic, suggest and replay policy, and list agents. It authenticates to the CP with a scoped API key, is read-only by default, and never returns bodies or secrets.
design: The command is a thin MCP server that calls CP REST APIs; it has no direct DB access. Flags: `--transport stdio|http`, `--listen :7071`, `--cp-url`, `--api-key-env WARDEN_API_KEY` (default), `--allow-writes`.

Tools map to API key scopes: explain_decision -> `audit:read`; query_traffic -> `traffic:read`; list_agents -> `agents:read`; suggest_policy, replay_policy -> `policy:read`. The server lists only tools the key's scopes allow (checked via `GET /api/keys/self`).

explain_decision(event_uid | agent+domain+time) calls new CP `GET /api/explain` which loads the policy version active at the event time, re-runs `policy.NewEvaluator` and returns matched rule, identity, grant, hook and MCP findings.
query_traffic uses `EventFilter`/`AggregatedFilter` with typed filters (agent, sub, domain, decision, tool, since, limit<=500); no free-form SQL.

suggest_policy wraps `policybuilder.Build` + `FormatYAML`; replay_policy wraps `policyeval.Evaluate` on fleet events. The only write tool, create_policy_draft, needs `--allow-writes` and `policy:draft`; nothing can approve or publish.
HTTP mode serves Streamable HTTP at `/mcp` and requires the caller to present the same API key as Bearer; responses are size-capped (256 KB).
done_when: Claude Code connected to `warden admin-mcp` with a read-only key can explain a specific deny, query recent traffic and replay a candidate policy, and cannot change anything.

summary: Policy can live in Git: the CP pulls YAML from a repo into drafts that go through the same replay and approval gates as console edits, and CI can lint and replay changes before merge. Approved versions can be rolled out to a canary subset of workers, watched, then promoted or rolled back.
design: CP config `gitops: {repo, branch, path, interval: 60s, auth: {sshKeySecret|tokenSecret}, mode: advisory|authoritative}` using go-git (pure Go) pull only; CP never pushes. In authoritative mode console edits to policy are disabled.

New commit -> parse files under `path` with the normal config loader + validation -> create a draft with provenance {source: git, commit, author, message}; drafts then run replay via `policyeval.Evaluate` and the Phase 2 approval gate unchanged.

CLI for CI: `warden policy lint <file>` (strict YAML parse + validation, non-zero exit) and `warden policy replay --candidate f --cp-url --api-key-env` (remote replay against fleet events; `--fail-on-new-allows`).

Canary: `rollouts` table {id, version, targets (worker ids or percent), status canary|promoted|rolled_back, started_at}. `ServePolicy` picks the version per worker identity (mTLS SAN worker id), ETag per version.

Status from heartbeats (`policyETag` already reported) plus canary vs stable deny rate and error rate from the fleet store; promote sets current version for all; rollback returns canary workers to stable.
done_when: A merged policy PR appears as a draft with replay results, is approved, rolled out to a canary worker, and promoted or rolled back from the console with status visible per worker.

summary: The control plane can run on Postgres instead of SQLite and as multiple replicas behind a load balancer. Background jobs run on exactly one replica via advisory-lock leader election, and policy long-polls on any replica wake within a second of a change on another.
design: Store selection via `--store-provider sqlite|postgres` and `--postgres-dsn-env` (DSN read from env, never from config file); analytics.NewFleetStore's existing `postgres` branch (currently 'not yet implemented') returns a new FleetPostgresStore; all other CP stores (policy versions, block list, agent/MCP registries, sessions, worker tokens/certs, grants, API keys, admin audit index, alerts) get a Postgres implementation behind their existing interfaces.

Driver: jackc/pgx/v5 via database/sql (`pgx/v5/stdlib`); migrations as embedded, numbered SQL files per store run by a small migrator holding `pg_advisory_lock(hash('warden_migrate'))` so concurrent replicas migrate once; schema version table `warden_schema_migrations`.

Leader election: a dedicated connection holds `pg_try_advisory_lock(<job-key>)` per background job family (retention, offboarding refresh, git sync, detection tick, alert delivery, backups); loss of the connection drops leadership; jobs from p4-bg-jobs gain a `Leader` gate; SQLite mode keeps a no-op always-leader implementation.

Fan-out: policy/bundle publish does `NOTIFY warden_policy, '<version>'`; each replica runs a LISTEN loop that calls policyServer.Refresh/policyWatch.set so `/policy?wait=` and `/connect/{id}/status?wait=` waiters wake on all replicas; a 3s poll (existing policyReloadInterval) remains as a fallback when LISTEN reconnects.

The fleet Query Builder on Postgres runs in a `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` transaction with `statement_timeout`, against a restricted role, and Schema() reports dialect `postgres`; WorkerRegistry live state stays per-replica in memory but last-seen is upserted to a `workers` table so the dashboard shows the whole fleet.

`warden control-plane migrate-store --from sqlite:<state-dir> --to postgres` copies all stores in dependency order, verifies row counts and checksums, and refuses to run against a non-empty target unless `--force`.
done_when: Three CP replicas on one Postgres serve policy, ingest and console traffic; killing the leader moves background jobs to another replica within 30s, and a policy edit on one replica wakes long-polls on all others.

summary: Workers emit one OpenTelemetry LogRecord per policy decision and one span per proxied request, continuing the agent's `traceparent`, over OTLP with mTLS. Operators get decision logs and request traces in any OTel backend with a fixed, documented attribute schema that contains no bodies or secrets.
design: Extend internal/observability.New to also build a LoggerProvider (otlploggrpc) and TracerProvider (otlptracegrpc) when `observability.logs.enabled` / `observability.traces.enabled` are set; replace the hardcoded `WithInsecure()` with a shared TLS config (`observability.otlp.tls: {caCert, clientCert, clientKey}`; defaults to the worker's mTLS cert from p2-worker-ca) and `headersEnv` for bearer auth.

Attribute schema `warden.*` defined once in internal/observability/schema.go: decision, reason, protocol, method, server.address, server.port, url.path (path only, query stripped), http.response.status_code, warden.agent.id, warden.proxy.id, enduser.id (sub), warden.groups, warden.grant_id, warden.mcp.tool, warden.dlp.classes, warden.secret_ref (hash/last4 ref only), warden.cost_usd, warden.policy.version; a unit test fails on any attribute key not in the schema.

Span per request started in internal/proxy handleHTTP; if the request carries `traceparent`/`tracestate` the span is a child, else a new root; Warden injects its own `traceparent` upstream only when `traces.propagate: true` (default false to avoid leaking topology to third parties). Child events mark stages (judge, dlp, mcp_scan, swap, upstream).

Decision LogRecord is emitted from the same place analytics.Event is recorded (a small `DecisionSink` fan-out next to StoreEvent), with severity INFO for allow, WARN for deny; trace_id/span_id linked.

Sampling: `traces.sampler: parentbased_traceidratio` with `traces.ratio` (default 0.1) and always-sample on deny; logs are not sampled but have a bounded batch queue (drop-oldest with `warden.otlp.dropped` counter) so exporter backpressure never blocks the request path.

CP ingest path: CP can optionally expose an OTLP/HTTP receiver (`/v1/logs`) that maps decision LogRecords into the fleet store, letting workers send a single stream; default remains `/central/ingest` and a separate OTel Collector for traces.
done_when: A worker configured with an OTLP endpoint produces decision logs and request spans in a test collector over mTLS, with traces continued from the agent's traceparent and no body, query string or secret value in any attribute.

summary: A Helm chart installs the Warden control plane (replicated, Postgres-backed, with secrets, ingress and certificates) and workers in sidecar or per-node daemon patterns with default-deny NetworkPolicy. It replaces the placeholder manifests in deploy/k8s with a tested, versioned install path.
design: Chart at deploy/helm/warden with subcharts-free templates: `controlPlane` (Deployment, replicas default 2, PDB, HPA optional, Service, Ingress, ServiceMonitor), `worker.mode: sidecar|daemonset|deployment`, `postgres.external.dsnSecretRef` (no bundled DB by default; optional bitnami dependency disabled).
Secrets only by reference: `existingSecret` keys for Postgres DSN, OIDC client secret, KMS credentials, break-glass hash; chart never renders secret values from values.yaml into ConfigMaps.

Certificates: cert-manager `Certificate` for CP ingress and optional CP intermediate CA, or `tls.existingSecret`; worker enrollment token delivered via a Secret consumed by an init step that performs the p2-worker-ca CSR flow.

Sidecar pattern ships a mutating-webhook-free approach: a `_helpers.tpl` named template `warden.sidecar` that app charts include, plus NetworkPolicy templates matching deploy/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml (agent egress only DNS; worker egress to 0.0.0.0/0:443 and CP). DaemonSet pattern uses hostPort + NetworkPolicy restricting agents to the node-local worker.
`values.schema.json` validates all values; CI runs `helm lint`, `helm template` + kubeconform, chart-testing (`ct install`) on kind, and a helm-unittest suite.
done_when: `helm install` on a kind cluster brings up two CP replicas on external Postgres and an agent pod with a Warden sidecar that can only egress through the worker, verified by chart-testing in CI.

summary: Token-signing, bundle-signing and worker-CA private keys can live in AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS or Vault transit instead of CP state. The CP signs through a Signer interface, and rotation creates a new KMS key version with the same overlap rules as local keys.
design: Promote the key manager's signing to `type Signer interface { KID() string; Algorithm() string; Public() crypto.PublicKey; Sign(ctx context.Context, digestOrMsg []byte) ([]byte, error) }` in a new package internal/kms; local Ed25519/ES256 keys become the `local` backend.

Backends: AWS KMS (`Sign` with ECDSA_SHA_256 on ECC_NIST_P256; Ed25519 not supported by AWS KMS so ES256 is required), GCP KMS (`asymmetricSign`, EC_SIGN_P256_SHA256 or EC_SIGN_ED25519), Vault transit (`/v1/transit/sign/<key>` with ed25519 or ecdsa-p256). DER ECDSA signatures are converted to JOSE r||s for JWTs.

Config per key purpose: `keys.{token,bundle,ca}.{backend: local|awskms|gcpkms|vault, keyRef, region, vaultAddr, authEnv}`; `kid` derived from key ARN/resource version so JWKS and bundle pins stay stable across restarts and replicas.

Worker-CA signing implements crypto.Signer over the KMS backend so x509.CreateCertificate works unchanged; bundle signing algorithm becomes negotiable (Ed25519 or ES256) with the algorithm recorded in the bundle header.

Rotation: `warden control-plane keys rotate --purpose token` creates/selects a new key version, publishes it in JWKS alongside the old one for the overlap window, then switches signing; failure to reach KMS fails issuance closed (no fallback to local key) and raises a self-monitoring alert.
done_when: With all three key purposes configured for a KMS backend, tokens, bundles and worker certificates verify on workers and no private key material exists in CP state or Postgres.
