summary: Operators set retention per data class (fleet analytics, admin audit, alerts, decision receipts) and Warden deletes and optionally exports expired data on a leader-run schedule. The CP enforces an explicit API version skew policy with workers and harnesses, and exposes self-monitoring metrics with starter alert rules.
design: Retention config `retention.{analytics,adminAudit,alerts,deadLetters,policyVersions}.{days, maxRows}`; replaces the single `--analytics-retention-days` flag (kept as alias). One retention job (leader-gated via p5-postgres-ha elector or p4-bg-jobs) deletes in bounded batches (default 5k rows/tx) to avoid long locks; policy versions keep current + last N regardless of age.

Export before delete: `retention.export.{enabled, sink: file|s3|gcs, format: jsonl.gz}` writes expired rows to an object store path `<prefix>/<table>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/part-N.jsonl.gz` with a manifest and SHA-256; delete only after a successful export; on-demand `GET /admin/export?table=&from=&to=` for audit (scope `audit:read`).
User data deletion: `DELETE /admin/users/{sub}/data` removes analytics rows and pseudonymizes `sub` in admin audit (hash with a CP salt) for privacy requests; recorded in admin audit.

Version skew: every CP response carries `Warden-API-Version: <major.minor>`; workers send `Warden-Worker-Version`; CP accepts workers N-1 minor behind and rejects older with 426 + JSON error; workers refuse a CP newer by a major version. A compatibility matrix test runs the previous release's worker against the current CP.

Self-monitoring: CP gets its own observability.New metrics (`warden_cp_policy_waiters`, `warden_cp_ingest_events_total`, `warden_cp_ingest_rejected_total`, `warden_cp_store_latency_seconds`, `warden_cp_leader`, `warden_cp_worker_stale_total`, `warden_cp_retention_deleted_total`, `warden_cp_kms_errors_total`, `warden_cp_cert_expiry_seconds`) on /metrics, a `/readyz` that checks store and KMS, and a PrometheusRule starter file.
done_when: Expired rows in every configured table are exported then deleted by one replica, an out-of-range worker version is rejected with 426, and CP self-monitoring metrics and alert rules fire in a test Prometheus.

Run under the leader elector; keep `--analytics-retention-days` as an alias.

Ship deploy/helm/warden/templates/prometheusrule.yaml and docs/alerts.md with rules for stale workers, ingest rejects, store latency, no leader, KMS errors, cert expiry < 7d and retention/export failures.
acceptance: Metrics appear on CP /metrics with no unbounded labels (label cardinality test)
/readyz returns 503 when the store is unreachable
promtool test rules passes for each alert

name: Retention + self-monitoring
label: retention-ops

name: Default-deny + TLS MITM
summary: Default-deny at TCP, dynamic per-domain TLS certificates, protocol detection, denylist precedence, rate limits and time windows.

name: Secret swap (shared)
summary: Agents hold placeholder tokens; the worker swaps in real secrets in headers, query and body at the edge, plus OAuth2 client-credentials, SigV4, HMAC and API-key injectors.

name: Scan, DLP, MCP verdicts
summary: Prompt-injection and credential-leakage scanning, PII detection, per-class DLP (block/redact/monitor), MCP tool policy, schema pinning, poisoning and call-chain analysis.

The worker reads a user token from Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT, or from X-Warden-Identity on HTTP that Warden terminates (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2). It verifies the token against the issuer's JWKS and strips both headers before forwarding, in every mode. It then records sub, verified email, groups and identity status on every event, receipt, decision log and fleet event. Each agent's identity mode is off (the default) or attribute. Attribute mode records identity and never blocks. Only status valid produces a policy subject, so later group and user rules can never match an unverified caller.
design: New package `internal/identity` (no such package exists yet; go.mod gains `github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3` pinned to a release at least two weeks old). It defines `Claims{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, GroupsTruncated, SID, Issuer, AZP, Nonce, IssuedAt, Expiry}`, the policy subject `Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID}` with `SubjectFrom(claims, status) *Subject` (nil unless status is valid; p1-group-policy, p1-block-list and later per-user features use this one type), `Status` (off|none|valid|invalid|expired|unverified|conflict), a bounded `Reason` (bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, wrong_azp, unknown_kid, alg_not_allowed, malformed, too_large, ttl_too_long, jwks_unavailable), the interface `Verifier.Verify(ctx, raw string, opts ...VerifyOption) (Claims, Status, Reason)` and `StripHeaders(http.Header)`, which deletes X-Warden-Identity and Proxy-Authorization. A fake verifier lives in test/fakes.

OIDC verifier. `NewOIDCVerifier(Config{Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, ClockSkew, MaxTokenTTL, GroupsClaim, AllowInsecureIssuer, CAFile})` does no network I/O at construction. Discovery (when JWKSURL is empty) and JWKS fetches happen lazily. They use a dedicated http.Client with Proxy=nil, a plain net.Dialer (not the proxy SafeDialer, so an issuer on a private network such as Dex on cp-net is reachable, like newControlPlaneHTTPClient in internal/worker/wiring.go), a 5s timeout and a capped response body. A Warden wrapper around the go-oidc key set allows at most one unknown-kid refetch per 30s per issuer (singleflight plus an interval floor) and keeps the last good keyset while fetches fail. Warden enforces this itself and does not rely on go-oidc to limit refetches. Allowed algorithms are exactly RS256 and ES256. The verifier checks iss exactly, checks that aud contains Audience, and checks azp against AllowedAZP when that list is set. exp and nbf are checked in Warden with ClockSkew (default 60s, max 5m), and exp-iat must not exceed MaxTokenTTL (default 1h). Tokens over 16 KiB are rejected before parsing. Groups are read from GroupsClaim (default `groups`), sorted, de-duplicated and capped at 64 entries of 256 bytes, with GroupsTruncated set. Email is lowercased and kept only when email_verified is not false. A bounded LRU (10k entries) keyed by sha256(token) caches results until min(exp, now+5m), and exp is re-checked on every hit. `WithNonce` lets the CP console login (W-P1-SSO-03) reuse the verifier with its own audience.

Config. `SettingsWire.Identity *IdentitySettings{DefaultMode, Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, GroupsClaim, ClockSkewSeconds, MaxTokenTTLSeconds, AllowInsecureIssuer}` (json `identity`, omitempty; absent means off). A matching local `identity:` YAML block serves standalone workers. Per-agent override is a new `Identity string` field added to both the existing `AgentSettings` and `config.AgentPolicy` (and rawAgent), so the existing `AgentSettings(a)` conversion in SettingsWireFromPolicy keeps compiling. A worker resolves its mode for the agent ID that `worker.defaultAgentID` already computes (Agents[0].ID, or `agent:<port>` via agentid.PortBindingIdentifier). Validation on the CP and locally accepts off|attribute and rejects `require` with a 'Phase 2' error; a worker's parseRemotePolicy does not reject a served wire for an unsupported mode, which W-P1-VRFY-07 handles by keeping the previous identity config. An http issuer is rejected unless allowInsecureIssuer is set. The block holds no secrets.

Hot reload. The verifier lives in a new atomic holder `identityP` on Proxy (same pattern as secretsP and judgeP). The SettingsApplier rebuilds the verifier only when the issuer, audience, JWKS URL, azp, skew or TTL settings change, so the key cache survives unrelated applies. If a rebuild fails, or a newer CP sends an unknown mode, the worker keeps the previous identity config and logs one warning. In-flight connections keep their snapshot.

Extraction. `handleConn` (internal/proxy/serve.go) captures Proxy-Authorization in its existing CONNECT header loop: Basic with username `session` (the password is the token) or Bearer. Any other form gives status invalid with reason malformed. Verification runs before `Policy.Evaluate`, so CONNECT deny events are attributed too. The result is a per-connection `connIdentity{Claims, Status, Reason, Expiry}` passed to handleTLS, tunnel, handleHTTP and handleGRPC. The worker consumes the CONNECT request, so this header is never forwarded today. X-Warden-Identity: Bearer is honored only on HTTP that Warden terminates. For HTTP/1.1 a new `identityStage` runs in runRequestStages right after readRequest and before judgeGate, so the judge, DLP and the secret swap never see the token. For HTTP/2 the same resolver runs at the top of `serveGRPCStream` (internal/proxy/grpc.go), before the swap and before copyGRPCHeaders. Raw tunnels (no CA, non-TLS traffic, unknown protocols inside TLS) are opaque: they carry only the CONNECT identity, and the worker logs one startup warning when attribute mode is on and no CA is configured.

Stripping is unconditional and is the one deliberate exception to default-off. `identity.StripHeaders` runs on every terminated HTTP/1.1 request and every h2 stream, in every mode, including when there are no identity settings. A user token therefore never reaches an upstream from traffic Warden terminates.

Status rules in attribute mode never block a request. A valid CONNECT identity applies to the connection until its exp (plus skew) passes; later requests on that connection get status expired. A per-request header applies when CONNECT carried no token. Two valid identities with different sub give status conflict and no subject, and the request proceeds; a 403 identity_conflict is reserved for require mode in P2. A token sent while mode is off gives status off with no verification. Keys that cannot be fetched give unverified, which is kept distinct from invalid. Only status valid yields a non-nil `identity.Subject` for p1-group-policy, p1-block-list and later per-user features. Every other status is treated as anonymous, so group- and user-scoped rules never match and default-deny holds. sub is the authoritative key for user rules, and email matching requires a verified email.

Recording. `analytics.Event` gains `UserSub, UserEmail, UserGroups, UserGroupsTruncated, UserSID, IdentityStatus, IdentityReason` with explicit snake_case json tags and omitempty (Event has no tags today except UID). Unattributed events, receipts and sync payloads therefore stay byte-identical, and old receipts keep verifying because Receipt keeps the signed EventJSON bytes. Every proxy event is stored through one new `p.recordEvent(ci connIdentity, e analytics.Event)`, which stamps the identity fields. This covers serve.go, tls.go, http.go, grpc.go, ws.go and storeDeny; pre-CONNECT parse failures pass the zero connIdentity. decisionLog adds user_sub, identity_status, identity_reason and groups_count. Email and the group list appear in operational logs only at debug level. The raw token is never logged, stored, signed, put in an error body or passed to the judge or MCP gateway.

Storage. The local SQLiteStore gets additive addColumnIfAbsent migrations for user_sub, user_email, user_groups (a JSON array, because LDAP DN group names contain commas), user_groups_truncated, user_sid, identity_status and identity_reason, plus an index on (user_sub, ts). The columns are added to insertColumns, the GetEvents scan and the GetOldestEventIDs SELECT and scan, which is the SyncWorker source. FleetSQLiteStore.migrate is a bare CREATE TABLE today, so the fleet side gets a new idempotent addColumnIfAbsent helper, the same columns and indexes, and extended StoreAggregatedEvent INSERT and GetEvents scans. Rollout order is CP first, then workers. A version mismatch drops or empties the fields and never errors.

Observability. A nil-safe `(*Metrics).RecordIdentityVerify(result, reason)` registers the OTel counter `warden.identity.verify.total{result,reason}` with bounded labels; P2 extends this instrument and does not add a new one. `RecordJWKSFetch(result)` registers `warden.identity.jwks.fetch.total{result}`. Identity time is recorded in the existing `warden.request.added_latency` histogram with stage=identity. Budget: p99 under 100µs for a cached token, and under 1ms uncached excluding key fetches.

Dashboard. `analytics.EventFilter.User` matches user_sub exactly or lower(user_email), using parameterized SQL only. It is exposed as `?user=` on /dashboard/api/traffic and /dashboard/api/analytics on worker and CP, and the analytics cache key includes the normalized user. Analytics adds a top-users table. The Query Builder schema already comes from PRAGMA table_info, so the user columns appear in it with no code change. index.html adds a user column and a filter box and renders claim values with textContent only.

Deployment and docs. Workers need egress to the issuer for discovery and JWKS, so deploy/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml and the compose templates allow worker to issuer traffic. docs/control-plane.md documents the identity block, the per-agent field, the transport rules (X-Warden-Identity only with TLS termination; Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT works everywhere and is recommended) and the rollout order. They also state that a P1 identity is a bearer assertion signed by the IdP and not yet bound to the agent; P2 adds binding and bundle-distributed JWKS.

Size limits, fixed for P1 and used everywhere (the identity contract, the W-P1-IDC-04 exec forwarder, the P2 forwarder and token service): a token is at most 16 KiB (larger is invalid with reason too_large before parsing), and the CONNECT header block is at most 32 KiB and 100 lines with a 10s read deadline (overflow gets 431 and a deny event with reason headers_too_large). 32 KiB leaves room for a 16 KiB token base64-encoded in Basic credentials.
done_when: On a real deployment (CP plus at least one worker with TLS termination, Dex from p1-dex) with an agent in attribute mode, a request with a valid Dex token produces a local event, a signed receipt, a decision log line and a CP fleet event. Each carries the user's sub, verified email and groups with identity_status=valid. This holds for Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT and for X-Warden-Identity, over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. The upstream never sees X-Warden-Identity or Proxy-Authorization on any terminated path, in any mode. Invalid, expired, conflicting and missing tokens, and tokens sent while Dex is unreachable, are recorded as invalid, expired, conflict, none and unverified respectively, have no policy subject, and are allowed. The worker starts and serves traffic with Dex down. warden.identity.verify.total reports each outcome. Existing warden.db and fleet DB files upgrade in place with no data loss, and existing receipts still verify.

tickets.title: Add internal/identity OIDC verifier with lazy JWKS, cache and config
tickets.body: Create the new package internal/identity with Claims, Status/Reason, the Verifier interface, StripHeaders and an OIDC verifier on go-oidc v3. Construction is lazy and never blocks, so the verifier can be built when Dex is down. Warden enforces the refetch floor, the exp/nbf skew and the size limits itself, so attribution never depends on library defaults. Add the identity settings block (SettingsWire, local YAML and the per-agent field) with validation. Nothing is wired into the proxy yet, so merging changes no behaviour.
requirements: New package internal/identity: Claims{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, GroupsTruncated, SID (optional), Issuer, AZP, Nonce, IssuedAt, Expiry}, Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID} and SubjectFrom(claims, status) *Subject, which returns nil for every status except valid, Status off|none|valid|invalid|expired|unverified|conflict, a bounded Reason set, Verify(ctx, raw, opts...) (Claims, Status, Reason), and StripHeaders(http.Header).

NewOIDCVerifier(Config) on github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3 (new go.mod dependency, pinned; govulncheck stays clean). It allows only RS256 and ES256, checks iss exactly, checks that aud contains Audience, and checks azp against AllowedAZP when that list is set.

Warden checks exp and nbf with ClockSkew (default 60s, max 5m) and rejects exp-iat above MaxTokenTTL (default 1h). It rejects tokens over 16 KiB with reason too_large before parsing. Confirm against the pinned go-oidc version which built-in time checks must be disabled.

No network I/O at construction. Discovery and JWKS fetches are lazy and use a dedicated http.Client (Proxy=nil, a plain net.Dialer rather than the proxy SafeDialer so private-network issuers are reachable, 5s timeout, capped body, optional CA file). An unknown kid triggers at most one refetch per 30s (singleflight plus an interval floor), and the last good keyset is kept. A failure to obtain keys returns status unverified with reason jwks_unavailable.

Groups come from GroupsClaim (default groups) and are sorted, de-duplicated and capped at 64 entries of 256 bytes, with GroupsTruncated set. Email is lowercased and kept only when email_verified is not false; EmailVerified is true only when the claim is literally true. A bounded LRU (10k entries) keyed by sha256(token) caches results until min(exp, now+5m), and exp is re-checked on every hit.

Config: IdentitySettings{DefaultMode, Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, GroupsClaim, ClockSkewSeconds, MaxTokenTTLSeconds, AllowInsecureIssuer} on SettingsWire (json identity, omitempty) and a local identity: YAML block. Add a new Identity string field to AgentSettings, AgentPolicy and rawAgent. Validation accepts off|attribute, rejects require with a Phase 2 error in the CP write path and local YAML (parseRemotePolicy on a worker does not reject a served wire for an unsupported mode; W-P1-VRFY-07 keeps the previous identity config, so a later CP that serves require never stalls P1 workers), and rejects http issuers unless AllowInsecureIssuer is set. DeepCopy and SettingsWireFromPolicy are extended. JSON and YAML keys are defaultMode, issuer, audience, allowedAZP, jwksURL, groupsClaim, clockSkewSeconds, maxTokenTTLSeconds and allowInsecureIssuer, and the per-agent key is `identity` on agents[]. allowedAZP has no built-in default (empty means no azp check); the reference configs and docs set [agent-harness, warden-cli].
Raw tokens never appear in errors, logs or test output; only bounded reasons do. WithNonce(n) lets W-P1-SSO-03 reuse the verifier with its own audience.
Add fakes.Verifier (map from token to Claims/Status/Reason, safe for concurrent use, counts calls) to test/fakes.

For status expired and for invalid with reason bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, wrong_azp, unknown_kid or ttl_too_long, Verify still returns the sub and email parsed from a well-formed payload, so W-P1-BLOCK-02 can deny on a match (a match can only deny). These claims never yield a Subject and are never cached as valid. malformed and too_large return empty Claims.
plan: Add go-oidc v3 to go.mod and create the new internal/identity/identity.go with Claims, Status, Reason, Verifier, VerifyOption/WithNonce and StripHeaders.

Add the new internal/identity/keyset.go: a rateLimitedKeySet wrapping the go-oidc remote key set (singleflight, 30s floor, last-good keys, Proxy=nil client, body cap), plus lazy discovery when JWKSURL is empty.

Add the new internal/identity/oidc.go: NewOIDCVerifier with algorithm allowlist, iss/aud/azp checks, Warden-side exp/nbf/TTL checks, size cap, groups and email normalisation, and an error-to-Reason mapping (errors.As on the go-oidc expiry error).
Add the new internal/identity/cache.go: a bounded LRU keyed by sha256(token) with expiry at min(exp, now+5m).

Add the new internal/config/identity.go with IdentitySettings, the local identity: block parsed through rawConfig, and validateIdentity. Add Identity to AgentSettings, AgentPolicy and rawAgent, and extend SettingsWireFromPolicy, its reverse projection and SettingsWire.DeepCopy in internal/config/settings.go.
Add fakes.Verifier to test/fakes/fakes.go.

Tests: the new internal/identity/oidc_test.go (httptest JWKS, RS256 and ES256 signers), keyset_test.go (rotation, refetch floor under -race, issuer down) and cache_test.go. Extend internal/config/settings_test.go with identity round-trip, DeepCopy and validation.
acceptance: A valid token returns status valid with its Claims. Wrong iss, wrong aud, wrong azp, expired beyond 60s skew, nbf in the future, alg none, HS256 signed with the public key, exp-iat over 1h and a 17 KiB token each return the expected Status and Reason: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestOIDCVerifier`.

After a JWKS rotation, a token with the new kid verifies after exactly one fetch, and 100 concurrent unknown-kid verifications within 30s cause at most one more fetch: `go test -race ./internal/identity -run TestJWKSRotation`.
With the issuer unreachable, NewOIDCVerifier returns immediately, and Verify returns status unverified with reason jwks_unavailable within the context deadline.
A group `cn=eng,ou=groups,dc=corp` survives intact, 100 groups are capped at 64 with GroupsTruncated=true, and email_verified=false leaves Email empty.

A SettingsWire with an identity block and per-agent Identity round-trips byte-identically, a SettingsWire without one marshals with no identity key, and mode require fails with a Phase 2 message: `go test ./internal/config -run 'Identity'`.
`scripts/check.sh` passes, including govulncheck with the new dependency.

An expired token and a token signed by an unknown key return their sub in Claims with status expired and invalid respectively, and SubjectFrom returns nil for both; a valid token with email_verified absent keeps Email but has EmailVerified=false: `go test ./internal/identity -run 'TestUnverifiedClaims|TestSubjectFrom'`.

tickets.title: Extract, verify and strip identity on CONNECT, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
tickets.body: Wire identity into the proxy. Capture Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT and X-Warden-Identity on terminated HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, verify both through a new identityP atomic holder, and carry the result on a per-connection connIdentity. Stripping must also run on the h2 path (handleGRPC/serveGRPCStream), because that path bypasses runRequestStages and copyGRPCHeaders forwards every other header. Attribute mode never blocks, and with no identity configured the only change is that the two headers are stripped.
requirements: A new identityP atomic.Pointer[identityHolder] on Proxy with identity() and SetIdentity(v, mode), mirroring secretsP, plus an optional Identity field on proxy.Config. A nil holder means mode off.

handleConn captures Proxy-Authorization in the CONNECT header loop (Basic user session, or Bearer; any other form is invalid/malformed) and verifies it before Policy.Evaluate with a 2s context. The result is a connIdentity{Claims, Status, Reason, Expiry} passed to handleTLS, tunnel, handleHTTP and handleGRPC. connIdentity keeps the unverified sub and email that Verify returns for expired and invalid tokens, for the W-P1-BLOCK-02 deny check only.

A new identityStage runs in runRequestStages after readRequest and before judgeGate. serveGRPCStream calls the same resolver before the secret swap and before copyGRPCHeaders. Both call identity.StripHeaders in every mode.

Status rules: CONNECT identity re-checked against Expiry on every request (expired after exp plus skew). Header identity is used when CONNECT had none. Two valid identities with different sub give conflict, and the request proceeds. A token sent in mode off gives off, with no Verify call. Only valid yields a non-nil Subject on requestScope.
New nil-safe (*Metrics).RecordIdentityVerify(result, reason) registers warden.identity.verify.total. Identity time is recorded in warden.request.added_latency with stage=identity.
When mode is attribute and no CA is configured, log one warning at startup that only CONNECT identity is available. The raw token never reaches logs, events, the judge or the MCP gateway.

Bound the CONNECT header loop in handleConn, which reads headers without any limit today: at most 32 KiB of header bytes and 100 lines (room for a 16 KiB token base64-encoded in Basic credentials) and a 10s read deadline that is cleared once the headers end. Overflow or timeout returns `431 Request Header Fields Too Large` (timeout just closes) and stores a deny event with reason `headers_too_large`, added to internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06).
plan: Add identityHolder, identityP, identity() and SetIdentity in internal/proxy/proxy.go, seeded from proxy.Config in New.

Add the new internal/proxy/identity.go with connIdentity, resolveConnIdentity(header value) and resolveRequestIdentity(ci, r *http.Request), which applies the status rules and calls identity.StripHeaders.

In internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn, read Proxy-Authorization in the header loop, build connIdentity before Policy.Evaluate, and pass it to handleTLS and tunnel. In internal/proxy/tls.go, pass it to handleHTTP and handleGRPC.
Add a connIdentity field and a Subject field to requestScope, and insert identityStage after readRequest in runRequestStages (internal/proxy/http.go).
In internal/proxy/grpc.go, pass connIdentity into serveGRPCStream and call resolveRequestIdentity at its top, before the swap and copyGRPCHeaders.
Add RecordIdentityVerify to internal/observability/observability.go and call it once per verification.

Tests: the new internal/proxy/identity_test.go (HTTP/1.1, WebSocket upgrade and h2 ALPN clients against a header-recording upstream, all modes, fakes.Verifier), a race test for SetIdentity, and BenchmarkIdentityStage next to http_bench_test.go.
acceptance: For HTTP/1.1, WebSocket upgrade and an h2 ALPN client, in mode off, with no settings and in attribute mode, the upstream never sees X-Warden-Identity or Proxy-Authorization: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityStripping`.
In mode off with a token present, fakes.Verifier records zero calls and the resolved status is off.

In attribute mode, invalid, expired, missing, unverifiable and conflicting tokens are all forwarded (200 from upstream) with status invalid, expired, none, unverified and conflict, a nil Subject, and a matching warden.identity.verify.total increment: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityAttributeMode`.
A CONNECT identity whose exp passes during a keep-alive session gives status valid on the first request and expired on a request after exp plus skew.
Concurrent SetIdentity swaps during traffic pass under `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityHotSwap`.
`go test ./internal/proxy -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkIdentityStage` shows the cached-token path under 100µs/op.

A CONNECT with 40 KiB of headers gets 431 and one deny event with reason headers_too_large and no dial, while a CONNECT carrying a 16 KiB token in Proxy-Authorization is accepted: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestConnectHeaderBounds`.

tickets.title: Record user fields on worker events, receipts, decision logs and sync
tickets.body: Worker side of recording. Add identity fields to analytics.Event with snake_case json tags and omitempty, so unattributed events, receipts and sync payloads stay byte-identical. Add the local SQLite columns, including in the GetOldestEventIDs read that feeds SyncWorker, and route every proxy event through one recordEvent helper that stamps the connection identity. The control-plane fleet store is handled in W-P1-VRFY-06.
requirements: analytics.Event gains UserSub, UserEmail, UserGroups []string, UserGroupsTruncated, UserSID, IdentityStatus and IdentityReason with json tags user_sub, user_email, user_groups, user_groups_truncated, user_sid, identity_status and identity_reason, all omitempty. Existing field names and tags are unchanged.

The local SQLiteStore adds the seven columns through addColumnIfAbsent (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' / INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0), plus an index on (user_sub, ts). user_groups is stored as a JSON array, never comma-joined.
insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, the GetEvents scan, and the GetOldestEventIDs SELECT and scan all carry the new columns, so the fields reach SyncWorker.

Every proxy event goes through a new p.recordEvent(ci connIdentity, e analytics.Event), covering serve.go, tls.go, http.go, grpc.go, ws.go and storeDeny. Only pre-CONNECT parse failures use the zero connIdentity.
decisionLog and logDecision add user_sub, identity_status, identity_reason and groups_count. Email and the group list are logged only at debug level, and the token never is.
Receipts cover the fields automatically, because SigningStore signs the marshalled Event. Old receipts keep verifying.
plan: Add the fields and json tags to Event in internal/analytics/analytics.go, plus new encodeGroups/decodeGroups (JSON) helpers.
Add the addColumnIfAbsent entries and the index in SQLiteStore migrate. Extend insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs.

Add recordEvent and connIdentity.stamp in internal/proxy/identity.go. Replace each direct analyticsStore().StoreEvent call in serve.go, tls.go, http.go, grpc.go and ws.go, and give storeDeny a connIdentity parameter.
Extend decisionLog and logDecision in internal/proxy/observe.go.

Tests: a migration test from a fixture warden.db without the columns (pattern of activity_columns_test.go), a golden marshal test for an identity-free Event, an internal/audit receipt test, a SyncWorker test that reads the fields from GetOldestEventIDs, and an AST test in internal/proxy.
acceptance: An old warden.db with rows opens with the new columns added, old rows intact with defaults, and a second open is a no-op: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestMigrateUserColumns`.

An identity-free Event marshals to the same bytes as before this change, and its receipt has no user_* keys. An attributed event's receipt contains "user_sub" and "identity_status":"valid" and audit.Verify passes: `go test ./internal/audit -run TestReceiptIdentityFields`.
A group named `cn=eng,ou=groups,dc=corp` round-trips through StoreEvent, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs unchanged.
An AST test fails if any non-test file in internal/proxy calls StoreEvent outside recordEvent: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestAllEventsCarryIdentity`.
A CONNECT to a denied host with a valid Proxy-Authorization token stores a deny event with the user's sub and status valid.
Captured decision log output contains user_sub and identity_status and never the raw token.

tickets.title: Add user filter and top-users breakdown to the dashboard
tickets.body: Let operators filter traffic and analytics by user on worker and CP dashboards. Add EventFilter.User across the local, central and fleet stores, expose ?user= on the traffic and analytics APIs (including the analytics cache key), and add a top-users table and a user column to the UI. The Query Builder schema already reads PRAGMA table_info, so the user columns appear there with no code change.
requirements: analytics.EventFilter gains User, matching user_sub exactly or lower(user_email) = lower(User), with parameterized SQL only. SQLiteStore, CentralStore and FleetSQLiteStore honor it (AggregatedFilter through embedding).
/dashboard/api/traffic and /dashboard/api/analytics accept ?user= (at most 320 characters, otherwise 400). The handleAnalytics cache key includes the normalized user value.
Analytics adds topUsers: the top 10 by request count with deny count, grouped by user_sub with the latest email for display, plus one unattributed bucket.
index.html gets a user column (email, falling back to sub) and a filter box that sets ?user=. Claim values are rendered with textContent only.
The filter uses the (user_sub, ts) index. The Query Builder needs no change; only a test covers it.
With no identity data, responses are unchanged apart from an empty topUsers list.
plan: Add User to EventFilter in internal/analytics/analytics.go and apply it in SQLiteStore.GetEvents, CentralStore.GetEvents/GetAggregatedEvents (internal/analytics/central.go) and FleetSQLiteStore.GetEvents/GetAggregatedEvents.
In internal/dashboard/dashboard.go, parse and bound ?user= in handleTraffic and handleAnalytics, and add the user to the analytics cache key (currently range + proxy).
Add the topUsers aggregate to the analytics computation for both worker and fleet stores.
Add the user column and filter box to internal/dashboard/index.html.
Tests in internal/dashboard/dashboard_test.go and internal/analytics (filter, cache key, schema, topUsers).
acceptance: With events for alice@corp and bob@corp in local and fleet stores, GET /dashboard/api/traffic?user=Alice@Corp returns 200 with only Alice's events on worker and CP, and ?user=<alice-sub> returns the same set: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestTrafficUserFilter`.
After /dashboard/api/analytics?range=24h&user=alice is cached, the same call with user=bob returns Bob's figures.
?user= longer than 320 characters returns 400.
GET /dashboard/api/query/schema lists user_sub and user_email, and POST /dashboard/api/query with `SELECT user_sub, count(*) FROM events GROUP BY user_sub` returns 200 with rows.
topUsers has at most 10 entries sorted by count descending, plus an unattributed bucket.

name: Verify user token
label: identity-verification

summary: Allow entries and MCP tool `allowWhen` conditions can be limited to IdP groups or specific users with `groups: [...]` / `users: [...]`. Entries without these fields behave exactly as today. A scoped entry never allows a request without a valid verified identity, a non-member is denied outright and never sent to the judge, and workers on older releases deny scoped destinations instead of allowing them. `warden policy eval` replay shows which users a candidate change affects.
design: Schema: `config.AllowlistEntry` gains `Groups []string` and `Users []string` (yaml/json omitempty), and `config.MCPToolCondition` and `rawMCPToolCondition` gain `Groups`/`Users` next to `AgentID`/`TimeWindow`. Validation trims, rejects empty values, deduplicates and sorts, and caps each list at 256 values of 256 bytes. A Users value containing '@' is an email and is lowercased; any other value is an exact `sub`. Groups are exact, case-sensitive literals. The denylist and task-scope (`mcp.scopes.list[].constraints`) allowWhen get no scoping in P1. Entries without the fields marshal byte-identically to today, so existing ETags do not change. Old binaries reading a new local YAML fail at startup (KnownFields(true)), which fails closed.

Merge safety: until enforcement lands, validation rejects non-empty Groups/Users with `not yet enforced`. W-P1-GPOL-03 lifts the guard for allow entries and W-P1-GPOL-04 for MCP tool conditions, and both depend on the fail-closed wire (W-P1-GPOL-06), so main never parses a scoped rule that some worker would treat as global.

Fail-closed wire: the CP keeps serving one shared, ETag-versioned body. When building `policyWire` it moves allow entries that have groups/users out of `allowlist` into a new `scopedAllowlist` field, and for MCP tools with a scoped allowWhen it puts the real condition in a new wire-only `AllowWhenScoped` field and sets the legacy `AllowWhen` to a reserved AgentID sentinel `!identity-scoped` (rejected by validation as a real agent id). New workers merge both back in `parseRemotePolicy`. Old workers ignore the unknown fields, so scoped destinations stay NoMatch (denied) and scoped tools fail the sentinel condition (denied). The worker heartbeat adds `features: ["groupPolicy"]` for visibility only, and the fleet view flags workers without it while scoped rules exist.

Subject: one type, `identity.Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID}`, defined with `SubjectFrom` and `Claims.EmailVerified` in the leaf package `internal/identity` by W-P1-VRFY-01, used by internal/policy, internal/mcp/gateway and internal/policyeval. `identity.SubjectFrom(claims, status)` returns nil unless the identity status is valid, so missing, invalid and expired tokens give a nil subject. A `users` email entry matches only when EmailVerified is true; `sub` entries always match exactly. P2 worker-bound and P3 per-user-limits extend this type rather than redefine it.

Evaluator: `EvaluateFor(domain, port, scheme, *identity.Subject) Result{Decision, Reason, Scoped}`; `Evaluate` keeps its signature and only ever returns Allow, Deny or NoMatch (a scoped-only match with no subject collapses to Deny). `load()` precompiles per-entry group/user sets and a `hasScoped` flag, so policies without scoped entries keep the current zero-alloc path. Per entry the order is port and domain, then principal, then time window, then rate limit, so non-members never consume a scoped entry's budget. A destination matched only by scoped entries returns `Conditional` (reason `identity_required`) for a nil subject and `Deny` (reason `group_not_allowed`) for a non-member; neither is judge-eligible. The denylist is still checked first. Rate-limit counters for scoped entries are keyed per entry index (today the key is `domain:port`, shared across entries); unscoped keys are unchanged. Per-user limits come in P3.

CONNECT path: `handleConn` switches exhaustively on the decision, with default meaning deny. Conditional without a CA gives 403 `identity_required`. Conditional with a CA proceeds to TLS with a `deferred` enum {none, judge, identity} that replaces the `needsJudge bool` passed to `handleTLS`; every non-HTTP/1 branch there (non-TLS bytes, h2 ALPN or preface/gRPC, unknown protocol inside TLS) fails closed when deferred != none. An Allow granted by a scoped entry using the Proxy-Authorization subject is allowed; without a CA the raw tunnel is closed at the token's `exp`. h2/gRPC clients must send identity on CONNECT.

Request path: a new `scopedPolicyStage` runs after `identityStage` (and the user block check) and before `judgeGate`, on every request of any session whose CONNECT result was Scoped or Conditional, calling the live evaluator with that request's subject. Keep-alive requests from different users and mid-session policy swaps are each decided correctly. In these sessions scoped rate limits are charged per request, and the CONNECT-time check uses a non-charging `PeekFor` (new). Deny writes 403 with Event.Reason and the decision-log reason `identity_required` or `group_not_allowed` plus the VRFY user fields.

MCP: `OnRequest` gains a `gateway.RequestMeta{Subject *identity.Subject}` parameter on proxy.MCPGateway, proxy.WSScanner and the ws.Pump interface, and on all callers and fakes. http.go passes the request subject; ws.Pump stores the subject verified on the upgrade request; the stdio pump passes nil, so group-gated tools are denied over stdio. `compileConditions` adds group/user sets and `conditionDenies` fails with the existing Kind `mcp_tool_condition` and Detail `no verified identity` or `user not permitted`. P1 gates whole tools only; per-group argument constraints come later. The session key (`agentID:domain`) is unchanged in P1.

Replay and lint: `policyeval.Evaluate` builds a subject from Event.UserSub/UserEmail/UserGroups only when the recorded identity status is valid, and maps Conditional to deny. EvalDiff gains `AffectedUsers` (up to 20, sorted), `AffectedUsersTotal` and `AnonymousCount`. `warden policy eval` prints them and accepts `--user`. A new `config.LintScoped` warns about scoped entries shadowed by an unscoped or wildcard entry for the same destination; workers log once per agent when scoped entries exist but that agent's identity mode is off.

Observability: `RecordBlocked("identity_required"|"group_not_allowed")` and a new OTel counter `warden.policy.scoped.total{result=allow|not_member|no_identity}` (Prometheus name warden_policy_scoped_total) with no user or group labels. Raw tokens, group lists and emails never appear in metric labels or debug logs.

Dashboard: the CP policy editor adds groups/users chip inputs per allow entry and per MCP allowWhen, saved through `/dashboard/api/policy` and the existing policyYAML write path; the worker and CP policy views show a `scoped` badge and the lint warnings. Sorted, normalized groups/users keep ETags and the P1 policy-history diff deterministic.
done_when: On a CA-enabled worker in attribute mode with `{domain: api.github.com, groups: [eng]}` and no unscoped entry for that host: a valid Dex token for an eng member is allowed over both Proxy-Authorization and X-Warden-Identity; a non-member gets 403 `group_not_allowed`; anonymous, invalid and expired tokens get 403 `identity_required`; within one keep-alive session requests from different users are each decided correctly; a Conditional CONNECT with no CA, or one that switches to h2 or raw bytes, is denied and the judge is never consulted. An MCP tool with `allowWhen.groups: [finance]` is denied to eng and allowed to finance in enforce mode. A worker on the previous release that receives this policy from the CP denies api.github.com and the gated tool, and the fleet view flags it. `warden policy eval` against a candidate that removes eng access lists only the affected eng users plus a count of anonymous events. Deny events, decision logs and metrics carry the two new reasons.

tickets.body: Enforce scoped allow entries in the worker at CONNECT and on every request, then lift the W-P1-GPOL-01 guard for allow entries. name: Group-aware policy
label: identity-policy

summary: Workers verify CP-issued Warden tokens using keys from the verified signed bundle, check that each token was minted for the agent the worker serves and for a key that is still registered, and can run an agent in `require` mode, where traffic without a valid bound token is refused. Workers call the CP over mTLS with the renewing worker cert instead of a bearer token. Everything is default-off and builds on the P1 internal/identity package, so off and attribute deployments behave exactly as in P1.
design: Scope: require mode and agent binding on the worker, built on the P1 internal/identity package (W-P1-VRFY-01/02/07) and the verified bundle from W-P2-SBND-04. Nothing in this feature exists in the code yet; internal/identity, the identityP holder and RecordIdentityVerify come from P1, and the bundle, registry and token service come from P2.

Per-worker agent binding: one worker serves one agent. The worker's agent id is the one W-P2-AREG-05 resolves (`warden run --agent-id`, then `central.agentID`, then worker.defaultAgentID, validated with agentid.ValidID), so judge lookups, the MCP session key, the decision line agent_id and binding use one value; this feature adds no key or flag of its own. A port-derived `agent:<port>` id is never registered, so binding fails with agent_unregistered. Several agents sharing one worker cannot be told apart in P2, and the docs say so.

Mode resolution for the bound agent stays in settings, as in W-P1-VRFY-07 and p2-agent-registry: SettingsWire agents[].identity for the bound id, then identity.defaultMode, then off. W-P2-WBND-03 lets the CP serve `require` there; a standalone (local-only) worker has no signed bundle, so its local YAML keeps rejecting require. A P1 worker that receives require keeps its previous identity config (W-P1-VRFY-07), which is the rollout risk W-P2-WBND-07 guards. The worker logs the effective mode and its source at startup and on change.

Rollout safety: under W-P1-VRFY-07 an old worker ignores a mode it does not know and would stay in attribute mode. Workers that implement require mode add `identity/require-v1` to the heartbeat caps (next to blocklist/v1 and agentreg/v1); the bound agentID is already reported by W-P2-AREG-05. The CP refuses a settings save that sets require for an agent (409 workers_lack_capability, overridable with an audited admin-only force) while a connected worker bound to that agent lacks the cap, and agents[].identity and identity.defaultMode become admin-only fields.

Bundle inputs: the worker takes token keys from the bundle `sections.tokenJWKS` (W-P2-SBND-02), the issuer from the top-level bundle field `tokenIssuer` (added by W-P2-WBND-06), and agent status and key thumbprints from `registeredAgents[].{status,jkt}` (W-P2-AREG-04). Warden tokens carry `email` and `email_verified` (only when verified) and the JOSE header typ `wt+jwt` (W-P2-TOKX-02). The worker takes all of these only from `RemoteProvider.Bundle()`, which reports only bundles that passed bundle.Verify against pinned keys (W-P2-SBND-04); a worker without pins gets no keys, and the worker never fetches keys from the CP at runtime.

Warden token verifier (new internal/identity/warden.go, next to the P1 OIDC verifier): alg is EdDSA or ES256 and must match the JWK kty and crv; typ is wt+jwt; kid must be in the bundle JWKS; iss equals tokenIssuer byte for byte; aud contains `warden-worker`, which is deliberately distinct from the P1 Dex data-plane audience `warden` (W-P1-DEX-01), so the two token kinds cannot be confused; exp and nbf use identity.clockSkewSeconds (default 60s, max 5m); exp-iat is at most 15m (ttl_too_long); sub, act.sub, sid, jti and cnf.jkt are required (missing_claim); tokens over 16 KiB are rejected before parsing.

Dispatch and back-compat: a new identity.MultiVerifier reads the unverified iss after the size cap. tokenIssuer goes to the Warden verifier; identity.issuer goes to the P1 OIDC verifier only when `identity.acceptDexTokens` is true and is invalid with reason unbound_token when it is false; anything else is invalid with reason wrong_iss. acceptDexTokens is a *bool whose default is true when identity.issuer is set, so P1 attribute deployments keep status valid after upgrade. Dex tokens never satisfy require mode (reason unbound_token). Each accepted Dex token is counted with token_type=dex and produces at most one deprecation WARN per hour. The worker refuses to install a bundle keyset whose tokenIssuer equals identity.issuer.

Claims and subject: identity.Claims gains Act, CnfJKT, Scope, KID and TokenType (dex|warden). identity.SubjectFrom fills the existing Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID=act.sub}; no new principal type is added, so policy, block-list and MCP code keep one subject type. Group normalization and caps are the same as P1. Scope is parsed but not enforced or stored in P2.

Binding, checked on every use and never cached: the bound agent must be in the bundle (agent_unregistered) with status active (agent_disabled); act.sub must equal the bound agent id (agent_mismatch); cnf.jkt must be in that agent's `jkt` list (cnf_mismatch). This gives agent match plus key liveness: removing a key or disabling an agent invalidates outstanding tokens within one long-poll. It is not proof of possession, because the token is a bearer token, and the docs say so. A signed per-CONNECT proof or agent client certs (cnf x5t#S256) are a later follow-up outside P2. The worker does not see allowed_groups, so a token minted before an agent's allowed_groups shrank stays valid until exp (at most tokenService.ttl, 15m); this is an accepted P2 gap, and disabling the agent or blocking the user cuts it at once.

Snapshot and hot path: {generation, tokenIssuer, jwks, agents (id to status and jkt set)} is built once per verified bundle apply and swapped atomically. The P1 result LRU is keyed by (generation, sha256(token)), so an emergency key removal (W-P2-KEYS-05) takes effect on the next request. Cost per CONNECT: one cached lookup, or one EdDSA/ES256 verify when uncached, plus a few map lookups; budgets are the P1 ones (p99 under 100µs cached, under 1ms uncached, no network I/O).

Require-mode enforcement: after the W-P2-AREG-05 agent_disabled check (403), the CONNECT must carry a valid, bound Warden token in Proxy-Authorization (Basic session:<token> or Bearer). Otherwise the worker returns 407 with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="warden"` and JSON {"error":"identity_required","reason":"<reason>"} before the block-list check, policy evaluation or any dial, and stores a deny event. On terminated traffic (HTTP/1, h2 streams, WebSocket upgrade, MCP over HTTP) identity failures are 403 JSON with Connection: close where applicable and never 401 or WWW-Authenticate, because a 401 after TLS termination looks like an upstream challenge and starts credential or OAuth discovery in MCP clients. An X-Warden-Identity header with a different sub or act gets 403 identity_conflict. MCP denies stay plain JSON like the existing mcpRequestScan 403; there is no JSON-RPC error body. The block list (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and default-deny policy, including GPOL EvaluateFor with the Warden subject, still run after identity passes. Before the first verified bundle, all require-mode traffic is denied.

Token expiry on open connections: the CONNECT identity is valid until exp plus skew. A request after that gets 403 identity_expired with Connection: close; idle HTTP/1 keep-alives are closed at exp; h2 connections get GOAWAY and in-flight streams finish within existing timeouts; raw tunnels and WebSockets close at exp plus skew. This runs through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry with an expiry timer, so clients and `warden identity exec` reconnect with a fresh token.

Recording: analytics.Event gains UserAct (json user_act) and IdentityTokenType (json identity_token_type), both omitempty, so unattributed events and receipts stay byte-identical. The worker SQLite store adds columns; the CP fleet store columns are a separate CP ticket. The warden.decision.v1 schema gets user_act and token_type with a schema_rev bump. Tokens, cnf values and Authorization headers are never logged, stored or put in error bodies.

Metrics: extend the P1 instrument warden.identity.verify.total{result,reason} with a bounded token_type label (dex|warden|none) and the reasons agent_mismatch, cnf_mismatch, agent_disabled, agent_unregistered, unbound_token and missing_claim; P1 reasons such as wrong_iss, unknown_kid, alg_not_allowed, ttl_too_long and jwks_unavailable are reused. There is no agent or sub label. Require-mode denials count on the existing warden.blocked.total with reasons identity_required, identity_expired and identity_conflict. A gauge warden.controlplane.clock_skew_seconds is estimated from the CP Date header on each long-poll. The worker dashboard identity summary is computed from stored events, because internal/dashboard does not read OTel metrics.

Worker-to-CP mTLS comes from p2-worker-ca: W-P2-WCA-03 builds the one cert-presenting client (`controlPlane.enrollment`, or `controlPlane.clientCert`/`clientKey` for an external PKI) used by RemoteProvider and HTTPRemoteStore and sends no Authorization header once a cert is loaded. W-P2-WBND-05 adds no config; it proves the no-downgrade and mid-poll renewal behaviour this feature relies on. In P2 only /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest are called this way; P3 adds POST /control/user-token (W-P3-PUS-07) and POST /control/connect/pending (W-P3-JIT-01) on the same client, both cert-only (mTLS), rate-limited, with the CP re-verifying the user token on each call; /central/secrets stays a human-only route. A worker-aggregator central target keeps its bearer token.

Degraded modes: with the CP down, workers keep verifying with keys from the last-known-good bundle in memory; no new tokens can be minted, so require-mode agents fail closed at most one token TTL (15 minutes) later. Operators alert on a rise in warden.identity.verify.total{result="expired"}. With Dex down, exchange fails at the CP and existing Warden tokens work until exp; the worker never contacts Dex for Warden tokens. A restart with the CP down reloads the bundle only from the opt-in W-P2-SBND-06 cache (`<controlPlane.stateDir>/bundle/`); without it the worker stays fail-closed. A client cert that expires during a CP outage keeps the last-known-good policy (W-P2-WCA-03).

Carry-forward from p1-block-list: no agent-kind block entry is added. Require mode closes the token-less gap that W-P1-BLOCK-02 left, and registry status=disabled, enforced by the worker as agent_disabled, is the agent-level kill switch.
done_when: On a compose deployment with a CP (token service, signed bundles, worker CA, agent registry) and one enrolled worker bound with `--agent-id` (W-P2-AREG-05) to a registered agent whose settings entry is in require mode, where the CP refused the switch while a worker without identity/require-v1 was connected: CONNECTs with no token, a Dex ID token, an expired, forged or unknown-kid Warden token, a token minted for another agent, a token whose agent key was removed, or a token for a disabled agent each get 407, no upstream dial and a deny event with the matching reason. A Warden token from POST /oauth2/token for a permitted user is accepted, and its local event, decision line and fleet event carry sub, act, sid, groups and token_type=warden with no token in any log. Blocking that user by email, or disabling the agent, denies new requests and closes open sessions within one long-poll cycle. Open connections close at token exp and the identity exec forwarder reconnects with a fresh token. With the CP stopped the worker keeps accepting unexpired tokens from its last-known-good bundle and denies everything after they expire, and a worker started before its first verified bundle denies all traffic. An attribute-mode agent on a P1 config still records Dex tokens as valid. All worker calls to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest use the renewing client cert with no Authorization header, and a renewal mid-run does not drop the long-poll.

tickets.title: Verify CP-issued Warden tokens against verified bundle keys
tickets.body: Add a Warden token verifier to the P1 internal/identity package that takes its keys, issuer and agents only from the last signed bundle that passed bundle.Verify, swapped atomically on each bundle apply. A dispatcher routes tokens by issuer so P1 Dex tokens keep working in attribute mode, and the result uses the existing identity.Claims and identity.Subject types. Nothing changes until a CP serves a bundle with tokenIssuer and jwks.
requirements: New internal/identity/warden.go: WardenVerifier implementing the P1 identity.Verifier interface. Allowed algs are exactly EdDSA and ES256, and the header alg must match the JWK kty/crv (none, HS* and RS* give alg_not_allowed). Header typ must be `wt+jwt` (else malformed). kid must be in the bundle `sections.tokenJWKS` (else unknown_kid). iss must equal the bundle `tokenIssuer` byte for byte. aud must contain the new constant identity.WardenWorkerAudience = "warden-worker", which is deliberately distinct from the P1 Dex data-plane audience `warden` (W-P1-DEX-01).

exp and nbf are checked with the P1 identity.clockSkewSeconds setting (default 60s, max 5m); exp-iat above 15m gives ttl_too_long; missing sub, act.sub, sid, jti or cnf.jkt gives the new reason missing_claim; tokens over 16 KiB give too_large before parsing. Signatures are checked with internal/keys.Verify (W-P2-KEYS-01).

identity.Claims gains Act, CnfJKT, Scope, KID and TokenType (dex|warden). SubjectFrom sets Subject.AgentID from act.sub and fills Email and EmailVerified from the token's email and email_verified claims. No Principal type is added. Scope is parsed but not enforced or stored.

New identity.MultiVerifier reads the unverified iss after the size cap: tokenIssuer goes to the WardenVerifier, identity.issuer goes to the P1 OIDC verifier only when acceptDexTokens resolves true and gives invalid/unbound_token when it resolves false, and any other iss gives invalid/wrong_iss. A Dex token never satisfies require mode (reason unbound_token, applied in W-P2-WBND-03).

New config field identity.acceptDexTokens (*bool, json/yaml acceptDexTokens, omitempty) on IdentitySettings and the local identity block, with DeepCopy and SettingsWire round-trip support. Unset resolves to true when identity.issuer is set and false otherwise. Each valid Dex token is recorded with token_type=dex and logs at most one WARN per hour naming the deprecation, with no token data.

Keys come only from `RemoteProvider.Bundle()` (W-P2-SBND-04), which reports only bundles verified against pinned keys; a worker without pins (legacy wire) installs no keys. Before the first verified bundle, Warden tokens return unverified/jwks_unavailable. A tokenIssuer equal to identity.issuer is refused with one ERROR log and leaves keys unavailable. The worker never fetches keys from the CP at runtime.

The snapshot {generation, tokenIssuer, jwks, agents} is swapped atomically with a monotonically increasing generation, and the P1 result LRU is keyed by (generation, sha256(token)), so a kid removed from the bundle stops verifying on the next request.

Raw tokens never appear in logs, errors, events or test output; debug logs carry only kid and an 8-hex sha256 fingerprint. The cached path stays under 100µs p99 and an uncached verify under 1ms, recorded under warden.request.added_latency stage=identity.
plan: internal/identity (from W-P1-VRFY-01): extend Claims with Act, CnfJKT, Scope, KID and TokenType; extend SubjectFrom; add reasons missing_claim and unbound_token to the bounded Reason set and add them to docs/identity-contract.md so TestContractDocMatchesConstants stays green.

New internal/identity/warden.go: WardenVerifier with an atomic.Pointer to a new keySnapshot type and SetBundle(tokenIssuer string, jwks []keys.JWK, generation int64); verification as in the requirements using internal/keys.Verify.
New internal/identity/multi.go: MultiVerifier dispatch by unverified iss, deprecation WARN rate limiter for Dex tokens, cache key including the generation.
internal/config: add IdentitySettings.AcceptDexTokens *bool plus a resolver method, local YAML field, DeepCopy and validation.

internal/worker/applier.go: in SettingsApplier.Apply, after the long-poll applies a verified bundle (W-P2-SBND-04), call WardenVerifier.SetBundle and swap the MultiVerifier through the P1 identityP holder (W-P1-VRFY-07). internal/worker/worker.go does the same at startup when the W-P2-SBND-06 cache was loaded.

Tests: internal/identity TestWardenVerifier, TestWardenKeysetSwap (-race), TestMultiVerifierDispatch and BenchmarkWardenVerify; internal/config TestIdentityAcceptDexTokensDefault; internal/worker TestBundleAppliesTokenKeys with a fake CP.
acceptance: Given a bundle JWKS with EdDSA kid K1: a valid K1 token returns valid with TokenType=warden and Subject.AgentID=act.sub; a K2-signed token gives unknown_kid; alg none and HS256 signed with the public key give alg_not_allowed; aud `warden` gives wrong_aud; exp-iat=20m gives ttl_too_long; missing cnf gives missing_claim. Command: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestWardenVerifier`.

A token cached as valid under K1 returns unknown_kid on the next Verify after a bundle without K1 is applied, and K2 tokens from the new bundle verify without a restart, with 100 concurrent verifications during the swap: `go test -race ./internal/identity -run TestWardenKeysetSwap`.

With identity.issuer set and acceptDexTokens absent, a valid Dex token returns valid with TokenType=dex; with acceptDexTokens false it returns invalid/unbound_token; with no identity.issuer the default resolves to false: `go test ./internal/config ./internal/identity -run 'TestIdentityAcceptDexTokensDefault|TestMultiVerifierDispatch'`.

A fake CP serving bundle v1 and then v2 with a rotated key causes a keyset swap with zero requests to any JWKS endpoint, and a worker with no pins (legacy wire) leaves Warden tokens at unverified/jwks_unavailable: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestBundleAppliesTokenKeys`.

`go test ./internal/identity -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkWardenVerify -benchmem` shows the cached path under 100µs/op, and a captured slog buffer from the tests above contains no substring of any test token.

tickets.title: Bind Warden tokens to the worker's registered agent and key
tickets.body: Using the worker agent id from W-P2-AREG-05, check that every Warden token was minted for that agent, that the agent is active, and that the token's cnf.jkt is one of the agent's current registry keys. This gives agent match plus key liveness, not proof of possession, and the docs say so. Record the agent (act) on worker events and decision lines.
requirements: The bound agent id is the one W-P2-AREG-05 resolves (`--agent-id`, then `central.agentID`, then worker.defaultAgentID); this ticket adds no config key or flag, so existing judge lookups do not change.

Binding runs in the P1 proxy identity resolvers (W-P1-VRFY-02) after signature verification, for Warden tokens only, in this order: bound agent not in the bundle agents gives agent_unregistered; status disabled gives agent_disabled; act.sub different from the bound agent gives agent_mismatch; cnf.jkt not in that agent's `jkt` list from Policy.RegisteredAgents (W-P2-AREG-04) gives cnf_mismatch. Every failure gives status invalid and a nil Subject.

Binding is checked on every use against the current snapshot and never cached. The thumbprint lookup is a map[string]struct{} built on bundle apply in the same atomic snapshot as the keyset, with 0 allocs/op.

In attribute mode a binding failure is recorded and the request continues as anonymous per policy. The block-list check (W-P1-BLOCK-02) still matches the parsed sub and email, because a match can only deny.

analytics.Event gains UserAct (json user_act) and IdentityTokenType (json identity_token_type), both omitempty, stamped only for valid identities, with local SQLite columns through addColumnIfAbsent in insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs. Identity-free events stay byte-identical.
decisionLog and the warden.decision.v1 schema gain user_act and token_type with a schema_rev bump. Tokens and cnf values are never logged.

docs/identity-contract.md and docs/control-plane.md state the guarantee (agent match and key liveness within one long-poll, not proof of possession), the one-agent-per-worker rule, and that a port-derived id such as `agent:8080` never matches a registry id.
plan: Reuse the W-P2-AREG-05 resolved agent id from the worker options; add no config key or flag.
internal/worker/worker.go: pass the resolved id into the identity binding check and log it with the effective mode and its source at startup.

internal/identity: new BindingCheck(snapshot, agentID, claims) (Reason, ok) next to WardenVerifier, reading the agents map from the W-P2-WBND-01 snapshot; add reasons agent_mismatch, cnf_mismatch, agent_disabled and agent_unregistered to the Reason set and the contract doc.
internal/proxy identity resolvers (resolveConnIdentity and resolveRequestIdentity from W-P1-VRFY-02): call BindingCheck after a valid Warden verify and downgrade the status on failure.

tickets.title: Enforce identity require mode on CONNECT and terminated traffic
tickets.body: Add the `require` mode for an agent whose served settings entry (agents[].identity) asks for it. A CONNECT without a valid, bound Warden token gets 407 before any dial, and identity failures inside a terminated tunnel get 403 JSON. The worker fails closed before its first verified bundle and advertises the identity/require-v1 heartbeat cap so the CP can refuse require for agents served by old workers.
requirements: Mode resolution for the bound agent: SettingsWire agents[].identity for the W-P2-AREG-05 agent id, then identity.defaultMode, then off. config validation now accepts `require` in served SettingsWire (CP write path and parseRemotePolicy); local YAML on a worker without controlPlane.endpoint keeps rejecting it, so a standalone worker never enters require. The effective mode and its source are logged on change and shown on /dashboard/api/status.

CONNECT in require mode: the W-P2-AREG-05 agent_disabled check runs first (403). Proxy-Authorization is mandatory and must verify (W-P2-WBND-01) and bind (W-P2-WBND-02) with TokenType=warden. Otherwise the worker writes 407 Proxy Authentication Required with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="warden"`, Content-Type application/json, Connection: close and body {"error":"identity_required","reason":"<bounded reason>"}, before the block-list check, Policy.Evaluate and any dial, and stores a deny event with the new Reason identity_required in internal/proxy/reasons.go.

Terminated traffic (runRequestStages, serveGRPCStream, WebSocket upgrade in ws.go, MCP over HTTP): an X-Warden-Identity header whose sub or act differs from the CONNECT identity gets 403 identity_conflict; a request after the CONNECT identity's exp plus skew gets 403 identity_expired with Connection: close; h2 streams get 403 on the stream. No 401 or WWW-Authenticate is ever written, and MCP denies are plain JSON like the existing mcpRequestScan 403, with no JSON-RPC body.

Fail closed: in require mode, before the first verified bundle, with an empty keyset, or with an unregistered bound agent, every CONNECT gets 407 with reason jwks_unavailable or agent_unregistered. A bundle loaded from the opt-in W-P2-SBND-06 cache lifts this at restart without the CP.

Default-deny is unchanged: the block list (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and policy evaluation, including GPOL EvaluateFor with the Warden subject, still run after identity passes. Attribute and off modes are byte-for-byte unchanged.
RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds `identity/require-v1` to caps; the bound agentID is already sent by W-P2-AREG-05. Old CPs ignore the cap.

Denials increment warden.blocked.total with reasons identity_required, identity_expired and identity_conflict, and warden.requests.total{decision="deny"}. Response bodies carry only bounded reason codes. The new mode, error codes and reasons are added to docs/identity-contract.md so TestContractDocMatchesConstants passes.

tickets.title: Use the worker mTLS client cert for all CP calls
tickets.body: W-P2-WCA-03 already builds the one cert-presenting CP client (`controlPlane.enrollment`, or `controlPlane.clientCert`/`clientKey`) for RemoteProvider and HTTPRemoteStore, so this ticket adds no config keys or transport. It proves the properties require mode depends on: every worker-plane CP call presents the cert, no call ever falls back to a bearer token, and a renewal never drops the long-poll. If p2-worker-bound adds a new CP call, it must use the same client.

A renewal swap during a held long-poll does not cancel it; the next handshake presents the new serial (W-P2-WCA-03 CloseIdleConnections).
A worker-aggregator central target that is not the CP keeps its bearer token.
Key material and PEM never reach logs; the existing `warden_worker_cert_expiry_seconds` gauge from W-P2-WCA-03 is the only expiry metric.

tickets.title: Close require-mode sessions at token expiry and document require mode
tickets.body: A CONNECT-bound Warden token lasts 15 minutes, but raw tunnels, keep-alives, h2 connections and WebSockets can stay open far longer. Close require-mode sessions at token expiry through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry, and close sessions whose agent or key was revoked by a bundle change. Write the require-mode section of the identity contract.
requirements: Sessions in require mode register in the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry with their token exp and kid. A single expiry timer (a min-heap, no per-connection goroutine) closes them: idle HTTP/1 keep-alives at exp; h2 connections get GOAWAY at exp and in-flight streams finish within existing timeouts; raw tunnels and WebSockets close at exp plus clockSkewSeconds.
Each closure writes one deny event with Reason identity_expired and calls RecordBlocked("identity_expired").

After each verified bundle apply, the registry re-checks require-mode sessions and closes those whose kid left the JWKS or whose binding now fails (agent disabled or key removed), with the matching reason.
Attribute-mode and anonymous sessions are not registered for expiry, so they see no change.

docs/identity-contract.md gains a require-mode section that adds to Contract v1 without changing any v1 header: Warden token on CONNECT, 407 and 403 bodies, the identity_conflict rule, close at exp, Dex tokens only in attribute mode, and that binding is agent match plus key liveness, not proof of possession.

docs/control-plane.md documents degraded modes: CP down means require-mode agents fail closed one token TTL later; Dex down affects only new exchanges; a restart with the CP down reloads the bundle only from the opt-in W-P2-SBND-06 cache, otherwise it stays fail-closed.
