name: Agent-bound tokens + mTLS
label: identity-enforcement

summary: A per-user mapping lets the worker swap a placeholder for an access token minted from the calling user's own OAuth grant, so two users of the same agent reach Google or GitHub with their own credentials. Refresh tokens and OAuth client secrets never leave the control plane: the CP is the only refresh authority and hands workers short-lived access tokens over worker mTLS, and only for a verified, agent-bound Warden token. A swap happens only when the placeholder appears in an allowed location of a request to one of the mapping's domains. Everything is off until `perUserSecrets.enabled` is set, and the static `secrets[]` path is unchanged.
design: Scope and flag: a new CP-local top-level block `perUserSecrets: {enabled (default false), workerCacheTTL (default 5m, max 15m), mappings[]}`, a sibling of `secretStore`; grants live in the CP-only `consent.store` (W-P3-CSIG-06). With it absent or disabled, GET /policy, the signed bundle and worker behaviour stay byte-identical. The static path (config.SecretMapping{Placeholder, EnvVar}, secrets.NewCache, storeFetcher, swapSecrets in internal/proxy/http.go and the header loop in serveGRPCStream in internal/proxy/grpc.go) is not changed. Enabling it requires `--bundles` offer or require (W-P2-SBND-02) and the token service (p2-token-service), because only bound Warden tokens can release a user's credential.

Trust split: grants live in the CP-only user credential store `consent.store` (W-P3-CSIG-06; backend aws|vault|echo, its own CP credentials, namePrefix default `warden-cp/`), never in the distributed secretStore. The CP sends the worker secretStore credential over SettingsWire.Secrets (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go, internal/config/settings.go SecretsSettings), so the CP refuses to start when consent.store overlaps it, and no worker IAM role or Vault policy is ever granted on the consent.store prefix. The consent block is `json:"-"`, never on SettingsWire or in a bundle. Refresh tokens and client secrets therefore never reach the tier that terminates agent TLS. This feature adds the Vault KV v2 backend (W-P3-PUS-01) that consent.store can then select (W-P3-PUS-02). Workers never receive stored per-user credentials (refresh tokens, grants, IdP links or client secrets) or any access to consent.store; they only receive the short-lived access token each mint returns (W-P3-PUS-07).

Keys and records: keys come only from the W-P3-CSIG-06 helpers: userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) (32 hex characters of a domain-separated SHA-256 over iss and sub; for a Warden token, iss is its idp_iss claim) and secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider) = `users/<userKey>/<provider>`, so subs containing '/', '+' or '=' cannot collide or traverse paths and two issuers never share a key. The stored record is the W-P3-BRKR-01 oauthbroker.TokenRecord v1 {v, grant_id, provider, client_id, token_type, access_token, refresh_token, scope, expiry, refresh_expiry, obtained_at}. Every SecretStore wraps a new `secrets.ErrNotFound`, and an optional `secrets.VersionedStore` (GetVersion/PutIfVersion) gives compare-and-swap where the backend has it (Vault KV v2 `options.cas`); W-P3-PUS-06 adds the guarded read and write helpers on top.

Mappings: `perUserSecrets.mappings: [{placeholder, provider, scopes, domains, in, agents}]` are validated on the CP. The provider must be in the p3-oauth-broker registry; domains is required and uses the allowlist domain grammar; `in` is header and/or query (default [header]; body is not supported); agents must pass agentid.ValidID. Placeholders must not equal or contain, or be contained in, a static placeholder or another mapping. The value-free mappings ship as the signed-bundle section `perUserSecrets`, and the broker scope cap (W-P3-BRKR-03, W-P3-JIT-01) reads the same list.

Identity precondition: a per-user placeholder is swapped only when the request's connIdentity (W-P1-VRFY-02) has Status valid, Claims.TokenType == warden (W-P2-WBND-01), passed the agent binding of W-P2-WBND-02 (act.sub equals the worker's bound agent), and the bound agent is listed in mapping.agents. Otherwise the worker answers 403 JSON {error: identity_required, reason: warden_token_required} with a deny event; it never writes 401 and never forwards. P1 Dex tokens never release a per-user credential.

Lazy, domain-bound swap: one shared resolver is called from swapSecrets and serveGRPCStream after the static swap. It looks for each per-user placeholder only in the locations listed in mapping.in, and only when one is present does it check the destination. A placeholder sent to a domain outside mapping.domains gets 403 reason secret_domain_mismatch and nothing is forwarded. A request with no per-user placeholder makes zero token lookups, header-only mappings never buffer the body (so the 10 MB 413 does not newly apply), and per-user placeholders are excluded from PlaceholderNames and the static Cache prefetch.

CP mint endpoint `POST /control/user-token`, accepted only from a worker cert principal (W-P2-WCA-04), never from `wwt_` tokens, user tokens or console sessions. Body {subject_token, placeholder, force_refresh, stale_ref}. The CP re-verifies the Warden token with its own token keys (iss, aud warden-worker, exp), takes userKey = secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub) from it, checks act.sub against the agentID that worker reports in its heartbeat (W-P2-AREG-03), that the token session is not revoked (W-P2-TOKX-07) and that the user is not blocked (W-P1-BLOCK-03). It then checks grant status and that mapping.scopes are all granted. It returns {access_token, expires_in, scope, grant_epoch, ref} with Cache-Control: no-store, or {error: grant_missing|scope_insufficient|reconsent_required|user_token_unavailable}.

CP refresh engine (new internal/oauthbroker/usertoken.go): an in-memory cache keyed (userKey, provider), with singleflight under oauthbroker.GrantLocks (W-P3-BRKR-04), the per-(userKey, provider) mutex shared with the connect callback, RevokeUserGrant and offboarding. It reuses the stored access_token while it has more than 60s left, measured from local receipt time, and otherwise runs the refresh_token grant through the W-P3-BRKR-07 client with the CP-held client secret. A rotated refresh token is persisted first (PutIfVersion where available) and only while the grant is still active, its epoch unchanged and its grant_id unchanged (W-P3-PUS-06); a response without refresh_token keeps the stored one. A forced refresh happens only when the current token's ref equals stale_ref, at most once per 30s per key. GitHub OAuth-app records (expiry 0, no refresh_token) are used as stored, and a forced refresh on one marks reconsent_required.

Outcome classification: a missing record or ErrNotFound gives grant_missing; required scopes not granted gives scope_insufficient; invalid_grant at refresh sets oauth_grants.state=reconsent_required, keeps the row and never triggers offboarding, because Dex and Google return invalid_grant for expiry and testing-mode limits too (p3-offboarding carry-forward). These three set s.authRequired so the JIT stage (W-P3-JIT-02) can ask for consent. Store errors, provider 5xx or timeouts, an unreachable CP or a mint timeout (5s) give 503 {error: user_token_unavailable} with Retry-After; they never forward and never send the user to re-consent.

Worker cache and revocation: tokens are held only in memory (never on disk or in the bundle cache), keyed (idp_iss, sub, agent, provider), LRU-bounded (10k), with TTL = min(expires_in - 60s, workerCacheTTL) on the monotonic clock from receipt and singleflight on miss. Revocation uses the signed-bundle section `userGrantEpochs` {userKey: epoch}, where epoch is the publish_log seq of the bump, so values only grow; portal revoke (W-P3-PORT-02) and offboarding bump it with publish_log reason `user_grant`, and entries older than 2 x workerCacheTTL are pruned so the section stays bounded. The worker interface is `UserTokenSource.AccessToken(ctx, ident, mapping)` and `Invalidate(key, staleRef)`, reused later by p4-park and p4-mcp-gateway. This section is the only grant-revocation channel to workers; p3-consent-portal adds no other.

401 retry: only on terminated HTTP/1 requests where a per-user token was swapped and the request is replayable (no body, or a body already buffered within maxBodySwapSize). The proxy keeps the pre-swap headers and RawQuery, drains at most 64 KiB of the 401, asks the CP with force_refresh and the stale ref, rebuilds the request, re-runs the swap and applyTransforms, and sends once. A second 401 is relayed; 403, h2, gRPC, WebSocket and streamed bodies are never retried.

Rollout and degraded modes: workers advertise heartbeat cap `usersecrets/v1`; the CP refuses to enable a mapping for an agent whose connected worker lacks it (409 workers_lack_capability, audited admin-only force, as in W-P2-WBND-07). An old worker forwards the literal placeholder, which leaks nothing. With the CP down, cached tokens work until their TTL and then requests get 503. Clock skew does not matter because only relative expires_in crosses the wire. In P3 one CP is the only refresh authority; p5-postgres-ha must add a per-key advisory lock or consistent routing of mints.

Observability and hygiene: worker OTel instruments `warden.user_token.total{provider,source=cache|cp,outcome}` and `warden.user_token.retry.total{provider,outcome}`, with lookup time under `warden.request.added_latency` stage=user_token; CP instruments `warden.cp.user_token.refresh.total{provider,outcome}` and `warden.cp.user_token.writeback_failures.total`. There is no sub or agent label, and provider is a registered id or `other`. New deny reasons in internal/proxy/reasons.go: secret_domain_mismatch, authorization_required and user_token_unavailable (identity_required already exists). Events carry the placeholder name, provider (new Event.UserTokenProvider, not the LLM cost field Event.Provider) and secrets.Ref only. Subject tokens, access tokens, refresh tokens, client secrets and provider error_description never appear in logs, rows, labels or error bodies.
done_when: In the compose deployment with the token service, worker CA, signed bundles and `perUserSecrets.enabled` on, grants in the CP-only consent.store, one enrolled worker bound to a registered agent, and users A and B who connected a Google provider (a fake provider in CI) through the broker: A's request with the per-user placeholder to a mapped domain carries A's access token upstream and B's carries B's; the same placeholder sent to an unmapped allowlisted domain is denied with secret_domain_mismatch and nothing is forwarded; a Dex or missing token gets 403 identity_required, never 401; an expired access token is refreshed transparently and an upstream 401 is retried exactly once, with any rotated refresh token persisted before use; a user with no grant or too few scopes is handed to JIT with nothing forwarded; a revoke stops the worker swapping that user's token within one long-poll; with the CP stopped, cached tokens work until workerCacheTTL and then requests get 503 user_token_unavailable; a provider outage never marks a grant reconsent_required; the worker's store credentials cannot read the grant prefix and no refresh token or client secret is ever on the worker; no token appears in any log, event, metric or error body; and with the feature off, /policy, the bundle and worker behaviour are byte-identical.

tickets.title: Add Vault KV v2 SecretStore, ErrNotFound and VersionedStore
tickets.body: Add a Vault backend that implements SecretStore over the KV v2 HTTP API, plus two contracts the per-user path needs from every store: a typed not-found error and optional compare-and-swap. Today only awsSecretStore has write support, its not-found error (ErrSecretNotFound) is AWS-specific, and the existing VaultFetcher is read-only and has no callers. This ticket is library-only in internal/secrets, so merging changes no behaviour; W-P3-PUS-02 registers it as a consent.store backend.
requirements: New internal/secrets/vault_store.go: `NewVaultSecretStore(cfg VaultStoreConfig, client *http.Client) (SecretStore, error)` with VaultStoreConfig{Addr, Mount (default "secret"), NamePrefix, Token, Namespace}. Get reads GET /v1/<mount>/data/<prefix><key> (.data.data.value); Put writes POST /v1/<mount>/data/<prefix><key> {data:{value}}; Delete is DELETE /v1/<mount>/metadata/<prefix><key> (all versions, 404 is success); List walks LIST /v1/<mount>/metadata/<prefix> recursively with a 10,000-key cap and never calls a data/ path.
Put on a new key also sets metadata max_versions=1, so a rotated refresh token is not recoverable from an older version.

New `secrets.ErrNotFound`. awsSecretStore.Get (wrapping ErrSecretNotFound), EchoStore and the env fetcher path wrap it, and the Vault store maps 404 to it. ErrSecretNotFound stays for the AWS client so existing callers keep working.

New optional interface `secrets.VersionedStore { GetVersion(ctx, key) (value string, version int64, err error); PutIfVersion(ctx, key, value string, version int64) error }` with `secrets.ErrVersionConflict`. The Vault store implements it with KV v2 `options.cas` (version 0 means create-only); AWS does not implement it.

Key path segments are escaped with url.PathEscape; keys containing '..', a leading '/' or an empty segment are rejected. Response bodies are capped at 1 MiB with io.LimitReader and the client has a 5s timeout.
Errors and logs carry only the key, mount, version and HTTP status; never the token, a value or a response body. VaultFetcher in internal/secrets/vault.go is left unchanged.
plan: internal/secrets/store.go: add ErrNotFound, VersionedStore and ErrVersionConflict next to the SecretStore interface.
internal/secrets/aws_store.go and internal/secrets/echo.go: wrap ErrNotFound on a missing key (keep errors.Is(err, ErrSecretNotFound) true for AWS).
New internal/secrets/vault_store.go: vaultSecretStore with Get, Put, Delete, List, GetVersion and PutIfVersion over net/http, X-Vault-Token and optional X-Vault-Namespace headers.
New internal/secrets/vault_store_test.go against an httptest KV v2 fake that records paths and supports cas, metadata and LIST.

New internal/secrets/conformance_test.go: one table-driven suite (Put/Get round trip, Delete idempotent, missing key wraps ErrNotFound) run against echo, the fake-client AWS store and the Vault store.
acceptance: Put then Get of key `openai` returns the value; after Delete the fake recorded DELETE on metadata/<prefix>openai and Get returns an error matching errors.Is(err, secrets.ErrNotFound). Verify with `go test ./internal/secrets -run 'TestVaultStore|TestStoreConformance' -race`.
With keys `a`, `b/c` and `b/d` stored, List returns all three as value-free SecretMeta and the fake saw zero requests to any data/ path.
With a stored version 2, PutIfVersion(key, v, 1) returns ErrVersionConflict and the value is unchanged; PutIfVersion(key, v, 0) on an existing key also conflicts.
A key of `../x` or `/x` is rejected before any HTTP call.
No test output or captured log line contains the fake Vault token or any stored value (log-capture assertion in vault_store_test.go).

tickets.title: Add the CP-local perUserSecrets config block and the Vault consent.store backend
tickets.body: Add the CP-only `perUserSecrets` block that turns the feature on and defines the value-free per-user mappings, and let consent.store (W-P3-CSIG-06) select the W-P3-PUS-01 Vault backend. Per-user mappings live here rather than in worker `secrets[]` so the CP, which caps scopes and mints tokens, is the single source of truth. The grant store itself, its credentials and its overlap check against the distributed secretStore come from W-P3-CSIG-06. With the block absent, nothing changes.
requirements: New internal/config/peruser.go: `PerUserSecretsConfig{Enabled bool; WorkerCacheTTL time.Duration; Mappings []PerUserMapping}` on Policy with `json:"-"`, parsed from top-level YAML `perUserSecrets` with KnownFields strict and EncodeNode support like secretstore.go. Defaults: enabled false, workerCacheTTL 5m (allowed 30s-15m).

When enabled, startup fails unless the provider is in the oauthbroker registry (W-P3-BRKR-01), the token service is enabled, `--bundles` is offer or require, and consent.store is configured and persistent; each error names the missing key.

tickets.title: Implement the CP user-token refresh engine
tickets.body: Add the CP-side engine that turns a stored grant into a usable access token. The CP is the only refresh authority, so refresh-token rotation cannot race across workers and refresh tokens and client secrets never leave the CP. The engine serializes per (userKey, provider), persists any rotated refresh token before handing out the new access token, and classifies outcomes so an outage never sends a user to re-consent. This ticket has no HTTP route; W-P3-PUS-07 exposes it.
requirements: New internal/oauthbroker/usertoken.go: `Engine.Token(ctx, userKey, provider string, need []string, force bool, staleRef string) (Minted, error)` with Minted{AccessToken, ExpiresIn, Scope, GrantEpoch, Ref} and typed errors ErrGrantMissing (from W-P3-PUS-06), ErrScopeInsufficient, ErrReconsentRequired and ErrTokenUnavailable.

Concurrency: golang.org/x/sync/singleflight plus oauthbroker.GrantLocks from W-P3-BRKR-04. `Engine.WithGrantLock(userKey, provider, fn)` takes that lock and drops the engine's cache entry for the key; RevokeUserGrant (W-P3-PORT-02) and offboarding call it. Before any write-back the engine re-checks that oauth_grants.state is active, the grant epoch is unchanged and the stored grant_id still matches (W-P3-PUS-06), so a refresh that overlaps a revoke or a reconnect cannot restore or overwrite the grant.

Lookup: a cached or stored access_token with more than 60s left, measured from local receipt time, is returned. Otherwise call oauthbroker.Refresh (W-P3-BRKR-07) with the CP-held client secret, under a 5s deadline.

Write-back: a response with a new refresh_token is persisted with the W-P3-PUS-06 StoreRotated helper (PutIfVersion on Vault, a grant_id read-compare under GrantLocks elsewhere) before the token is returned; a response without refresh_token keeps the stored one. Put is retried 3 times with short backoff (100ms, 400ms, 1.6s) while the rotated token is held in memory; on final failure the rotated token is kept in memory for that key and written again on the next refresh, last_refresh_status=writeback_failed is recorded, the writeback failure counter increments, and a high `user_token_writeback_failed` Finding is published (DedupKey from the opaque userKey and provider, never sub or email). There is no encrypted write-back queue in P3: a CP restart before the next successful write forces re-consent for that user and provider.

Classification: ErrNotFound or no grant row gives ErrGrantMissing; `need` not a subset of granted scopes gives ErrScopeInsufficient; ErrRefreshInvalidGrant sets oauth_grants.state=reconsent_required, keeps the row and returns ErrReconsentRequired (never offboarding); store errors, provider 5xx, network errors and timeouts give ErrTokenUnavailable. Records with expiry 0 and no refresh_token are returned as stored; force on such a record (ErrNotRefreshable) gives ErrReconsentRequired.
force is honoured only when the current token's Ref equals staleRef, and at most once per 30s per key; otherwise the current token is returned.
A migration adds oauth_grants.last_refresh_at and last_refresh_status with addColumnIfAbsent; the reconsent_required state already exists in W-P3-BRKR-02. No value column is added.

Only the OAuth `error` code is logged, as a bounded enum; never error_description, bodies or token values. CP instruments warden.cp.user_token.refresh.total{provider,outcome} and warden.cp.user_token.writeback_failures.total.
plan: Use oauthbroker.Refresh from W-P3-BRKR-07 for the provider call.
New internal/oauthbroker/usertoken.go: Engine with the cache map, singleflight.Group, key mutexes, the force window and WithGrantLock.
internal/oauthbroker grant store (W-P3-BRKR-02): add the last_refresh columns migration and a SetState method.
Read and write TokenRecords at secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider) in consent.store through the W-P3-PUS-06 LoadGrant and StoreRotated helpers.
Add the two CP instruments in internal/observability with nil-safe Record methods.
Tests in internal/oauthbroker/usertoken_test.go with a fake provider token endpoint and an in-memory VersionedStore.
acceptance: 100 concurrent Token calls for one key with an expired stored token cause exactly 1 provider refresh, and all callers get the same token. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestEngineSingleflight -race`.
A provider response with a new refresh_token produces exactly one PutIfVersion before Token returns; a response without refresh_token produces zero writes.
invalid_grant sets oauth_grants.state=reconsent_required and returns ErrReconsentRequired; a provider 503 or a store 500 returns ErrTokenUnavailable and leaves state active.

A revoke run under WithGrantLock while a refresh is in flight (test hook pauses the refresh) leaves the record deleted after both finish. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestEngineRevokeRace -race`.
Two force calls with the same staleRef within 30s cause one refresh; a force with a staleRef that no longer matches returns the current token without refreshing.
No test output or captured log contains an access token, refresh token or client secret.

tickets.title: Swap per-user placeholders only for bound identities on mapped domains
tickets.body: Add the worker resolver that replaces a per-user placeholder with the calling user's access token, used by both swapSecrets in http.go and serveGRPCStream in grpc.go. It runs only when the placeholder actually appears in an allowed location, only for a valid, agent-bound Warden token, and only toward the mapping's domains, so an agent cannot send a user's token to a paste site or an LLM API. A missing grant never forwards the request and never returns 503; it hands off to the JIT stage.
requirements: New internal/proxy/usertoken.go: a userTokensP atomic holder {src UserTokenSource; mappings []PerUserMapping} with Proxy.SetUserTokens and userTokens(), following the secretsP pattern. A nil holder keeps today's behaviour byte for byte.

The resolver runs after the static swap. For each mapping it checks only the locations in mapping.in (header values, RawQuery) and makes zero UserTokenSource calls when no per-user placeholder is present. It never reads or buffers the body.

Order of checks once a placeholder is present: destination domain in mapping.domains, else 403 reason secret_domain_mismatch; connIdentity Status valid with Claims.TokenType warden, else 403 {error: identity_required, reason: warden_token_required}; bound agent in mapping.agents, else 403 {error: identity_required, reason: agent_not_mapped}. Nothing is forwarded on any deny, and no 401 is written.

connIdentity keeps the raw Warden token in an unexported field only while the userTokens holder is set, for the mint call; W-P3-JIT-02 sends the same token to the CP pending endpoint; it is never logged or stored.

Token errors: grant_missing, scope_insufficient and reconsent_required set s.authRequired{provider, scopes}; until W-P3-JIT-02 lands, the response is 403 JSON {error: authorization_required, provider} with Cache-Control: no-store. user_token_unavailable gives 503 with Retry-After. AccessToken gets a 5s context.

serveGRPCStream applies the same resolver to request metadata and the same denies as an h2 403 on the stream. Per-user placeholders are excluded from cfg.PlaceholderNames, so the static Cache never prefetches them.

Swapped placeholders go to s.swappedNames, secrets.Ref(token) to s.refs, and the mapping's provider to Event.UserTokenProvider (W-P3-PUS-10); Event.Provider is untouched. Before swapping, the pre-swap header clone and RawQuery are kept on requestScope for W-P3-PUS-05. secret_domain_mismatch, authorization_required and user_token_unavailable are added to internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06).

Buffered responses: a per-user access token that the upstream echoes in a buffered response must not reach the agent. Reuse the existing response scanning path (internal/proxy/response_scan.go ResponseScanner, applied to buffered scannable responses) rather than a second scanner. The implementer first adds a test that checks whether the existing scanner covers swapped per-user values; if it does not, extend it to take the request's swapped per-user values and replace each occurrence with its placeholder before the body is written. Streamed or oversize responses keep the scanner's existing limits, documented in W-P3-PUS-12.

acceptance: Users A and B with Warden tokens on the same agent send `Authorization: Bearer GOOGLE_USER` to gmail.googleapis.com, and the fake upstream sees each user's distinct token. Verify with `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestPerUserSwap -race`.
The same placeholder sent to an allowlisted domain outside mapping.domains gets 403 secret_domain_mismatch, the token source is called 0 times and upstream receives 0 requests.
A request with no per-user placeholder causes 0 token source calls; a header-only mapping with an 11 MB body forwards without a 413.

A Dex token, an invalid token or no identity gets 403 identity_required with reason warden_token_required and no 401; a grant_missing result gets 403 authorization_required with 0 upstream requests; user_token_unavailable gets 503.
An h2 stream carrying the placeholder in metadata is swapped for a valid identity and denied on the stream for an unmapped domain. Verify with `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestPerUserSwapGRPC`.
Captured logs and the stored event contain the placeholder name and provider but no token substring.

tickets.title: Retry once on upstream 401 with a CP-refreshed token
tickets.body: When an upstream rejects a swapped per-user token with 401, ask the CP for a fresh token and resend the request once, so a token revoked or rotated early does not fail the agent's call. The retry rebuilds the request from the pre-swap snapshot and re-runs applyTransforms, because the swap edits headers in place and signing transforms must sign the new request. Retries are limited to replayable HTTP/1 requests, and the CP's stale_ref check and 30s window prevent an always-401 upstream from flooding the provider.
requirements: A new stage retryUserToken401 in runRequestStages between forward and relayResponse acts only when: status is 401, at least one per-user token was swapped, the request has no body or s.bodyRead is true within maxBodySwapSize, the request is not an Upgrade, and it is the first attempt.

The 401 body is drained with io.CopyN up to 64 KiB; if it is larger or resp.Close is set, the upstream connection is closed and the replay dials fresh, reusing the existing stale keep-alive replay path in forward.

The worker calls UserTokenSource.Invalidate(key, staleRef) and AccessToken with force_refresh and the stale ref, restores the pre-swap headers, RawQuery and buffered body, resets s.refs and s.swappedNames, re-runs the static swap, the per-user resolver and applyTransforms, then forwards once.
reconsent_required or grant_missing on the re-mint returns the authorization_required 403 (later JIT); user_token_unavailable relays the original 401. A second 401 is relayed unchanged.
403, h2/gRPC streams, WebSocket upgrades and streamed bodies are never retried. One forwarding event records the final status and `user_token_retried: true`.

The OTel counter warden.user_token.retry.total{provider,outcome} with outcome in success|second_401|not_replayable|mint_failed|reconsent is nil-safe; retry time goes to warden.request.added_latency stage=user_token_retry.

Tests in internal/proxy/usertoken_retry_test.go with a scripted fake upstream (401 then 200, always 401, 401 with large body) and a fake UserTokenSource that records force calls.
acceptance: Upstream returns 401 then 200: the agent receives 200, upstream saw exactly 2 requests with different Authorization values, and the body is byte-identical. Verify with `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestPerUserRetry401 -race`.
Upstream always returns 401: the agent receives the second 401, upstream saw exactly 2 requests, and the metric records outcome=second_401.
A WebSocket upgrade or a gRPC stream that gets a 401 is not retried (1 upstream request, outcome=not_replayable); a request that swapped only static secrets gets no retry and 0 Invalidate calls.
A re-mint returning reconsent_required gives the agent 403 authorization_required with exactly 1 upstream request.
A request whose auth transform signs headers carries a fresh signature on the retry (the fake upstream verifies it).

tickets.title: Add guarded grant record read and write helpers
tickets.body: The refresh engine must never overwrite a grant that changed under it: a reconnect writes a new grant_id, and a revoke deletes the key. Add one pair of helpers in internal/oauthbroker that read a TokenRecord with its store version and write a rotated record back only if the stored grant is still the one that was read, using Vault KV v2 compare-and-swap where available and a read-compare under oauthbroker.GrantLocks elsewhere. Keys come from the W-P3-CSIG-06 helpers and the record type from W-P3-BRKR-01, so this ticket adds no second key scheme or record format. Library only; W-P3-PUS-03 calls it.
requirements: `LoadGrant(ctx, store, userKey, provider) (TokenRecord, Version, error)` reads secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider), parses the W-P3-BRKR-01 TokenRecord and returns ErrGrantMissing (defined here, reused by W-P3-PUS-03) on secrets.ErrNotFound.

`StoreRotated(ctx, store, userKey, provider, rec TokenRecord, read Version) error`: on a secrets.VersionedStore it calls PutIfVersion with the read version; on other stores it re-reads and compares grant_id before Put, and the caller must hold GrantLocks for the key. A changed or deleted grant returns ErrGrantChanged and writes nothing.
rec.GrantID must equal the grant_id that was read; a mismatch returns ErrGrantChanged without a write.
Errors carry only the key and version, never a value; the helpers do no logging.
plan: New internal/oauthbroker/grantio.go with LoadGrant, StoreRotated, Version, ErrGrantMissing and ErrGrantChanged.
New internal/oauthbroker/grantio_test.go against the W-P3-PUS-01 Vault KV v2 fake and fakes.MemorySecretStore (W-P3-CSIG-06).
acceptance: With the Vault fake at version 2, StoreRotated with read version 1 returns ErrGrantChanged and the stored value is unchanged. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestStoreRotated`.

On a non-versioned store, a reconnect that wrote a new grant_id between LoadGrant and StoreRotated makes StoreRotated return ErrGrantChanged with no Put, and a deleted key also returns ErrGrantChanged.
LoadGrant on a missing key returns ErrGrantMissing, and no error string contains a token.

tickets.title: Add the worker-mTLS mint endpoint POST /control/user-token
tickets.body: Expose the refresh engine to workers through one CP route that accepts only a worker cert principal and the user's agent-bound Warden token. The CP re-verifies the token itself, so a compromised worker can mint only for users whose valid tokens pass through it, and only for its own agent. The response holds a short-lived access token and nothing else.
requirements: Route `POST /control/user-token` is mounted only when perUserSecrets.enabled. WorkerAuthenticator (W-P2-WCA-04) accepts only a cert principal here; `wwt_` tokens, console sessions, portal sessions and API keys get 401. The route is added to the W-P1-SSO-05 route table as worker-plane.

Request {subject_token, placeholder, force_refresh, stale_ref} with a 32 KiB body cap. The CP verifies subject_token with identity.WardenVerifier (W-P2-WBND-01) built from its own token KeySet and issuer: typ wt+jwt, aud warden-worker, exp with skew. act.sub must equal the agentID the calling worker last reported in its heartbeat (W-P2-AREG-03), the token's sid must not be revoked (W-P2-TOKX-07 SessionStore), and the user must not be blocked (W-P1-BLOCK-03 BlockStore).

The placeholder must name a mapping whose agents include act.sub; the CP then calls Engine.Token(userKey, provider, mapping.scopes, force_refresh, stale_ref) with userKey = secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub) from the verified token.

Responses: 200 {access_token, expires_in, scope, grant_epoch, ref}; 403 {error: identity_required|agent_not_mapped}; 409 {error: grant_missing|scope_insufficient|reconsent_required, provider, scopes}; 503 {error: user_token_unavailable} with Retry-After; 429 when rate-limited. Every response has Cache-Control: no-store.
Rate limits: a token bucket per worker (200/s, burst 400) and per (userKey, provider) (20/s); a limited call returns 429 and the worker treats it as user_token_unavailable.

Each successful mint calls GrantStore.TouchLastUsed(userKey, provider, now) (W-P3-BRKR-02 throttles it to one write per minute per pair); this is its only caller and it feeds the portal last_used_at. Logs carry worker id, provider, outcome and ref only; never subject_token or access_token.
plan: New internal/oauthbroker/mint.go: the handler, request parsing and the error-to-status mapping.
internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: mount the route behind WorkerAuthenticator in cert-only mode when the engine is configured.
Build the CP-side WardenVerifier from the token service KeySet.JWKS() and issuer, refreshed on KeySet.Subscribe.
Use the internal/ratelimit token bucket from W-P3-BRKR-03 for the per-worker and per-key limits; no dependency is added.
Tests in internal/oauthbroker/mint_test.go with an httptest TLS server, a test worker CA, minted Warden tokens and a stub Engine.
acceptance: A cert-authenticated worker bound to agent support-bot posting a valid token for user A gets 200 with expires_in > 0 and Cache-Control: no-store. Verify with `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestMintEndpoint -race`.
The same request with a `wwt_` bearer and no cert gets 401; a token whose act.sub is another agent gets 403 identity_required; a Dex ID token gets 403 identity_required.
A token whose session was revoked through TOKX-07, or whose user is on the block list, gets 403 and the Engine is not called.
Engine results map to 409 grant_missing, 409 reconsent_required and 503 user_token_unavailable with Retry-After.
No captured log or error body contains the subject token or access token.

tickets.title: Serve perUserSecrets and userGrantEpochs as signed-bundle sections
tickets.body: Ship the value-free mappings and the revocation epochs to workers as two signed-bundle sections, and guard against enabling a mapping for an agent served by workers that cannot enforce it. Epochs are what lets a portal revoke or offboarding drop cached tokens on every worker within one long-poll. This ticket is CP-only; the worker side is W-P3-PUS-09.
requirements: Section `perUserSecrets`: [{placeholder, provider, scopes, domains, in, agents}] plus workerCacheTTL, built from PerUserSecretsConfig. A reflect test proves the section type has no value-bearing field. A config change appends a publish_log row with reason `per_user_secrets`.

Section `userGrantEpochs`: {userKey: epoch}, keyed by secrets.UserKey values so no sub appears on the wire, from a new cpstate table user_grant_epochs(user_key, epoch, bumped_at). New `EpochStore.Bump(ctx, userKey)` sets epoch to the publish_log seq of the new `user_grant` row, so values only grow.
W-P3-PORT-02 (revoke) and offboarding call EpochStore.Bump; this ticket provides the method and a test caller only.
The retention ticker prunes rows with bumped_at older than 2 x workerCacheTTL; a prune does not append a publish_log row.
Both sections are absent when the feature is disabled, so the bundle is byte-identical. Legacy /policy (no bundle) never carries either section.

Rollout guard: a settings save that enables the block or adds an agent to a mapping returns 409 {error: workers_lack_capability, workers: [ids]} when a connected worker bound to that agent lacks heartbeat cap `usersecrets/v1`; an admin may pass force=true, which the admin audit records with the worker ids.
plan: internal/bundle: register the two section names and their Go types.
internal/controlplane: build the sections in policyServer.Refresh next to tokenJWKS (W-P2-SBND-02).
New internal/controlplane/grant_epochs.go: the cpstate migration, EpochStore.Bump and the prune hook in the retention ticker.
internal/controlplane settings save handler: the usersecrets/v1 capability check, reusing the per-worker caps stored for W-P2-WBND-07.
Tests: section content and byte-identity when disabled, Bump monotonicity across prune, the 409 guard and the audited force.
acceptance: With the feature enabled, the signed bundle has sections.perUserSecrets with the configured mapping and no token or secret field. Verify with `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBundlePerUserSections`.
EpochStore.Bump appends a `user_grant` publish_log row, wakes long-poll waiters and the next bundle carries the new epoch; a second Bump after a prune yields a larger epoch.
With the feature disabled, the bundle payload bytes equal a golden file captured before the change.
Adding an agent to a mapping while its connected worker lacks usersecrets/v1 returns 409 workers_lack_capability; force=true by an admin succeeds and is audited; an editor cannot force.

tickets.title: Add the worker UserTokenSource with memory cache and epoch invalidation
tickets.body: Add the worker-side token source that calls the CP mint endpoint over the shared cert client and caches access tokens in memory only. It applies the signed-bundle sections on every policy apply, so mapping changes take effect live and a revoke drops cached tokens within one long-poll. The worker never sees refresh tokens or client secrets.
requirements: New internal/worker/usertoken.go: cpUserTokenSource implementing `UserTokenSource { AccessToken(ctx, ident Identity, m PerUserMapping) (Token, error); Invalidate(key CacheKey, staleRef string) }` over the W-P2-WCA-03 shared CP client. Token.String redacts the value.

Cache: in-memory LRU (default 10,000 entries) keyed (idp_iss, sub, agent, provider); TTL = min(expires_in - 60s, workerCacheTTL) measured on the monotonic clock from receipt; singleflight on miss; nothing is written to disk or the bundle cache, so a restart starts empty.

On each verified bundle apply (RemoteProvider.Bundle(), W-P2-SBND-04) the worker swaps the mapping set into Proxy.SetUserTokens and evicts every entry whose grant_epoch is lower than the served userGrantEpochs value for its userKey (secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub)). A bundle without the perUserSecrets section sets the holder to nil.

Error mapping from the mint response: 409 codes become typed grant errors; 5xx, 429, timeouts (5s) and transport errors become user_token_unavailable. A cache hit while the CP is down keeps working until its TTL.
RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds `usersecrets/v1` to caps when the worker supports it.
Instruments: warden.user_token.total{provider,source,outcome} and lookup time in warden.request.added_latency stage=user_token. A cache hit adds under 20µs p99.
plan: New internal/worker/usertoken.go with the client, LRU (container/list) and singleflight.Group.
internal/worker/applier.go: read the two sections on apply, rebuild the mapping set and call ApplyEpochs.
internal/worker/wiring.go: construct the source when the shared cert client exists and pass it to Proxy.SetUserTokens.
internal/config/remote.go Heartbeat: add the cap.
Tests in internal/worker/usertoken_test.go against an httptest mint fake, plus BenchmarkUserTokenCacheHit.
acceptance: 100 concurrent misses for one key make exactly 1 mint call. Verify with `go test ./internal/worker -run TestUserTokenSource -race`.
An entry minted at grant_epoch 3 is evicted when the applied bundle carries epoch 4 for that userKey, and the next call mints again.
With the mint fake stopped, a cached token is returned until its TTL and then user_token_unavailable is returned; no call returns a grant error.
A bundle without the perUserSecrets section leaves the proxy holder nil, and the heartbeat body includes usersecrets/v1.
`go test ./internal/worker -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkUserTokenCacheHit` reports under 20µs per op.

tickets.title: Record the per-user token provider on analytics events
tickets.body: Add a separate event field for the OAuth provider whose user token was swapped, so the consent portal can show which agents used a grant. The existing analytics.Event.Provider holds the LLM cost provider and must not be reused. Events without a per-user swap stay byte-identical.
requirements: analytics.Event gains UserTokenProvider (json user_token_provider, omitempty) and UserTokenRetried (json user_token_retried, omitempty).

The local SQLite store and FleetSQLiteStore add both columns with addColumnIfAbsent in insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs, following the W-P1-VRFY-03 pattern.
AggregatedEvent and the ingest path carry the fields to the CP so W-P3-PORT-01 can query by user_sub and user_token_provider.

W-P3-PUS-04 sets UserTokenProvider when a per-user token was swapped and W-P3-PUS-05 sets UserTokenRetried; p.recordEvent copies both from requestScope. Event.Provider is untouched. The field name is shared by p3-jit and p3-consent-portal; no other per-user provider field is added.
The value is a registered provider id only; no token, ref or scope is stored in this field.
plan: internal/analytics/analytics.go and fleet.go: add the fields.
internal/analytics SQLite stores: add the columns and read/write paths.
internal/proxy recordEvent: copy the two fields from requestScope fields that W-P3-PUS-04 and W-P3-PUS-05 fill.
Tests: round trip through both stores, an old database file gains the column, and an event without the field serializes byte-identically.
acceptance: An event with UserTokenProvider=google round-trips through SQLiteStore and FleetSQLiteStore. Verify with `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestUserTokenProviderColumn`.
Opening a database created before the change adds the columns without data loss.
An event with no per-user swap marshals to the same JSON bytes as before the change, and Event.Provider is unchanged for LLM events.

tickets.title: Add the per-user secrets end-to-end integration test
tickets.body: Prove the done-when end to end under the integration build tag: a CP with the token service, worker CA, signed bundles and perUserSecrets, one enrolled worker bound to an agent, and two users with grants from a fake OAuth provider. The test covers isolation between users, domain binding, refresh, the 401 retry, revocation, outages and the trust split. It uses in-process fakes so CI needs no Docker.
requirements: New test/fakes/oauthprovider: authorize, token (code and refresh_token grants, optional rotation, scripted invalid_grant and 503) and a userinfo-free upstream that records Authorization per request.
Users A and B connect through /connect/start and /connect/callback (W-P3-BRKR-04) against the fake provider; grants land in a Vault KV v2 fake behind consent.store under `warden-cp/users/`.

Assertions: per-user tokens upstream, secret_domain_mismatch, 403 identity_required for a Dex token, transparent refresh of an expired token, one retry on 401 with the rotated refresh token persisted before use, and authorization_required for a user with no grant.
Revocation: EpochStore.Bump plus deleting the grant stops the swap within one long-poll. CP stopped: cached tokens work until workerCacheTTL, then 503. Provider 503: grant status stays active.

Trust split: the worker's distributed secretStore credential cannot list or read `warden-cp/` in the fake, and a scan of the worker process's config, bundle cache and logs finds no refresh token or client secret.
A byte search of all captured logs, events and metrics finds no token value.
plan: New test/fakes/oauthprovider package and reuse the Vault KV v2 fake from W-P3-PUS-01.
New test/integration/peruser_secrets_test.go (build tag integration) building the CP and worker in process with the W-P2-WCA test CA and minted Warden tokens.
Drive requests through the worker with a test client that sends Proxy-Authorization and the placeholder header.
Add log, event and metric capture with the token byte search at the end.
acceptance: `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestPerUserSecrets -race` passes.
The fake upstream log shows A's and B's distinct tokens and exactly 2 requests for the 401 case.
After the epoch bump, the next request from A gets authorization_required with 0 upstream requests.
The final token byte search reports 0 matches.

tickets.title: Document per-user secrets for operators and agent authors
tickets.body: Write the guide for configuring per-user secrets safely: the grant store and its IAM or Vault policy, mappings and their domains, the identity requirement, and the failure modes. Operators need to know why the grant store must be separate from the distributed secretStore, and agent authors need the exact response codes.
requirements: New docs/per-user-secrets.md: the perUserSecrets block with every key and default, a Google and a GitHub mapping example, and the preconditions (consent.store, token service, --bundles, worker certs, bound agent).
Example Vault policy HCL and AWS IAM policy that give the CP read and write on the consent.store prefix (`warden-cp/*`) and give workers no access to it (shared with the W-P3-CSIG-06 docs).

A table of responses: 403 identity_required (warden_token_required, agent_not_mapped), 403 secret_domain_mismatch, 403 authorization_required, 503 user_token_unavailable, and when the 401 retry happens.

Limits stated plainly: provider tokens are per (user, provider), so a grant's scopes are shared by every mapped agent and the per-agent controls are domains, agents and the scope check; no scope narrowing on refresh in P3; one CP is the refresh authority until p5-postgres-ha; a refresh-token write-back that still fails after the short in-memory retry raises a metric and a Finding, and a CP restart before recovery forces re-consent (no encrypted queue in P3); per-user tokens are redacted only from buffered responses.

docs/control-plane.md and docs/architecture.md link to the guide and show the mint flow, listing POST /control/user-token as a worker-cert (mTLS) only, rate-limited worker→CP call whose subject token the CP re-verifies.
plan: New docs/per-user-secrets.md.
Update docs/control-plane.md with POST /control/user-token and the two bundle sections.
Update docs/architecture.md with the trust split diagram text.
Add TestPerUserSecretsDoc in internal/config that parses the key table in docs/per-user-secrets.md and compares it with the PerUserSecretsConfig fields.
acceptance: docs/per-user-secrets.md exists and every config key it lists matches a field in internal/config/peruser.go (checked by a doc test like TestContractDocMatchesConstants). Verify with `go test ./internal/config -run TestPerUserSecretsDoc`.
Every deny reason in the response table is a constant in internal/proxy/reasons.go.
`scripts/check.sh` passes.

name: Per-user secrets (refresh)
label: refresh-model

summary: When a per-user placeholder cannot be resolved because the user has no grant, the worker does not forward the request. It asks the CP to create or reuse a pending authorization and answers with a structured authorization_required response: a 403 JSON body for HTTP, a JSON-RPC result or error for MCP, and grpc-status 7 for gRPC. The CP owns the authorize and status URLs, derives the scopes from policy, and serves a status long-poll that wakes within a second of consent. Deployments without perUser mappings never enter this path.
design: Scope and opt-in: the JIT stage runs only when W-P3-PUS-04 sets s.authRequired because the worker UserTokenSource (W-P3-PUS-09) got grant_missing, scope_insufficient or reconsent_required from the CP mint (W-P3-PUS-07). Deployments without perUser mappings never enter the stage and behave byte-identically. Requests from users who already hold a grant pay no JIT cost.

Error split, always fail-closed: A grant error gives 403 authorization_required. user_token_unavailable (CP, grant store or provider refresh down) stays the W-P3-PUS-04 503 {error:"user_token_unavailable"} with Retry-After and creates no pending. CP unreachable, 4xx/5xx, 429 or the breaker open gives 503 {error:"authorization_unavailable"} with Retry-After. No path forwards the request or sends any part of it upstream.

Shared wire types: new leaf package internal/connect (no CP, SQLite or oauthbroker imports) holds AuthorizationRequired, PendingRequest/PendingResponse, the Status enum (pending|granted|denied|expired) and the HTTP, JSON-RPC and gRPC response builders. internal/proxy uses it now; internal/mcp/stdio and the P4 MCP gateway (W-P4-MGW-07) can use it later.

HTTP body (403, Content-Type application/json, Cache-Control no-store), written by a new writeJSONResponse helper beside writeErrorResponse in internal/proxy/http.go: {error:"authorization_required", version:1, kind:"oauth_connect", reason:"grant_missing"|"scope_insufficient"|"reconsent_required", provider, scopes, pending_id, authorize_url, status_url, status_token, expires_at, expires_in, message}. It never carries sub, email, an access token or the upstream URL, and never uses 401 or WWW-Authenticate (same rule as W-P2-WBND-03). Keep-alive is kept when the request body was fully read; otherwise Connection: close.

The CP owns all URLs and text. authorize_url = <consent.publicURL>/portal/connect/<pending_id> (the W-P3-PORT-03 landing page) and status_url = <consent.publicURL>/connect/<pending_id>/status. consent.publicURL is a new CP-local key in the W-P3-CSIG-01 consent block: absolute https (http only for loopback), defaulting to the origin of consent.oidc.redirectURL, never on the policy wire. The worker copies URLs from the CP response unchanged. message comes from a fixed CP template built from the agent id, provider display name and scopes; nothing supplied by the agent or upstream is stored or shown on the portal.

Worker to CP: POST /control/connect/pending {subject_token, placeholder, reason, request:{method, host, path, mcp_tool}} on the single cert-presenting CP client from W-P2-WCA-03, listed in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route table. Like POST /control/user-token (W-P3-PUS-07), it accepts only a worker cert principal (W-P2-WCA-04) and re-verifies the user's Warden token on the CP with the same verifier, so idp_iss, sub and the agent (act.sub, which must equal the worker's heartbeat agentID from W-P2-AREG-05, stored by W-P2-AREG-03; else 403 agent_mismatch) come from the token, never from the worker. user_key = secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub). The CP derives the provider and scopes = mapping.scopes ∩ provider.AllowedScopes from the perUserSecrets mapping (W-P3-PUS-02) with the W-P3-BRKR-01 CapScopes helper; the worker never sends sub, agent or scopes. An unknown placeholder or an agent not in the mapping gets 409. Limits (internal/ratelimit from W-P3-BRKR-03): 60/min per worker principal and 20 active pendings per user_key, else 429. With /control/user-token this is one of two accepted new worker→CP calls, used only after a grant error; both are worker-cert (mTLS) only, rate-limited and re-verify the user token on the CP, and docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md list them (W-P3-JIT-01).

CP create-or-reuse in internal/oauthbroker on top of the W-P3-BRKR-02 GrantStore: if an active grant already covers the scopes, return {status:"granted"} and the worker re-runs swapSecrets once. Otherwise return the active pending for (user_key, agent_id, provider, scopes_key), backed by a partial unique index WHERE status='pending' with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and a re-read, or create one: 128-bit random id, consent.connect.pendingTTL (W-P3-BRKR-01, default 15m), origin jit, created_by_proxy_id, reason and request metadata (method, host, path without query, MCP tool) in the W-P3-BRKR-02 request columns, which the W-P3-PORT-03 landing page shows. status_token = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(CP-local key, pending_id)), so a reused pending returns the same token and nothing is stored.

MCP over HTTP: the stage classifies the request itself, using s.wasMCP when set and otherwise protocol.IsMCP on the cached s.reqBody (mcpRequestScan returns early when s.gw is nil). tools/call with an id gets HTTP 200 with JSON-RPC result {isError:true, content:[{type:"text", text: message + authorize_url}], structuredContent: <body>} and the request id echoed verbatim. Other methods with an id get JSON-RPC error -32042 (MCP URL-elicitation-required) with data {elicitations:[{mode:"url", elicitationId: pending_id, url: authorize_url, message}], warden: <body>}. Notifications, batches and legacy HTTP+SSE POSTs get the HTTP 403 JSON. The reply is application/json unless Accept excludes it, in which case one SSE message event is sent. This JSON-RPC answer is a documented exception to the W-P2-WBND-03 rule that MCP denies stay plain JSON. stdio is out of scope: internal/mcp/stdio does no secret swap, and a stdio server's own egress gets the HTTP 403.

h2 and gRPC: serveGRPCStream in internal/proxy/grpc.go swaps outside runRequestStages, so the same JIT logic runs there. Non-gRPC h2 streams get the 403 JSON; application/grpc gets grpc-status 7 (PERMISSION_DENIED) with grpc-message 'authorization_required <authorize_url>'. Neither forwards anything.

Worker cost and resilience: CP calls time out after 3s and are de-duplicated with singleflight per (user_key, agent, provider). A bounded LRU (10,000 entries) caches the pending response until min(expires_at − 30s, 5m) and drops entries when userGrantEpochs[user_key] changes. After a CP failure a per-key breaker fails fast for 5s. The UserTokenSource lookup (W-P3-PUS-09, which never caches grant errors) still runs on every request, so a retry right after consent succeeds.

Status: GET /connect/{id}/status?wait=Ns, clamped with parseWait (moved from internal/controlplane/policyserver.go to new internal/longpoll so oauthbroker can use it) to 1–60s, returns {status, reason, expires_at, expires_in} with Cache-Control no-store. Accepted credentials: Authorization: Bearer <status_token> (constant-time compare; never in the URL because the worker records Event.URL), a worker credential whose heartbeat agentID equals the pending's agent_id (the P4 park waiter path), or a portal session (W-P3-CSIG-04) whose (iss, sub) matches the pending. Unknown ids and wrong credentials all get the same 404. The handler re-reads the row on entry, on every wake, every 5s and on timeout, and reports expires_at <= now as expired without waiting for the retention ticker.

Waking: waiters wait on the W-P3-BRKR-02 GrantStore Subscribe channel, which closes on CompletePending and on expiry, so the BRKR-04 callback and the PORT-03 decline call sites do not change. A thin decorator adds one rule: CompletePending(granted) also marks every active pending for the same (user_key, provider) whose scopes are a subset of the granted scopes as granted and closes their channels. Waiters are bounded at 2,048 global and 8 per pending (429 Retry-After: 1 beyond that); a map entry is removed when its last waiter leaves.

Degraded modes: CP down gives 503 authorization_unavailable while requests that already hold a grant keep working. IdP down means portal login fails and the pending stays pending until expiry. Clients use expires_in, so clock skew does not matter. A worker restart loses only its cache; the CP de-duplicates. A CP restart drops in-flight polls and clients re-poll; pendings persist in SQLite. Cross-replica wakeups wait for p5-postgres-ha; the 5s re-read keeps answers correct meanwhile.

Events and observability: each JIT response stores one deny event through recordEvent (W-P1-VRFY-03) with Reason authorization_required or authorization_unavailable (added to internal/proxy/reasons.go from W-P1-JAUD-06 and to RecordBlocked; user_token_unavailable comes from W-P3-PUS-04), the pre-swap URL from W-P1-JAUD-05, user_sub stamped, and the OAuth provider in Event.UserTokenProvider (W-P3-PUS-10), never Event.Provider (that is the LLM cost provider). bridgeEvent in internal/alertpipeline raises no finding for these reasons. Worker counter warden.jit.total{outcome, provider} with provider limited to configured ids, else other. CP counters for pending and status outcomes, completed_at on pendings, and one info log per state change without sub. No token, status_token or body appears in any log or event.

Back-compat and rollout: the CP is upgraded first; a worker that gets 404 from an older CP treats it as authorization_unavailable. The authorization_required body is versioned and fields may only be added. Operators must allowlist the consent.publicURL origin for agents that should poll status; JIT never auto-allows it.
done_when: In a deployment with a CP running consent, the OAuth broker and the portal, an enrolled worker with a cert (W-P2-WCA) and a perUser Google mapping: a request missing a grant gets a 403 authorization_required body matching the golden fixture and docs/schemas/authorization_required.v1.json, the fake upstream receives zero requests, and one deny event with Reason authorization_required is stored. An MCP tools/call over Streamable HTTP gets the isError result with its own request id whether or not the MCP gateway is configured, and an h2 gRPC call gets grpc-status 7. authorize_url opens the portal landing page; after consent, a status long-poll held with the status_token returns granted within 1s on a single-replica CP, and the agent's single retry reaches upstream with that user's token. With the CP stopped the worker returns 503 authorization_unavailable, with the CP refresh path failing it returns 503 user_token_unavailable, and neither forwards the request. A deployment with no perUser mappings behaves byte-identically to before.

tickets.title: Add CP endpoint to create or reuse pending authorizations
tickets.body: Add POST /control/connect/pending on the CP so a worker can turn a missing grant into a pending authorization the user can approve. The CP authenticates the worker, re-verifies the user's Warden token so the user and agent never come from the worker, derives the scopes from the perUserSecrets mapping, and creates or reuses one pending per (user, agent, provider, scopes). It owns the authorize and status URLs, the user-facing message and the status token, so nothing the agent or worker supplies reaches the portal. This is control-plane only and is mounted only when consent.providers is configured.
requirements: Route POST /control/connect/pending in internal/oauthbroker, mounted in controlplane.go Handler() only when consent.providers is non-empty (otherwise 404), accepting only a worker cert principal from WorkerAuthenticator (W-P1-WTOK-02, W-P2-WCA-04), like W-P3-PUS-07, and listed as worker-plane in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route table. wwt_ tokens, user tokens, portal or console sessions and wak_ keys get the uniform 401.

Request body {subject_token, placeholder, reason, request:{method, host, path, mcp_tool}} is capped at 32 KiB, like W-P3-PUS-07, and decoded with DisallowUnknownFields. The CP verifies subject_token with the W-P3-PUS-07 WardenVerifier and takes idp_iss, sub and act.sub from it; act.sub must equal the worker's heartbeat agentID (W-P2-AREG-05, stored by W-P2-AREG-03), otherwise 403 agent_mismatch; a Dex or invalid token gets 403 identity_required. user_key = secrets.UserKey(idp_iss, sub). reason is grant_missing, scope_insufficient or reconsent_required.

Scopes are derived, never taken from the worker: the provider and scopes = mapping.scopes ∩ provider.AllowedScopes come from the perUserSecrets mapping for the placeholder, using the W-P3-BRKR-01 CapScopes helper, canonicalized (sorted, de-duplicated) into scopes_key. An unknown placeholder or an agent not listed in the mapping returns 409 and writes no row.

If an active grant in GrantStore already covers the scopes, return 200 {status:"granted"}. Otherwise return the active pending (status=pending and expires_at > now) for (user_key, agent_id, provider, scopes_key) with 200, or create one with 201: 128-bit random base64url id, TTL consent.connect.pendingTTL (W-P3-BRKR-01), origin jit, created_by_proxy_id from the worker principal, reason, and request metadata (method, host, path without query, MCP tool) in the W-P3-BRKR-02 request columns.

A migration on pending_authorizations (W-P3-BRKR-02) adds scopes_key, origin, created_by_proxy_id and the JIT reason (completed_at and the request columns already exist), plus a partial unique index on (user_key, agent_id, provider, scopes_key) WHERE status='pending'. Inserts use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING followed by a re-select, so racing workers get one row.

Response {status, pending_id, authorize_url, status_url, status_token, expires_at, expires_in, message}. URLs are built from new CP-local key consent.publicURL (absolute https, http only for loopback, default the origin of consent.oidc.redirectURL, never on the policy wire). status_token = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(CP-local key, pending_id)) with the key generated on first use and kept in CP SQLite. message comes from a fixed template (agent id, provider display name, scopes). The body never contains sub or email.

Limits (internal/ratelimit from W-P3-BRKR-03): 60 requests/min per worker principal and 20 active pendings per user_key; over either, 429 with Retry-After. Counter warden_cp_connect_pending_total{outcome=created|reused|already_granted|rejected|rate_limited} and one info log per call with pending_id, proxy_id, agent, provider, scopes_count and outcome; no sub at info level and never the status_token.

docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md replace the statement that there are exactly three worker→CP calls with the full list: /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, plus the two P3 calls POST /control/user-token (W-P3-PUS-07, on a worker cache miss) and POST /control/connect/pending (this ticket, deny path only, fail-closed). Both P3 calls require a worker cert (mTLS, W-P2-WCA-04), are rate-limited per worker principal, and the CP re-verifies the user's Warden token on every call.

tickets.title: Return structured 403 for HTTP when a grant is missing
tickets.body: Add a jitDeny stage in internal/proxy that runs when W-P3-PUS-04 reports a missing grant. It asks the CP for a pending through a new CreatePending call on the shared cert-presenting CP client and answers 403 authorization_required, or 503 when the CP or secret backend is unavailable; the request is never forwarded. A bounded cache with singleflight keeps agent retries from reaching the CP. This is worker-only and runs only for perUser mappings.
requirements: New jitDeny stage in runRequestStages right after swapSecrets, entered only when W-P3-PUS-04 set s.authRequired (grant_missing, scope_insufficient or reconsent_required). user_token_unavailable keeps the W-P3-PUS-04 503 and makes no CP call. The stage never calls forward or dialUpstream.

New RemoteProvider.CreatePending(ctx, connect.PendingRequest) on the W-P2-WCA-03 shared CP client, injected through a new atomic Proxy seam (SetPendingCreator; nil means unavailable), with a 3s timeout and a 16 KiB response limit. It sends the raw Warden token that W-P3-PUS-04 keeps on connIdentity as subject_token, the placeholder name, the reason and the request metadata; never sub, agent or scopes.

Worker cache: LRU of at most 10,000 entries keyed by (user_key, agent, provider) holding the response until min(expires_at − 30s, 5m), dropped when userGrantEpochs[user_key] changes; singleflight per key; a CP failure opens a 5s per-key breaker. A {status:"granted"} reply makes the stage re-run swapSecrets once and continue normally.

Success: 403 written by a new writeJSONResponse(w, status, headers, v) helper with Content-Type application/json, Cache-Control: no-store and the internal/connect AuthorizationRequired body (version 1). Connection: close when the request body was not fully read. CP timeout, 4xx, 5xx, 429, open breaker or nil creator give 503 {error:"authorization_unavailable", provider, message} with Retry-After: 5.

Golden fixtures in internal/proxy/testdata/jit/ and new docs/schemas/authorization_required.v1.json, checked against the internal/connect structs with the W-P1-JAUD-02 struct-tag comparison (no new Go dependency).

Each response stores one deny event through recordEvent with Reason authorization_required or authorization_unavailable (added to internal/proxy/reasons.go and RecordBlocked), the JAUD-05 pre-swap URL, user_sub, and the OAuth provider in Event.UserTokenProvider (W-P3-PUS-10), never Event.Provider. logDecision gains pending_id. bridgeEvent in internal/alertpipeline returns no finding for these two reasons or user_token_unavailable.

Counter warden.jit.total{outcome=created|reused|already_granted|cache_hit|cp_unavailable|rate_limited, provider} in internal/observability, provider limited to configured ids else other. No token, status_token or body is logged.
With no perUser mappings the stage never runs and the allow path gains no allocations or locks.

tickets.title: Return JSON-RPC results for MCP calls missing a grant
tickets.body: MCP clients treat a plain 403 as a transport error, so the model never sees the authorize link. When the request is MCP over HTTP, answer a missing grant with a JSON-RPC result or error that carries the same authorization_required object and the original request id. Detection must not depend on the MCP gateway being configured. The stdio wedge is out of scope because it does no secret swap.

tickets.title: Add /connect/{id}/status long-poll on the CP
tickets.body: Add GET /connect/{id}/status so the agent, the user's portal or a P4 park waiter can wait for a pending to finish and then retry. The agent usually does not hold a Warden user token, so the endpoint accepts the per-pending status_token, a worker credential bound to the pending's agent, or the user's portal session. Waiters are woken through a notifying GrantStore decorator, so the callback and decline call sites do not change. This is control-plane only.
requirements: GET /connect/{id}/status in internal/oauthbroker, mounted only when consent is configured and listed in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz route table. Response 200 {status: pending|granted|denied|expired, reason, expires_at, expires_in} with Cache-Control: no-store; never sub, email or scopes.

Auth: Authorization: Bearer <status_token> compared in constant time with the JIT-01 HMAC; a worker credential (WorkerAuthenticator) whose heartbeat agentID equals the pending's agent_id; or a W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session whose (iss, sub) matches the pending. Unknown ids and any other credential get the same 404 body. A token in the query string is ignored.

wait uses ParseWait in new package internal/longpoll (moved from internal/controlplane/policyserver.go parseWait, same 1s–60s clamp; absent means answer at once). A terminal status returns immediately; each waiter's timer is min(wait, expires_at − now). Status is computed lazily, so expires_at <= now reads expired before the retention ticker runs.

Waiters wait on the W-P3-BRKR-02 GrantStore Subscribe channel, which closes on CompletePending and on expiry. A thin decorator around GrantStore adds one rule: CompletePending(granted) also marks every active pending for the same (user_key, provider) whose scopes are a subset of the granted scopes as granted, sets completed_at and closes their channels.
The handler re-reads the row on entry, on every wake, every 5s and on timeout, so a missed wake only delays the answer and multiple CP replicas stay correct.
Limits: 8 waiters per pending and 2,048 in total, else 429 with Retry-After: 1. Client disconnect frees a waiter at once and the map entry is removed when its last waiter leaves.

Gauge warden_cp_connect_status_waiters and counter warden_cp_connect_status_total{result=pending|granted|denied|expired|not_found|limited}. One info log per pending state change with pending_id, provider, agent, outcome and duration; no sub at info level, never the status_token.
plan: New internal/longpoll: ParseWait and the min/max constants; internal/controlplane/policyserver.go calls it instead of its local parseWait.
New internal/oauthbroker/waiters.go: waiterHub with limits and cleanup over GrantStore.Subscribe, and matchingStore wrapping CompletePending with the new CompleteMatchingPendings.
New internal/oauthbroker/status_http.go: credential resolution (status_token, worker principal, portal session), uniform 404, select over hub channel, timer, 5s re-read ticker and ctx.
internal/controlplane/controlplane.go Handler(): wrap the store with matchingStore, mount the route, add the authz table row.
Tests in internal/oauthbroker/status_http_test.go and internal/longpoll/longpoll_test.go.
acceptance: Given a waiter on wait=30s holding the status_token, CompletePending(granted) makes it return granted within 1s: `go test -race ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestStatusLongPoll`.
Given two pendings from different agents for the same user and provider, completing one wakes both waiters with granted.
Given wait=120s and a fake clock the wait is clamped to 60s and returns pending; when expires_at passes during the wait the response is expired without a ticker run.

A wrong status_token, another user's portal session, a worker credential for a different agent and an unknown id each get 404 with identical bodies: `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestStatusAuth`.

`go test ./internal/controlplane` passes with parseWait moved to internal/longpoll.

tickets.title: Document the authorization_required contract
tickets.body: Add docs/jit-authorization.md so agent and client authors know what a missing grant looks like on each protocol, how to wait for consent and when to retry. The schema and golden fixtures are created by W-P3-JIT-02 and W-P3-JIT-03; this ticket writes the contract around them and a drift test that keeps the examples in the doc equal to the fixtures.
requirements: Sections for HTTP/1.1 (403 authorization_required, 503 authorization_unavailable and user_token_unavailable), h2 and gRPC (grpc-status 7), MCP over HTTP (tools/call result, -32042 error, notifications and batches, JSON and single-event SSE), and MCP over stdio (the server's own egress gets the HTTP 403).
Status endpoint: the three accepted credentials, the status_token sent as a Bearer header and never in a URL, wait clamped to 1–60s, statuses, uniform 404, 429 limits and lazy expiry.

Retry guidance: poll with wait <= 60s; after granted retry the original request once; retry non-idempotent calls only after the user confirms; stop on denied or expired; honour Retry-After on 503; use expires_in rather than local clock math.
