name: JIT 403 + long-poll
label: jit-authorization

summary: Operators can set rate limits and daily estimated-cost caps per verified user, optionally split by agent, so one user cannot use up a shared provider budget. Limits apply per request after an allow decision and never turn a deny into an allow. The control plane rolls up fleet spend per user per UTC day and publishes over-budget users on the signed policy wire, and the dashboard shows per-user requests, denies and estimated cost.
design: Scope and gate: default off. With no `policy.userLimits`, `policy.defaultUserLimit` or `policy.anonymousLimit`, GET /policy and its ETag are byte-identical (golden test) and `BenchmarkEvaluate` shows no extra allocations. Limits are checked only after the existing allow decision, never turn Deny, NoMatch or Conditional into Allow, and never touch secret swap.

Config (W-P3-PUL-01): new `config.UserLimit{Name, Match UserLimitMatch{Users, Groups, Agents, Domains []string}, PerAgent bool, RateLimit string, DailyCostUSD float64}`, `Policy.UserLimits []UserLimit`, `Policy.DefaultUserLimit *UserLimit` and `Policy.AnonymousLimit *UserLimit` (yaml/json omitempty). `Name` is required and unique in userLimits (agent-id charset); `default` and `anonymous` are reserved for the two single rules. Users and Groups use the W-P1-GPOL-01 normalizer; an email value matches only when `identity.Subject.EmailVerified`. Domains use the `policy.MatchDomain` dialect and empty means all domains. RateLimit uses the existing `validateRateLimit` (second, minute, hour). At most 256 rules. `config.LintUserLimits` warns on overlapping rules in one tier, dailyCostUSD with no CA, and agents whose identity mode is not require.

Precedence: exactly one rule applies to a request. Tiers in order are rules matching by users, then by groups, then agents-only rules, then `defaultUserLimit`; within a tier the first rule in list order whose match fields and domains both match wins. A nil subject (no, invalid or expired token) uses only `anonymousLimit`, keyed by the worker's resolved agent id, and is never charged to a sub read from an unverified token. A strict per-user guarantee needs identity mode require; this is documented.

Evaluator (W-P3-PUL-03): `EvaluateFor(domain, port, scheme, *identity.Subject) Result`, `PeekFor` and `identity.Subject` from P1 (W-P1-GPOL-02, W-P1-VRFY-01) are kept unchanged. New `ChargeUserLimit` and non-charging `PeekUserLimit` take the same arguments plus the agent id and return the P1 `Result` with two additive fields, `LimitRule` and `RetryAfter`. Bucket key `ul:<name>:<sub>` plus `:<agentID>` when PerAgent (anonymous: `ul:anonymous:anon:<agentID>`), so a rule has one budget across all its domains. Buckets live in a sharded map that `load()` does not re-make: `Replace` drops only buckets of rules whose canonical definition hash changed or that were removed, so blockedUsers or costBlockedUsers changes never reset windows. Expired buckets are swept about once a minute; at `maxUserLimitBuckets` (100000) a new key is denied fail-closed and counted.

Proxy (W-P3-PUL-09): new `userLimitStage` in `runRequestStages` after identityStage, the W-P1-BLOCK-02 blockStage and the W-P1-GPOL-03 scopedPolicyStage, before judgeGate, charged per request so a keep-alive session carrying several users limits each correctly. h2 streams are charged in `serveGRPCStream`, WebSocket upgrades once per upgrade, and raw tunnels (no CA) once at CONNECT; a TLS-terminated CONNECT uses PeekUserLimit only. Over the rate: 429 `{"error":"user_rate_limited"}` with integer Retry-After. The worker heartbeat adds cap `userlimits/v1`.

Cost input (W-P3-PUL-06): `recordAllowEvent` today prices from `req/resp.ContentLength` and clamps -1 to 0, so chunked and SSE LLM responses cost $0. Counting wrappers on the forwarded request body and the response copy (including relayMCPSSE and serveGRPCStream) supply the bytes actually relayed whenever Content-Length is unknown. This fix ships with no flag because it is a bug fix: streamed responses were priced at $0. Caps are on estimated spend (bytes/4 with the built-in prices in `cost.defaultProviders`) and are documented as such.

Worker cost cap (W-P3-PUL-04): new `cost.Ledger` keyed by (UTC day, sub or anon key, rule name), owned by the worker and passed to the proxy, fed from `recordAllowEvent` and seeded at boot from the local SQLite store (sum of today's cost_usd by user_sub and limit_rule). Before a request to a destination `Estimator` tracks, the request is refused when spend so far is at or over the rule's DailyCostUSD, or when the wire lists the sub for that rule today: 403 `{"error":"user_cost_limited"}` with Retry-After to the next UTC midnight. When a cost-capped rule applies to a tracked destination that cannot be measured (raw tunnel, no CA, WebSocket), the request is denied with `user_cost_unmeasurable`. The cap is soft: it can overshoot by in-flight requests and by fleet sync lag.

Analytics: reuse the P1 user columns, (user_sub, ts) index, `EventFilter.User`, ?user= filters and topUsers (W-P1-VRFY-03/04/06). W-P3-PUL-02 adds only `Event.AgentID` (json `agent_id,omitempty`) and `Event.LimitRule` (json `limit_rule,omitempty`) on the worker. W-P3-PUL-07 fills the existing fleet `agent_id` column at ingest (central_http.go stores only ProxyID today), adds `limit_rule`, and adds the rollup `user_usage_daily(day, sub, agent_id, limit_rule, email, requests, denies_json, cost_usd)` updated in the StoreAggregatedEvent transaction only when the event insert succeeded, so a retried batch never double counts. The rollup is kept 35 days regardless of events retention and maxEvents pruning.

Fleet cost blocks (W-P3-PUL-08): the CP recomputes today's over-cap (sub, rule) pairs from the rollup on a 30s debounce after ingest and at startup, looking up each rule's DailyCostUSD by name in the served policy. It serves `costBlockedUsers: [{sub, rule, day}]` inside policyWire (sorted, omitempty, at most `config.MaxCostBlockedUsers` = 5000), computed state that is never stored in policy_versions so a rollback cannot clear it. Each change appends a `policy_publish_log` row with reason `user_cost` and calls Refresh, so W-P2-SBND-02 signed bundles get a new seq. One shared `config.ValidateCostBlockedUsers` runs on the CP and in parseRemotePolicy. Workers ignore entries whose day is not the current UTC day, so blocks lapse at midnight even when the CP is down.

Degraded modes: CP down, workers keep the last-known-good list until each entry's day ends and their local ledger and rate buckets keep enforcing. Worker restart: ledger reseeded from local SQLite; rate buckets start empty (documented). IdP down: new tokens fail verification and fall into anonymousLimit. Rollup or recompute error: the CP keeps the last list and counts the error, never serving an empty list because of a failure. Analytics provider memory: the CP aggregator is disabled with one WARN.

Dashboard (W-P3-PUL-05): `GET /dashboard/api/usage/users?window=24h|7d|30d&sort=cost|requests&limit=` (path chosen so it does not collide with the W-P3-OFFB-03 `/dashboard/api/users/{sub}/...` routes) returns per-user requests, denies by reason, estimated cost, top agents, matched rule, cap and today's block state from the rollup. It has a W-P1-SSO-05 authz row with role viewer and Scope `traffic:read` (W-P2-APIK-02). The Users usage view sorts by cost, flags users at or over their cap, drills down via ?user=, renders claims with textContent only, and warns when connected workers lack `userlimits/v1`.

Observability: `RecordBlocked` for `user_rate_limited`, `user_cost_limited` and `user_cost_unmeasurable`, added to internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06) and the warden.decision.v1 reason enum with a schema_rev bump (W-P1-JAUD-02). New OTel counter `warden.user_limit.denied.total{kind=rate|cost|unmeasurable}` and gauge `warden.user_limit.buckets`, never with sub, email or group labels. The decision log carries limit_rule. CP in-memory `warden_cp_cost_blocked_users` gauge and `warden_cp_cost_recompute_errors_total` counter are left for W-P5-RETN-06 to export.

Rollout safety for cost caps: workers that enforce dailyCostUSD (W-P3-PUL-04) add `usercost/v1` to the heartbeat caps, because an older worker fails open on cost caps. A policy save that adds a rule with dailyCostUSD, or sets one on an existing rule, returns 409 `{"error":"workers_lack_capability","capability":"usercost/v1","workers":[ids]}` while any connected worker lacks that cap, unless the admin sends `force=true`, which is recorded in the admin audit row (the W-P2-WBND-07 pattern).
done_when: On a managed deployment with two CA-enabled workers that advertise userlimits/v1, an operator sets `{name: eng-llm, match: {groups: [eng], domains: [api.openai.com]}, rateLimit: 60/minute, dailyCostUSD: 5}` and an anonymousLimit. A verified eng user over 60 requests a minute gets 429 user_rate_limited with Retry-After while another eng user on the same agent continues, and an unrelated policy or block-list change does not reset that window. A user whose streamed LLM calls push estimated spend past $5 gets 403 user_cost_limited on one worker, and within the debounce plus one long-poll cycle on the other worker through the signed costBlockedUsers entry; the block survives a worker or CP restart and lapses at the next UTC midnight even with the CP stopped. Dropping the token lands the request in the anonymous bucket. With no limits configured, /policy and its ETag are byte-identical. The Users usage view (viewer role or a traffic:read key) shows per-user requests, denies by reason, estimated cost and top agents, and no metric label carries a sub or email. A save that adds a dailyCostUSD rule returns 409 while a worker without usercost/v1 is connected, unless an admin forces it with an audited force=true, and the streamed-response cost fix (W-P3-PUL-06) ships without a flag.

tickets.title: Add userLimits config, costBlockedUsers wire type and validation
tickets.body: Add the per-user limit rules and the wire-only cost block list to config.Policy and to the CP policyWire, with one shared validator used by the YAML parse, parseRemotePolicy and the CP. Nothing enforces the rules yet, so a fail-closed guard rejects any non-empty userLimits, defaultUserLimit or anonymousLimit until W-P3-PUL-09 and W-P3-PUL-04 lift it, following the W-P1-GPOL-01 pattern. With none of the keys set, YAML, /policy and the ETag stay byte-identical.
requirements: New `config.UserLimit{Name string; Match UserLimitMatch; PerAgent bool; RateLimit string; DailyCostUSD float64}` and `UserLimitMatch{Users, Groups, Agents, Domains []string}`; `Policy.UserLimits` (yaml/json `userLimits,omitempty`), `Policy.DefaultUserLimit *UserLimit` (`defaultUserLimit,omitempty`) and `Policy.AnonymousLimit *UserLimit` (`anonymousLimit,omitempty`), added to rawConfig.Policy so strict YAML (KnownFields) accepts them.

New `config.CostBlockedUser{Sub, Rule, Day string}` (json `sub`, `rule`, `day` as YYYY-MM-DD) and `Policy.CostBlockedUsers` (json `costBlockedUsers,omitempty`, yaml `-`, never accepted from local YAML). New `config.MaxCostBlockedUsers = 5000`.

New `config.ValidateUserLimits`: Name required, unique and in the agent-id charset, with `default` and `anonymous` reserved for the single rules; each rule needs RateLimit and/or DailyCostUSD; RateLimit goes through the existing `validateRateLimit`; DailyCostUSD is 0 (no cap) or > 0 and <= 1e6; at most 256 rules; Users and Groups use the W-P1-GPOL-01 normalizer; Domains use the allowlist domain dialect. defaultUserLimit and anonymousLimit take no Match. Errors name `policy.userLimits[i].<field>`.

New `config.ValidateCostBlockedUsers`: at most MaxCostBlockedUsers entries, sub non-empty and <= 255 bytes with no control characters, rule in the name charset, day a valid date; called from parseRemotePolicy so a bad row is rejected and the worker keeps its last good policy. Errors name the index, never the sub.
Guard: validation rejects non-empty userLimits, defaultUserLimit or anonymousLimit with `not yet enforced`; W-P3-PUL-09 lifts it for rateLimit-only rules and W-P3-PUL-04 for dailyCostUSD.

`Policy.DeepCopy` deep-copies UserLimits, every Match slice, both pointers and CostBlockedUsers. `controlplane.policyWire` gains UserLimits, DefaultUserLimit, AnonymousLimit and CostBlockedUsers (all omitempty), and `policyYAML` keeps the three YAML keys so `Server.WritePolicy` never drops them.

New `config.LintUserLimits(cfg) []string` warns on overlapping rules in one tier, dailyCostUSD set with no CA configured, and agents whose identity mode is not require. Warnings carry rule names only.

internal/config/remote.go parseRemotePolicy: run ValidateCostBlockedUsers and ValidateUserLimits on the decoded wire policy.

Tests: validation table with indexes, DeepCopy aliasing, parseRemotePolicy round trip with the guard bypassed by a test hook, golden /policy body and ETag without the fields.

tickets.title: Add per-user limit matching and counters to the policy evaluator
tickets.body: Teach internal/policy to pick the one user limit that applies to a request and to charge its rate bucket, without changing the P1 `EvaluateFor(domain, port, scheme, *identity.Subject) Result`, `PeekFor` or `identity.Subject`. User-limit buckets must survive `Replace`, because today load() re-makes the counters map and every costBlockedUsers or blockedUsers change would reset every user's window fleet-wide. This ticket is policy-package only; the PUL-01 guard still rejects userLimits, so merging changes nothing.
requirements: Keep EvaluateFor, PeekFor, Evaluate and identity.Subject unchanged. Add `ChargeUserLimit(domain string, port int, scheme Scheme, subj *identity.Subject, agentID string) Result` and non-charging `PeekUserLimit` with the same arguments. Result gains additive fields `LimitRule string` and `RetryAfter time.Duration`; over the limit it returns Decision Deny with Reason `user_rate_limited`.

Selection: users tier, then groups tier, then agents-only tier, then defaultUserLimit; within a tier the first rule in list order whose match fields and Domains both match. Users match by sub, or by email only when EmailVerified. A nil subject uses only anonymousLimit. No matching rule means Allow with empty LimitRule.
Bucket key `ul:<name>:<sub>` plus `:<agentID>` when PerAgent; nil subject `ul:anonymous:anon:<agentID>`. One budget per rule across all its domains.

Buckets live in a new 64-shard map separate from e.mu that load() does not re-make. On Replace, buckets are kept for rules whose canonical definition hash is unchanged and dropped for rules that changed or were removed. Allowlist per-entry counters keep today's behaviour.
Expired buckets are swept about once a minute, amortized on charge. At `maxUserLimitBuckets` (100000) after a sweep, a new key is denied with user_rate_limited (fail closed) and counted.

New `MatchUserLimit(subj, agentID, domain) (UserLimitRule{Name, DailyCostUSD, PerAgent}, bool)` and `IsCostBlocked(sub, rule string, now time.Time) bool`, which builds its set in load() from Policy.CostBlockedUsers and ignores entries whose day is not now's UTC day.
Hot path: with no user limits, BenchmarkEvaluate adds 0 allocations and changes by 5% or less; ChargeUserLimit with 256 rules stays under 1 microsecond per op.

Tests in internal/policy/userlimit_test.go: precedence, per-agent split, anonymous key, Replace preservation, sweep with a fake clock, cap, -race concurrency, and a benchmark.

tickets.title: Cap daily estimated cost per user in the worker
tickets.body: Add a worker-owned per-user, per-rule, per-UTC-day spend ledger fed from recordAllowEvent and seeded from local analytics at boot, and refuse requests to cost-tracked destinations once a user's spend reaches the rule's dailyCostUSD or the CP lists them in costBlockedUsers. Sessions that cannot be measured are denied for cost-capped rules instead of passing unmetered. This ticket is worker-only and lifts the PUL-01 guard for dailyCostUSD.
requirements: New `cost.Ledger` in internal/cost keyed by (UTC day, sub or anon key, rule name), bounded at 100000 keys, dropping previous-day keys at UTC rollover; owned by the worker and passed to the proxy through a new `proxy.Config.UserCost` seam, not stored in the evaluator.
New `cost.Estimator.Tracks(domain) (provider string, ok bool)`. Only tracked destinations are subject to cost caps; untracked destinations are never denied for cost.

At boot the worker seeds the ledger from the local SQLite store with a new `SQLiteStore.CostByUserSince(ctx, since)` (sum of cost_usd grouped by user_sub and limit_rule since UTC midnight, using the W-P3-PUL-02 index).

In userLimitStage, before forwarding to a tracked destination with a matched rule that has DailyCostUSD: deny when ledger spend is at or over the cap, or when `IsCostBlocked(sub, rule, now)` is true. Response 403 `{"error":"user_cost_limited"}` with Retry-After in seconds to the next UTC midnight; the deny event carries Reason, the VRFY user fields and LimitRule.
When such a rule applies to a tracked destination that cannot be measured (raw tunnel without CA at CONNECT, WebSocket), deny with 403 `{"error":"user_cost_unmeasurable"}`.

recordAllowEvent adds the estimate to the ledger and sets Event.LimitRule. Add `user_cost_limited` and `user_cost_unmeasurable` to internal/proxy/reasons.go and the decision schema enum with a schema_rev bump, and call RecordBlocked; increment `warden.user_limit.denied.total{kind=cost|unmeasurable}`.
The cap is soft: overshoot is bounded by in-flight requests on this worker plus fleet sync lag; documented in W-P3-PUL-10. Logs never carry email or per-user spend above debug.
RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds `usercost/v1` to caps once this ticket lifts the guard, so the CP can refuse cost-cap rules while older workers that would fail open are connected (W-P3-PUL-08).

tickets.title: Add per-user usage and cost dashboard view
tickets.body: Give operators one place to see who is using which providers and how much they are spending. Serve per-user usage from the W-P3-PUL-07 rollup at a new route classified in the authz table, and add a Users usage view that flags users at or over their cap and warns when connected workers do not enforce user limits. The route path avoids the W-P3-OFFB-03 `/dashboard/api/users/{sub}` routes.

200 body: `{window, from, to, users:[{sub, email, requests, denies:{reason:n}, costUSD, todayCostUSD, topAgents:[{agentID, requests, costUSD}], limitRule, capUSD, atLimit, costBlocked}], unattributed:{requests, costUSD}}`. atLimit is todayCostUSD >= capUSD; costBlocked comes from the served costBlockedUsers.

On the CP the data comes from `UsageByUser` on the fleet store (W-P3-PUL-07); on a standalone worker dashboard the same handler uses the local SQLiteStore implementation. Responses are cached 30s keyed by window, sort and limit, like handleAnalytics.

Fleet view: when the served policy has user limits, show 'N connected workers do not enforce user limits' for workers whose heartbeat caps lack `userlimits/v1` (W-P1-BLOCK-04, W-P1-GPOL-07 caps registry).

tickets.title: Count relayed bytes for cost estimates on streamed responses
tickets.body: recordAllowEvent prices requests from `req.ContentLength` and `resp.ContentLength` and clamps -1 to 0, so chunked uploads and chunked or SSE LLM responses, the normal shape for LLM APIs, are recorded at $0 and a daily cost cap would never fire. serveGRPCStream allow events gain CostUSD and Provider for tracked destinations, which they lack today.

tickets.body: Control-plane half of recording. Ingest stores only ProxyID today, so the existing fleet agent_id column is always empty; fill it from Event.AgentID and add the limit_rule column. Add a per-day per-user rollup updated in the same transaction as the event insert, so fleet cost totals and the dashboard survive events pruning and are never double counted when a worker retries a batch.

tickets.title: Publish fleet cost blocks as costBlockedUsers from the control plane
tickets.body: A per-worker ledger alone lets a user spend the cap once on every worker. The CP recomputes today's spend per (sub, rule) from the W-P3-PUL-07 rollup and serves over-cap users as costBlockedUsers on the policy wire, appending a publish_log row on every change so signed bundles move to a new seq instead of reading as equivocation. CP only; it runs only when the served policy has a dailyCostUSD rule.
requirements: A new userCostAggregator in internal/controlplane runs after ingest through the existing `ingest.SetOnEvents` hook, debounced to at most once per 30s, plus once at startup and at each UTC midnight. It runs only when some rule sets DailyCostUSD and the analytics provider is sqlite; with provider memory it logs one WARN and stays off.

Each run reads `TodayCostByRule` for the current UTC day, looks up each rule's DailyCostUSD by name in the served policy (unknown or removed names are skipped), and builds a sorted `[]config.CostBlockedUser{Sub, Rule, Day}` capped at MaxCostBlockedUsers and checked with ValidateCostBlockedUsers. Anonymous spend is never published.
The list is computed state merged into policyWire in loadPolicy like blockedUsers and never stored in policy_versions, so a rollback cannot clear it. Entries for past days are never served.

When the list changes, append a policy_publish_log row with reason `user_cost` (W-P1-PVER-05 pattern) and call policyServer.Refresh so W-P2-SBND-02 bundles get a higher seq and long-poll waiters wake. An unchanged list writes nothing.

A query error keeps the previous list and ETag, logs one ERROR `user_cost_recompute_failed` without subs, and increments the in-memory `warden_cp_cost_recompute_errors_total`; gauge `warden_cp_cost_blocked_users` holds the list size, both for W-P5-RETN-06 to export.

summary: When a request needs a user grant or connected account that does not exist yet, the worker can hold it for a short time while the CP notifies the user. If the user completes the flow in time the request continues; otherwise the agent gets the normal JIT 403.
design: Per-agent settings `park: {enabled: false, maxWait: 20s (cap 60s), notify: true}` distributed in SettingsWire; worker-wide `park.maxConcurrent` (default 256) and `park.maxPerUser` (default 8). Overflow returns the JIT 403 immediately.

Worker calls CP `POST /internal/park` (worker mTLS) with {sub, agent, provider, scopes or grant request, method, host, path-without-query}; CP reuses or creates the pending authorization from p3-connect-links, sends the notification, and returns {authorization_id, status_url}.

New package internal/park: `Waiter.Wait(ctx, statusURL, deadline)` long-polls `GET /connect/{id}/status?wait=` until completed, denied or deadline. Effective deadline = min(maxWait, client hint `X-Warden-Max-Wait`, global cap).

On completion the worker invalidates the per-user token cache entry and re-runs the secret swap stage, then forwards. The request body stays in memory (already bounded by maxBodySwapSize) and is never persisted.

Client-gone safety: a watcher on the client conn aborts the park when the client closes; the request is never forwarded after abort. Metrics `warden_park_total{outcome}` (resumed|timeout|denied|client_gone|overflow) and `warden_park_wait_seconds`.
done_when: With park enabled, a request missing a grant is held, the user gets a Slack/email link, and completing the flow within maxWait lets the original request succeed; otherwise the agent receives the JIT 403.

summary: Workers expose MCP gateways at `/mcp/{gateway}` over Streamable HTTP. Each gateway bundles several upstream MCP servers from the registry, presents one namespaced tool list, routes calls to the right upstream, and applies the existing verdict engine and per-user credentials, so agents get one MCP URL instead of many.
design: New package internal/mcp/hub (the existing internal/mcp/gateway stays the verdict engine). Served on a dedicated worker listener `mcpGateway.listen` (default off, e.g. :8090, optional TLS) because agents call it directly, not through CONNECT.

Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <warden session token>` verified like proxy identity; agent from `act.sub` (or port mapping when identity is off); session id `Mcp-Session-Id` (128-bit random), idle TTL 30m, max 1024 sessions per worker; DELETE ends a session.
Gateway definitions in the CP and bundle: `gateways: [{name, servers: [{registryId, tools: [...]}]}]`; effective tools = gateway selection ∩ registry approvedTools ∩ policy.

tools/list fans out to upstreams in parallel (per-upstream timeout 5s), names tools `server__tool`, drops tools that fail pins; tools/call splits the prefix, runs `OnRequestCtx` with session key `agent:gateway:server`, forwards, then `OnResponse` on the result. Only tools are proxied in v1; resources/prompts return method not found.

Upstream HTTP/SSE traffic loops back through the worker's own forward proxy so allowlist, DLP, secret swap, per-user placeholders and audit apply unchanged; stdio upstreams are launched after `stdio.VerifyBinary`/`VerifyEd25519` with registry integrity.
Per-user upstream sessions keyed by (sub, server) when the server needs per-user credentials; missing grant -> Phase 3 JIT tool error or park.

summary: Operators can attach external checks before a request is forwarded and after a response returns: signed webhooks, OPA (REST or embedded) and CEL expressions. Hooks can only add restrictions, never allow something policy denied, and each has a timeout and fail mode.
design: New package internal/hooks with `Hook` interface `Evaluate(ctx, Input) (Result, error)`; Result is `allow|deny` + bounded reason. Pre hooks run after policy/MCP verdict allow and before secret swap; post hooks run on response metadata before relay.

Input is bounded metadata: identity (sub, groups, agent, grant_id), domain, port, method, path without query, MCP tool name, DLP classes, findings kinds. Tool args are passed only to in-process hooks (CEL, embedded OPA) with `includeArgs: true`; remote hooks never get bodies or args.

Config `hooks: [{name, stage: pre|post, type: webhook|opa|cel, match: {agents, domains, tools}, timeout: 200ms, failMode: open|closed, ...}]` distributed in settings; total pre-hook budget 500ms per request.
Webhook signs with the existing `X-Warden-Timestamp`/`X-Warden-Signature` v1 HMAC scheme from internal/integration/webhook (exported as a shared helper); response `{decision, reason}`.

OPA: REST `POST {url}/v1/data/{path}` or embedded `github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/rego` with a local bundle; result `deny` bool or {deny, reason}. CEL: `github.com/google/cel-go`, compiled at load, `denyIf` expression.
Metrics `warden_hook_duration_seconds{hook}`, `warden_hook_decisions_total{hook,decision}`, `warden_hook_errors_total{hook,kind}`; deny events use Reason `hook_<name>`.

name: Secret backend
summary: ENV, HashiCorp Vault KV and AWS Secrets Manager providers with a TTL cache; GCP is interface-only.

Each worker can write a separate JSON decision stream, one line per stored analytics event, to stdout, stderr or a rotating file, with verified user identity fields. A SIEM shipper (Vector, Fluent Bit, Splunk UF) can read it without parsing operational logs. The schema is versioned, closed and documented, and never holds bodies, headers, query values or secret values. Two existing gaps are fixed first: swapped secrets can reach Event.URL today, and most deny events have no reason.
design: Fix first (W-P1-JAUD-05): swapSecrets in internal/proxy/http.go rewrites s.req.URL.RawQuery with the real secret, and recordAllowEvent, relayMCPSSE and the post-forward event sites then build fullURL from s.req.URL.RequestURI(). The real value can reach SQLite, signed receipts, logDecision lines and central sync. requestScope gains a new auditURL field captured in readRequest before swapSecrets and applyTransforms; every StoreEvent and logDecision site in internal/proxy uses it.

Deny reasons (W-P1-JAUD-06): every deny site sets Event.Reason from one bounded set shared with Metrics.RecordBlocked (policy, no_tls, judge, dlp, mcp_*; later tickets add headers_too_large (W-P1-VRFY-02), user_blocked (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and identity_required / group_not_allowed (W-P1-GPOL-03) to the same set; attribute-mode identity itself never denies). storeDeny in serve.go stops dropping its reason argument, and a test fails on any deny event with an empty Reason.

New package internal/auditlog. Record is a closed struct and FromEvent(analytics.Event, Meta) Record is the only mapping from Event. It never marshals Event, so SecretRef, Evidence, bodies, headers and future Event fields cannot leak. Each line is json.Marshal(Record) plus a newline, written in one Write; slog is not used, so no time/level/msg keys appear. p5-otlp should map this Record to OTel attributes instead of keeping a second allowlist.

Placement off the request path: analytics.WithOnBatch becomes additive (several tees; alerts.Observe uses it today). The auditlog Sink is a tee on the async writer's goroutine, so it sees each event once, after compliance tagging and signing, and is not affected by the managed apply loop rebuilding the TaggingStore. The tee hands each batch to the sink's own bounded channel without blocking; a separate goroutine writes through a bufio.Writer flushed once per batch. A full channel drops the batch and counts it, so a slow disk can never back-pressure the async writer or requests.

Failure mode: the stream is best effort; the SQLite store and signed receipts stay the record of truth. A write error or drop never blocks or fails a request; it increments a counter and logs a rate-limited WARN without record content. With enabled and output file, a path that cannot be opened fails startup, like signedReceipts.log. The stream does not need the CP or the IdP.

Config in the existing node-local audit block (Config.Audit is json:"-", restart only): audit.jsonLog {enabled: false, output: stdout|stderr|file, path, maxSizeMB: 100, maxBackups: 10, maxAgeDays: 30, compress: false, fileMode: 0600, query: drop|keys}. Parsed in parseAudit and checked in validateAudit (internal/config/audit.go). Rotation uses gopkg.in/natefinch/lumberjack.v2 pinned in go.mod; the first file is created with fileMode so lumberjack keeps that mode on rotation. When output is stdout, the operational logger moves to stderr so the streams never mix.

Schema warden.decision.v1, one line per stored event: schema, schema_rev, ts (UTC RFC 3339 nanoseconds), proxy_id (expanded central.proxyId, else os.Hostname()), proxy_id_source, agent_id, boot_id (random per process), seq (per boot, assigned at the tee so drops show as gaps), decision, reason, protocol, domain, port, method, url_path (pre-swap path only, userinfo and fragment removed, max 2 KiB), query_keys (sorted names only, when query: keys), status, latency_ms, tool, provider, cost_usd, dlp_action, dlp_rule, dlp_partial, data_classes, swapped_refs (placeholder names), compliance, judge_reason (max 512 bytes, control characters removed), user{status, sub, email, groups, groups_truncated, sid}, truncated. User fields other than status appear only when status is valid; groups are capped at 64. A whole line is capped at 16 KiB. event_uid is not in v1 because it is only set at central sync.

Versioning: docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json and warden.admin.v1.json (JSON Schema 2020-12, additionalProperties false). v1 accepts only additive optional fields with a schema_rev bump; Record, schema file and docs change in the same PR, enforced by a reflection test. Consumers must ignore unknown fields. Breaking changes ship as v2 next to v1 for one minor release.

CP admin lines: the CP reads the same audit.jsonLog block and passes the writer to the p1-admin-audit middleware, which emits warden.admin.v1 lines after the admin audit row is stored. Collectors route both streams on the top-level schema field.

Metrics in internal/observability, nil-safe: warden.auditlog.lines.total{schema}, warden.auditlog.write_errors.total{reason}, warden.auditlog.dropped.total. A startup INFO line shows output, path and schema version.
done_when: With audit.jsonLog.enabled: true and output: file on a real worker, every stored analytics event (CONNECT/tcp, HTTPS, MCP over HTTP, SSE and WS, gRPC) produces exactly one line that matches warden.decision.v1, with proxy_id, boot_id and a gap-free seq under normal disk conditions. Every deny line has a non-empty reason from the documented set. User sub, email and groups appear only for valid tokens. A request with a secret placeholder in its query never shows the real value in the line, the SQLite row, the receipt or the operational log. A failing disk increments write or drop counters without failing requests. Files rotate at maxSizeMB and keep at most maxBackups. A CP policy save emits one warden.admin.v1 line, and the documented Vector config ships both streams from the compose recipe into a test sink.

tickets.title: Record the pre-swap URL on events and decision logs
tickets.body: swapSecrets in internal/proxy/http.go writes the real secret into s.req.URL.RawQuery, and several event sites later build fullURL from s.req.URL.RequestURI(). A placeholder in a query string therefore puts the real value into Event.URL, which goes to SQLite, signed receipts, logDecision and central sync. Capture the URL in readRequest, before swapSecrets and applyTransforms, and use that copy at every StoreEvent and logDecision site. This must land before any export of Event.URL.
requirements: requestScope gets a new auditURL string field set in readRequest from scheme, s.domain and the original escaped path and query, before swapSecrets and applyTransforms run.
Every StoreEvent and logDecision call in internal/proxy (http.go, ws.go, grpc.go) that builds a URL uses auditURL instead of s.req.URL.RequestURI().
The forwarded upstream request is unchanged: the real secret is still swapped into the outgoing query.
No real secret value appears in Event.URL, the signed receipt, the operational decision log or central sync payloads.
No config flag: this is a leak fix with no new behaviour; events now carry the placeholder the agent sent.
No new logging of secret values, headers or bodies is added.
plan: internal/proxy/http.go: add auditURL to requestScope and set it in readRequest (around the existing fullURL build at line ~327).
internal/proxy/http.go: replace the post-swap fullURL builds in recordAllowEvent, relayMCPSSE and the post-forward event sites (~866, ~908, ~1064, ~1104) with s.auditURL.
internal/proxy/ws.go and internal/proxy/grpc.go: use the scope's auditURL where they record a URL after the swap.
New test in internal/proxy/http_test.go (or a new swap_url_test.go): send a request with ?key=<placeholder> through a proxy with a fake secret source, a signing store and a buffered logger.
Assert the upstream test server received the real value, and that the stored Event.URL, the receipt line and the log buffer contain the placeholder and never the real value.
acceptance: A request to https://api.example.test/v1/x?key=<placeholder> reaches the upstream with the real value in the query.
The stored Event.URL contains the placeholder, and the real value is absent from the Event, the signed receipt line and the operational log output.
The same holds for an MCP SSE request and an allowed request recorded by recordAllowEvent.
`go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestSwappedQueryNotRecorded` passes, and `scripts/check.sh` passes.

tickets.title: Set a bounded Reason on every deny event
tickets.body: Most deny events have an empty Event.Reason today: storeDeny in internal/proxy/serve.go takes a reason and drops it, and the CONNECT deny paths (policy, no_tls) never set it. A SIEM cannot tell a policy deny from a no_tls, judge or DLP deny without it. Fill Reason on every deny site from the same bounded set used by Metrics.RecordBlocked, and document the set.
requirements: storeDeny sets Event.Reason from its reason argument.
The CONNECT deny paths in serve.go (policy, no_tls) and every deny StoreEvent in http.go, ws.go, grpc.go and tls.go set Reason.

Reason values come from one bounded set defined as constants in a new internal/proxy/reasons.go and shared with RecordBlocked calls; free text is never stored in Reason. Later deny reasons (headers_too_large from W-P1-VRFY-02, user_blocked from W-P1-BLOCK-02, identity_required and group_not_allowed from W-P1-GPOL-03) are added to this file by those tickets.
Existing MCP reasons keep their current values so stored events and dashboards stay compatible.
Allow events keep an empty Reason.
No config flag: the field already exists and the change only fills it.
plan: New internal/proxy/reasons.go: constants for policy, no_tls, judge, dlp and the existing mcp_* values, plus a Reasons() list for docs and tests.
internal/proxy/serve.go: storeDeny passes reason into the Event; the policy and no_tls paths at ~108 and ~132 set Reason.
internal/proxy/http.go, ws.go, grpc.go, tls.go: set Reason on each deny event using the constants that match the existing RecordBlocked call.
New test internal/proxy/reasons_test.go: drive each deny path with a recording store and assert Reason is non-empty and in Reasons().
docs/architecture.md: list the reason values in the analytics event section.
acceptance: A CONNECT to a domain not in policy stores a deny event with Reason policy.
A CONNECT to a TLS-required domain without TLS stores Reason no_tls; judge and DLP denies store judge and dlp.
Every deny event produced in the test run has a Reason contained in Reasons().
`go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestDenyReasons` passes.

tickets.title: Add internal/auditlog decision stream on the async writer tee
tickets.body: Create new package internal/auditlog that writes one warden.decision.v1 JSON line per stored analytics event to stdout, stderr or a rotating file. The sink runs as a tee on the async analytics writer's goroutine and hands batches to its own bounded queue, so it adds no I/O to the request goroutine and cannot stall the async writer. Config sits under the existing audit block as audit.jsonLog, off by default. Write errors and drops are counted and never fail a request.
requirements: Config: audit.jsonLog {enabled: false, output: stdout|stderr|file, path, maxSizeMB: 100, maxBackups: 10, maxAgeDays: 30, compress: false, fileMode: 0600, query: drop|keys (default drop)} in internal/config/audit.go. Validation rejects file output without a path, unknown output or query values, and maxSizeMB <= 0. Restart only.
Record: closed Record struct built only by FromEvent(analytics.Event, Meta); never marshals Event. Fields as listed in the feature design; event_uid is not included.

Content limits: url_path keeps only the path (no userinfo, fragment or query values), max 2 KiB; query_keys only when query is keys; judge_reason max 512 bytes with control characters removed; groups max 64 with groups_truncated; whole line max 16 KiB with truncated true.
Identity: user.status is always set when the event has an IdentityStatus; sub, email, groups and sid are written only when status is valid.

Placement: analytics.WithOnBatch becomes additive so alerts.Observe and the sink both run. The tee assigns seq and enqueues without blocking; a full queue drops the batch and increments warden.auditlog.dropped.total. A single goroutine writes each line with one Write through a bufio.Writer flushed per batch.

Output: file output uses lumberjack.v2 pinned in go.mod; the first file is created with fileMode. A file that cannot be opened at startup fails startup. When output is stdout, the worker's operational logger is moved to stderr and this is logged once.

Metrics: nil-safe RecordAuditLogLine(schema), RecordAuditLogWriteError(reason) and RecordAuditLogDropped(n) on observability.Metrics, backed by warden.auditlog.lines.total, warden.auditlog.write_errors.total and warden.auditlog.dropped.total. Error logs are rate limited and never include record content.
Back-compat: with the block absent or enabled false there is no tee, no goroutine and no change to analytics rows, receipts or fleet ingest.
plan: internal/config/audit.go: add JSONLogConfig to AuditConfig, a jsonLog block in rawAudit, defaults in parseAudit and checks in validateAudit; tests in internal/config/audit_test.go.
internal/analytics/async.go: change WithOnBatch to append to a slice of tee funcs and call each in order; extend TestAsyncWriter_OnBatchTee for two tees.
New internal/auditlog/record.go: Record, Meta{ProxyID, ProxyIDSource, AgentID, BootID} and FromEvent with the URL, query, truncation and identity rules.

New internal/auditlog/sink.go: New(cfg config.JSONLogConfig, meta Meta, m *observability.Metrics) (*Sink, error), Observe([]analytics.Event) for the tee, a bounded queue, the writer goroutine, and Close(ctx) that drains the queue and closes lumberjack.
internal/observability/observability.go: register the three auditlog counters in newMetrics and add the nil-safe Record methods.

internal/worker/worker.go: when pol.Audit.JSONLog.Enabled, build Meta (proxy_id from expandEnv(pol.Central.ProxyID) else os.Hostname(); agent_id from buildJudge), create the Sink, add analytics.WithOnBatch(sink.Observe) to asyncOpts, route the operational logger to stderr for stdout output, and close the sink after asyncStore.Close().

Tests: internal/auditlog/record_test.go (URL rules, caps, identity gating), sink_test.go (one line per event, seq order, rotation, file mode after rotation, full queue drops without blocking, failing writer), and internal/worker/analytics_chain_test.go (compliance tags reach the line, a compliance toggle keeps the sink).
acceptance: With output file, driving an allowed HTTPS request, a policy deny, a no_tls CONNECT deny and a WebSocket upgrade produces as many lines as analytics rows, each with schema warden.decision.v1 and consecutive seq values: `go test -race ./internal/auditlog ./internal/worker -run 'TestDecisionStream|TestAnalyticsChain'`.
An Event with URL https://u:p@api.example.test/v1/x?token=abc#frag gives url_path /v1/x and none of token=abc, u:p or #frag; with query keys the line has query_keys ["token"] and still no value.
An event with IdentityStatus invalid and a sub claim produces user.status invalid and no user.sub, user.email or user.groups.
With maxSizeMB 1 and maxBackups 2, writing 3.5 MB leaves at most one active file plus two backups, all with mode 0600, and no line split across files: `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestRotation`.
With a writer that always errors or blocks, 10 tee'd events still produce 10 SQLite rows, the request handler returns its normal status, and write_errors or dropped increases.
With output stdout, stdout carries only lines whose schema is warden.decision.v1 and operational records go to stderr.
Config `audit: {jsonLog: {enabled: true, output: file}}` with no path, or output syslog, fails to load with an error naming audit.jsonLog: `go test ./internal/config -run TestAuditJSONLogConfig`.

tickets.title: Publish decision v1 JSON Schema with closed-field and leak tests
tickets.body: Add docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json and pin it to auditlog.Record with tests, so the schema and the code cannot drift and no unreviewed Event field can reach the stream. The tests compare struct tags with the schema in both directions, check that every analytics.Event field is either mapped or explicitly excluded, and prove that secrets, evidence and header names never appear in a line. No new Go dependency is added.
requirements: docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json uses JSON Schema 2020-12 with additionalProperties false at every object level, schema as a required const, ts required with format date-time, and reason as an enum taken from the W-P1-JAUD-06 set.

The schema description states the versioning rule: additive optional fields only in v1 with a schema_rev bump; breaking changes ship as v2 next to v1 for one minor release; consumers ignore unknown fields.
A reflection test compares Record json tags (including nested user) with the schema properties and required list in both directions.
A leak-guard test fails when an exported analytics.Event field is neither mapped in FromEvent nor listed in an explicit excludedEventFields list (SecretRef, Evidence and others).
A negative test proves that a fake secret value, SecretRef, Evidence strings and header names (Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key) never appear in emitted bytes.
Validation uses the reflection checker plus a per-property type check, so go.mod gains no JSON Schema library.
plan: Add new docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json.

New internal/auditlog/schema_test.go: load ../../docs/schemas/warden.decision.v1.json, compare properties and required with Record tags, and check each property's JSON type against a fully populated marshaled Record.
New internal/auditlog/leak_test.go: TestEventFieldsAccountedFor walks reflect.TypeOf(analytics.Event{}) against the mapped and excluded lists.
In leak_test.go add TestNoSecretLeak: build an Event with SecretRef, Evidence, a fake secret in the URL query and JudgeReason, write it through a Sink to a buffer, and scan the bytes.
Assert the reason enum in the schema equals proxy.Reasons() from W-P1-JAUD-06.
acceptance: Adding a field to Record but not the schema, or the reverse, makes `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestDecisionRecordMatchesSchema` fail and name the field.
Adding an exported field to analytics.Event without mapping or excluding it makes `go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestEventFieldsAccountedFor` fail and name the field.
`go test ./internal/auditlog -run TestNoSecretLeak` passes and finds no secret value, SecretRef, Evidence or header name in the output.
`scripts/check.sh` passes.

tickets.title: Write CP admin audit lines as warden.admin.v1 JSON
tickets.body: Let the control plane read the same audit.jsonLog block and pass an auditlog writer to the admin audit middleware from W-P1-AAUD-02, so every CP mutation also produces a warden.admin.v1 line for the SIEM. The line is written only after the admin audit row is stored, and a write failure never fails the admin request. This ticket also owns docs/schemas/warden.admin.v1.json, because the admin record only exists after W-P1-AAUD-02.
requirements: cmd/proxy/controlplane.go runControlPlane builds the writer when pol.Audit.JSONLog.Enabled and passes it to the middleware through a new controlplane.Config field; cmd stays construction only.

New closed AdminRecord: schema warden.admin.v1, schema_rev, ts, cp_id, boot_id, seq, actor{sub, email, role}, auth_method, action, target, target_ref, outcome (ok|denied|rejected|error, the W-P1-AAUD-02 set), before_hash, after_hash, request_id, and chain_seq, entry_hash, prev_hash and key_id copied from the stored admin_audit row so the shipped copy anchors the chain. The periodic `admin_audit.checkpoint` lines from W-P1-AAUD-02 are written as warden.admin.v1 records too. Request bodies, tokens and cookies are never fields.

The line is written after adminaudit.Store.Append succeeds, through an adminaudit.Emitter (the W-P1-AAUD-02 seam), outside the chain mutex. A write error logs a rate-limited WARN (the CP has no metrics endpoint in P1) and does not roll back the stored row or change the response.
Denied (403) mutations are written with outcome denied.
The existing admin_audit operational log line stays unchanged whether or not the sink is enabled; with output stdout the CP operational logger moves to stderr.
Default off: with audit.jsonLog absent or disabled, CP behaviour is unchanged.
plan: New internal/auditlog/admin.go: AdminRecord and a WriteAdmin(rec AdminRecord) method on the sink, sharing the queue, caps and metrics from W-P1-JAUD-01.

cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: construct the sink with Meta{ProxyID: hostname, ProxyIDSource: hostname}, set the new controlplane.Config.AuditLog field, close it on shutdown, and move the operational logger to stderr for stdout output.

internal/controlplane: when the writer is non-nil, register an adminaudit.Emitter (W-P1-AAUD-02 seam) that builds AdminRecord from the stored entry and calls WriteAdmin, chained after the default slog emitter.
Add new docs/schemas/warden.admin.v1.json and internal/auditlog/admin_test.go with the same closed-field reflection test as W-P1-JAUD-02.
Tests in internal/controlplane: policy save, viewer 403, disabled sink and failing writer cases.
acceptance: With audit.jsonLog enabled and output file, an admin policy save adds exactly one line with schema warden.admin.v1, outcome ok, actor.sub set and before_hash different from after_hash: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAdminAuditJSONSink`.
A viewer's policy save that returns 403 adds one line with outcome denied, and the policy is unchanged.
With the sink disabled, the operational logger still records admin_audit and no audit file is created.
With a writer that errors, the policy save still returns 200 and the admin audit chain still verifies.
A request body field named token with a value never appears in the emitted line.

tickets.title: Document SIEM shipping with Vector and Fluent Bit examples
tickets.body: Write docs/siem.md so operators can turn on the decision and admin streams and ship them to a SIEM. Ship the Vector and Fluent Bit examples as real files, add a compose override that enables the stream on a shared volume, and check the docs against the schemas in the default test gate. Running the shipper binaries is an opt-in integration step.
requirements: docs/siem.md explains the streams versus operational logs, the audit.jsonLog config, a field table for both schemas checked against docs/schemas, the reason set, the versioning rule, and gap detection with boot_id and seq.
Rotation and retention guidance: typical bytes per line, how to size maxSizeMB and maxBackups, and that the SQLite store and receipts stay the record of truth.

Security guidance: default fileMode 0600, using fileMode 0640 with a shared group for a shipper running as another UID, read-only mounts for sidecars, TLS to the SIEM endpoint, the PII note on user.email, and that path segments are not scrubbed.

Example files docs/siem/vector.yaml (file source, JSON parse, route on schema, http or splunk_hec sink with a console alternative) and docs/siem/fluent-bit.conf (tail input, json parser, rewrite on schema).
Kubernetes guidance: output stdout with a node-level collector filtering on the schema key, operational logs on stderr.
New deploy/compose/docker-compose.siem.yml override enables audit.jsonLog output file on a shared volume and runs Vector with a file sink.

summary: Warden can send messages to a specific person, not just an alert channel: connect links, grant approval requests, parked-request prompts and expiry warnings, by Slack DM or email. It reuses the internal/integration router for delivery, retries and dead-lettering, and finds the Slack user by the person's email.
design: Add an optional capability interface `UserNotifier { NotifyUser(ctx, UserMessage) error }` in internal/integration, discovered by type assertion like `Alerter`. `UserMessage{ID, Kind, Recipient{Sub, Email}, Title, Text, ActionURL, ActionLabel}`; ID is deterministic for idempotent delivery.

Router gains `DeliverUser(msg)` using its existing per-binding queues, backoff and dead-letter; user messages are not deduped by AlertManager and are bound by `notifications.channels` order instead of alert match clauses.

New integrations `slack` (internal/integration/slack: bot token, `users.lookupByEmail` with 24h cache and 1h negative cache, `conversations.open` + `chat.postMessage` with a button) and `email` (internal/integration/email: SMTP with STARTTLS, text + HTML).

New package internal/notify `Service.Send(ctx, kind, sub, data)` in the CP: resolves email from the user directory captured at sign-in, renders embedded templates per kind, tries channels in order with `fallbackToEmail`, dedups per (sub, kind, ref) for 10 min and rate-limits 10 per user per 5 min.
Messages carry only bounded fields (agent name, provider, scopes, purpose, URL); a check like `assertEgressSafe` rejects anything over size caps.
done_when: A connect link or grant approval for a user arrives as a Slack DM (or email when Slack lookup fails) with a working action link, with retries and dedup visible in the integrations status.

summary: Warden ships reference OpenTelemetry Collector configurations that forward worker decision logs, traces and CP admin audit to Splunk, Datadog and Microsoft Sentinel. Each comes with collector authentication and a starter pack of dashboards and detections.
design: Reference configs under deploy/otel-collector/: `base.yaml` (otlp receiver with mTLS + bearertokenauth extension, memory_limiter, batch, attributes processor that drops any non-`warden.*`/semconv keys, transform to set `source=warden`), and `splunk.yaml`, `datadog.yaml`, `sentinel.yaml` exporter overlays using the contrib distribution.

Splunk: `splunk_hec` exporter (token from env, index/sourcetype `warden:decision`, `warden:admin_audit`); Datadog: `datadog` exporter for logs and traces with `DD_API_KEY` env; Sentinel: `azuremonitor`/Logs Ingestion API via a DCR and a custom table `WardenDecision_CL` schema file.
Admin audit and break-glass events from the CP are emitted as OTel logs (`warden.event.kind=admin_audit`) through the same pipeline so SIEM sees both data-plane and control-plane activity.

Starter pack per SIEM: dashboard JSON (decisions by agent/user, top denied hosts, DLP classes, secret swaps, break-glass use) and detections (deny spike per user, new destination for agent, DLP credentials class allowed, break-glass login, policy widened without approval, revoked user still active), mapped to existing MITRE/OWASP tags from internal/audit.
Validation: CI runs `otelcol-contrib validate --config` on each file and an e2e that sends fixture OTLP logs through the base config into a file exporter and asserts the attribute allowlist.
done_when: Each reference collector config validates in CI, forwards fixture decision and admin-audit logs to its SIEM format, and the starter dashboards and detections import cleanly.
